countries.name: Madagascar
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: Madagascar - Tropical Cyclones, 2026
summary:
Madagascar has experienced successive cyclones that have significantly disrupted access to food, health care, and other essential services for numerous communities. Within a ten-day period, two severe storms intensified an already critical situation.

Cyclone Fytia developed on January 28, 2026, made landfall three days later, and traversed Madagascar until February 1. The cyclone resulted in extensive flooding and widespread displacement before subsiding and returning to sea on February 2. Cyclone Gezani subsequently impacted the region, arriving on February 11, just ten days after Fytia.

Tropical Cyclone Fytia

Cyclone Fytia arrived in Madagascar as a Category 3 storm on January 31, bringing heavy floods to the northwest. By February 8, official reports indicated 14 fatalities, with more than 31,000 people displaced and over 200,000 individuals affected across 35 districts, particularly within the Boeny Region. The cyclone had repercussions in nine regions: Boeny, Analamanga, Melaky, Sofia, Vakinankaratra, Betsiboka, Atsinanana, Alaotra Mangoro, and Itasy.

Tropical Cyclone Gezani

Cyclone Gezani moved swiftly through Madagascar, entering the Mozambique Channel near Antsalova at approximately 5 p.m. on February 11 before degrading into a tropical storm. The event was marked by substantial rainfall nationwide, prompting governmental requests for international assistance. On February 12, central-western Madagascar faced forecasts of further rain and strong winds, resulting in a red alert for wind and flooding. The Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System (GDACS) estimated that 1.9 million residents were exposed to Category 1 or higher wind speeds (119–153 km/h), with maximum winds peaking at 211 km/h (Category 4). The GDCA assigned a score of 2.5 (red) to the impact assessment.

countries.name: Paraguay
dtype.name: Fire
name: PRY: Fire - 02-2026 - Forest Fire - Villa Hayes
summary:
Between Wednesday, February 4 and Thursday, February 5, 2026, a large forest and grassland fire was recorded in the rural area of Río Verde, district of Villa Hayes (Paraguayan Bajo Chaco). The event generated dense smoke that significantly reduced visibility and deteriorated air quality, with a perceptible impact not only in the area of the fire but also in localities of the Bajo Chaco and the metropolitan area of Asunción.

The fire predominantly affected grasslands, a type of fuel characteristic of the region that favors the rapid spread of fire under conditions of high temperatures and wind. The National Forestry Institute reported the detection of at least 18 heat sources through satellite monitoring during the morning of February 5.

The affected area is estimated at 400–460 hectares, differences attributable to the different measurement times and the methods used (satellite analysis versus operational evaluations in the field). The fire was brought under control after more than eight hours of continuous work, with the participation of volunteer firefighters and the support of air resources from the Armed Forces.

There were no fatalities, injuries or displacements, although thousands of people were exposed to the effects of smoke, which generated preventive recommendations to reduce exposure, especially in vulnerable populations. Subsequent weather conditions, characterised by high temperatures, maintained the risk of fire reactivation in the absence of sufficient rainfall.

summary:
Aux environs de 23 heures de la nuit du 05 février 2026 dans l’arrondissement de Darak, les GANEs ont fait incursion dans la ville et ses environs faisant une attaque dont le bilan s’élève à 5788 personnes déplacés et de plusieurs personnes blessées et d'importants dégâts matériels (deux antennes du réseau MTN incendié et presque toutes les infrastructures publiques incendiées). Ceci a causé un afflux massif de population  vers les zones plus sécures de HILE ALIFA, BLANGOUA et Makary et vers certaines localités plus proches au pays voisin le TCHAD. On note jusqu’à qu’aujourd’hui 1201 ménages installés dans les sites de l’arrondissement de Blangoua (1571 personnes) et de Hilé-Alifa (4217 personnes). La population déplacée est composé d'un nombre important de personnes à besoins spécifiques ( 1078 femmes enceintes et femmes allaitantes; 1965 enfants de moins de 05 ans). Ces personnes ont trouvé refuge dans des sites de fortune (écoles, gares routières, délégation d'arrondissement de l'agriculture et du développement rurale), ainsi que dans des familles d'accueil. 

cette situation vient trouver déjà une communauté hôte fragilisée par les effets des changements climatiques, par un contexte sécuritaire volatile, et des communautés pour la plupart en situation d'insécurité économique.

dès les premières arrivées, le comité départemental du Logone et Chari  aux côtés des comités d'arrondissement de Blangoua et de Hilé-Alifa ont mené une évalaution rapide de la situation. Selon ce rapport, les besoins immédiats de ces personnes  se rapportent pour l'essentiel à l'alimentation, aux abris et latrines, à l'accès à l'eau, aux médicaments, aux articles essentiels de ménages. En attendant l'évaluation approfondie,  qui sera menée par le CICR conjointement avec la SN, la situation de ces populations déplacées est de plus en plus alarmante et une assistance d'urgence est indispensable.  Des arrivées continuent ainsi que le rescencement. Considérant la situation actuelle,  les risques problables à craindre sont les maladies telles que le choléra ou autre maladies hydriques, l'aggravation de la malnutrition au regard du nombre importants d'enfants de moins de 5 ans, la séparation des familles...

countries.name: Australia

name: AUS: Flood - 02-2026 - 2026 Big Rivers Flooding
summary:
On Wednesday 4 February, the Northern Territory Government issued an emergency declaration for Daly River - Nauiyu approximately 220 kilometres southwest of Darwin, in anticipation of major flooding. The road into Daly River has been blocked off and schools and shops have been shut. Only a few officials, including police, some residents and animal welfare officers, remain (approx. 60 people). Three-quarters of the airstrip is underwater and there are currently no passable roads into the town. 

The Incident Controller and NT Police Superintendent could not give a timeline for when residents could expect to return to their homes as the water levels were “very slow moving”. Before residents could return home the town and its essential services would need to be assessed for damage and cleaned up, with recovery efforts to be determined by road access. The Police Superintendent stated, “it will be several days or up to a week before we can get assessments in, depending on how much damage or how quickly the water recedes.” 

An evacuation centre was established on Wednesday 4 February at the Darwin Showgrounds (Foskey’s Pavilion) to support residents evacuated from the Nauiyu community (Daly River). Of the people that were evacuated, 298 people including 110 children, are still staying at Foskey Pavilion at the Darwin Showgrounds, with some vulnerable patients being cared for at the Free Spirit resort. Some people who had been staying at Free Spirit have now relocated to Foskey. (Secure NT). Other community members are staying with family and friends in the Darwin region. The Nauiyu community has experienced recurrent flooding in recent years, resulting in multiple evacuations to Darwin due to flood impacts.

countries.name: Greece
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: GRC: Population Movement - 02-2026 - Chios Maritime Collision
summary:
On the night of 3 February 2026, a deadly maritime collision occurred off the eastern Aegean island of Chios, involving a speedboat carrying migrants and a Greek Coast Guard patrol vessel. The incident rapidly escalated into one of the most severe migration‑related maritime tragedies in recent years, prompting an extensive search and rescue operation across the area. According to statements from the Hellenic Coast Guard, the migrant speedboat failed to respond to visual and audio warnings and instead changed course, leading to a direct collision with the Coast Guard vessel. The impact caused the speedboat to capsize and sink, throwing all passengers into the sea. The collision took place approximately 1.5 nautical miles off Chios, within Greek territorial waters. The vessel, about 8 meters in length, was carrying an estimated 35 to 39 migrants, many of whom were not wearing life jackets.

Across all verified reports, the confirmed death toll reached 15 people. Fourteen bodies—11 men and 3 women—were recovered from the sea, while an additional woman died later in the hospital due to her injuries. Among the survivors, at least 25 migrants, including 11 minors, were rescued and transported to Chios General Hospital, where several required immediate surgical intervention for severe trauma. Two Coast Guard officers were also injured during the incident, one suffering a shoulder dislocation and the other a concussion. Tragically, two pregnant women who survived the collision later lost their unborn children as a result of the physical and emotional trauma sustained.

Authorities launched a large‑scale emergency operation, deploying multiple Coast Guard patrol vessels, divers, and a helicopter equipped with thermal imaging technology, while private boats with specialized divers assisted underwater searches. The operation concentrated on locating survivors and any potentially missing passengers, as the exact number of people on board the migrant vessel remained uncertain. Medical teams on Chios were placed on high alert to manage the sudden influx of injured individuals requiring urgent care.

According to survivor testimonies, the majority of the passengers were Afghan nationals, with one Moroccan individual also on board. Investigations into the incident continue, as authorities work to determine the full circumstances surrounding the collision and assess the ongoing humanitarian needs of those affected.

countries.name: Nigeria
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: NGA: Population Movement - 02-2026 - Population Movement
summary:
On Tuesday, 3rd February 2025, at about 18:00 HRS, suspected members of an Armed Opposition Group (AOG) invaded the Woro community in the Kaiama Local Government Area of Kwara State. According to the residents, the attackers, estimated to be about 200 in number, stormed the community and began shooting sporadically, causing panic among residents. The assailants operated freely in the community for over one hour before security forces were mobilised. The delayed response from the military was due to the long distance over 50 kilometres from Kaiama to the Woro community, coupled with the deplorable condition of the access road, which hindered timely intervention.
According to the residents, the attackers killed several people during the invasion
and set many houses ablaze. Although details are still sketchy, unconfirmed reports indicate that about 162 persons were killed in the attack, but information from the state government puts the number of deaths at 75. At least six corpses were seen at the palace of the Emir of Woro. The attackers also set the Emir’s palace on fire before fleeing the area.
About 200000 people were affected by banditry in 2 communities in Kaiama local
government area of Kwara state; 162 people were reported dead, 10000 people
were displaced, and 70 people were injured.
In summary, about 200,000 people were affected by banditry in 2 communities, 1
local government areas in Kwara state; 162 people were reported
dead, 11 casualties were hospitalized, 11,000 people were displaced, 86 people were injured

countries.name: Zimbabwe
dtype.name: Flood
name: ZWE: Flood - 02-2026 - Zimbabwe Floods Preparedness and Response Project
summary: Zimbabwe has experienced above normal above-normal rainfall in several parts of the country following the release of the Seasonal Forecast by the Meteorological Services Department (MSD). Prolonged and intense rainfall, coupled with incidents of hailstorms, has resulted in localized flooding, damage to infrastructure, and increased humanitarian risks. In response to the evolving situation, MSD has issued several flood advisories highlighting areas expected to be affected and outlining recommended preparedness and early action measures to avert or minimise loss of life and property. The Department of Civil Protection (DCP), in collaboration with partners, continues to closely monitor the situation and coordinate preparedness and response activities at national and sub-national levels. Flooding has had wide-ranging impacts on households, livelihoods, and essential services across affected areas. Many households have experienced displacement, loss of shelter, and damage to household goods, with women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities facing heightened vulnerability. Both rural and urban communities have been affected, and continued rainfall is likely to result in further displacement. Livelihoods reliant on agriculture, petty trading, and informal employment have been disrupted, while livestock losses are anticipated due to drowning, prolonged exposure to cold and wet conditions, restricted access to grazing land, and increased risk of livestock disease in flooded zones. The agricultural sector has been significantly impacted, with flooding and hailstorms damaging crops at various growth stages, including maize, horticulture, and small grains. Waterlogging has reduced crop yields in some areas, while hailstorms have destroyed standing crops, threatening household food security and income sources. Flooding has also affected essential social services, with schools in flood-prone areas sustaining damage or being temporarily closed, disrupting learning. Health risks have increased due to a higher likelihood of waterborne diseases such as cholera, typhoid, and diarrhoeal illnesses, particularly in areas with compromised water and sanitation systems. Access to health facilities has been constrained in some locations due to flooded roads and damaged infrastructure. Additionally, minor injuries linked to collapsing structures and debris have been reported, while displacement and overcrowding in temporary shelters have heightened protection risks, especially for vulnerable population groups.

countries.name: Costa Rica
dtype.name: Civil Unrest
name: ITT: Civil Unrest - 02-2026 - National Elections 2026
summary:
On Sunday, February 1, 2026, in Costa Rica, all persons qualified to cast a vote have been summoned, the voting process before the receiving boards to elect President and Vice Presidents of the Republic and deputies to the Legislative Assembly according to articles 133 of the Political Constitution and 150 of the Electoral Code.

Based on the above, the massive mobilization of people during election hours coupled with caravans of vehicles that support the different candidates, coupled with the fact that due to the hubbub many people may commit reckless acts that may affect their own personal integrity or against other vulnerable people, not to mention that the probability of an environment of polarization where, people who may resort to violence because of their political preferences, increase the risk of injuries and deaths in the country.

The Costa Rican Red Cross is part of the National System of Risk Prevention and Emergency Care, as the first responder responsible for out-of-hospital care, so it has developed a plan for anticipation and prepositioning of resources to respond effectively to any incident that is the result of situations in the national elections.

countries.name: Morocco
dtype.name: Flood
name: MAR: Flood - 01-2026 - Inondations à Ksar El Kébir (Province de Larache)
summary:
De fortes précipitations dans le nord-ouest ont entraîné une montée des eaux de l’oued Loukkos et l’inondation de quartiers bas à Ksar El Kébir. Les autorités provinciales ont activé et maintenu un niveau d’alerte maximale et déployé des moyens (protection civile, pompage, barrières de sable, curage des réseaux). Des évacuations et hébergements temporaires sont signalés.

  • Facteurs aggravants :

    • Sols saturés + poursuite des pluies + effet de marée freinant l’écoulement vers la mer.
  • Risques de désinformation : circulation de vidéos trompeuses  signalée par des médias.

3) Impacts humanitaires (à ce stade, selon sources ouvertes)

  • Déplacements/évacuations : des familles auraient dû évacuer ; installation de tentes et hébergement provisoire dans des internats (lycée Oued Al Makhazine, lycée qualifiant Al Mohammedia).
  • Infrastructures/Services : routes inondées, circulation perturbée ; coupures d’électricité temporaires dans certains quartiers exposés (mesures préventives).

countries.name: Spain
dtype.name: Flood
name: ESP: Flood - 01-2026 - Storm Leonardo
summary: In recent days, storm Leonardo has caused very significant flooding in Andalusia and Extremadura, with thousands of people evacuated, roads cut off, and rivers and reservoirs overflowing. In Andalusia, several thousand evacuees have been recorded (around 7,000 across the region) due to flooded homes, risk of building collapses, and rising river levels such as the Guadalquivir, which has clearly exceeded alert thresholds in stretches like Córdoba; in addition, dozens of regional and local roads have been closed and there have been disruptions to railway lines. In Extremadura, the main focus is on the southwest, due to increased flow in rivers such as the Guadiana and the Ardila and concern over a major surge of water linked to the possible overflow of the Valuengo dam (Badajoz), which has forced the evacuation of around 200 people and the activation of regional flood plans due to high water levels and reservoir releases.

countries.name: Portugal
dtype.name: Storm Surge
name: PRT: Storm Surge - 01-2026 - Kristin storm
summary:
The hazard took the form of a severe winter storm that swept across Portugal, bringing exceptionally strong winds, intense rainfall, and dangerous sea conditions. The force of the storm caused widespread physical damage, with trees uprooted, roofs torn from buildings, power lines brought down, and roads and railways blocked or rendered unsafe. In several areas, heavy rain led to flooding and landslides, further compounding the destruction and limiting access for emergency services.

The storm occurred in a context of already unstable weather conditions, with saturated ground and repeated Atlantic systems increasing the country’s vulnerability. As the event unfolded, civil protection authorities activated emergency response mechanisms, and thousands of firefighters, police officers, and other responders were deployed. Although the most intense phase of the storm has passed, the situation remains one of recovery and assessment, with ongoing clean-up operations and repairs to essential infrastructure.

The affected population includes residents of coastal, central, and northern regions, particularly those living in exposed locations or in housing more vulnerable to extreme weather. Elderly people, individuals with reduced mobility, and families with limited resources were especially impacted, as power outages and access restrictions reduced their ability to cope independently. Emergency responders themselves were also affected, facing hazardous working conditions and, in some cases, injury.

People have been affected in multiple ways. Some lost their lives and others were injured due to collapsing structures or falling debris. Several households were forced to leave their homes, either temporarily as a precaution or because the buildings were no longer safe to inhabit. Hundreds of thousands experienced interruptions to electricity and basic services, disrupting heating, communications, work, schooling, and access to healthcare. Beyond the physical damage, the storm has had significant social and emotional consequences, creating stress, uncertainty, and financial strain for individuals and communities as they work to recover and rebuild.

Population affected by service disruption

  • People without electricity at peak: between 450,000 and 855,000 customers

Emergency response and incidents

  • Emergency occurrences recorded: more than 5,400 nationwide

  • Emergency personnel deployed: approximately 18,000 responders

Meteorological severity

  • Maximum wind gusts: up to 150 km/h

countries.name: Malaysia
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: MYS: Epidemic - 01-2026 - Tuberculosis
summary:
By February 2026, Malaysia’s Ministry of Health (MOH) reported a sharp rise in tuberculosis (TB) cases, with 3,161 cumulative cases recorded by Epidemiological Week 6 and 596 new cases in that week alone. Sabah was the most affected state, reporting 755 cases, followed by Selangor (596 cases), Sarawak (332 cases), Johor (280 cases), and Kuala Lumpur/Putrajaya (244 cases) (Ministry of Health Malaysia, 2026; Bernama, 2026a). For example, in Sabah, district hospitals such as Queen Elizabeth Hospital faced overcrowding in respiratory wards, while Selangor’s urban clinics reported long queues for GeneXpert testing, reflecting the strain on diagnostic services highlighted by MOH (The Star, 2026; Bernama, 2026a).

The outbreaks also diverted resources within the health system. Staff and equipment were reallocated, slowing routine care and creating backlogs. Public health teams faced heavier workloads in contact tracing and community screening. For example, MOH deployed mobile screening units in Johor for migrant workers and expanded outreach in Sarawak’s rural longhouses, consistent with its emphasis on targeted screening (Ministry of Health Malaysia, 2026; The Straits Times, 2026; Bernama, 2026b). Preventive measures during festive gatherings and Ramadan were reinforced, with MOH stressing the risks of enclosed, poorly ventilated spaces (Bernama, 2026a).

For the population, the outbreaks increased morbidity among vulnerable groups and heightened anxiety in dense urban areas. Long treatment regimens (6–9 months) led to absenteeism and income loss, while stigma discouraged timely care. For example, TB patients in Kuala Lumpur reported difficulty keeping jobs due to frequent clinic visits, and indigenous communities in Sabah struggled with access to treatment centers (Ministry of Health Malaysia, 2026). Behavioral changes included greater mask use, avoidance of crowded spaces, and improved ventilation during gatherings. Overall, the 2026 TB outbreaks underscored persistent health equity challenges in Malaysia, particularly in Sabah and Selangor.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Pluvial/Flash Flood
name: ARG: Pluvial Flood / Flood - 01-2026 - Severe Storms in San Rafael Mendoza
summary:
During the evening of January 24, 2026, a severe storm with heavy rains, hail and gusts of wind was recorded in the department of San Rafael, province of Mendoza, causing significant impacts and complications in mobility and basic services.

As a result of the flooding of the Diamante River registered simultaneously with the storms, there was the evacuation of at least 63 people, mainly in the area of Los Coroneles, due to the entry of water into homes located on the south bank of the river, including people who had to take refuge in trees due to the rapid advance of the water. The emergency generated significant material losses, with homes severely affected and families who lost all their belongings. Likewise, people with health problems derived from the situation were reported, who required transfer and care in hospitals.

Weather forecasts indicate a medium probability of new storms over the next few days, increasing the risk of new floods of the Diamante River and worsening impacts

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Fire
name: ARG: Fire - 01-2026 - Luis Guillon Structural Fire Buenos Aires
summary:
During the night of January 24 and early morning of January 25, a structural fire broke out in the town of Luis Guillón, Esteban Echeverría district, corresponding to the facilities of the "Modular Home" factory, a company dedicated to the construction of prefabricated houses with an area of 7800 m². During the day on Sunday, cooling, structural dismantling and control of outbreaks were carried out. A house adjacent to the factory had minor damage from the fire and permanent heat.

Fire personnel and other first responders were affected by gas inhalation, lacerations and cuts. Neighbors, company workers and passers-by traveled the area throughout the time that the intervention lasted, some of them visibly affected by the outcome and their sources of work.

countries.name: Indonesia
dtype.name: Landslide
name: IDN: Landslide - 01-2026 - Devastating Landslide Hits West Bandung Regency
summary:
1. Incident Overview

Heavy rainfall on Saturday (24/01) triggered significant soil movement and landslides across the Cisarua and Lembang districts. The disaster resulted in a debris flow consisting of mud, sand, and large boulders that swept through river channels into residential areas.

2. Cause of Incident

The landslide was triggered by a natural blockage of soil and rock material in the river channels on the upper southern slopes of Mount Burangrang. This "natural dam" held back a massive volume of water until it suddenly breached, sending high-velocity debris (mud, sand, and boulders) downstream toward settlements.

3. Impact Assessment

Based on data from PMI West Java, BPBD West Java, and media reports:

  • Affected Population: 151 families (606 individuals).

  • Displaced Persons: 606 individuals currently in shelters.

  • Casualties: 34 confirmed dead; 38 individuals remain missing.

  • Property Damage: 30 houses heavily damaged or buried under debris.

4. Current Situation & Response

  • Evacuation: Displaced residents whose homes were destroyed are currently sheltered in Pasirlangu Village, Cisarua, while others are staying with relatives.

  • Victim Identification: The Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) team has identified several victims, and their remains have been handed over to their respective families.

  • Search and Rescue (SAR): Operations are ongoing using a combination of heavy machinery and manual efforts. Search efforts face challenges due to unstable soil conditions (risk of aftershocks) and extreme weather.

  • Mapping: SAR operations are being conducted systematically based on coordinate points mapped by field teams.

5. Government Action & Policy

  • Emergency Status: The West Bandung Regency Government has declared an Emergency Response Period from January 24 to February 6, 2026.

  • Weather Modification: As of Thursday (29/01), the government is conducting Weather Modification Operations (OMC). This involves cloud seeding around the Mount Burangrang area to reduce rainfall intensity and facilitate smoother disaster management operations.

countries.name: Afghanistan
dtype.name: Cold Wave
name: AFG: Cold Wave - 01-2026 - Afghanistan: Cold Wave and Heavy Snow Fall-2026
summary:
According to Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS) field reports, heavy snowfall and rainfall across multiple provinces have caused significant loss of life, injuries, and widespread damage. Over the past several days, at least 56 people have been killed and 40 injured as a result of snowfall, avalanches, snowstorms, flooding, roof collapses, and landslides.

Data received by the ARCS (DM-EOC) indicate that 59 houses have been fully destroyed and 225 houses partially damaged. In addition, 910 livestock deaths and damage to 1,087 agricultural lands have been reported across the provinces of Helmand, Uruzgan, Kandahar, Kabul, Daikundi, Parwan, Nangarhar, Nooristan, Maidan Wardak, Khost, Badghis, Ghor, Balkh, Jawzjan, and Faryab.

The impact of the severe winter conditions has significantly affected communities at the provincial and district levels. Prolonged snowfall, rainfall, and extreme cold have resulted in restricted access to food supplies, basic health services, winterization items, and essential household needs, alongside acute shortages of fodder for livestock. Access constraints are further compounded by blocked main roads and secondary routes, limiting mobility and humanitarian access. Migrants, returnees, and host communities are among those affected.

Households are facing increasing difficulties in heating shelters, safeguarding livelihoods, and meeting basic needs. The situation is particularly critical in high-altitude and hard-to-reach provinces, including Badakhshan, Bamyan, Nooristan, Ghor, Panjshir, and Laghman, as well as parts of Badghis, Sar-e-Pul, Faryab, Balkh, Jawzjan, and Nangarhar, where road closures, village isolation, and continued livestock losses persist.

Many districts are experiencing severely limited access to fuel, adequate shelter, food, and healthcare services during the winter season. Harsh weather conditions, poor infrastructure, and ongoing economic constraints continue to hamper relief efforts and transportation. Children, older persons, displaced populations, and communities in remote areas remain the most vulnerable and in need of humanitarian assistance.

countries.name: Greece
dtype.name: Flood
name: GRC: Flood - 01-2026 - Floods_21/01/2026
summary:
The severe flooding has affected several areas of Greece, triggered by intense rainfall. The event has resulted in significant disruptions to daily life, damage to infrastructure, and increased risks to public health and safety. Key impacts include inundation of residential areas, destruction of property, power and water supply outages, and blocked transport routes.

Two people lost their lives due to the extreme weather that hit Greece, mainly Attica. A 56‑year‑old woman died in Ano Glyfada when torrential floodwaters swept a car into her while she was trying to cross the street, and a 53‑year‑old coast guard officer died in Paralio Astros (Kynouria) after being swept into the sea by a powerful wave while trying to secure boats during the storm. 

The situation is evolving, with emergency response services actively engaged in rescue, evacuation, and relief operations. National and local authorities have implemented emergency measures, including activating civil protection mechanisms, issuing evacuation orders, and issuing safety advisories. Weather or environmental conditions remain unstable, which may further exacerbate existing risks. Access to affected areas is partially restored, and assessments are ongoing to determine the full extent of the damage.

The hazard has affected several people across the areas. Vulnerable groups—including older persons, children, and individuals with chronic health conditions—are disproportionately impacted. Many households have experienced displacement, loss of livelihoods, or damage to essential assets. Public services such as schools, healthcare facilities, and community infrastructure have been temporarily disrupted.

Affected communities are facing challenges related to shelter, access to clean water, sanitation, and psychosocial well-being. Immediate needs include emergency shelter, basic relief items, timely information, and continued support to restore critical services and enhance community resilience.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Pluvial/Flash Flood
name: ARG: Pluvial flood / flood - 01-2026 - Pilcomayo River Flood
summary:
Current situation and risk analysis

The hydrometeorological situation in the province of Salta has been becoming more complex in recent weeks due to the simultaneous flooding of the Bermejo and Pilcomayo rivers, due to the persistence of rains in Bolivian and Argentine territories. In the Pilcomayo River, the level is at 5.56 meters in Misión La Paz (5:15 p.m. on 1/21/2026), which generates a medium risk scenario due to overflows that implies the possibility of overcoming the defense rings of Santa Victoria Este and nearby communities.

The hydrological situation is relevant. The water has entered Provincial Route 54 at the height of Misión La Paz; taking into account this scenario, if the force of the water breaks this sector, the flood would advance directly towards the community of KM II and 1000 meters further on KM I. 

Today, the level in Misión La Paz is at 5.2 meters (4:15 p.m.), registering a downward trend compared to the 5.56 meters of the previous day. In the upper basin (Bolivia), stations such as Villa Montes (3.25m 16:20hs) and Aruma (6.07m 15:15hs) also report low levels, indicating a temporary gradual relief. But the possibility of rains arriving on Tuesday 27 is not ruled out, according to the extended forecast of the National Meteorological Service to date.

So far, throughout the province the rains have impacted more than 300 families in at least 15 municipalities, which positions the provincial system in a state of high activity led by the Ministry of Social Development of the Province. 

The team of the Argentine Red Cross Humanitarian Camp is on the ground carrying out activities normally, preparing equipment and supplies in case it is necessary to activate emergency interventions and monitoring critical points.

countries.name: Suriname
dtype.name: Other
name: SUR: Other - 01-2026 - confirmed outbreak of the mosquito-borne disease, chikungunya
summary: In January 2026, Suriname reported a confirmed outbreak of Chikungunya. The chikungunya virus, which is transmitted through mosquito bites, has re-emerge in the country after serveral years of relative absence. The Ministry of Health officially announced the outbreak following confirmation of eight (8) positive cases. None of the infected individuals had recently traveled abroad, indicating that the virus is spreading locally. The confirmed cases were identified by both the Central Laboratory of the Bureau for Public Health (BOG) and  the Laboratory of the Academic Hospital Paramaribo (AZP). Based on reported cases and observed patterns of spread, six (6) neighborhoods have been classified as High-Risk areas. These are Marowijne Project, Blauwgrond, Geyersvlijt, Clevia, Tamansari and Richelieu.  The small rainy season is still ongoing and a large number of mosquitoes have been observed in various parts of Suriname. The areas as mmentioned are closely being monitored due to increased reports of infections and environmental factors that may support mosquito breeding and transmission.

countries.name: Algeria
dtype.name: Flood
name: DZA: Flood - 01-2026 - Algeria: Floods and Heavy Rains
summary:
On Tuesday, 20 January 2026, a severe weather system brought widespread unsettled conditions across Algeria, with heavy rainfall, strong winds, and snowfall at higher elevations. The National Meteorological Office issued Level 2 weather alerts for multiple wilayas in the western and central regions.

The heavy rains triggered flash floods in several provinces, including Relizane, Chlef, Tiaret, Tissemsilt, Médéa, and Aïn Defla. Civil Defense authorities confirmed at least one fatality—a 60-year-old man whose body was recovered near Oued Al-Safa in Relizane province. Several injuries and temporary evacuations have been reported, though exact numbers are still being consolidated.

The floods caused significant disruption to daily life, including:
• Inundation of homes, particularly in low-lying and informal settlements
• Road closures and traffic disruption due to flooded routes and debris
• Partial collapses of residential walls (no injuries reported)
• Damage to agricultural land and livestock losses in rural areas
• Temporary disruption of electricity and water supply in some localities

The National Meteorological Office warned of continued severe weather, forecasting rainfall exceeding 120 mm in some areas, strong winds reaching 80–90 km/h, and heavy snowfall in mountainous areas above 1,100 meters. Snow and ice alerts (Level 2) were issued for Tlemcen, Naama, Tiaret, Tissemsilt, Sidi Belabbès, Saida, northern El Bayadh, Laghouat, and ;lDjelfa, with snow thickness estimated between 5 and 15 cm.

An estimated 4.6 to 4.9 million people reside in the affected wilayas, which include both urban centers and rural communities in flood-prone catchment areas. The situation remains fluid, with authorities continuing response operations and damage assessments.

countries.name: Pakistan
dtype.name: Complex Emergency
name: PAK: Complex Emergency - 01-2026 - Displacement from Tirah & Kurram, KP, Pakistan
summary:
In January 2026, authorities and residents initiated the displacement and relocation of families from Tirah Valley in Khyber District, amid concerns over a potential security operation. According to the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), the evacuation process continued through late January, with over 11,400 families registered and more than 10,000 relocated to safer areas such as Bara and Peshawar by late January.

Heavy snowfall in the last weeks of January exacerbated displacement hardships. The cold conditions, combined with slow registration procedures and snow-blocked roads along the 110-km Tirah-Bara route, forced many displaced families to spend nights outdoors in freezing conditions.

Across northern and north-western Pakistan, including Tirah Valley and Kurram District, heavy snowfall and severe winter conditions have been reported since mid-January. Rescue 1122 teams conducted ongoing operations following intense snow, rescuing individuals stranded by snow in Tirah Valley and surrounding districts.

The presence of snow and cold weather has disrupted evacuation movements, and increased protection and humanitarian needs among displaced families, particularly women, children, older persons, and those with limited resources

countries.name: Israel
dtype.name: Other
name: ISR: Other - 01-2026 - Infant Daycare Health Emergency
summary: A unregistered daycare facility in Jerusalem noticed an infant unconscious and not breathing and summoned Magen David Adom ALS team.  Upon arrival, the team began CPR on the infant and transported to the nearest trauma facility.   However the facility then noticed a second infant unresponsive and summoned Magen David a second time.  The ambulance crew began CPR on the second infant and trnasported as well while calling for all the infants at the facility to be evaluated medically.  55 infants in total were transported to nearby hospitals.  the first 2 infants were subsequently declared dead at the hospitals.  The remaining 53 infants were cleared medically and released from the hospitals.  The situation is under investigation and review.

countries.name: Tunisia
dtype.name: Flood
name: TUN: Flood - 01-2026 - Tunisia
summary:
Since 18 January 2026, eastern and northern Tunisia have been hit by exceptionally heavy rainfall, resulting in widespread flooding across 15 regions and affecting an estimated 25,000 people, including isolated rural and mountainous communities that remain difficult to access. The situation has led to five confirmed fatalities, with several individuals still unaccounted for, and continues to evolve as hydrological risks persist, particularly from rivers originating in Algeria following the cyclone’s movement in that direction. The emergency remains dynamic, with the potential for further impacts in the coming days.

Approximately 400 people have been relocated to temporary shelters, with the Tunisian Red Crescent Society (TRCS) actively supporting evacuation and relief efforts at the request of national authorities. Key priorities identified through initial assessments include health services (with continuity of care for people with chronic conditions), mental health and psychosocial support, WASH interventions, shelter and clothing, and food assistance, particularly ready-to-eat meals and milk for children. Operational needs such as vehicles, fuel, PPE for volunteers, and replenishment of relief stocks remain critical to sustain access to hard-to-reach areas and ensure continuity of the response.

countries.name: Guatemala
dtype.name: Civil Unrest
name: GTM: Civil Unrest - 01-2026 - Situación Social en Guatemala
summary:
Las autoridades del Ministerio de Gobernación de Guatemala informaron en conferencia de prensa que el sábado 17 de enero se registraron alteraciones del orden en los centros penitenciarios de Fraijanes II, Renovación I y el sector 11 del Centro Preventivo de la zona 18, en el departamento de Guatemala. Esta situación, indicaron, es reacción al retiro de privilegios a los líderes de las estructuras criminales que se encuentran en estos centros de privación de libertad[1]. Se registraron destrozos y toma de guardias penitenciarios como rehenes.

 

A consecuencia de ello, las fuerzas de seguridad civil, con el apoyo del Ejército de Guatemala, mantienen control perimetral total de esas instalaciones. Se ejecutan de manera coordinada y contundente, los protocolos operativos que tienen como propósito restaurar plenamente el control, orden y la protección de personal, así como de las áreas geográficas circundantes. El Ministro de Gobernación indicó que el Gobierno de Guatemala no pactará con ningún grupo armado y que se continúa trabajando en el control de los centros preventivos y de cumplimiento de condena.

 

En la mañana del domingo 18 de enero, con el apoyo de las fuerzas armadas, tanto civiles como militares, se retomó el control en el centro Renovación 1, así como la liberación de rehenes. Derivado de esta acción, desde las primeras horas del día se registraron 12 ataques a la Policía Nacional Civil (PNC), los cuales, en conferencia de prensa del Ministro de Gobernación, indicó que han dejado como resultado 7 agentes de la PNC fallecidos, 10 agentes heridos, 7 pandilleros capturados y 1 pandillero fallecido.


[1] Ministerio de Gobernación de Guatemala. https://guatemala.gob.gt/ministerio-de-gobernacion/

countries.name: Spain
dtype.name: Transport Accident
name: ESP: Transport Accident - 01-2026 - Train Accident
summary: On January 18, 2026, two high‑speed trains derailed in Adamuz (Córdoba) when an Iryo train traveling from Málaga to Madrid left the track and entered an adjacent line, where a Renfe Alvia train was passing, causing a lateral collision that resulted in at least 21 deaths and 25 serious injuries, along with dozens of other affected passengers. The severity of the incident led Renfe and Adif to suspend all high‑speed rail service between Madrid and Andalusia, disrupting connections with Seville, Córdoba, Málaga, and Huelva, while emergency teams worked to rescue trapped passengers and assist the injured.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Landslide
name: ARG: Landslide - 01-2026 - Cerro Hermitte Landslide
summary:
Between the early hours of January 17 and 18, 2026, a landslide of magnitude was recorded on Mount Hermitte, in the city of Comodoro Rivadavia, province of Chubut. The event generated a mass removal that caused serious structural damage and partial collapses in homes located mainly in the Sismográfica, El Marquesado and Los Tilos neighborhoods, in addition to affecting some homes on Mazaredo Street.

As a result of the movement of soil, there were deep cracks in the ground, walls, floors, roofs and streets, as well as damage to basic infrastructures such as gas and water networks, increasing the level of risk for the resident population. Faced with this situation, local authorities ordered preventive and restrictive evacuations in the affected areas.

At the time of this report, more than 90 families (approximately 450 people) are displaced from their homes and housed in evacuation centers and temporary accommodations set up by the municipality. No deaths, injuries or missing people are registered. The evacuation is maintained as a preventive measure due to the persistent instability of the terrain and the risk of further displacement.

Local emergency teams continue to work in the area to secure the area, assist the evacuated population and monitor the evolution of the phenomenon. The situation remains under constant evaluation by the competent authorities.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.society_name: The South African Red Cross Society
dtype.name: Flood
name: ZAF: Flood - 01-2026 - Limpopo and Mpumalanga Floods
summary:
In Limpopo, it is estimated that over 980 households (4900 people) have been affected by heavy rains, with 17 mortalities and numbers continuing to rise as assessments are ongoing. On the 12th January 2026, the South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Red Level 10 weather warning for Limpopo. Prior to the Red Level 10 alert, SAWS had already issued Orange Level 9 and Orange Level 6 warnings for disruptive rainfall across parts of eastern and central Limpopo, signifying high risk of flooding of roads, settlements, mudslides, soil erosion and danger from fast-flowing watercourses.

The inclement weather has materialised in the form of persistent heavy rainfall, affecting several areas within Vhembe and Mopani District, resulting in significant damage to homes, roads, livelihoods and other critical infrastructure. Due to the ongoing rain challenges, SARCS provincial and branch disaster teams were activated on the 16th of January 2025. SARCS LP disaster team has reported that the infrastructure damage includes the road between Hlengani and Lombard Matiyane, as well as the Makuleke Bridge, which has sustained notable damages. SARCS disaster teams have also confirmed that the road between Maphophe and Botsoleni was flooded, leading to one reported injury. In Makhado, strong winds and heavy rainfall resulted in roofs being blown off and at least 60 houses completely collapsing. Damage to road infrastructure in this area has been reported to the relevant government departments.

In Musina, damage to road infrastructure has been reported, with immediate reconstruction initiated at the cut-off bridge over the Mutale River in Mutale B village. The Nkotswi Bridge has overflowed, rendering it impassable and preventing residents from crossing to the other side to access essential services. Additionally, three people were trapped in Gwakani on Sunday, 11 January 2026, due to rising water levels (Three people stranded in the Mutale River outside Thohoyandou - SABC News - Breaking news, special reports, world, business, sport coverage of all South African current events. Africa's news leader.)

At the same time, Thulamela Municipality has recorded a high number of affected households. Immense damage has been reported at the Tshidumbi Bridge, which connects Shayandima to Itsani, as well as in Tshipako, Thenzhani, Muraga, and Gondeni Sekstroom. Further assessments are ongoing, although access challenges continue to limit assessment coverage in some areas andSARCS has confirmed the following

    • Musina: 103 damaged households
    • Collins Chabane Municipality: 100 damaged households
    • Makhado: 25 damaged households
    • Giyani: 122 damaged households
    • Thulamela Municipality: 300 damaged households

An evacuation centre with 86 residents who have lost their homes and possessions was established in Giyani, Mbalula village due to devastating floods andone child remains missing.. Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with local authorities and emergency services actively engaged.

Officials warned residents to avoid crossing flooded rivers and to follow SAWS and disaster management guidance Limpopo Provincial Government on challenges posed by the recent heavy rainfall and flooding | South African Government. Furthermore, South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa has visited flood-hit areas in Limpopo to assess the situation and support relief efforts as the province continues to deal with ongoing destructive rain and flooding  (President Ramaphosa's response to Limpopo flooding: A visit to affected areas)

In Mpumalanga, it is estimated that over 1000 households (5000 people) have been affected by heavy rains, with 20 mortalities and numbers continuing to rise as assessments are ongoing. Most fatalities were linked to drownings from overflowing rivers and damaged bridges (19 dead in Mpumalanga since November as inclement weather persists). SAWS forecasters noted that rainfall totals in parts of Mpumalanga and Limpopo over recent weeks have approached what is usually recorded over a six-month period (Weather service warns of continued heavy rain across Mpumalanga and Limpopo)

SARCS MP has confirmed households have been damaged across Nkomazi Local Municipality, City of Mbombela, Thaba Chweu, and Bushbuckridge. Floodwaters have washed away bridges and made roads inaccessible, severely hampering emergency response capacity and isolating communities (Weather service warns of continued heavy rain across Mpumalanga and Limpopo). Through the activation of local volunteers, the following impacts across affected communities:

    • Southern Region (Wards 41, 43, 45): 150 families affected
    • Eastern Region (Wards 11, 30, 33, 36): 30 families affected
    • Central Region (Wards 12, 14, 18, 22, 23, 29): 170 families affected
  • Municipal infrastructure damage has been reported, including:
    • Schools: Thekwane Primary School, Shishila Primary School, Somcuba Primary School, and Gedlembane High School
    • Roads and bridges: Damage reported to the D2296 Provincial Road (culvert), Ema19 Bridge 

SARCS and municipal teams are still jointly conducting assessments to determine the full scale of damage and priority needs. Besides assessments and distribution of relief, SARCS is also doing early warning disseminations to those in high-risk areas where impacts have been forecasted to continue.

Bushbuckridge municipality temporarily suspended classes for two days because flooding and heavy rain impaired access to schools. Severe weather and flood risk led to closures and evacuations at Kruger National Park (a major tourism site that extends into Mpumalanga) to protect visitors and staff (Floods force evacuations from South Africa's Kruger National Park; 19 dead in other regions | AP News). Flooding and storm impacts have damaged infrastructure, with reports of power outages and inaccessible areas, complicating rescue and relief efforts.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Fire
name: ARG: Fire - 01-2026 - Patagonia Forest Fires
summary:
During the first days of January 2026, large-scale forest fires were recorded in Patagonia, with active outbreaks in the provinces of Chubut, Río Negro and Neuquén, which maintained a dynamic and highly complex behavior throughout the period analyzed, strongly conditioned by environmental and territorial factors. In the Epuyén area, the advance of the fire towards the south face of Mount Pirque configured a scenario of special complexity, due to the fact that it is a sector with very limited land accessibility, where entry is only possible by air or lake boats. In this sector, scattered houses are located on the coastline, which increases the exposure of the population and hinders protection tasks and eventual evacuation.
Within the framework of the emergency due to the forest fires in the region, the preventive evacuation of approximately 3,520 people was recorded, including both local residents and a relevant proportion of tourists and temporary visitors, in a context of high seasonal influx typical of the summer period.
As for material damage, preliminary surveys on the ground reported the total loss of 24 homes, mainly located in urban-forest interface sectors. Likewise, the area affected by the fire reached an estimated 30,000 hectares, covering areas of native forest, natural vegetation and peri-urban areas in the affected provinces.

According to the National Meteorological Service, the towns of Epuyén and El Bolsón show an unfavorable scenario, with weather conditions that sustain and enhance the danger of forest fires.
The combination of strong wind, moderate-high temperatures and little rainfall keeps both locations at high risk.

dtype.name: Epidemic
name: GTM: Epidemic - 01-2026 - ALERTA ROJA INSTITUCIONAL POR CONFIRMACIÓN DE CASOS DE SARAMPIÓN EN GUATEMALA
summary:
El Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social de Guatemala, por medio de la Dirección de Epidemiología y Gestión de Riesgo, durante el año 2025 giró 3 alertas epidemiológicas y activó el sistema de alerta institucional y el abordaje de posibles casos o brotes de Sarampión, siendo esto, a través de la coordinadora interinstitucional, complementados con los niveles establecidos por el Sistema Nacional CONRED, en el Plan Nacional de Respuesta -PNR- y Plan Institucional de Respuesta Multiamenaza -PIRM-. 
El 02 de enero de 2026, se notifica al país un caso de paciente masculino de 24 años de edad, originario y con residencia en El Salvador, confirmado con fecha de inicio de exantema 24 de diciembre 2022, e informe de resultados positivos para Sarampión al 30 de diciembre. Como antecedente importante del posible contagio, fue por la participación en una actividad religiosa masiva, la cual conglomeró aproximadamente 2 mil personas, provenientes de varios países de la región, incluyendo México, EE. UU. y Centroamérica, incluyendo la participación de connacionales de los 22 departamentos de Guatemala. 
Siendo las regiones con mayor cantidad de participantes: 
	Metropolitana 791
	Petén 103
	Chimaltenango 102
	San Juan Sacatepéquez 85
	Salamá, Baja Verapaz 86
A raíz de esta información compartida por el mecanismo del Reglamento Sanitario Internacional y Centro Nacional de Enlace, se realizan las gestiones correspondientes para la activación de los equipos de respuesta inmediata del MSPAS.
Dentro de los factores de riesgo que incrementan la probabilidad de contagión de Sarampión, son:
	Coberturas heterogéneas.
	Una población susceptible no vacunada (por 10 años las coberturas están por debajo del nivel óptimo<95%).

countries.name: Malaysia
dtype.name: Flood
name: MYS: Flood - 01-2026 - East Malysia Monsoon Flood
summary:
Since 6 January 2026, Sarawak has been affected by monsoon floods, with several districts experiencing significant impact. As of 11 January 2026, a total of 2,640 evacuees from 913 families are currently housed in active temporary evacuation centres (PPS) across the state. Serian remains the most affected with 1,413 evacuees from 492 families, followed by Bintulu with 406 evacuees from 143 families, while Samarahan shows a decrease to 371 evacuees from 118 families. Sibu, Mukah, and Miri remain relatively stable. The widespread flooding has also disrupted education, with 42 schools expected to be unable to operate due to cut-off access, inundation, or use as PPS, while 24 District Education Offices continue operations and some schools implement alternative teaching methods.

Meanwhile in Sabah, the flood situation that began in early January continues to improve in some areas. As of 2:00 PM today, 367 residents from 138 households remain at two PPS — Pusat Pemindahan Kekal Selagon and Dewan Sri Dayang in Beaufort District — while conditions in other affected districts show a gradual decline in evacuee numbers. The downward trend is attributed to receding river levels and improving weather conditions, although some areas continue to face persistent floodwaters.

Relief operations in both Sarawak and Sabah remain ongoing, with authorities monitoring the evolving situation, maintaining PPS operations, and ensuring the safety and welfare of affected residents while coordinating with education and disaster management agencies to manage impacts on schools and communities.

countries.name: Australia
dtype.name: Fire
name: AUS: Fire - 01-2026 - Victorian January Bushfires
summary:
On 9 January 2026, extreme heat and heightened fire danger across western and central Victoria led to the rapid escalation of multiple grass and scrub fires. These fast‑moving bushfires posed significant risks to communities, triggering Advice, Watch and Act, and Emergency Warning messages from VicEmergency as conditions deteriorated. 

Later that day, the Victorian Premier declared a State of Disaster for 18 affected Local Government Areas and one Alpine Resort. Widespread evacuations occurred across rural areas, with Emergency Relief Centres activated and stood down as required. Sadly, one fatality has been confirmed. The fires have resulted in substantial damage to the built environment, community assets and natural landscapes. Current reports indicate the loss of more than 500 structures, including an estimated 180 homes, and over 400,000 hectares of land burnt.

More than 1,000 farms have been impacted, with approximately 15,000 livestock deaths reported to date, a figure expected to increase. There have also been extensive impacts to native flora and fauna. Numerous road closures were put in place, and damage to poles, lines and associated assets caused telecommunications and power outages. Some drinking water supplies were contaminated and subsequently declared unsafe for consumption.

On 13 January 2026, the 2026 Victorian Bushfire Appeal was launched to support fire‑affected communities: www.vic.gov.au/2026-Victorian-Bushfire-Appeal

countries.name: Indonesia
dtype.name: Flood
name: IDN: Flood - 01-2026 - Widespread flooding affecting multiple regencies in Central Java
summary:
1. Situation Overview

Following high-intensity rainfall since January 16, 2026, widespread flooding has affected 10 administrative areas in Central Java. The floods were triggered by the overflowing of several major rivers (Gelis, Piji, Dawe, Dombo, Silugonggo, Widodaren, Godo, Penut, Waridin, and Aji) as well as tidal flooding (ROB) in coastal areas.

2. Regional Impact Highlights

  • Kudus Regency: The most severely impacted with inundation levels of 20–70 cm across 9 districts. This resulted in 48,359 affected individuals and 2,127 displaced. Infrastructure damage includes 5,890 houses, 45 schools, and 11 places of worship. Additionally, 24 landslide points were recorded, causing 3 fatalities.

  • Pati Regency: Flood depths reached 30–100 cm across 19 districts. Significant impact on public facilities: 452 places of worship, 65 schools, and 12 markets were inundated.

  • Pekalongan (City & Regency): Extreme water levels reaching up to 130 cm, forcing over 2,800 people to flee to evacuation centers.

  • Demak & Kendal: Significant flooding affecting over 48,000 residents combined, with primary causes being river overflow and high sedimentation.

3. Cumulative Impact Data

  • Total Affected: 41,418 Households / 143,367 Individuals.

  • Displaced Persons: 5,285 Individuals.

  • Casualties: 3 Deaths (due to landslides).

  • Infrastructure Damage: 11,175 submerged houses, 572 places of worship, 110 schools, 26 health facilities, and 12 markets.

4. Current Status & Weather Forecast

While floodwaters are gradually receding in most areas and residents have begun post-flood cleanup, Kudus and Demak remain partially inundated, particularly on village roads and the Kudus–Pati alternative route. The Pantura Highway (Main Northern Arterial Road) is accessible but has sustained severe damage (potholes).

  • Weather Outlook: BMKG forecasts light to moderate rain across Central Java for the afternoon of Jan 19. Residents are urged to remain vigilant for potential secondary flooding.

5. Emergency Response & Legal Status

  • State of Emergency:

    • Kudus Regency: 7-day emergency period (Jan 12 – 19, 2026).

    • Pekalongan City: 14-day emergency period (Jan 17 – 31, 2026).

  • PMI (Indonesian Red Cross) Actions:

    • Mobilization of 105 personnel for rapid assessment and evacuation.

    • Establishment of Field Kitchens (Dapur Umum) in Pati and other regions.

    • Distribution of 6,460 ready-to-eat meals, 6,000 packs of instant noodles, and 630 kg of rice.

The Ministry of Public Health and Social Assistance of Guatemala, through the Directorate of Epidemiology and Risk Management, during the year 2025 issued 3 epidemiological alerts and activated the institutional alert system to address possible cases or outbreaks of Measles. Activation through the inter-institutional coordinator, complemented by the levels established by the National CONRED System, in the National Response Plan (PNR) and the Institutional Multi-Hazard Response Plan (PIRM). As an important antecedent of the possible contagion, was the participation in a massive religious activity, which brought together approximately 2 thousand people, from several countries in the region, including Mexico, the United States and Central America, including the participation of nationals from the 22 departments of Guatemala.

countries.name: Mozambique
dtype.name: Flood
name: Mozambique : Floods - 01-2026
summary:
Mozambique is experiencing a large-scale flood emergency triggered by persistent and intense rainfall since late December 2025. The Mozambique Red Cross (CVM) has been supporting the Government activation of anticipatory actions with evacuations, distribution of relief items, and dissemination of early warning messages. This was done through the activation of the Floods Early Action Protocol (EAP) and other mechanisms. Despite these efforts, the scope and scale of the emergency has exceeded local capacities and on 16 January 2026, the Government of Mozambique activated a nationwide Red Alert, in response to the deterioration of weather conditions and the heightened risk of severe flooding and related hazards across the country.

As of 27 January 2026, official data from INGD indicate that over 690'000 people (150'000 households) have been affected nationwide by the floods. More than 100,000 people are living in over temporary accommodation centres. The provinces most severely affected are Gaza, Sofala and Zambézia, with significant impacts also reported in Maputo, Inhambane, Manica and Tete.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.society_name: Red Cross Society of Bosnia and Herzegovina
dtype.name: Flood
name: BIH: Flood - 01-2026 - Floods and snowfall
summary:
Bosnia and Herzegovina is currently experiencing a combination of heavy rainfall and snowfall, causing rapid rises in river levels, particularly the Neretva, Trebižat, Drina, and Bosna. Saturated soils and these conditions increase the risk of flash floods, localized flooding, landslides, and road disruptions, as well as temporary interruptions to water and electricity supply.

High-risk cities and municipalities include Mostar, Goražde, Konjic, Olovo, Bihać, Zvornik, Bratunac, Bijeljina, and Foča.

Several communities already face flooding of homes, yards, and farmland.

Households in Zvornik, Bijeljina, Foča, and Bratunac are particularly at risk due to rising Drina River levels.

Civil protection measures are active, including sandbagging, mobilization of emergency services, and river monitoring.

Landslides, rockfalls, and river overflows are affecting regional and local roads; some roads in Herzegovina-Neretva Canton, Zenica-Doboj Canton, and eastern Bosnia are temporarily impassable.

Disruptions to water supply (e.g., Goražde) and electricity (Tuzla Canton, Olovo) impact access to essential services.

Civile protection of Republik of Srpske has requested from colleges from Montenegro to reduce the release of water from the Piva River to limit the rise of the Drina.

Continued precipitation and snowmelt may further increase river levels and trigger new localized floods.

Transport disruptions may impede emergency logistics and access to critical areas.

Without timely intervention, households and infrastructure in the most affected zones could experience significant damage.
Conclusion 
The situation represents a high risk of floods and landslides in priority municipalities and cities, with potential impacts on population, households, infrastructure, and mobility. Civil protection measures are ongoing, and further developments will depend on weather conditions and the effectiveness of emergency responses.

countries.name: Serbia
dtype.name: Other
name: SRB: Other - 01-2026 - Extreme winter condition and floods
summary:
Since 4 January, severe winter weather conditions including heavy snowfall, strong winds, and low temperatures have affected several areas of Serbia, resulting in significant humanitarian impact and disruptions to essential services.

The municipalities of Loznica, Valjevo, Osečina, Ivanjica, Vladimirci, Krupanj, Mali Zvornik, and Majdanpek have been among the most affected. Heavy snow accumulation caused restricted access to communities, disrupted transportation, and led to widespread power outages due to damage to electricity distribution networks. Prolonged electricity cuts particularly affected urban, rural and hard-to-reach areas, negatively impacting heating, water supply, and access to basic services.

In response to identified immediate needs, the Red Cross of Serbia provided emergency assistance to over 300 households, including food and hygiene parcels, blankets, sleeping bags, drinking water, and candles, prioritizing households affected by power outages and limited access to essential services.

Concurrently, flooding occurred in Kosovo and Metohija following the overflow of the Ibar and Sitnica rivers. The municipalities of Kosovska Mitrovica, Zvečan, Kosovo Polje, and Gračanica were affected by localized flooding of residential areas, agricultural land, and critical infrastructure, posing risks to the livelihoods, health, and safety of the population. The Red Cross of Kosovo and Metohija has been engaged in monitoring, coordination, and response activities prioritising community support services for over 100 households, including water pumping, household disinfections, and setting up dehumidifiers.  

The evolving situation continues to require close monitoring, coordination, and readiness for potential scale-up of humanitarian assistance, should conditions deteriorate.

countries.name: Venezuela
dtype.name: Other
name: TTO: Other - 01-2026 - Political Situation in Venezuela
summary: In the early morning of Saturday 3rd January 2026, news sources from local and international stations indicated that the United States conducted a military operation in Venezuela which led in the capture of its President. This was later confirmed by a Press Conference held by the United States government. Venezuela is geographically very close to Trinidad and Tobago and in the past, Trinidad and Tobago has experienced knock-on effects of the political and economic challenges that occur in Venezuela including population movement. At this time there is no immediate or visible crisis, so the Trinidad and Tobago Red Cross Society continues to monitor the situation.

countries.name: Afghanistan
dtype.name: Flood
name: AFG: Flood - 01-2026 - AFghanistan: Flash Floods 2026
summary:
Following heavy and sustained rainfall, flash floods occurred in January 2026 across parts of western and south-western Afghanistan, affecting communities in Farah, Herat and Uruzgan provinces. Low-lying areas and settlements located along riverbeds were particularly impacted. The floods resulted in loss of life, injuries, and widespread damage to shelters, livelihoods and agricultural land, reflecting the broader pattern of seasonal flooding currently affecting several parts of the country.

According to preliminary information compiled by the Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS), a total of 2,100 families were affected. The floods caused 17 deaths and 11 injuries, with no cases of missing persons reported. Shelter damage was significant, with 256 houses completely destroyed and 385 houses partially damaged, particularly in several districts of Farah province. In addition, the floods had a severe impact on livelihoods, resulting in the loss of 494 livestock and damage to approximately 8,400 jeribs of agricultural land, further increasing vulnerabilities among farming and pastoral households.

ARCS, through its provincial branches and volunteers, is monitoring the evolving situation and conducting initial assessments in coordination with local authorities and Movement partners. Priority humanitarian needs identified include emergency shelter and essential household items for families whose homes were destroyed or damaged, food assistance and multipurpose cash support, as well as livelihood and agricultural recovery assistance, including livestock support. With continued winter conditions and the possibility of further rainfall, affected communities remain at risk of additional flooding, underscoring the need for timely humanitarian support.

countries.name: Gambia, Republic of The
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: GMB: Population Movement - 01-2026 - Boat Accident (capsized migrant boat off the Gambian coast- Jinack)
summary:
On Wednesday, the 31st of December 2025, another boat that was said to have departed from the same Jinack village in The Gambia, carrying between 235 to 250 people intended for the Canary Islands, was reported to be in distress since after midnight and eventually capsized along the coastline between Gambia and Senegal on 1st of January 2026. About 235 were reported as onboard the boat, 114 were rescued and out of which 39 were hospitalized at the country’s main referral hospital in Banjul. It has been confirmed that the Senegalese authorities have rescued 14 people along its waters, including 10 dead bodies. So far, 7 other dead bodies have been recovered including a 2 year-old child by Gambian authorities. More than 100 people are still missing while search and rescue efforts by both The Gambia and Senegal remains on course.

 Another press release was shared on Thursday, 1st of January 2026 by the Ministry of Defense, confirming the maritime incident and the joint efforts by the Navy and local fishermen leading to the rescuing of many people onboard the boat.

 The Gambia Red Cross has since been working with relevant authorities to respond to the situation, providing humanitarian assistance to the affected persons.

 The Gambia Red Cross teams at HQ have deployed personnel to support in coordination and response, whilst the team in the region of North Bank have reported that, Jinack including other communities are all affected and have lost their loved ones in this tragic incident.

There is a high risk of trauma on the survivors and that of the families of those who are dead and missing. This poses significant exposure to health-related stress affecting their mental health and wellbeing. 

Additionally, there has been series of reports of boat departures from Jinack area and interceptions by authorities from coastal communities, all intended for the Canary Islands. These activities highlight the dire situation and the need to be on high alert for potential humanitarian response operations. There is a report of 2 potential departures this very night and the authorities are on high alert. These numbers will continue to increase in the coming days as there are different points of departures of potential migrants. There will be need to support both the affected migrants, their immediate families and host communities.

 The Regional Teams(North Bank Region, Banjul, Kanifing Municipality, West Coast Region of The Gambia) will continue to monitor the situation and as more information becomes available, updates will be shared.

countries.name: Ecuador
dtype.name: Pluvial/Flash Flood
name: ECU: Pluvial flood / flood - 01-2026 - Flooding due to river overflows
summary:
Since January 1, 2026, Ecuador has experienced a significant increase in rainfall, which has caused 1,486 adverse events to date, including floods, landslides and subsidence. These events have affected the country's 24 provinces, generating impacts in 189 cantons and 562 parishes. In view of this situation, the National Secretariat for Risk Management has declared Affectation Level 4, reflecting the magnitude of the damage and the territorial extension of the emergency.

By means of Resolution No. SNGR-036-2026, issued on February 20, 2026, the National Secretariat of Risk Management declared a Red Alert for the rainy season 2026 in the provinces of Carchi, Esmeraldas, Guayas, Loja, Los Ríos and Pichincha. Likewise, an Orange Alert was established in Azuay, Bolívar, Cañar, Chimborazo, Cotopaxi, El Oro, Imbabura, Manabí, Morona Santiago, Napo, Orellana, Santa Elena, Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, Sucumbíos and Zamora Chinchipe, and a Yellow Alert in Pastaza and Tungurahua.

Limitations are currently identified in the initial collection of information on humanitarian needs, owing to the limited availability of staff in some decentralized self-governments. 

In this context, the Ecuadorian Red Cross, in coordination with national and local authorities, is keeping its humanitarian response mechanisms active. The branches prioritize actions aimed at gathering information on humanitarian needs through EVIN assessments, the provision of psychosocial support to affected people, pre-hospital care, and support in the distribution of humanitarian assistance, including food kits, hygiene and tools. These interventions are developed with a people-centred approach, prioritising the protection, dignity and safety of the most vulnerable communities.

countries.name: Uruguay
dtype.name: Drought
name: URY: Drought - 12-2025 - Sequías e incendios forestales
summary:
Uruguay atraviesa un escenario climático complejo caracterizado por un déficit hídrico persistente en varias cuencas del país, especialmente en la región al sur del río Negro, donde se han acumulado precipitaciones por debajo de los valores normales durante todo el año 2025. Esta situación ha generado afectaciones múltiples tanto en el acceso al agua potable como en la producción agropecuaria y ganadera. El contenido de agua en el suelo es inferior al promedio, lo que compromete la germinación de cultivos de verano y reduce la disponibilidad de pasturas. Al mismo tiempo, el abastecimiento de agua potable enfrenta presión operativa, principalmente en zonas rurales o periurbanas, donde el uso de pozos y tajamares está comprometido.

En paralelo, el riesgo de incendios forestales y agropecuarios es extremadamente alto, especialmente en el sur del país. El Instituto Uruguayo de Meteorología (INUMET) ha emitido alertas continuas en base al Índice de Peligro de Incendios Forestales (FWI), destacando condiciones propicias para la ignición y propagación de fuego, como temperaturas altas, baja humedad relativa y vegetación seca. Ya se han registrado incendios con consecuencias materiales y humanas en departamentos como Montevideo y Canelones, lo que refleja un escenario de riesgo combinado: déficit hídrico + calor extremo + alta inflamabilidad de la vegetación.

Las afectaciones humanitarias incluyen restricciones en el acceso al agua en zonas rurales, necesidad de distribución alternativa de agua para consumo humano y animal, y posibles impactos en la seguridad alimentaria por la afectación a la producción agropecuaria. La situación podría agravarse durante los meses de verano si no se revierte la tendencia de precipitaciones por debajo de lo normal.

name: WRC: Other - 12-2025 - MPOX
summary: The epidemiological situation of Mpox in Cameroon highlights a confirmed circulation of the virus in four regions, namely the Centre, the Littoral, the South and the South-West. According to information shared by the Ministry of Public Health (MINSANTE) through its situation reports (SitRep), a total of 86 suspected cases have been reported nationwide, including 72 samples analyzed, confirming 10 cases of Mpox. The geographical distribution of cases shows the presence of the disease in both urban and peri-urban areas, with particular attention paid to the Littoral region, in particular the city of Douala, where a recent concentration of cases has been observed. The Mpox outbreak in Douala poses a high level of risk, due to confirmed human-to-human transmission in dense urban settings, high population mobility and concentration of cases in several health districts. Occasional shortages of laboratory reagents, logistical constraints in the delivery of samples, insufficient disinfection equipment and the limited capacity of some health facilities increase the risk of underdetection, delay in care and sustained community transmission. In addition to these factors, there are socio-behavioural challenges, including potential stigma and a still insufficient awareness, which can hinder the use of care and adherence to prevention measures. This situation underscores the need to maintain enhanced surveillance, continue epidemiological investigations and consolidate response actions, in order to prevent the geographical spread of the epidemic to other areas of the country and limit the pressure on the health system.

name: TZA: Flood - 12-2025 - Flood in Kilosa Morogoro region
summary:
The floods were triggered by heavy rains end of December 2025 across several parts of Kilosa District, Morogoro Region, causing rivers to overflow and inundate surrounding communities. The sudden rise in water levels led to widespread flooding in low-lying and flood-prone areas, damaging or destroying residential houses, public infrastructure, roads, and farmlands. As a result, normal community life was severely disrupted, access to basic services was constrained, and many households were forced to flee their homes to seek safety.

The impact of the floods was significant, with many families displaced after their houses were submerged or rendered uninhabitable. An estimated 1,500 people were accommodated in temporary evacuation sites, including Tindiga Primary School, while others sought refuge with relatives or in makeshift shelters. Displaced households lost essential household items, food stocks, and productive assets, while damage to roads and infrastructure further limited access to markets, health facilities, and clean water. Flooding of agricultural land also affected livelihoods, increasing the risk of food insecurity among already vulnerable populations.

The current context remains fragile, with displaced families relying on humanitarian assistance for shelter, food, and basic non-food items. Overcrowding in temporary shelters has increased health and WASH risks, including exposure to waterborne diseases. Vulnerable groups, such as children, women, older people, and persons with disabilities have been disproportionately affected due to limited coping capacities. Government authorities, in collaboration with humanitarian actors including TRCS, continue to provide emergency assistance while exploring long-term solutions, including relocation to safer areas, to reduce recurrent flood risks in Kilosa District.
