summary:
On December 15, the Ministry of Health reported that surveillance, diagnostic, and monitoring protocols have been activated to contain the spread of seasonal influenza A (H3N2) subclade K, following the confirmation of two cases in minors residing in Lima. Both children— a one‑year‑old treated at the Villa El Salvador Emergency Hospital and an eight‑year‑old admitted to Hipólito Unanue Hospital— have already been discharged and are out of danger.

Deputy Minister of Health Leonardo Rojas stated that the detection of this subclade prompted the immediate reinforcement of epidemiological actions nationwide. Meanwhile, César Munayco, director of the National Center for Epidemiology, Prevention, and Disease Control (CDC Peru), explained that this subclade has been circulating since August and originated between the United States and Australia, having been identified in more than 30 countries. He also noted that the risk of an epidemic is low because it is not the winter season.

Authorities reiterated the importance of preventive measures such as frequent handwashing, proper ventilation of indoor spaces, wearing a mask when experiencing respiratory symptoms, and reducing contact with vulnerable individuals. They also emphasized that the influenza vaccination campaign is ongoing, prioritizing children under five, older adults, and pregnant women as part of the National Vaccination Schedule.

In the days prior, the Ministry of Health issued an epidemiological alert to strengthen surveillance, timely diagnosis, and the response capacity of public and private health facilities, especially in light of increased mobility during the year‑end holidays.

countries.name: Chile
dtype.name: Other
name: CHL: Other - 12-2025 - Computer Threat
summary:
INC Ransom - Incidente en Curso

El 16 de diciembre de 2025 la Agencia Nacional de Ciberseguridad – ANCI informa lo siguiente:

Desde el CSIRT Nacional, comunicamos detalles técnicos de un incidente de efecto significativo en curso, el cual afecta a uno o más servicios esenciales u operadores de importancia vital.

INC Ransom

Recientemente, se han identificado ataques correspondientes al grupo de amenaza INC Ransom. La técnica de acceso inicial identificada hasta ahora es el acceso a la administración de un firewall FortiGate, permitiendo el acceso a la red institucional.

Este actor de amenaza fue observado por primera vez a finales de 2024, presentando patrones de compromiso similares y el mismo impacto resultante: secuestro de información en instituciones de alto flujo financiero y que almacenan grandes volúmenes de datos. Este actor de amenaza ejecuta la fase de acceso inicial mediante el uso de credenciales comprometidas u obtenidas a través de un corredor de acceso inicial (Initial Access Broker). El acceso se realiza a firewalls FortiGate que no tengan configurados controles de seguridad, tales como autenticación multifactor (MFA).

Estos accesos se realizan desde VPS o VPN de terceros, por lo que utiliza un canal de acceso "limpio", principalmente desde servicios ubicados en Estados Unidos, Reino Unido y Francia; para ingresar a la red institucional o, generar políticas en el firewall para permitir el acceso desde otros orígenes, y permitiendo habilitar puertos y crear vectores de acceso potencialmente explotables con el objetivo de amplificar la intrusión.

Posteriormente, debido a ausencias de controles de segmentación, el actor de amenaza realiza movimiento lateral a través de protocolos comúnmente habilitados para la administración, incluyendo RDP, NetBIOS y SSH. Con esto, el atacante se desplaza a infraestructura de virtualización, para realizar la encriptación de todas las máquinas contenidas en este, ocasionando la caída simultánea de múltiples servicios.

 

 

Recomendaciones

·        Levantar listado de proveedores con acceso remoto (VPN, RDP/VDI, SSH, herramientas de soporte remoto); con este listado, eliminar cuentas no usadas, genéricas o sin dueño claro; exigir cuentas nominativas.

·        Habilitar controles MFA obligatorio y de autenticación en todas las cuentas de usuario, y exigir MFA para todo acceso remoto (VPN/SSO/VDI), sin excepciones.

·        Aplicar una política de contraseñas robusta y, si es posible, acceso condicional (por país/IP, riesgo, horario).

·        Accesos de terceros deben ingresar a una zona segregada (jump server/bastion) y con rutas explícitas hacia objetivos autorizados.

·        Bloquear movimiento lateral: restringir RDP/SMB/SSH por segmentos, y permitirlos solo donde corresponda.

·        Controles de red y endurecimiento del canal remoto

·        Permitir VPN solo desde IPs permitidas cuando sea viable, o por “allow-list” de ubicaciones/ASN.

·        Deshabilitar split-tunneling si no es necesario; revisar posture checks si existen.

·        Asegurar que el acceso remoto esté registrado y con timeout/bloqueo por inactividad.

 

Ataque Cibernético a servidores de SERNAGEOMIN – Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería

El 18 de diciembre de 2025 SERNAGEOMIN informa lo siguiente:

Comunicado Oficial: Sernageomin informa sobre ataque cibernético a sus servidores

El Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería (Sernageomin) comunica que fue afectado por un ataque informático, el cual provocó la interrupción temporal del portal institucional y de las plataformas internas del organismo.

Al detectarse la situación, se activaron de inmediato los protocolos de emergencia y se convocó al Comité de Crisis para proteger la operación crítica del Observatorio Volcanológico de los Andes del Sur (OVDAS) y garantizar la continuidad de los servicios esenciales, especialmente los relacionados con los trámites mineros y administrativos.

Actualmente, el monitoreo volcánico de OVDAS se está realizando de manera normal y recibiendo la información del instrumental que se encuentra instalado en los diferentes volcanes a lo largo del país y en permanente coordinación con el Servicio Nacional de Protección Civil y Emergencia (Senapred).

En materia minera la Subdirección Nacional de Minería junto a las direcciones regionales del Servicio han habilitado canales de comunicación directo con las empresas con el objetivo de dar continuidad a los procesos y trámites, los cuales se complementan con la atención presencial en las oficinas OIRS de cada regional.

En el caso de las solicitudes de Atenciones Técnicas Geológicas (ATG), referidas a permisos municipales, se habilitó la plataforma “Cerofilas”, a la que puede acceder mediante el siguiente enlace: https://sernageomin.cerofilas.gob.cl/

Investigación

Una vez detectado el incidente informático, se reportó a la Agencia Nacional de Ciberseguridad (ANCI), con quienes estamos trabajando de manera coordinada desde ese momento, y se reforzó la colaboración con Senapred.

Ayer lunes se presentó la denuncia formal ante el Ministerio Público y se está gestionando una querella criminal con el fin de identificar a los responsables y establecer las sanciones legales correspondientes.

Finalmente, los equipos de Sernageomin trabajan para restablecer la operatividad de los sistemas e implementar medidas adicionales de ciberseguridad, asegurando que todas las aplicaciones internas y herramientas digitales funcionen con normalidad en el menor tiempo posible.

Hackeo a Clinica Davila

El 18 de diciembre se informa de hackeo a Clinica Davila, filtrando información d epacientes y exámenes.

Desde la clínica aseguran que activaron los protocolos de seguridad apenas notaron el hackeo a su base de datos, durante la tarde de este jueves 18 de diciembre.

“Clínica Dávila tomó conocimiento de un incidente informático provocado por terceros. De inmediato se activaron los protocolos de seguridad establecidos, lo que permitió controlar la situación con rapidez y mantener en todo momento la continuidad en la recepción y atención de pacientes. En estos momentos, la clínica se encuentra operando con normalidad”, expresan a través de un comunicado de prensa.

“El hecho fue debidamente informado a las autoridades competentes y actualmente se encuentra bajo el análisis forense de expertos en la materia. Los resultados de dicha investigación permitirán a la clínica adoptar las acciones correspondientes a la brevedad”, sentencian.

 

 

DEVMAN Ransomware - Investigación de Amenazas

 

El 19 de diciembre la ANCI publica lo siguiente:

Desde el CSIRT Nacional, parte de la Agencia Nacional de Ciberseguridad (ANCI), compartimos información técnica relacionada a uno o más patrones de comportamiento observados por el equipo, los cuales podrían afectar sistemas e infraestructura digital del país.

Durante los últimos días hemos identificado actividad vinculada al grupo de ransomware DEVMAN dentro del ciberespacio nacional, comprometiendo parcialmente la operatividad de un servicio esencial.

A partir de la investigación realizada por especialistas de la Agencia Nacional de Ciberseguridad (ANCI), identificamos TTP relacionados históricamente al afiliado de este ransomware, los cuales ponemos a disposición de la comunidad para que puedan tomar las medidas necesarias de mitigación.

Actualizaremos esta alerta con información directamente relacionada a la actividad reciente en el futuro próximo.

Ransomware DEVMAN

Este grupo de ransomware surgió aproximadamente entre abril y julio del 2025. DEVMAN no es un desarrollo desde cero, si no una variante del ransomware DragonForce, el que comparte gran parte de su código con Conti y LockBit 3.0.

DEVMAN comenzó como un afiliado para otros grupos de RaaS (Ransomware-as-a-Service) como Qilin, APOS y DragonForce.

Observaciones

DEVMAN se caracteriza por utilizar métodos de accesos iniciales más tradicionales y oportunistas, suele ser por medio de servicios RDP, VPN, Phishing y movimientos laterales, también muestra una clara preferencia por industrias donde la interrupción operativa es costosa, lo que aumenta la presión para pagar. Su foco principal ha sido Asia-Pacífico, África y Latinoamérica.

A torrential rain fell on the entire Province of Kongo Central during the  whole night of December 9 to 10, 2025 and it continues in the early morning of December 10.

The latter caused flooding and collapse of houses everywhere,  but especially in the  City of BOMA where the rain continued until 2:00 p.m. The waters coming from various rivers in the City and the ring roads (Bangu, Kalamu, Kifu, Nsindi) increased the flow of  the Kalamu River to such an extent that the base of the old bridge on the Kabondo bank collapsed around 8:30 a.m. while there were passengers as well as some Internet users who filmed the passage of the rainwater full of garbage with the hope of visualizing if it ever took away victims.

All these people  all fell under the collapsed bridge, leaving them with only one survivor, living in the Onatra camp in the Commune of Kabondo.

This survivor was saved thanks to the heroism of a  FARDC soldier, the commander  of Camp Barick, who managed to evacuate  him directly by two volunteers of the Red Cross of the DRC/Boma  to  the Central HGR of Boma where one of the Volunteers was appointed as a nurse while waiting for the arrival of his relatives.  

It is unfortunately sad to report the disappearance of two people for whom a PLF volunteer from the city is mobilized to collect additional information (Secondary).

summary:
On January 3rd, the United States launched a military operation against Venezuela, successfully capturing its president, Nicolás Maduro, and First Lady, Cilia Flores. This sudden action has heightened tensions in the region and drawn global attention to the ongoing political crisis in Venezuela.

In response to this military operation, the Government of Guyana has activated its security plans to ensure the safety and security of its citizens, preparing for any potential direct or indirect impacts on the nation. This includes increased surveillance, reinforced border security, and readiness to assist any citizens who may need help.

The Guyana Red Cross Society is actively monitoring the situation and unfolding events, assessing the humanitarian needs that may arise from the conflict, and coordinating with local and international agencies to provide necessary assistance.  

Furthermore, the government is in communication with neighboring countries to discuss collective security measures and regional stability, emphasizing the importance of diplomatic efforts in resolving the crisis peacefully.

countries.name: Chile
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: CHL: Population Movement - 11-2025 - Population Movement Chile - Peru Border
summary:
The Chile-Peru border in the place known as La Concordia pass, located between the border complexes of both countries, has been the focus of attention during the last week due to the presence of people in human mobility who seek to return to their countries of origin through this border. Because they are people with irregular migratory status, they are not allowed to enter Peru, but neither are they allowed to return to Chile.

This situation has become more visible because the interim president of Peru has declared a state of emergency with a decree approved on Friday, November 28, 2025 that will be in force for 60 days https://busquedas.elperuano.pe/dispositivo/NL/2463985-1 , which has also led to the mobilization of military agents to the border.

The media have covered this situation showing an increase in people, likewise, organizations in the northern zone have confirmed that part of the people are children and adolescents, the elderly, people with underlying diseases, in addition to obvious needs for protection, humanitarian aid and to reestablish contact between family members.

On the part of the Chilean state, no alert has been declared or call for technical tables to address people's humanitarian needs.

The foreign ministries of Chile and Peru agreed to coordinate joint operations and patrols, share information, unify criteria for migration cases and ensure the operation of border crossings, with technical and follow-up meetings to evaluate progress.

countries.name: Sri Lanka

name: Sri Lanka - Tropical Cyclone Ditwah, 2025
summary:
The flood and landslide situation resulting from Cyclone Ditwah affected an estimated of more than 1.5  million people across the country, and  643 people are reported dead, and 183 people are reported missing (Sri Lanka Brief). According to the UN, the severely affected districts include Gampaha, Colombo, Puttalam, Mannar, Trincomalee, Batticaloa, Kandy, Badulla, Matale, Vavuniya, Kegalle. Over 200 severe landslides damaged or destroyed around 100,000 houses, with 6,176 fully damaged and more than 95,213 partially damaged across multiple districts. (Disaster Management Centre).

 The affected people have lost their homes, agriculture, livestock, etc. Access to clean water remains a major concern, with reports of drinking water sources being contaminated with floodwater. The initial data shows that  622 water schemes were severely damaged, including 85 major urban water supply schemes and 540 water treatment plants. Approximately 413,000 household connections were disrupted, representing more than 14 per cent of national connections. In rural areas, around 538 community-managed schemes are affected, reducing access for roughly 751,000 people. Many dug wells remain inundated, increasing contamination risks and the likelihood of waterborne disease as floodwaters recede.

 As of 15 December, the water has receded; however, the devastation is more visible than ever. Physical infrastructure, including roads swept away by floods and landslides, is gradually reconnecting to the wider network. However, it is expected to take a considerable amount of time to reconstruct. Severe disruption to electricity, mobile, and communications was reported in northern districts in the initial days of the disaster, which is now restored but not completely.   

 It is reported that nearly 70,055 people are still living in 762 safety centres (Disaster Management Centre), including schools converted into emergency accommodation. These temporary accommodations are not designed to support a large number of people with proper sanitation, which might result in water-borne and vector-borne diseases. Children residing in the safety centres require psychosocial support as they might be going through trauma, which will have long-term risks if not addressed on time.

 Floods and cyclone Ditwah caused severe damage to education, agriculture, and health services. About 1,185 schools are in flood-affected areas, impacting nearly 459,000 school-age children, 28,900 teachers, and 68,000 preschoolers. As of 16 December, 159 schools remain closed, many serving as safety shelters. Agriculture suffered heavily, with 564,000 hectares of paddy at risk and 96,000 hectares of other crops plus 13,000 hectares of vegetables destroyed by floods and strong winds. Health services were also disrupted, as 243 health institutions reported major damage and over 200 faced access issues. Power and water outages cut off essential services, affecting over 100 facilities, including critical hospital units like operating theatres. UN Resident Coordinator’s Office.

As of 15 December, the SLRCS reached out to 12,941 peopel with essential households- dry rationsm hygiene packs, baby kits, baby sheets, towels, sarang, kaftan, sleeping mats, jerry cans etc. Additionally, 4,981 people were reaced with teh emerency first aid services. Hygien promotion activities are ongoin in te communities by mobilizing 300 volunteers across affected districts. Similarly, more than 15,000 liters of bottled water distributed and 271 women/irls reacehd wit 271 packs of sanitary napkins distributed in the safety centres and at the communities. The SLRCS distributed 100 materenity kits and 200 dignity kits wit te support from UNFPA reaching to 300 prenant women, lactating mothers and adolescent girls.

countries.name: Indonesia
dtype.name: Flood
name: Indonesia: Flood, 2025
summary:
North Sumatra Flood & Landslide Situation Update

  • Event Overview: Heavy rainfall since Friday (Nov 21) triggered flooding (water levels 30–100 cm) across three regions in North Sumatra: Mandailing Natal Regency, Central Tapanuli Regency, and Sibolga City.

  • Mandailing Natal: The Parlampungan River overflowed, submerging Muara Batang Gadis District. This affected 520 households (1,800 people), causing 1,800 displacements and inundating several roads.

  • Central Tapanuli (Tapanuli Tengah): The Aek Lumut River overflowed, affecting seven districts. Additionally, high-intensity rain triggered a landslide in Mardame Village (Sitahuis). This impacted 1,902 households (7,608 people), resulting in 45 displacements, 4 fatalities, and 1 heavily damaged house.

  • Sibolga City: Floods submerged roads (30–50 cm), while two landslides caused the Sibolga–Tarutung Highway to collapse, rendering it impassable.

  • Total Impact: A total of 9,408 people (2,422 households) affected, 1,845 displaced, 4 confirmed deaths, and 1 house heavily damaged. (Source: BPBD & PMI North Sumatra).

  • Current Status: While some areas remain inundated, residents in receding areas have begun returning from shelters to clean up mud and debris.

 

North Aceh Flood Situation Update

  • Event Overview: Heavy rains and strong winds on Sunday (Nov 23) caused four rivers (Krueng Jambo Aye, Krueng Keureuto, Krueng Pase, and Krueng Mane) to overflow, resulting in floodwaters ranging from 10 to 80 cm deep.

  • Affected Areas: Seven districts in North Aceh were impacted: Langkahan, Baktiya Barat, Muara Batu, Tanah Jambo Aye, Seunuddon, Syamtalira Aron, and Samudra.

  • Impact: A total of 4,555 people (2,551 households) were affected, with 1,754 individuals displaced to relatives' homes. Assessments regarding further displacement and damage are ongoing. (Source: PMI Aceh & BPBD).

  • Emergency Response: The North Aceh Government declared a state of emergency for the flood disaster for a duration of 54 days, effective from November 23, 2025, to December 15, 2025.

  • Current Status: While some areas remain inundated, some residents have begun returning from evacuation sites to clean up mud and debris in their homes.

 

West Sumatra Flood & Landslide Situation Update

  • Event Overview: High-intensity rainfall since Sunday (Nov 23) triggered floods and landslides across 13 districts/cities in West Sumatra, including Padang, Padang Pariaman, Solok City, Agam, Tanah Datar, and Pasaman.

  • Key Regional Impacts:

    • Padang Pariaman: Several rivers (Batang Anai, Ulakan, Lubuak, and Kamumuan) overflowed, affecting 1,824 people (608 households). Damage includes 608 submerged homes, 2 heavily damaged houses, 1 school, 1 building, and 2 damaged bridges.

    • Solok City: Overflowing rivers (Batang Lembang and Batang Gawan) affected 1,279 people in Lubuk Sikarah District, displacing 25 individuals.

    • Other Areas: Flooding affected hundreds of residents in Padang City, Agam, Tanah Datar, and Pasaman, with water levels ranging from 10–50 cm.

  • Total Impact: A total of 4,122 people (1,437 households) were affected. Damages include 608 submerged houses, 2 heavily damaged homes, 1 school, 1 building, and 2 bridges. Currently, 25 people are displaced. (Source: BPBD & PMI West Sumatra).

  • Current Status: While floodwaters persist in some areas, residents have begun returning from evacuation sites to clean up mud and debris.

countries.name: Malaysia

name: Malaysia - Northeast Coast Flood, 2025
summary:
As of 23 November 2025, flood-affected areas across six states have recorded significant displacement, with a total of 7,998 victims from 2,953 families accommodated in 42 temporary evacuation centres (PPS). Kelantan remains the most severely affected, with 7,275 people from 2,642 families relocated to 31 PPS across four districts. Terengganu reported 304 victims from 88 families in two PPS within one district. Kedah has 234 victims from 80 families placed in three PPS, while Penang recorded 93 victims from 21 families accommodated in two PPS. In Sarawak, Miri continues to be affected, with 44 victims from six families in one PPS, while Perlis recorded 48 victims from 16 families housed in three PPS within a single district. The overall situation highlights the ongoing impact of floods across multiple states, emphasizing the need for continued monitoring, coordination, and support for affected communities to ensure their safety and welfare.

Earlier, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a heavy continuous rain warning at the severe level for Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu, Bachok, and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan, effective from today until 24 November. A continuous rain alert at the cautionary level was also issued for Perlis, Kedah, Penang, and Perak (Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Hulu Perak, and Kuala Kangsar) for the same period. Similar conditions are forecast for Kelantan (Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Kuala Krai, and Gua Musang) and Terengganu until 26 November, indicating a continued risk of flooding and the need for vigilance in affected areas.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: ZWE: Epidemic - 11-2025 - HAND, FOOT AND MOUTH DISEASE (HFMD) OUTBREAK, ZIMBABWE
summary: Zimbabwe has experienced an ongoing Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) outbreak affecting several provinces, including Harare, Bulawayo, Manicaland, Mashonaland East and Mashonaland West. Most confirmed cases have been detected among children below five years old, particularly those in preschool and early primary school settings where close contact and shared facilities increase transmission risk. The primary impacts on the health system have included increased outpatient visits at primary health facilities due to parents seeking assessment and reassurance for affected children. The recent outbreak is one of the first times the country has seen a large, widely reported national outbreak and is officially highlighted at the national scale by the Ministry of Health and Child Care, WHO and the national media. While HFMD is generally mild and self-limiting, the rise in suspected cases has increased routine caseloads in busy urban clinics and school-linked health posts. The outbreak has also required additional resources for surveillance, case recording and community communication, stretching existing staff and disease monitoring systems. Health workers have had to intensify health education efforts, especially around hygiene, early recognition of symptoms and preventing transmission in schools and childcare centres. At the community level, the outbreak has led to high levels of concern among parents and school administrators, resulting in short-term disruptions to learning in some settings as affected learners stayed home. Schools and daycare centres have faced pressure to improve hygiene infrastructure and procedures, including handwashing facilities, disinfection routines and monitoring of symptomatic children. In some cases, the increased flow of children into clinics for mild cases has temporarily diverted attention from other essential services. While the disease has not caused serious medical complications in Zimbabwe, the cumulative psychosocial and operational impacts on families, caregivers and frontline health providers have been notable.

name: IDN: Volcanic Eruption - 11-2025 - Mount Semeru, East Java Province, Indonesia
summary:
Mount Semeru Eruption Overview

  • Eruption: Occurred on Wednesday, Nov 19, at 16:00 WIB.

  • Ash Column: Observed ~2,000 meters above the summit, blowing from north and northwest.

  • Seismicity: Recorded max amplitude of 40 mm with a duration of 16 minutes.

Current Status (As of Nov 19, 17:00 WIB)

  • Alert Level: Level IV (Awas/Warning).

  • Seismic Activity: High activity recorded, including 118 eruption quakes, 1 pyroclastic flow signal, and 30 avalanche quakes.

Impact & Evacuation

  • 307 people affected by volcanic ash rain in Supiturang Village, Candipuro District.

  • 129 people evacuated to 4 designated points (Penanggal Village Hall, Gunung Sawur, Sumber Mujur Village Hall, Candipuro District Office).

  • By the time of the eruption, there were 78 hikers recorded entering Semeru area. All hikers reported at Ranu Kumbolo are scheduled to descend towards Ranu Pani starting at 08:00 AM (GMT+7).

Government Response & Safety

  • Emergency Declaration: 7-day Emergency Response Status declared from Nov 19 to 25 Nov, 2025.

  • Exclusion Zones: Authority prohibited any activity within 20km around the summit and 8 km from the crater.

  • Warnings: Avoid river banks (Besuk Kobokan, Besuk Bang, etc.) due to lahar (cold lava) risks.

  • Infrastructure: Power outages reported in the affected areas.

countries.name: Viet Nam
dtype.name: Flood
name: Viet Nam - Flood, 2025
summary:
According to local government, heavy rainfall has persisted since 16 November 2025, causing severe flooding along the Ba River in Đắk Lắk. Emergency flood levels have also been recorded on the Kon River in Gia Lai and the Krông Ana River in Đắk Lắk. Several rivers have reached their peak and are beginning to recede, while others continue to rise. Widespread inundation is impacting areas from Thua Thien Hue to Khanh Hoa, with a heightened risk of flash floods and landslides. Disaster risk levels currently range from Level 1 to Level 4, depending on the river basin.

According to rapid reports from provincial authorities, heavy rainfall and landslides have caused significant impacts as follows:

 1. Human Impact

·       16 deaths: Hue (2), Da Nang (1), Dak Lak (1), Khanh Hoa (11), Gia Lai (1).

·       5 missing: Quang Tri (1), Da Nang (3), Khanh Hoa (1).

 2. Housing

  • 91 houses damaged (Quang Tri 3; Da Nang 32; Quang Ngai 42; Dak Lak 8; Lam Dong 6).
  • 43,282 houses flooded across multiple provinces (largest in Gia Lai and Dak Lak).

 3. Agriculture

  • 10,055 ha of rice and crops damaged
    (major losses in Khanh Hoa: 7,951 ha; Dak Lak: 1,049 ha).

 4. Livestock

  • 6,511 animals dead or swept away
    (Dak Lak heavily affected with 5,282 animals lost).

 5. Transport

·       47 locations on national highways flooded or blocked due to landslides.
Major disruptions include:

·       Severe collapse on QL20 (Mimosa Pass, Lam Dong) at Km226+700:
~70m of roadbed destroyed (40m deep). Traffic fully halted; authorities have closed the section and are directing detours.

 6. Irrigation Infrastructure

  • 650m of embankments damaged (Quang Tri 100m; Khanh Hoa 550m).
  • Nuoc Ngot Reservoir (Khanh Hoa):
    150m of wave-protection wall damaged; ~10,000 m² of the downstream slope eroded.

name: COD: Flood - 11-2025 - Floods in the city of Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo
summary:
The torrential rain that fell in the city of Kinshasa on the night of Tuesday, November 11 and Wednesday, November 12, 2025 precisely at 1:05 a.m. caused significant material damage with deaths recorded.

Flooding has been reported in all the communes of the capital, mainly due to the flooding of the N'djili, Nsanga and Makelele rivers, not to mention the Congo River and the insufficiency or absence of pipes, causing worrying erosion on the hills.

Several major infrastructures were affected, including two broken bridges between Kauka and Matonge in the commune of Kalamu.

The Lufungula market in Lingwala and  Kalembelembe have become inaccessible.

Most of the municipalities and homes were submerged, making it difficult for vehicles and pedestrians to circulate in all areas of the city.

The seasonal climate forecast for the months of November, December 2025 and January 2026 indicates that during this period near-normal rainfall is expected in the cities of Kinshasa, Kolwezi, Manono, Bondo, Bunia Butembo, Goma, Lubumbashi, Mbuji-Mayi, Kikwit, Bandundu, Matadi, Boma,  Mounda, Kindu and Tshikapa.

Highlights indicate that the climate   outlook over this period will be in excess in a northern part of the country. And the near-normal outlook is expected in most of the country.

There is a probability of heavy rainfall which can lead to flooding and landslides in all the cities mentioned above.

summary:
The humanitarian situation in Tanganyika province is taking a critical turn with the massive influx of displaced people from Uvira in South Kivu province.  Volunteers are mobilized at the ports of Kabimba and Kalemie following the  context of growing security tensions in the city of Uvira and its surroundings with the fight between the FARDC and AFC/M23. In the two entrances, our volunteers have already registered 2,375 households, i.e. 14,250 people, this is the first wave of displaced people who have arrived in the city of Kalemie.

In addition, the Kalemie health zone is among the health zones with high reports of cholera cases in the Province of Tanganyika. This aspect is a threat to the populations of Kalemie, the most vulnerable of which are the displaced. There is a lack of water in the reception areas, and the increase in food prices. An urgent response to the needs of the vulnerable is relevant to alleviate suffering and improve their living conditions.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: ARG: Cyclone - 11-2025 - Extratropical Cyclone - Misiones
summary:
A convective system generated multiple consecutive tornadoes with gusts of up to 180 km/h, roof damage, and the fall of trees and power poles across areas of southern Brazil and the province of Misiones, Argentina. According to official reports, a vertically developed storm cell produced two consecutive tornadoes —the first in Dionísio Cerqueira (Santa Catarina, Brazil), a border city with Bernardo de Irigoyen (Misiones, Argentina), and the second in Rio Bonito do Iguaçu (Paraná, Brazil), approximately 200 kilometers west of the Argentine border.

The system was associated with an extratropical cyclone centered over southern Brazil, which created favorable conditions for severe thunderstorms, hail, gusts exceeding 70 km/h, and the formation of multiple tornadoes over Brazilian territory. The storm cell moved toward northeastern Argentina, affecting several areas of the province of Misiones before reaching southern Paraguay.

Misiones: the intense wind gusts, heavy rainfall, and hail generated roof damage, broken power line poles, damaged homes, and overturned vehicles in. The Police Operations Center of the General Directorate of Security reported that the impacts were mainly concentrated within the jurisdictions of Regional Units II (Oberá), IV (Puerto Rico), and XI (Aristóbulo del Valle). The most affected municipalities were Campo Grande, 25 de Mayo, and Colonia Alberdi, with additional disruptions reported in Leandro N. Alem, Villa Bonita, General Alvear, and nearby localities. The company Energía de Misiones reported a failure in the 33 kV line connecting Oberá and Alem, leaving several towns without power. Areas of El Soberbio, San Vicente, and 25 de Mayo also remain without electricity as repair work continues.

countries.name: Chile
dtype.name: Volcanic Eruption
name: CHL: Volcanic eruption - 11-2025 - ACTIVITY OF THE PLANCHÓN PETEROA VOLCANIC COMPLEX - PUYEHUE - CORDÓN CAULLE -
summary:
VOLCANIC COMPLEX PETEROA BANANA
According to the information provided by the Volcanic Observatory of the Southern Andes (OVDAS) of the National Geology and Mining Service (SERNAGEOMIN), the Planchón Peteroa Volcanic Complex maintains its Yellow technical alert level
In relation to the last Volcanic Activity Report (RAV), which evaluated the period between October 16 and 31, 2025, it is reported that the Volcanic Complex maintained activity levels above the base threshold, with persistent records of earthquakes associated with fluid dynamics (some short and others long-lasting).

On the surface, pulsatile columns of gases are maintained with occasional increases in pyroclastic material, and episodes where these emissions remain visible for several hours. Likewise, the occasional presence of nocturnal incandescence is confirmed.

Finally, the available websites showed a notable emission of sulfur dioxide (SO2) into the atmosphere. These antecedents suggest a transition from a predominantly hydrothermal domain to one with greater magmatic participation, where the deep contribution would have intensified the interaction with the shallow hydrothermal system, favoring sustained degassing processes and a greater openness of the surface system. This transition explains the intensification of emissions, the appearance of incandescence, SO2 anomalies and the recently observed seismic variations.

In consideration of this technical background provided by SERNAGEOMIN, and in coordination with the Regional Presidential Delegation of Maule, the Regional Directorate of SENAPRED maintains the Preventive Early Warning for the communes of Molina, Curicó, Romeral and Teno, due to the activity of the Planchón Peteroa Volcanic Complex. which has been in force since July 18, 2025 and until the conditions warrant it.

Similarly, SENAPRED maintains the 4-kilometer security perimeter around the main crater of the volcanic complex.

ACTIVITY OF THE PUYEHUE – CORDÓN CAULLE VOLCANIC COMPLEX

According to information provided by the Southern Andes Volcanological Observatory (OVDAS) of the National Geology and Mining Service (SERNAGEOMIN), the Puyehue – Cordón Caulle Volcanic Complex maintains its technical alert level at green[1]. 

Through its Volcanic Activity Report (RAV) that evaluates the period between October 1 and 31, it is indicated that the activity remained at levels considered low, suggesting stability in the volcanic complex. 

Likewise, the images provided by the fixed cameras, installed in the vicinity of the complex, did not register degassing columns or variations associated with surface activity. Finally, no anomalies were reported in sulfur dioxide (SO2) emissions into the atmosphere in the sector near the volcanic complex.  

In consideration of this technical background provided by SERNAGEOMIN, SENAPRED maintains the Preventive Early Warning, for the communes of Lago Ranco, Río Bueno and Futrono in the Los Ríos Region and Puyehue in the Los Lagos Region, due to the activity of the Puyehue Cordón Caulle Volcanic Complex. which remains in force from April 26, 2024 and until the conditions of the event warrant it. 

Finally, SERNAGEOMIN continues the permanent monitoring of the volcano online and the Regional Directorate of SENAPRED will maintain coordination with the members of the Regional System of Disaster Prevention and Response to timely alert and provide an adequate response to possible emergency situations resulting from the volcanic condition.

countries.name: Democratic Republic of Congo
countries.society_name: Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
dtype.name: Biological Emergency
name: COD: Biological emergency - 11-2025 - Poisoning and detrition of biodiversity in the Province of Haut Katanga.
summary:
Kassapa, a district of the Annex Commune in the copper-bearing city of Lubumbashi, capital of the Province of Haut-Katanga, experienced on the night of 04/11/2025 the starting point of a deadly course of acid spilling.

Precisely, it was from the Chinese mineral processing plant " CDM " located 15 km from the city center of Lubumbashi that this spill had escaped from its basin, crossing several pipes, food fields, springs and rivers including " Kassapa', " kamayibwe ", " Kalubwe ", " Tsansansa ", " Lubumbashi " and then " Kafubu " poisoning and destroying biodiversity (fish, frogs, crabs).

Ill-intentioned, some people have collected these intoxicated sightless fish to sell them in various markets in the city, thus poisoning in turn a large part of the population who now have stomach aches, headaches, dizziness and vomiting, including significant environmental and economic damage.

At the current stage, several people who have consumed these fish are showing the above symptoms, others are serious, many farmers who have lost their fields are without resources and the water sources are poisoned and deprive a large part of the population of this basic foodstuff. And if nothing is done urgently with the return of rain, this spill is likely to easily reach other points and sources of water in the city and outside it, with even more serious consequences for the population and for the environment.

countries.name: Philippines
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: PHL: Cyclone - 11-2025 - TYPHOON TINO (KALMAEGI) and SUPER TYPHOON UWAN (FUNG-WONG)
summary:
Two tropical cyclones — Typhoon TINO (KALMAEGI) and Super Typhoon UWAN (FUNG-WONG) , affected the Philippines in succession this November 2025, bringing heavy rains, strong winds, and widespread impacts across Visayas, Palawan, and Luzon.

 

Typhoon TINO (KALMAEGI)

Entered PAR: 02 November 2025, 5:30 AM (as Tropical Storm)

Intensified into Typhoon: 03 November 2025, 8:00 AM

Exited PAR: 06 November 2025, 12:30 AM

All TCWS lifted: 06 November 2025, 5:00 PM

 

Track Summary:

TINO crossed the Visayas and Palawan areas, making eight landfalls between 04–05 November 2025. Life-threatening winds and heavy rains were reported over Eastern Visayas, Northern Cebu, Negros, and Palawan before it exited PAR and moved toward Vietnam.

 

Landfall:

·       Silago, Southern Leyte – 04 Nov, 12:00 AM

·       Borbon, Cebu – 04 Nov, 5:10 AM

·       Sagay City, Negros Occidental – 04 Nov, 6:40 AM

·       San Lorenzo, Guimaras – 04 Nov, 11:10 AM

·       Iloilo City – 04 Nov, 1:20 PM

·       Magsaysay, Cuyo Island – 04 Nov, 7:10 PM

·       Batas Island, Palawan – 05 Nov, 4:10 AM

·       El Nido, Palawan – 05 Nov, 4:40 AM

 

Super Typhoon UWAN (FUNG-WONG)

Entered PAR: 07 November 2025, 10:00 PM (as Typhoon)

Upgraded to Super Typhoon: 09 November 2025, 5:00 AM

Made Landfall: 09 November 2025, 9:10 PM in Dinalungan, Aurora

Exited PAR: 11 November 2025, 1:30 AM

 

Track Summary:

UWAN rapidly intensified into a Super Typhoon and brought destructive winds and heavy rainfall over Bicol Region, Aurora, Central, and Northern Luzon. After crossing Luzon, it weakened over the West Philippine Sea and exited PAR early morning of 11 November 2025.

·       Typhoon TINO (Nov 2–6): Primarily affected Visayas and Palawan with multiple landfalls and flooding.

·       Super Typhoon UWAN (Nov 7–11): Severely affected Luzon, including Bicol, Aurora, and Ilocos Regions, with typhoon- to super typhoon-force winds.

·       The two cyclones brought successive weather disturbances within a 10-day period, prompting sustained preparedness and response operations from national and local DRRMCs.

countries.name: Viet Nam
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: VNM: Cyclone - 11-2025 - Typhoon Kalmaegi
summary:
According to several sources and local goverments, Typhoon Kalmaegi (Storm No. 13) made landfall in central Viet Nam on 6 November 2025, bringing destructive winds and torrential rains that triggered widespread flooding, landslides, and infrastructure damage across multiple provinces. The storm weakened into a tropical system as it moved westward, but not before causing significant humanitarian impacts, particularly in Đắk Lắk and Gia Lai provinces.

In Đắk Lắk Province, 

  • Two people lost their lives and two others were injured when their homes collapsed due to landslides.
  • The storm destroyed 12 houses, unroofed 326, and flooded 147 homes.
  • Infrastructure was heavily affected, including severe erosion of the Bach Dang embankment, with estimated damages of VND 150 billion (approximately CHF 4.6 million).
  • The local aquaculture sector also suffered major losses, with nearly 54,000 fish cages damaged, amounting to over VND 21 billion (CHF 643,000) in damages.

In Gia Lai Province,

  • One person died and two others were injured as a result of structural collapse.
  • More than 2,300 homes were affected — 43 completely destroyed and 2,282 unroofed.
  • The storm also caused the sinking of a boat, three landslides along key transport routes, and flooding of up to 80 cm in several coastal residential areas. 
  • Thousands of hectares of rice and crops were submerged, and significant losses of livestock and poultry were reported.
  •  Power and telecommunications systems were disrupted, with widespread outages still ongoing. Initial damage estimates in Gia Lai exceed VND 80.2 billion (CHF 2.46 million), with figures expected to rise as assessments continue in remote areas.

Local authorities and humanitarian actors are actively engaged in emergency response efforts, focusing on damage assessment, debris clearance, and support to affected households.

countries.name: Philippines
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: PHL: Cyclone - 11-2025 - TYPHOON TINO (KALMAEGI)
summary:
On 30 October at 2 AM, a Low-Pressure Area (LPA 10i) was being monitored outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR). By 1 November at 2:00 AM, it intensified into a Tropical Depression (formerly LPA 10i), still located outside the PAR. At 8 PM on the same day, it further intensified into a Tropical Storm with the international name “KALMAEGI.”

On 2 November at 5:30 AM, Tropical Storm KALMAEGI entered the PAR and was assigned the domestic name “TINO”. By 2 PM on the same day, Tropical Storm TINO (KALMAEGI) intensified into a Severe Tropical Storm.

On 3 November at 11 AM, Tino intensified into a Typhoon.

Typhoon Tino made landfall in Silago, Southern Leyte, at 12 AM on Tuesday, November 4, 2025. It made its second landfall in Borbon, Cebu, at 5:10 AM, and its third landfall in Sagay City, Negros Occidental, at 6:40 AM.

A total of 57,867 families or 187,536 individuals were affected in 1,137 barangays in regions MIMAROPA, 6, NIR, 7, 8, and CARAGA. Of which, 38,107 families or 122,519 individuals were served inside 1,628 ECs and 14,551 families or 46,034 individuals were served outside ECs.

countries.name: Paraguay
dtype.name: Other
name: PRY: Other - 11-2025 - Severe Storms
summary:
Paraguay's Directorate of Meteorology and Hydrology (DMH) issued multiple alerts for the affected departments, due to the development of storm nuclei that generated intense rains, strong to very strong wind gusts and hail.

San Pedro: In this department, a severe weather episode was recently recorded characterized by an intense hailstorm that caused structural damage – homes and schools without roofs – and accumulation of ice in the streets.
The most affected areas were the districts of Santaní, Guayaibí and Itacurubí del Rosario, where approximately 200 homes were damaged by the storm. This region was one of the hardest hit by hail and strong winds, which also impacted the livelihoods of families, causing total loss of crops and the death of small animals.

Canindeyú: This department is also listed in the WWD bulletins as an area at risk of storms with hail, strong winds and heavy rains. In the Laurel neighborhood, around 40 homes were reported affected by the storm.

countries.name: Thailand
dtype.name: Flood
name: THA: Flood - 11-2025 - Flooding from tropical rainfall and river overflow
summary:
According to the report from Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) Thailand is still experiencing tropical rainfall, resulting in ongoing flooding, including both flash floods and river overflow. As of 12 November 2025, flooding persists across 17 provinces—Ayutthaya, Nakhon Sawan, Suphan Buri, Phichit, Sukhothai, Phitsanulok, Lop Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chai Nat, Ang Thong, Sing Buri, Uthai Thani, Kamphaeng Phet, Uttaradit, Nonthaburi, Phetchabun, and Pathum Thani—covering northern, central, and northeastern regions.

The floods have affected 56 districts, 443 sub-districts, and 2,882 villages, impacting approximately 135,762 households (around 467,604 people). To date, 16 fatalities have been reported.

Weather Forecast (12–13 Nov 2025) : Scattered rain and cooler mornings expected in upper Thailand due to weak high-pressure influence. Southern Thailand will continue to face thunderstorms with waves up to 2 meters.
Typhoon “Fung-Wong” is moving northeast towards Taiwan and poses no impact to Thailand. 24 major reservoirs are above 80% capacity, including Bhumibol, Sirikit, and Khun Dan. Continuous
monitoring for spillover and downstream impact is ongoing.

countries.name: Cuba
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: Cuba - Hurricane Melissa - October 2025
summary:
Hurricane Melissa rapidly intensified from a tropical wave to a Category 5 storm by 28 October 2025, becoming one of the strongest hurricanes ever recorded in the Caribbean. In response, Cuba activated extensive preparedness measures, including mass evacuations, sheltering, and closures of schools and transportation systems. Over 735,000 people were evacuated prior to the Hurricane making landfall.

After passing over Jamaica, Melissa made landfall in Santiago de Cuba on 29 October as a Category 3 hurricane, bringing 10–25 inches (250-635 mm) of rainfall, severe flooding, landslides, and storm surge. The Cuban Red Cross supported evacuations, psychosocial first air and support, and preparedness actions.

Preliminary assessments show 150,000 houses damaged—including 95,000 in Santiago de Cuba—and major disruptions to electricity, water, communications, and transport. Around 450,000 people lack access to safe water, and damage has impacted 642 health facilities and 2,117 schools, affecting more than 670,000 students. As of 14 November, about 54,000 people remain evacuated.

The affected provinces were already recovering from Hurricanes Oscar and Rafael (2024) and now face a multi-crisis emergency compounded by ongoing outbreaks of dengue, Oropouche, and chikungunya, with 30% of the population recently affected. Response priorities focus on life-saving assistance, restoring essential services, and strengthening community resilience amid overlapping challenges.

countries.name: Bahamas

name: BHS: Cyclone - 10-2025 - Hurricane Melissa
summary:
According to the Meterological Dept, Hurricane Melissa has become a deadly CAT 4 storm.  Melissa a slow moving storm has caused heavy rains,  deadly floods and mud slides in the region of Jamaica, Hispaniola and Cuba.

Melissa is projected to enter into the Crntral and Southeastern Bahamas by Wednesday the 29th.  

On Friday October 24th, 6:30 pm, President Sumner, Director General Pinder, Disaster representatives Carl Smith and Dr Trevor Johnson held a meeting based on information from the DRMA that a potentially catastrophic storm was forming in the Atlantic with potentially devastating impacts on The Bahamas.

On Saturday October 25th a flight was sent from The Bahamas and Bahamian students in Jamaica were given the opportunity to evacuate to New Providence  

DG Pinder got in contact with Volunteer, Staff and Group leaders to advise on the need to implement preparedness. Regular weather advisory are also shared through WhatsApp.

On Sunday Oct 26th, the DRM partially activated its NEOC and it was later fully activated. 

DG is connecting with NEOC virtually and Red Cross representatives are scheduled to be stationed physically on Oct 28th

On its current trajectory and with the potential of devastation on lives, The government of The Bahamas has allowed residents in low lying areas to evacuate voluntarily.  Planes are being made available for passage in areas not in the path of the storm

Shelters have been opened.  Red Cross are assisting in Shelter Management.  

The Red Cross Branch leaders for Inagua Ms Leah Ferguson reports that special flights from Inagua  with made available by the government.

There were reportedly 2 flights of 296 passengers and a regular carrier with 55 people evacuated from the island that began to experience flooding from Saturday 26th October.  

Residences from Acklins reported two special flights with approximately 100 people being evacuated from that island. 

Evacuation flights are expected to continue through Tuesday the 28th.

Data from other Southern islands such as Mayaguana and Crooked Island is pending per future updates. 

The Kendal GL Isaac's stadium has been opened as a primary shelter and registration point in New Providence to house evacuees.

countries.name: Tanzania, United Republic of
dtype.name: Civil Unrest
name: TZA: Civil Unrest - 10-2025 - TANZANIA GENERAL ELECTION PREPAREDNESS
summary:
General elections in Tanzania are scheduled for October 2025, with the process including Presidential, Parliamentary, and Local Government elections across the country. The election process commenced earlier in the year with party primaries and nomination procedures, which have already generated incidents and tensions in various regions.
Timeline of the 2025 Elections (key milestones)
August 2025: Political party primaries for councilor and parliamentary candidates in various regions.
October 2025: General election voting day nationwide.
October–November 2025: Proclamation of results for Presidential, Parliamentary, and Local Government races.
All election processes are to be completed within the constitutional timeframe before the end of 2025.
Political & Social Context
The upcoming elections are unfolding against a backdrop of growing political polarization, reports of violence, governance-related disputes, and concerns over political freedoms. Several high-profile political developments and security incidents have already been recorded since the start of the nomination process, raising questions about the safety of candidates, transparency, and public trust in the process.
Key Indicators Observed Since the Start of the Election Process
Opposition Boycott of Electoral Code of Ethics
CHADEMA, Tanzania’s main opposition party, boycotted the signing of the 2025 Electoral Code of Ethics, refusing to attend the INEC-led ceremony in Dodoma. Secretary General John Mnyika confirmed that no representatives participated. INEC warned that non-signing parties, such as CHADEMA, may be barred from fielding candidates in the October general elections.
Resignation of Senior Officials and Related Security Concerns
The resignation of several senior officials — including the Kawe MP and the Ambassador to Cuba and Caribbean countries — followed public criticism of the national governance system and ongoing abduction incidents. Shortly after, the ambassador’s relative was reportedly abducted, further intensifying public concern.
Violent Attack on Candidate in Upanga West
On August 4, during a councilor election in Upanga West, Dar es Salaam, candidate Khallil Karim was allegedly attacked by rivals. He accused outgoing councilor Adnan Kitwana Kondo and others, who appeared in widely circulated video footage. (Source:(https://www.instagram.com/p/DM7CiaYN5Bw/?igsh=MWN0ajZma3pyYXY4eA)
Kidnapping and Assault of Deputy Minister’s Family Members
Deputy Health Minister Dr. Godwin Mollel reported that his wife and aide were kidnapped and assaulted in Siha, Kilimanjaro, allegedly by supporters of a rival candidate. He stated their car was attacked and another vehicle burned. District Commissioner Dr. Christopher Timbuka confirmed the case is under police investigation.
(Source:https://www.instagram.com/reel/DM7hGw_Nf7g/?igsh=Z2J2a3dtcDN2cDFw)
Violence in Kivule Ward During CCM Primaries
On August 4, violence broke out in Kivule Ward, Dar es Salaam, during CCM primaries for councilor and parliamentary candidates, disrupting voting and heightening tensions among supporters. Authorities have yet to release an official statement.
(Source:https://www.instagram.com/reel/DM7dLNNi578/?igsh=bmxtbzI1M3JyOW0y)
Widespread Tensions Over Candidate Removal
Violence and unrest have been reported in Mbeya, Mwanza, Morogoro, Pwani, and Manyara following CCM’s removal of incumbent councilors from nomination lists. In Kitangiri Ward, Ilemela, Mwanza, residents demand reinstatement of former councilor Donald Ndaro, whose name was omitted despite a Central Committee directive. Ndaro says he is still awaiting official confirmation after following up with regional officials since August 1.
Source:https://www.instagram.com/reel/DM5cDypCMmk/?igsh=cGlobHA3eGxuZWNt)
Conclusion: These incidents point to a potentially volatile election season. The combination of party boycotts, high-profile resignations, targeted violence against candidates and political figures, and intra-party disputes indicates heightened political tension. The pattern of violence and intimidation, if unaddressed, could escalate as the October 2025 general elections approach, requiring heightened readiness by humanitarian and peacebuilding actors to support affected communities, monitor potential displacement, and prevent further violence.

countries.name: Viet Nam

name: VNM: Flood - 10-2025 - Heavy rain
summary:
According to local goverment, from 25 to 28 October, heavy rainfall has  caused severe flooding and landslides across Central Viet Nam, notably in Thua Thien Hue, Da Nang, Quang Nam, and Kon Tum. A Level 3 disaster risk warning was issued for Hue and Da Nang, with water levels remaining dangerously high. Emergency rescues were conducted in multiple locations, and over 430 households in Kon Tum were isolated due to landslides. Hospitals in Hue were flooded, prompting patient evacuations, while Quang Ngai reported over 30 landslide points and major road blockages.

As of 28 October, widespread damage was reported in five provinces. One person is missing, nine houses were damaged, and over 3,000 households (8,630 people) were evacuated. Agricultural losses include over 400 hectares of crops and fruit trees, and hundreds of livestock and poultry. Infrastructure damage includes eroded canals, damaged roads and bridges, and landslides disrupting transport and isolating communities.

countries.name: Costa Rica
dtype.name: Flood
name: CRI: Flooding - 10-2025 - Indirect effects of Hurricane Melissa
summary:
On Sunday, October 19, the IMN Weather Advisory detailed that Tropical Wave #40 at that time was moving towards the Caribbean Sea due to a possible cyclonic development of this, recommending surveillance of this system and it was during October 20 and 21 the IMN maintained informative updates: reported instability associated with tropical waves (including #39 and #40) and raised the watch due to the high probability of cyclogenesis in the Caribbean and on October 21 reported that tropical wave #40 evolved into tropical storm Melissa.

 As Melissa strengthened in the Caribbean, the IMN began to issue advisories about the indirect influence of the storm on the Costa Rican climate: persistence of moisture, active Intertropical Convergence Zone, and emphasis on rainfall and unstable conditions especially in the South Pacific and southern coasts of the Central Pacific. These advisories (and updates of October 24–26) mentioned continuity of surveillance for possible heavy rains, waves and risk of landslides in vulnerable areas.

 Faced with this scenario, the National Emergency Commission, at 4:30 p.m. on Saturday, October 25, 2025, decreed Alert #36, Orange in the Pacific coastal regions, Yellow for the Central and Northern regions, and green for the Caribbean, where the Municipal and Communal Emergency Committees are instructed to monitor local conditions based on the IMN reports, in addition to preparing response mechanisms and keeping operational units informed of situations that arise, as well as maintaining activation and monitoring.

 Given the above, and according to the National Emergency and Disaster Response Plan, the Costa Rican Red Cross established Response Level 3 for the Guanacaste, Puntarenas and South regions, where there is a concentration of personnel in Auxiliary Committees, cancellation of activities and training, establish Regional CCOs and determine the deployment of ENI rapid response personnel and specialized units.

 As the rains have increased, a response is being provided to rescues due to landslides in mountainous areas, evacuations of communities impacted by floods, transfers of people to shelters, out-of-hospital care for people affected by accidents due to adverse weather conditions.

In the early morning of October 30, a series of rains occurred in the northern zone that increased the institutional response work, to contribute to the evacuation in sectors such as, for example, in localities such as Pénjamo in the North Zone and in the City of Cartago.

countries.name: Jamaica
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: Jamaica - Hurricane Melissa - October 2025
summary:
Hurricane Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope as a Category 5 storm with sustained winds of approximately 185 mph (295 km/h), putting it among the most intense Atlantic hurricanes on record, and one of the strongest to hit the island in modern history.
Upon striking, the storm brought catastrophic winds, storm surge and torrential rainfall totalling up to 1 000 mm (40 in) in mountainous areas — triggering widespread flooding and landslides.

Reports of damage to infrastructure are still incomplete, but information provided by UNOSAT and Microsoft AI for Good indicates damage of up to 80% to roofs in small areas where clouds allowed access to satellite images. As of 29 October, the UNOSAT Building Damage Assessment for Black River Village, Saint Elizabeth Parish, Jamaica identified approximately 314 destroyed and 1,183 damaged buildings.

Jamaica’s location in the hurricane-prone Caribbean region makes it highly vulnerable to tropical storms, especially during the Atlantic hurricane season.

countries.name: Nigeria

name: NGA: Other - 10-2025 - Insurgency: Multiple Attacks by Non-state Actors (Armed Opposition Groups).
summary:
At about 00:01 a.m., midnight and 04:00 a.m. on Thursday, 23 October 2025, several non-state actors launched coordinated assaults on four Nigerian military positions in Dikwa, Mafa, Gajibo, and Katarko, situated in Sector 1 (Borno State) and Sector 2 (Yobe State). Dikwa town is 91km from Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State; Mafa town is 53km from Maiduguri; Gajibo town is 100km from Maiduguri. Katarko town in Gujba LGA is 23km from Damaturu, the capital of Yobe State. Both Borno and Yobe states are situated in the NE, Nigeria, where there has been a protracted complex emergency since 2009.

In all instances, Nigerian military troops stood firm and professionally repelled the attacks, leaving behind over 50 corpses of armed opposition group members, and several others fled away with wounds. A military hierarchy also reported that some of the troops sustained injuries.

The Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI released a press statement and affirmed that intelligence further revealed that the armed opposition groups who attacked Dikwa and Gajibo (Borno state) manoeuvred from the Cameroon axis, while those that attacked Katarko (Yobe state) emerged from the Timbuktu Triangle, a known non-state actors’ enclave.

IED Explosion: An Improvised Explosive Device (IED) planted by Armed Opposition Groups (AOGs) exploded after a dog stepped on it on the roadside between Gujba and Katarko, Yobe state.

Nigerian Military Response: A Military Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) team is currently scanning the area to ensure safety and neutralise any other potential threats.

A lot of civilians' objectives, such as lorries, cars, other vehicles and several items including merchandize mearnt to be sold and which were been transported by lorries were burnt by non-state actors , became collateral damage among other property. UNHUB located in Dikwa was also affected.

countries.name: Uganda
dtype.name: Transport Accident
name: UGA: Transport Accident - 10-2025 - Fatal Road Traffic Crash along Kampala-Gulu Highway
summary:
The Uganda Red Cross Society Emergency Call centre received an alert about a bus accident that occured in the wee hours of Wednesday 22/10/2025 in Kiryandongo district along the Kampala-Gulu highway. Uganda Red Cross Ambulance attached to Kiryandong refugee response operations swiftly responded, in company of the Uganda Police and the Disrict Health team by rescuing all the injured passengers and referring to Kiryandongo General hospital as well as Panyadoli Health Centre IV that is located within the vicinity of Kiryandingo refugee settlement.

According to initial press report issued by Uganda Police, at least 46 people have been confirmed dead in the accident that involved two buses and two other vehicle that were all plying along the Kampala-Gulu highway. 

The accident happened at Asili farm in Kitaleba village along  Kampala-Gulu highway  in Kiryadongo District. Police said the crash involved an Isuzu bus registration number UAM 045V belonging to Planet company and another bus registration number UBF 614X belonging to Nile star company, as well as a Toyota Surf registration number CGO 5132AB 07 and a Tata truck registration number UBK 647C.

Preliminary Police report states that just past midnight of Wednesday 22/10/2025, the Nile Star bus traveling from Kampala to Arua tried to overtake the Tata truck while the other bus traveling from Adjumani to Kampala was also attempting to overtake the Toyota Surf vehicle from the oppostite side. The driver of the Planet bus swerved to the right lane hence concurrently having a head-on and side collision between the Nile star bus and the Planet bus, which left the drivers of the Toyota Surf vehicle and the Tata truck to lose control of there respetive vehicles, hence overturning several times, eventually falling into the valley, injuring and killing their occupants. 

All involved casualties were immediately referred to Kiryandongo general hospital, Panyadoli Health Centre IV within Kiryandongo refugee settlement and other health nearby facilities to receive emergency care; while all the dead bodies were conveyed to Kiryandongo hospital mortuary awating post-mortem examination.

In total, Uganda Red Cross ambulance was able to refer 21 casualties to Kiryandongo General hospital, while 2 additional ambulances have been deployed from Luwero and Gulu to provide back-up and support intra-facility referrals to St. Mary's Hospital, Lacor in Gulu and to Mulago National referral hospital.  

The death toll is likely to increase based on the serious nature of injuries sustained by many of the passengers.

countries.name: Kenya
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: KEN: Epidemic - 10-2025 - Cholera Outbreak in Nairobi
summary:
Nairobi County is currently experiencing a second wave of cholera this year following the confirmation of a new case in Roysambu Sub-county. The patient, a female student, was admitted and is receiving treatment at Kenyatta University Teaching, Referral and Research Hospital.

This development follows an ongoing cholera outbreak in Narok County, which has reported 115 cases and 5 deaths since the index case was identified on September 17, 2025.

Roysambu is an urban area bordering informal settlements such as Mathare and Kamukunji, which presents a heightened risk for rapid disease transmission due to high population density and limited access to adequate sanitation. There is need to intensify disease surveillance efforts in Nairobi to rapidly identify and report suspected cholera cases to prevent further spread.

Key Gaps
Limited active case search/finding
Need for enhanced Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE).
Coordination support required for immediate and effective multi-stakeholder response.

name: Philippines: Davao Oriental Earthquake, 2025
summary:
On October 10, 2025, two tectonic earthquakes struck near Manay, Davao Oriental. The first, at 9:43 AM (07.22°N, 126.97°E; depth 23 km), registered a maximum intensity of VI and was felt across Davao de Oro, Davao del Norte, Davao Occidental, Davao Oriental, Cotabato, Sarangani, South Cotabato, and Surigao del Norte. A tsunami warning was issued by DOST-PHIVOLCS, prompting forced evacuations in coastal areas after a 30 cm tsunami wave was detected at 10:20 AM, but the warning was lifted at 1:43 PM. Later that day, at 9:12 PM, a second magnitude 6.8 quake (07.07°N, 126.90°E; depth 37 km) occurred in the same area with an intensity of VI in Manay, triggering another tsunami warning for Surigao del Sur, Davao Oriental, and Surigao del Norte, which was cancelled at 11:12 PM after no significant waves were observed. As of 5:00 AM on October 11, 2025, a total of 752 aftershocks had been recorded, 311 plotted, and 14 felt, with magnitudes ranging from 1.2 to 6.8, based on data from the Mati monitoring station.

A total of 3,519 families or 8,436 persons were affected. Of which, 2,468 families or 7,915 persons were served inside 7 ECs.

33 damaged houses were reported across Region XI and CARAGA, consisting of 5 totally damaged and 28 partially damaged houses, according to NDRRMC. Meanwhile, the Philippine Red Cross (PRC) recorded 15 shelter damages, with 11 partially and 4 totally damaged, pending validation.

Based on PRC Chapter reports:

Under hospital damages, a total of six (6) facilities were affected: three in Davao Oriental—Manay District Hospital (major damage), Davao Oriental Provincial Hospital (minor cracks), and Awuyon Community Municipal Hospital (minor cracks); and three in Davao del Norte—Tagum Doctors Hospital, Tagum Global Hospital, and Rivera Medical Hospital Inc. in Panabo (all with broken glass and cracks).

Fourteen (14) schools sustained minor structural damages such as wall cracks, while one church in Davao Oriental was reported damaged. In total, 40 public structures (5 hospitals, 14 schools, 1 church, and 20 establishments) were recorded as damaged, with Davao del Norte and Davao Oriental among the most affected areas.

Since the day before yesterday, Tuesday, October 07 until today, heavy rains have caused flooding in the localities of Carnot and Sibut in the Central African Republic. Indeed, the city of Carnot (Prefecture of Mambéré) is located more than 400 from Bangui in the western part of the country. Tandisque Sibut is a locality in the Prefecture of Kemo, 188 km from Bangui to the northeast. 

The alerts of these shocks were reported to the central headquarters, in particular to the Disaster Management Department, on Wednesday, October 08, 2025.

The Central African Red Cross, which has a strong presence throughout the country, has deployed volunteers to the localities concerned to carry out the first assessments. 

It emerges that the first trends for the city of Carnot are in the order of more than three hundred households already affected by this hazard. 

Concerning the location of Sibut, evaluations are underway. 

The danger is that these floods have caused the destruction of shelters. It is also important to remember that the risk of spreading diseases should not be neglected.

summary:
Since March 2025, the Government of Djibouti has issued several official communications granting a one-month period for all individuals residing irregularly in the country to voluntarily return to their countries of origin. This measure was introduced as part of a broader effort to address national security concerns.

An estimated 150,000 or more irregular migrants currently reside in Djibouti City alone, excluding those in other regions. The government’s messaging has specifically targeted this population.

Since the beginning of May 2025, an average of approximately 600-800 individuals per day have opted for voluntary return. Additionally, between 200 and 300 people daily are being escorted by local police to the country’s borders.

The movement continues, particularly as operations have now expanded to interior regions such as Tadjourah and Arta.

These events occurred amid continuous heavy rainfall and strong gusty winds associated with a low-pressure system over northern Bangladesh and adjoining Indian states. The combined impact resulted in the destruction or damage of approximately 2,000 houses, injury to around 100 people and uprooting of thousands of trees, causing extensive damage to shelter, local infrastructure, and standing crops in multiple unions.

name: EGY: Flood - 10-2025 - Egypt: Nile River Flood
summary:
Situational Overview

Hazard and Context

The current event is characterized by a significant and prolonged increase in Nile River water levels, leading to extensive flooding in low-lying riverside areas. The government has issued early warnings to the 15 governorates considered most vulnerable to these high water levels, with the increased flow expected to persist until the end of October (1). The most severe localized impacts are reported in Menoufia Governorate, particularly in the Ashmoun district, though other areas such as Beheira and Assiut are also experiencing impacts. Official authorities have activated contingency plans to monitor water movement and have issued urgent warnings calling for the immediate evacuation of inundated residential and agricultural properties to ensure the safety of lives and assets.  

Affected Population and Impact

The most immediate humanitarian concern is the population residing in villages affected by the overflow, primarily in Delhamo and Ashmoun Center, where multiple houses have become partially or fully submerged, rendering them largely uninhabitable. Affected population reports they are unable to evacuate their homes because alternative accommodation is unavailable. The flooding severely impedes daily life and access to essential services; residents have resorted to using rudimentary means, such as small boats, for movement to work and schools. While a confirmed count of the affected population remains unavailable, initial official data indicate that approximately 1,084 feddans (acres) of land across Ashmoun, Menouf, El Sadat, and El Shohada are exposed to the risk of inundation. Furthermore, localized damage has been reported, including submerged livestock sheds in Gizey village, Menouf Center; however, there are no confirmed reports of loss of life. (2)

countries.name: Somalia
dtype.name: Complex Emergency
name: Somalia -  Complex Emergency
summary: Escalating humanitarian crisis in Puntland and Somaliland: Somalia is facing a rapidly worsening humanitarian crisis in Puntland and Somaliland, where prolonged dry conditions have affected over 2.5 million people across 26 districts including 887,000 people in severely impacted areas. Rural communities are experiencing acute shortages of water and food, compounded by significant funding cuts that have severely weakened the humanitarian response. This is not a seasonal shock, it is a systemic collapse driven by climate change, insecurity and the erosion of essential services. Years of recurrent drought, environmental degradation and collapsing essential services have left communities on the brink. The failure of the 2025 Gu rains, usually from March through April, has intensified an already dire situation. Communities now face the threat of another failed Deyr rainy season, from October through December.
