Myanmar Red Cross Society (MRCS) Response (as of 30 September 2025) and the IFRC network’s support 

Since the earthquake, MRCS has reached more than 200,000 people across 30 townships with the support from the Movement partners and external partners. More than 99,359 people have received health care, and more than 1.3 million liters of safe drinking water have been distributed. Sanitation and hygiene services have reached 170,961 people through the clean water supply, construction of latrines, distribution of water tanks and water filters, distribution of hygiene kits and cleaning materials, and hygiene awareness sessions. 

More than 157,904 people have received household items such as shelter kits, mosquito nets, and kitchen sets.  Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) reached more than 15,015 households. This is in addition to 23,424 households reached through Complementary Cash Assistance. In addition, 150 households received cash assistance for latrines. More than 126,922 people have received food and livelihood assistance, mainly mobilized locally from individuals and non-Movement partners of MRCS. 

Considering protection, gender and inclusion (PGI), more than 19,220 people have been reached with gender and age specific items such as dignity kits, infant kits, and delivery kits. 300 metric tonnes of relief and goods arrived in country from the IFRC Network, other partners, and donor governments. 

32 National Societies globally have, to date, supported MRCS in this operation (financially, with in-kind donations, or with technical support). MRCS has deployed over 698 volunteers from its network of trained and experienced volunteers countrywide.

countries.name: Costa Rica
dtype.name: Volcanic Eruption
name: CRI: Volcanic eruption - 03-2025 - Poás Volcano Activity
summary:
Context

The Poás Volcano is an active stratovolcano located in the province of Alajuela, 45 km northwest of San José, the capital of the country and is part of the Central Volcanic Mountain Range, with an approximate altitude of 2,708 meters above sea level.

Background 

Green Alert in Poás Volcano National Park

The Technical Advisory Committee (CAT), in Volcanology and Seismology, made up of OVSICORI-UNA, RSN (ICE-UCR), has been reporting in recent months an increase in the activity of the Poás volcano, particularly in the last days of February and the beginning of March, manifesting itself with eruptions and exhalations of gas very frequent until March 3.

In addition, the decrease in the level of the lake has generated a greater presence of ash and particles in the plume of gases expelled after each eruptive event, sometimes being dispersed by the wind in the surroundings of the summit and the main viewpoint.

The eventual drop in the level of the lake, the constant phreatic eruptions and the decrease in the wind speed over the top of the volcano, increases the probability of impact with volatile products (gases and ash), to the public visitation area within the Poás Volcano National Park, so the National Emergency Commission decreed Green Alert number 4 valid for the area included in the Poás Volcano National Park.

Change in the level of activity emitted by OVSICORI

The Volcanological and Seismological Observatory of Costa Rica, in a statement issued on March 7, 2025, reported that between March 1 and 3, there was an increase in the energy of the phreatic eruptions that began on March 1 at 5:47 PM with an eruption whose ash column was ejected between 300-400 m on the surface of the hyperacidic lake (the part of the plume made up of steam, gases and aerosols rose further to around 1000 m). From then until March 3, 7 eruptions of comparable magnitude were recorded. Eruptive activity continues with frequent small eruptions at Boca C (north) and sporadic larger eruptions at Boca A.

In relation to seismic and acoustic activity, 2 long-period events (LP) greater than those commonly recorded in Poás were recorded during the 18 hours prior to the eruption of March 1st. From the increase in eruptive activity on March 1, an increase in volcano-tectonic activity was recorded, both distal and proximal. A maximum of 7 distal earthquakes were reached on March 5. Most of the events are located on the southwest flank.

The amplitude of the tremor oscillated over the weekend when the largest eruptions occurred and stabilized at moderate amplitude from the 4th.

Geodetic monitoring has detected a new geological deformation in the form of vertical uplift that, this time, not only affects the immediate area of the crater, but also the rest of the GNSS stations located at the summit. This uplift is associated with a volcano extension.

The eruptions of March 1 and 2 emitted a large amount of ash that, due to its humidity, fell mainly inside the crater despite reaching greater distances in small quantities. The proportion of juvenile material in this ash decreased compared to January 5. Since this date, ash was reported in the air on March 6. In addition, the eruptions ejected large ballistic ballistics (80 cm) more than 200 m away. The largest ballistics were emitted from Mouth A (south of the crater).

Consequently, the volcano's activity level is increased from WARNING (level 2) to CAUTION (level 3 on a scale of 4).

Activity on March 25

The OVSICORI reported that the volcano maintains a continuous eruption of small but very frequent pulses. A continuous seismic tremor is observed with a frequency range between 0.6 and 11 Hz, in addition, a background acoustic tremor is observed increasing its intensity. At 07:47 am an eruption occurred which raised a column of sediment and ejected some ballistics around the bottom of the crater.

The volcano maintains a high and constant degassing of both mouth A and mouth C, where the H2S/SO2 and CO2/SO2 ratios continue to increase mainly at mouth A.

With respect to the deformation of the volcanic edifice, inflation continues.

Green Alert issued by the CNE.

Based on the evident increase in eruptive activity on March 25 reported by OVSICORI, marked by abundant gas outflow, constant presence of small and some medium explosions, as well as ash outflow.

Reports in several surrounding communities, indicating strong odors, and in some cases ash fall, are beginning to be much more frequent and constant.

In view of this, the CNE establishes the condition of Green Alert for the following cantons:

  • Alajuela
  • Poás
  • Greece
  • Sarchí
  • Orange tree
  • Río Cuarto
  • Zarcero
Green and Yellow Alert issued by the CNE.
 
The National Emergency Commission, based on the technical-scientific analysis that indicates that:
  • The seismic signal of the last 24 hours recorded is very strong, and although it has slight periods of pause, it remains at very high values. The seismic behavior of the last week is very variable, but in general there is a lot of activity.
  • Since Monday, March 24, the eruptive activity is much more intense, to date the explosions have raised columns of gases and ash, the latter still very loaded with moisture, which favors it to fall to the bottom of the same crater, but some events have managed to throw small rocks (up to 10 cm or more). to the western rim of the crater.
  • Gas fluxes remain very high, an important change in their composition, which would indicate that there is less and less moisture content in the volcanic system, favoring the emission of more toxic gases.
  • A high explosive potential, frequent pulses, stone throwing, and constant gas output are maintained.
  • This scenario compromises the safety of the operations of the Poás Volcano National Park, both for park officials and visitors.
  • Reports are maintained, in some surrounding communities, indicating strong odors, and in some cases ash fall, although they are not yet permanent or frequent.

Establish the green alert for the cantons established in green alert #5 and raise the Poás Volcano National Park sector to yellow alert.

Orange and Green Alert issued by the CNE

The OVSICORI has informed the SNGR authorities that, based on the activity of frequent eruptions that have reached columns of up to 1000 meters, the Poás volcano maintains a high explosive potential, frequent earthquakes, rock throwing and frequent gas outflow. On the other hand, the accumulation of a layer of ash of a considerable volume towards the west of the crater adjacent to the headwaters of the Desagüe and Agrio rivers has been confirmed, which generates favorable conditions for the descent of lahars in case of rainfall in the sector. This scenario compromises both officials and visitors, the safety of operations in the Volcano Four National Park and Likewise, in the basins of the previously mentioned rivers, punctual cuts are maintained in some surrounding communities, indicating colors and in some cases ash fall.

Therefore, the state of ORANGE ALERT is established for thePoás Volcano National Park and the Toro Amarillo district of the Canton of Sarchí (including the basins of the Desagüe and Agrio rivers) maintaining the green alert for the rest of the geographical areas defined in the previous alert.

countries.name: Afghanistan
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: Afghanistan: Population Movement, 2025
summary: The recent deadline imposed to expel approximately 1.5 million Afghan nationals by end of 2025 has significantly deteriorated the humanitarian landscape, primarily along the formal border crossing points in Torkham and Spin Boldak (Nangarhar and Kandahar provinces). The initially imposed deadline, which ended on March 31, 2024, has forced many families to return to Afghanistan, resulting in a considerable influx of returnees, with a spike on April 5, 2025. The situation at the Torkham and Spin Boldak borders reflects a pressing humanitarian crisis, with thousands of families returning under already challenged circumstances. The need for comprehensive support systems, including emergency health services, food security, and emergency shelter, is paramount to ensure the safety and well-being of returnees and maintain a dignified process. Immediate response interventions are required to address the needs of people crossing and to facilitate a smoother re-integration process for Afghans returning.

countries.name: Tanzania, United Republic of
dtype.name: Flood
name: TZA: Flood - 03-2025 - High rainfall and strong wind
summary:
Between March 21-24, 2025, heavy rainfall and strong winds severely impacted Musoma (Mara Region) and Ulanga (Morogoro Region), causing widespread destruction, displacement, and urgent humanitarian needs.

In Musoma, storms damaged 524 households, destroying 165 houses and leaving 65 people in temporary shelters. Critical infrastructure, including sewage systems, power, and water supply, was severely affected, with contaminated water sources increasing the risk of a cholera outbreak.

In Ulanga, 433 houses collapsed, displacing 2,165 people who are now in evacuation centers or seeking refuge with relatives. Families lost food stocks, household items, and crops, worsening food insecurity. The situation remains critical as rainfall continues, increasing the risk of further damage.

Emergency response efforts, including food distribution, shelter support, and psychosocial assistance, are ongoing. However, urgent humanitarian support is needed, including food, shelter, water treatment supplies, and healthcare services, to assist affected communities.

countries.name: Nigeria
dtype.name: Other
name: NGA: Other - 03-2025 - Communal Clash
summary:
The communal crisis between Ilobu, Ifon-Osun, and Erin-Osun in Irepodun and Orolu Local government areas of Osun State, is an agelong one that started over 100 years ago on the land and boundary disagreement reoccurred on the 19th March 2025 which resulted in significant humanitarian needs. The Nigerian Red Cross Society has supported the Government through the State Emergency Management Agency to respond to the crisis. In the recent crisis which started on 19 March 2025 several homes and businesses set ablaze, forcing many women and children to flee.

According to the assessment by the Nigerian Red Cross, there are:

1. Damage and Destruction: Widespread destruction of homes, businesses, and infrastructure was observed. Specifically, over 700 houses were burnt in the three towns during the incidents, resulting in significant loss of property and livelihoods Over 83 shops, 3 mosques, 5 Schools, and 4 churches were also burnt, exacerbating the humanitarian crisis.

2. Businesses Affected: Thousands of businesses, including small-scale enterprises and market stalls, were affected, leading to loss of income and livelihoods for many individuals and families.

3. Displacement: Over 5000 individuals and families were displaced, with some taking refuge in the IDP camps set up by the State Government and closed state.

4. Injuries and Fatalities: Reports of deaths, degrees of injuries, and fatalities were confirmed, with some individuals already receiving medical attention.

countries.name: Kenya
dtype.name: Flood
name: KEN: Flood - 03-2025 - Kenya floods
summary: The MAM long rains began in March and peaked in mid-April 2025. Rainfall is expected to continue, with isolated heavy downpours in Nairobi, the Central Highlands, Lake Victoria Basin, and parts of the Rift Valley. Water levels in the Tana River Basin may exceed alert thresholds from 24th April, increasing flood risk. Fourteen counties have reported impacts, with Homa Bay, Marsabit, Turkana, Tana River, Isiolo, and West Pokot most affected. Damage to roads and bridges has disrupted access to critical services and livelihoods. Most of the affected areas lack adequate insurance coverage for assets, and the National Society is currently assessing how best to support the most vulnerable families impacted by the disaster.

countries.name: Congo
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: Congo Population Movement 2025
summary:
Two ethnic groups, the Nounous and the Tekés, living in the DRC Mai-Ndombe province, have been ghting over land for years. On
Sunday 09 February 2025, a Nounou traditional chief was assassinated by the Tekés, triggering a conict that led to killings and forced the
population to move to Congo-Brazzaville. These people have taken refuge in the districts and villages of Ngabé, Mpouya, Gamboma,
Bouémba, Mossaka and Makotimpoko, which are in the North Pool department, a basin and plateau bordering the DRC.
On February 11, 2025, there were 8,779 displaced persons from the DRC, and as of February 14, 2025, the number of displaced persons
had risen to 18,296, according to the Ministry of Social Aairs. On this same date, the Ministry of Social Aairs, Solidarity and
Humanitarian Action of the Republic of Congo requested the support of the Congolese government's partners, to respond to the massive
population movements in the DRC.
A total of 3,049 households were received by the Congolese government and accommodated in reception centers, schools, churches,
some with host families.

summary:
Derivado de la inconformidad de la publicación de acuerdos gubernamentivos que establecen la obligatoriedad del seguro para el transporte colectivo, de carga, de motocicletas y vehículos particulares, la población, a nivel nacional rechaza las disposiciones del Gobierno Ejecutivo por lo que, a nivel nacional se registran desde hoy protestas en la ciudad de Guatemala y en diversas carreteras principales que conectan a todo el país.

Diversos grupos sociales han convocado al paro nacional el 19 de marzo, por lo que se prevé que las protestas continúen en los próximos días.

The fire completely destroyed 45 houses and 13 rice bans leaving 333 people homeless. The affected families have lost their shelter food supply and essential belongs, increasing their vulnerabilities. The cause of the fire remains unknown and the National Disaster Management Agency and sierra leone red cross society are assessing the situation to determine the level of impact.

countries.name: Kyrgyzstan
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: KGZ: Epidemic - 03-2025 - Measles outbreak
summary: With 4169 suspected cases, including 3,739 measles cases, the healthcare system is likely experiencing significant strain. Hospitals, clinics, and health professionals are overwhelmed with the high number of patients, leading to longer waiting times, limited resources, and increased workload for medical staff. Intensive care units and pediatric wards are under pressure due to the severity of measles cases, particularly with the two recorded deaths.The need for more diagnostic services has increased, as 540 cases were laboratory-confirmed. This likely puts pressure on testing facilities, requiring faster turnaround times for results to guide treatment and containment efforts.Given that measles is a preventable disease, a shortage or delay in vaccine availability could exacerbate the situation. The need for large-scale vaccination campaigns is critical to prevent further spread, but logistical challenges, such as reaching rural or remote areas (e.g., Naryn, Talas, and Batken provinces), complicate immunization efforts. There may also be a backlog in vaccination schedules or programs, as health facilities divert resources toward handling the current outbreak. The government and international organizations may need to allocate additional funding to support response. Other routine healthcare services such as maternal and child health, chronic disease management, and non-urgent medical procedures may be delayed or diverted to manage the outbreak, leading to disruptions in regular healthcare delivery. Potential Spread to Vulnerable Populations: The spread of measles, particularly in densely populated areas like Bishkek (2,098 cases), could disproportionately affect vulnerable populations such as children, the elderly, and those with weakened immune systems. Public health services may be strained by the dual burden of controlling the outbreak while maintaining regular healthcare services for these groups. Economic Impact: Health-related costs such as medical treatments, vaccines, and hospitalization will create economic burdens on families, communities, and the national health system. For affected families, particularly in rural areas, the financial impact can also extend to lost wages and costs for transportation to treatment centers. The outbreak could lead to stigma and fear surrounding measles cases, especially if the deaths of children increase public concern. Schools and other community spaces may close or implement restrictions to limit exposure, leading to social disruptions and a potential loss of educational opportunities for children. Families affected by measles could experience emotional distress, particularly those who lost children to the disease. Primary Effects on the Affected Population: Health Complications: Measles can cause severe complications, including pneumonia, encephalitis, and even death, especially in children and unvaccinated individuals. The vulnerable population, including those who are malnourished or immunocompromised, is at a heightened risk of severe outcomes. In remote or rural regions (e.g., Naryn, Talas, Batken provinces), access to healthcare services may be limited, either due to geographic barriers or the overwhelming demand on local healthcare infrastructure. These areas may face difficulties in receiving timely medical attention, diagnostic services, or vaccinations.

summary:
According to the Ministry of Emergency Situations, an earthquake with a magnitude of 5 MSK-64 occurred on March 12 at 09:11 a.m. The epicenter was located 3 km north of Osh city. The intensity of the tremors reached 5 points in Osh city, as well as in the villages of Tashtak, Nariman, and Kyrgyz-Chek, and 4 points in Kara-Suu city.

Following an assessment by the Ministry of Emergency Situations, it was determined that 12 schools, 1 kindergarten, 1 FMC, 12 houses, and 26 other buildings were affected

The RCSK is monitoring the situation and is ready to provide assistance if requested.

countries.name: Benin
dtype.name: Other
name: BEN: Other - 03-2025 - STRONG WIND
summary:
On the night of Monday, March 10 to Tuesday, March 11, 2025, a violent thunderstorm accompanied by strong gusts of wind and precipitation hit the commune of Zogbodomey, causing significant material damage and affecting many families.  

The powerful winds caused the collapse or partial destruction of several homes in the districts of Akiza, Kpokissa and Tanwe-Hessou, leaving more than 800 people homeless. Among the victims are pregnant women, people with disabilities, children, as well as infants under five years old, thus increasing the vulnerability of the affected populations.  

In addition to private homes, significant damage was also caused to public infrastructure. The police station of the district of Kpokissa saw its roof torn off by the force of the wind, compromising the proper functioning of the security services in the area.  

Faced with this situation, the day after the disaster, Tuesday 11 March, volunteers from the Local Committee of the Red Cross mobilised on the ground to accurately assess the extent of the damage. Through reconnaissance visits and surveys of affected populations, they are working to collect detailed data on the losses and urgent needs of victims in order to guide relief and humanitarian assistance actions.

countries.name: Malaysia
dtype.name: Flood
name: Malaysia Flood March 2025
summary:
As of 8:00 PM on 10 March 2025, the flood situation in Sabah has worsened, with 4,555 individuals from 1,493 families seeking refuge in relief centres. The affected districts include Tenom, Beaufort, Membakut, and Sook.

In Tenom, eight relief centres are sheltering 1,162 people from 435 families, while Beaufort has four operational centres housing 1,719 individuals from 556 families. Membakut's two centres are accommodating 896 people from 302 families, and Sook’s two centres are providing refuge for 778 evacuees from 200 families.

A total of 37 villages across these districts have been impacted, including 10 villages each in Beaufort, Membakut, and Tenom, five in Sook, and two in Keningau. Infrastructure has been severely affected, with heavy rainfall leading to road closures in Beaufort, Tenom, and Keningau. Notably, the Keningau-Kimanis road remains closed due to two landslides.

In response to the escalating situation, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) to strengthen coordination between federal and state agencies to ensure that effective assistance reaches those affected.

The situation remains fluid, with authorities closely monitoring weather conditions and providing essential aid to the affected communities.

countries.name: Mongolia
dtype.name: Fire
name: MNG: Fire - 03-2025 - Wild Fire
summary: A wildfire started on 9 March 2025 in the eastern region of Mongolia, affecting Dornod, Khentii, and Sukhbaatar provinces. The fire continues to spread across the region, impacting 11 locations. Response efforts are being led by the local emergency management agency. As of 10 March 2025, a total of 66 households have been affected, with homes, animals, animal shelters, and other assets damaged or destroyed. A local emergency has been declared, lasting until June 2025, with the local emergency operation center in Dornod province (that has been affected the most) province activated to contain the fire and support the affected population. As a member of the State emergency commission, the National Society's local branches are working closely with authorities and communities to assess the needs and losses of those affected.

countries.name: Guatemala
dtype.name: Volcanic Eruption
name: GTM: Volcanic eruption - 03-2025 - Fuego volcano eruptive activity, Guatemala
summary:
The Fuego volcano in Guatemala has been erupting since Sunday, March 9. According to the Special Volcanological Bulletin BEFGO 006-2025 issued by the National Institute of Seismology, Volcanology, Meteorology and Hydrology - Insivumeh, the decrease in pyroclastic flows of weak and moderate characteristics is recorded in the Seca and Ceniza canyons. which generates ash fall in surrounding areas.

Currently, the volcano generates pyroclastic flows that run along the slopes of Las Lajas and Jute, in a SW direction. Meanwhile, the volcanic ash fall is moving in a northwesterly direction.

As a preventive measure in the face of the increase in fire activity, National Route 14 that connects Escuintla with Sacatepéquez and Chimaltenango remains closed.

It is estimated that some 125 families are sheltered in prevention due to the possible continuity of volcanic activity.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Flood
name: ARG: Flood - 03-2025 - Bahia Blanca
summary:
The city of Bahía Blanca is facing a serious hydrometeorological event, characterized by extraordinary rainfall that reached 200 mm in just four hours during the early morning of Friday, March 7, 2025. This figure represents about one-third of the city's annual historical average, which is 629 mm. In response to this situation, the National Meteorological Service has raised the alert from Orange to Red, predicting that the rains will continue, with a possible additional accumulation of between 50 and 100 mm in the short term. The event is ongoing so the local system is carrying out rescue and evacuation processes. Access to the city is mostly limited, cut off or with restricted access. 

In the face of this emergency, the municipal authorities have declared an absolute cessation of activities of all kinds until further notice. The measures include the suspension of public transport, the cancellation of classes and the closure of the airport. In addition, Penna hospital has been evacuated to ensure the safety of patients and staff.

Several evacuation centers have been set up to attend to the affected families. At the moment, 40 people are reported evacuated, and it is anticipated that this number could increase in the coming hours. In Villa Caracol, the Natan Center is functioning as a shelter. In General Daniel Cerri, the Sansinena Club has been designated as an evacuation center. The Division of the V Army Corps is receiving evacuees, and in the Güemes neighborhood an evacuation center has been established on Belén Street.

countries.name: Democratic Republic of Congo
countries.society_name: Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
dtype.name: Flood
name: COD: Flood - 03-2025 - Floods in Maniema in Kailo territory
summary:
On Friday night of March 07, 2025, the villages on the banks of the Congo River in the  health areas of Elila, Lokando, Pembeliba, Lubao1, Lubao2, Mingazi mbili in Kailo territory were surprised by a torrential rain accompanied by a strong  wind that caused very significant human and material damage. It should be noted that in recent years, the province of Maniema has observed unusually enormous atmospheric disturbances (flooding, heavy and torrential rains, strong winds, etc.) which are destabilizing communities. These phenomena, which are not yet under control by the population and the authorities, cause so much enormous damage. According to experts, these phenomena are effects of climate disruption.

Among these damages, the following were the removal of roofs or frameworks, the collapse or collapse of the walls of family homes and public buildings (schools, health centres, churches, etc.), the loss of food stocks for families, etc.

Many latrines and wells were flooded in all these areas, raising fears of waterborne diseases.

Among the victims of this crisis are children, people with disabilities, the elderly, the chronically ill, pregnant women, single mothers, etc.

countries.name: Cameroon
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: CMR: Cholera EAP
summary:
Cameroon faces recurrent cholera outbreaks, exacerbated by seasonal floods, inadequate WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) infrastructure, and rapid urbanization. Historical outbreaks, such as the 2021–2022 epidemic, which recorded 6,652 suspected cases and 132 deaths, highlight
vulnerabilities in high-risk regions like Littoral, Southwest, and Center. Climate change and population displacement further amplify the risks, making early intervention crucial. The Early Action Protocol (EAP) was developed collaboratively through multi-stakeholder workshops in 2024, involving the Cameroon Red Cross (CRC), the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Water and Environment, WHO, UNICEF, MSF, and other key partners. A comprehensive risk analysis was conducted to prioritize districts based on historical cholera incidence, vulnerability indices, and climatic factors, ensuring a targeted and effective response. The protocol aims to support 2,500 households—approximately 13,500 people—living in 56 high-risk districts identified as cholera “hotspots.” These areas are characterized by poor access to WASH services, overcrowding, and high exposure to floods, making them particularly susceptible to outbreaks.

countries.name: Somalia
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: SOM: Epidemic - 03-2025 - Leishmaniasis Outbreak
summary:
Since January 3, 2025, Erigavo Regional Hospital in the Sanaag region has reported five cases of leishmaniasis, a disease not historically
prevalent in those areas of Somaliland. Among these cases, four tested positive for Leishmania IgG through Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDTs),
raising concerns about the potential emergence of a localized outbreak. Subsequent laboratory analysis confirmed two fatalities from
Rugay and Cirshiida in Erigavo district, highlighting the severity of the situation. The most recent case (01) was officially confirmed on
February 26, 2025, as a kalzar type, further underscoring the ongoing transmission risk.
Despite these hospital-reported cases, the extent of leishmaniasis (Visceral Leishmaniasis—Kala-Azar) within the broader community
remains uncertain due to limited surveillance data. The lack of comprehensive epidemiological insights poses challenges in assessing
transmission dynamics and potential risk factors, necessitating an urgent and coordinated response.
On March 2, 2025, in response to the worsening situation, the Ministry of Health Development (MoHD) has formally issued a request
letter to urgently inform the partners of the critical public health concerns regarding the recent outbreak of Leishmaniasis in the Sanaag
region, triggering an appeal to humanitarian partners for urgent intervention. This request serves as an official call for support, urging
international and local organizations to assist in disease control, medical treatment, and prevention efforts. The trigger date, marked by
the release of this request letter, signifies the government's acknowledgment of the crisis and its need for external aid to combat the
outbreak effectively

countries.name: Honduras

name: AUS: Cyclone - 03-2025 - TC Alfred - NSW/QLD
summary: Ex-Tropical Cyclone Alfred reached Queensland Moreton Bay islands in the early hours of Saturday 08 March. The cyclone impact is estimated to be a 300km (190-mile) stretch of coastline from Maroochydore on the Sunshine Coast to Byron Bay in New South Wales. Flood and severe weather warnings are in place with evacuation orders issued, stretching over dozens of communities in south-eastern Queensland and northern New South Wales. Storm surges have already caused significant damage to parts of the east coast, with the cyclone producing winds in excess of 100 kilometres an hour. Authorities remain concerned about the impact of flooding and thunderstorms, which could bring more damaging wind and heavy rain. At the time of reporting more than 42,000 homes and businesses in New South Wales are without power and 290,000 without power in Queensland. Schools are closed in both states, with road, public transport and airport closures also impacting affected communities and emergency services response. Nine evacuation centres are open across southeast Queensland and 19 across northern New South Wales.

Mogoditshane, and Kgatleng districts. Rainfall peaked at 235mm in Kokotsha (Kgalagadi) and 160mm in Mogoditshane, with over 50mm

contaminated water and sanitation.
Based on Assessment conducted from 21-24 by the NS as of February 21, 2025, many people were affected, including children, pregnant
women, the elderly, and migrants, especially the ones leaving in low lying areas across 14 districts. The floods conducted to the

opened on 4th March 2025 as the situation was worse, with the exception of Linchwe II Junior Secondary School only opens on 17th

residents into evacuation centers. 2,318 people were evacuated and other thousands displaced as at 26 February 2025.
As at 02.03. 2025, 402 persons are still in evacuation centre and the rest released to return home. Several major roads were closed,

countries.name: Timor-Leste
dtype.name: Flood
name: Timor Leste: Flood sEAP, 2025
summary:
The frequent occurrence of extreme weather and climate events poses a great threat to community and national level development in Timor-Leste as their impacts cause catastrophic loss and damage. Timor-Leste is prone to natural hazards such as floods, landslides, drought, cyclones and earthquakes. Of these hazards, the most common is flood, followed by drought and storms . With its shoreline of more than 700 km, nearly 65 percent of the population resides in low-lying areas. Most rural communities reside along the coastline, survive on basic incomes, and rely on farming and fishing
. The result of the Household and Building Damages Assessment (HBDA) survey conducted in the five most affected municipalities following the 2021 Tropical Cyclone Seroja showed that nearly 75 percent of the households reported being vulnerable to floods, followed by cyclones (32 per cent) and landslides (29 per cent). 
 
From 2013-20236 catastrophic floods have been a major hazard affecting Timor-Leste. According to Timor-Leste Civil Protection Authority (CPA), over the last ten years (Baze de Dadus Dezastre Timor-Leste), floods have affected 29,696 households with 6,797 houses destroyed, causing 28 human
casualties and 9 people missing across the country. The six most impacted municipalities over the last years are Dili, Covalima, Manatuto, Viqueque, Manufahi and Oecusse. The disastrous floods associated with landslides and strong winds caused by the 2021 Tropical Cyclone Seroja affected nearly 31,500 households or approximately 179,000 individuals and with reported loss of 44 lives throughout the country7. The total damage caused by the
catastrophic event was estimated at nearly US$308 million.

countries.name: Indonesia
dtype.name: Flood
name: Indonesia: Flood EAP, 2025
summary:
The IFRC Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) has approved a total of CHF 517,485 for the implementationof the Indonesian Red Cross (Palang Merah Indonesia) Floods EAP. The approved amount consists of an allocation of CHF 316,873 for readiness and prepositioning and CHF 200,612 allocated to implement early actions once the defined triggers are met. 
 
Allocations are made from the Anticipatory Pillar of the DREF, under the DREF appeal code MDRID027. Unearmarked contributions to DREF are encouraged to guarantee that sufficient funding is available for the Early Action Protocols being developed.

Floods are a recurrent and escalating disaster in Indonesia, with over 2,500 flood events recorded between 2007 and 2021, affecting millions of people annually and causing extensive damage to infrastructure.
 
The Indonesian Red Cross has developed the Early Action Protocol (EAP) as a guide for implementing anticipatory actions to reduce the impacts of floods based on complex analysis of flood risks with a 5-year return period across the country. The development of this EAP and its implementation involve coordination with national and sub-national government agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB), the Indonesian
Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), Local Disaster Management Agencies (BPBD) and The Indonesian Red Cross Community-based Disaster Preparedness volunteers (SIBAT), to ensure readiness for and timely activation of pre-agreed early actions when defined trigger thresholds are reached.
 
Utilizing available weather forecasts, particularly those with an 80 per cent probability of heavy rainfall, the EAP informs targeted early actions triggered at 6 days and at 72 hours before anticipated floods occur in line with existing local capacities.
 
The EAP is targeting 2,500 households / 10,000 people and aims to reduce and mitigate the Loss of Life/Injuries: through dissemination of early warning, evacuation planning, first aid, and community feedback mechanisms; Livelihood Damage: by providing unconditional cash grants to support affected households; Water Contamination: by promoting household-level water management and hygiene; Disease Outbreaks: through health promotions.

countries.name: Ecuador
dtype.name: Flood
name: ECU: 2025 Floods and environmental pollution
summary:
Since January 2025, Ecuador has been experiencing an increasingly complex emergency situation resulting from the convergence of two large-scale crises: a prolonged rainy season with intense floods and landslides, and a major environmental emergency caused by an oil spill in the coastal province of Esmeraldas. According to the Secretariat for Risk Management (SitRep No. 70, 20 March 2025), 1,897 adverse events had been recorded by mid-March, with widespread impact across 23 provinces, 193 cantons, and 651 parishes.

The provinces of Manabí, Guayas, El Oro, Los Ríos, and Esmeraldas have been particularly affected. Manabí has registered over 62,950 people impacted and 226 separate events, followed by Guayas with 18,334 people affected, and Los Ríos with 16,289. These impacts include destroyed homes, flooded communities, damaged roads and bridges, disrupted water systems, and affected livelihoods (SitRep No. 70, 20 March 2025). In total, more than 111,000 people are reported as affected, with 14,155 people displaced and more than 31,521 houses damaged or destroyed. These figures are expected to rise.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAG) reported the loss of over 13,700 hectares of crops and more than 96,000 animals affected or dead. Manabí, Guayas, El Oro and Los Ríos—regions highly dependent on small-scale farming—have seen significant damage to plantations of cacao, bananas, passion fruit, and oil palm. These losses are affecting subsistence agriculture and local economies, further aggravating the vulnerability of already at-risk communities (SitRep SNGR, 20 March 2025).

Health conditions have also been deteriorating. As of mid-March, the Ministry of Health had confirmed over 9,566 cases of dengue across the country. Damage to water systems, poor drainage, and the accumulation of stagnant water have contributed to the proliferation of disease vectors. In addition to physical health risks, there are growing concerns over mental health and psychosocial wellbeing, particularly among displaced and isolated populations (SitRep SNGR, 14 March 2025).

On 13 March 2025, a major oil spill occurred in Cube Parish, Quinindé Canton, Esmeraldas Province, due to a rupture in the Trans-Ecuadorian Oil Pipeline System (SOTE) caused by a landslide (SitRep SN Esmeraldas No. 1 to 4, March 2025). The spill reached the Caple, Viche, and Esmeraldas rivers—primary sources of drinking water and irrigation—contaminating ecosystems and leaving approximately 300,000 people at risk of unsafe water consumption (France 24, 15 March 2025; Phys.org, 18 March 2025). Official estimates indicate that approximately 300,000 people are at risk due to disrupted access to potable water caused by the contamination of primary river sources.

Governmental reports and international media confirm the severe impact of the oil spill on community livelihoods. Over 8,700 people have been directly affected by the loss of water access, soil contamination, and the destruction of farming plots used for cacao and oil palm cultivation. Affected communities include Cube, El Vergel, El Roto, San Mateo, and Chinca, among others. In some sectors, households have been forced to rely on unsafe tanker water, with reports of cross-contamination with fuel.

The oil spill also caused serious ecological harm to the Esmeraldas River Estuary Mangrove Wildlife Refuge and surrounding natural reserves. Cleanup efforts have been delayed by poor road access, continued rains, and lack of technical capacity on-site. With 95% of the potable water service affected in the immediate region, community tensions have increased, and response actors have highlighted growing protection risks (Mongabay, 20 March 2025).

Meanwhile, meteorological authorities (INAMHI) forecast 45 to 60 additional days of high-intensity rainfall as of mid-March, likely exacerbating the flood crisis and delaying recovery efforts (INAMHI Bulletin, 16 March 2025).

countries.name: Benin
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: BEN: Population Movement - 02-2025 - Benin Population movement
summary:
A month after the triple point attack in the commune of Banikoara, and following the threats reported a few days ago, the Non-State Armed Groups (NSAGs) reportedly murdered two people in the village of Tchafarga in the commune of Tanguiéta, on the night of February 6 to 7, 2025 and demanded that the population leave the village. As a result, population movements were observed between 7 and 9 February 2025, with residents of Tchafarga, Sangou and Batia heading towards Tanguiéta centre to find refuge and ensure their safety. These villages are located near the Pendjari Park.  

During the month of December 2024, UNICEF requested the support of the Beninese Red Cross for the installation of four tents to serve as classrooms at the Kara public primary school, in the Birni-Lafia district, Karimama commune. However, during the mission, the team deployed by the CRB was only able to set up one tent due to a lack of equipment.   On the night of February 8 to 9, 2025, this tent branded with UNICEF branding was unfortunately destroyed by armed groups. 

This Tuesday, February 11, 2024 at around 6 p.m., Fulani herdsmen were intercepted by Non-State Armed Groups (NSAGs) in Nanimbou, 5 km from Tanguiéta. Part of their herd was seized. This incident caused an influx of Peuhl to the city, transported on tractor trailers, joining internally displaced persons (IDPs) who had left Tchafarga and Sangou. This situation confirms the presence of these armed men on the outskirts of Tanguiéta.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: ZWE: Epidemic - 02-2025 - Malaria outbreak
summary: The malaria outbreak has resulted in increased morbidity and mortality, with 85 confirmed deaths reported as of 26 April 2025. The surge in malaria cases has placed additional pressure on healthcare facilities, particularly in rural areas where resources are limited. Clinics and hospitals have faced increased patient loads, leading to potential shortages in medical supplies and staff fatigue. The focus on managing the malaria outbreak has diverted attention and resources from other essential health services, such as maternal and child health programs, immunizations, and management of chronic diseases. Other secondary effects include absenteeism from work among adults and from school among children, affecting their academic performance and long-term educational outcomes. The outbreak has also caused anxiety and stress among community members, particularly in areas with high infection rates. Fear of contracting the disease and concerns about the availability of treatment have impacted mental well-being. The province is also facing a cholera outbreak, which started on the 4th of November 2024 in Kariba district.

dtype.name: Flood
name: TZA: Flood - 02-2025 - Mtwara Floods In Tanzania
summary:
Background

Heavy rains have caused severe flooding across Mtwara Region, leading to widespread destruction and displacement. The floods have significantly impacted infrastructure, homes, and livelihoods, leaving many families in urgent need of assistance.

Impact and Humanitarian Needs

  • Housing Damage:
    • 195 houses have completely collapsed.
    • 746 houses have been fully submerged in floodwaters.
  • Displacement: Hundreds of families have been forced to evacuate, seeking shelter in temporary camps or with relatives.
  • Infrastructure Damage: Roads and bridges have been damaged, limiting access to affected communities and making relief efforts challenging.
  • Health Risks: The risk of waterborne diseases such as cholera and malaria has increased due to stagnant water and lack of sanitation.
  • Livelihood Disruption: Flooded farmlands threaten food security, impacting both subsistence farmers and market supply chains.
  • Immediate Needs: Urgent humanitarian assistance is required, including emergency shelter, food, clean water, and medical support.

Response Efforts

  • Tanzania Red Cross Society (TRCS) and local authorities are working to provide relief assistance to displaced families.
  • Emergency shelters are being set up for those who have lost their homes.
  • Health and hygiene promotion efforts are being intensified to prevent disease outbreaks.
  • WASH interventions are being prioritized, including distribution of water purification tablets and hygiene kits.

Next Steps

  • Ongoing assessments to determine additional needs and long-term recovery plans.
  • Expansion of cash assistance programs to help affected households rebuild their lives.
  • Coordination with humanitarian partners to ensure a sustainable response and disaster preparedness measures.

summary:
Since 21 June, prolonged and heavy rainfall in Huu Lung District, Lang Son Province has led to rising water levels in the Trung and Thuong Rivers and local streams, resulting in flooding and landslides across the district.

countries.name: Panama
dtype.name: Biological Emergency
name: PAN: Biological Emergency - 02-2025 - Oropouche Outbreak
summary:
The National Department of Epidemiology of the Ministry of Health (Minsa), this Tuesday, January 28, an outbreak of oropouche fever after the analysis of samples collected at the health center of Metetí, in the province of Darién, confirmed 34 cases.

The authorities of the Ministry of Health, through Resolution 0098 of January 31, 2025, orders the Regional Health Directorate of Darién to coordinate the actions that are necessary to monitor, contain and implement the preparations for the response to the Oropouche outbreak.

Oropouche fever has resurfaced in Panama after more than 30 years since it was last detected. In November 2024, the first case was detected in a 31-year-old man. Although it was not considered a cause for alarm, authorities and health experts warned about the risks associated with the virus, especially in pregnant women, as it could be linked to fetal death and the development of congenital anomalies.

Oropouche fever is a febrile infection caused by the bite of Culicoides and Culex mosquitoes (known as "gnats").

The head of Epidemiology of the Minsa, Blas Armién, explained that of a total of 58 samples evaluated by a research team from the Gorgas Memorial Institute of Health Studies through polymerase chain reaction tests, 34 cases were positive.

He added that the temporal distribution of cases corresponds to December 2024 to January 15, 2025. The detection of positive cases suggests that the outbreak of oropouche continues actively in the affected area.

The age group between 40 and 49 years old is the most affected with an attack rate of 87.5%.

countries.name: Greece

name: GRC: Earthquake - 02-2025 - Ιntense earthquake activity
summary:
Intense seismic activity has been observed in recent days in the Cyclades, specifically in the sea area of Anydros, between Thira and Amorgos, which has concerned residents and the country's government.
More than 200 earthquakes (with a maximum magnitude of 4.5) have been recorded in the last few days in the area of Anudros, between Thera and Amorgos. The seismic sequence has continued to increase over the last 48 hours. The current seismic activity on the island of Andros is due to submarine faults in an NE-SW direction and is unrelated to volcanic activity.
The Greek government has taken precautionary measures for the safety of citizens on the islands of Santorini, Amorgos, Anafi, and Ios.
The Committees recommend avoiding gatherings in enclosed areas, avoiding approaching abandoned buildings, avoiding access to ports: Ammoudiou, Armeni, Korfu, Old Port of Fira, to proceed to the removal of dangerous elements of non-structural vulnerability in their buildings and the emptying of water in swimming pools (swimming pools), to choose safe routes when moving through the urban fabric and the provincial road network, particularly in areas with steep slopes where landslides are likely to occur and where there is a direct route away from coastal areas in the event of strong earthquakes.
Still on the island of Santorini, a team of the 1st EMAK with a rescue dog and two teams of the 1st Special Forestry Operations Unit, as well as a team of drone operators and aerial rescuers, have gone to the island of Santorini as a precautionary measure.
Also, schools in Thira, Anafi, Ios, Paros, and Amorgos will remain closed until Friday, 07/02/2025.
A message via 112 was sent to the residents of Santorini, warning them of the risk of landslides due to earthquake activity and noting that access to the areas of Ammoudi, Armenia, and the Old Port of Fira in Thira is prohibited.
For now, the largest earthquake recorded is 4.6 magnitude between Santorini and Amorgos. 
Historically, the island of Santorini has been hit by a 7.5 magnitude earthquake in 1956. 
It was 9 July 1956, at 5:11 am, when the devastating earthquake struck. The epicenter was south of the island of Amorgos (the easternmost island of the Cyclades) in the Aegean Sea. 
The 7.5 on the Richter scale left 53 people dead and over 100 injured, causing the volcano of Thera to erupt, which almost flattened Santorini and caused a massive tidal wave - a tsunami. 
Still, it has been listed as the biggest earthquake of the 20th century across Europe, from the Urals to Gibraltar and from Malta to Lapland. 
The work on the main earthquake was completed by the devastating aftershock 13 minutes after magnitude 7.2.

countries.name: Georgia

name: GEO: Other - 02-2025 - Snow Storm in Georgia
summary:
Since February 21, 2025, western Georgia has been struggling with a severe winter storm, causing widespread damage and humanitarian challenges. The most critical impact was recorded on March 1, but as of today, March 7, the disaster is still ongoing, with heavy snow and extreme weather conditions continuing to affect Guria, Adjara, Imereti, and Mtskheta-Mtianeti. Many villages remain isolated, thousands of people are still without electricity, and emergency responders are facing serious challenges in reaching those in need.

In Guria, snowdrifts continue to block roads, leaving villages like Chokhatauri, Gogole District, and Ozurgeti cut off from essential supplies. Residents of Buknari, Kvenobani, and Basileti remain stranded, while people in Jumati, Konchati, and Kokati face food shortages and worsening conditions. With ongoing snowfall, there is still no clear timeframe for when access to these areas will be restored.

In Imereti, around 30,000 people are still without electricity, and 149 villages remain inaccessible. Schools remain closed, and relief efforts are slowed down by the extreme weather. In Adjara, conditions have not improved, as Batumi continues to face power outages and mobility restrictions due to icy roads. In Khulo, Shuakhevi, and Keda, nearly 20 villages remain surrounded by snow, and some homes are still buried. Reports indicate a serious lack of food, medical supplies, and heating, while avalanche risks remain high.

The death toll stands at three, with recent reports confirming that people have died from collapsed roofs and exposure to freezing temperatures. Emergency responders and military personnel are still working to clear roads and evacuate people from the hardest-hit areas, but the ongoing snowfall makes their work extremely difficult.

The Georgia Red Cross Society (GRCS) has been active on the ground, providing food, hygiene supplies, and psychological support. However, as the disaster enters its third week, humanitarian needs are growing, and additional aid is urgently required. If conditions do not improve soon, the crisis could escalate further, leaving thousands in life-threatening situations. The priority remains ensuring food, heating, and medical assistance reach the most vulnerable before the situation deteriorates further.

summary:
On 29 January 2025 a severe weather event caused by two tropical lows resulted in record breaking flood conditions impacting much of North and Far North Queensland. Severe weather warnings stretched from the Gulf Country, across the tropical coast and into the Burdekin Region.

The flooding resulted in evacuations of people with impacts to homes, small business, and to communities at large. Some communities were isolated as a result of flood waters with some areas relying on supply drops from helicopters and planes. Power networks and the road transport system were heavily affected. 

All levels of government, including local, state and the Commonwealth are providing support to the response, early relief and recovery required for this event.

Australian Defence Force personnel deployed in addition to members of emergency services from other states and territories.

Key financial assistance measures announced by the government, include the Australian Government Disaster Relief Allowance and the Australian Government Disaster Relief Payment. There are also a range of other payments available through the state of Queensland.. 5,690 insurance claims have been lodged as at 16/02/2025.

countries.name: Uganda

name: UGA: Epidemic - 01-2025 - Ebola Virus Outbreak
summary:
On 30 January 2025, the Ministry of Health declared an outbreak of Sudan Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Kampala District. This declaration followed confirmation from three national laboratories: the Central Public Health Laboratories, the Uganda Virus Research Institute, and Makerere University Laboratories.


The index case was a 32-year-old male nurse employed at Mulago National Referral Hospital. He initially presented fever-like symptoms and sought treatment from multiple health facilities, including Mulago National Referral Hospital in Kampala, Saidina Abubakar Islamic Hospital in Matunga, Wakiso District, and Mbale Regional Referral Hospital, as well as from a traditional healer.


The patient had a five-day history of high fever, chest pain, and difficulty breathing, which later progressed to unexplained bleeding from multiple body sites. Despite medical intervention, the patient experienced multiple organ failure and subsequently succumbed to the illness at Mulago National Referral Hospital. Following the confirmation of this index case, the Ministry of Health activated the Incident Management Team and dispatched Rapid Response Teams to Mbale City and Saidina Abubakar Islamic Hospital in Matugga to list all of the contacts and isolate them. Since the identification of the index case on 30 January 2025, ongoing investigations and contact tracing have led to a steady increase in the number of contacts, reaching 265 as of 10 February 2025, across the districts of Kampala, Wakiso, Jinja, Mbale, and other areas. Of the listed contacts, 62 per cent are health workers who have been quarantined at the National Isolation Centre in Mulago. As of 10 February 2025, there were nine confirmed cases, including the index case.

countries.name: Malaysia

name: MYS: Flood - 01-2025 - East Malaysia Monsoon Flood
summary:
Severe monsoon floods continue to devastate Sabah and Sarawak, displacing thousands and causing widespread disruption. Since 28 January 2025, continuous heavy rainfall, compounded by high tides and the Northeast Monsoon, has led to rising water levels, road inundations, and landslides. In Sarawak, the situation worsened due to the collision of extreme monsoon rains with high tides, triggering large-scale evacuations and the activation of multiple relief centers.

As of 31 January 2025, 12,486 evacuees from 3,648 families have been relocated to 62 temporary relief centers (PPS) in Sarawak. Bintulu remains the most severely impacted district, sheltering 5,885 evacuees from 1,649 families, followed by Serian (2,307 evacuees, 709 families) and Samarahan (2,005 evacuees, 670 families). Other significantly affected districts include Sibu (1,163 evacuees, 293 families), Miri (650 evacuees, 172 families), and Kuching (475 evacuees, 153 families), with a single evacuee recorded in Mukah. In Miri, continuous heavy rainfall triggered a major landslide, resulting in the tragic loss of five lives. 

In Sabah, while the flood situation remains relatively stable, the number of evacuees has slightly increased to 5,216 individuals from 1,820 families, compared to 5,195 evacuees the previous night. 33 PPS remain operational across nine affected districts, with Kota Marudu recording the highest number of displaced individuals (2,944 evacuees from 1,095 families), followed by Pitas (806 evacuees, 298 families) and Lahad Datu (514 evacuees, 136 families). Additional affected areas include Telupid, Paitan, Kota Belud, Beaufort, Beluran, and Tongod, where relief efforts are ongoing.

The State Disaster Management Committees in both Sarawak and Sabah are actively coordinating response efforts to ensure the safe relocation of affected communities and the continued operation of relief centers. Authorities report an increasing trend of evacuations in Pitas, while conditions in other districts remain stable. Humanitarian agencies and government response teams continue to work together, delivering food, medical aid, and essential supplies to displaced populations as flood response operations intensify. 

According to the latest weather forecast from MetMalaysia on 1 February 2025, a monsoon surge is expected between February 4 and 7, potentially bringing continuous heavy rainfall across Sabah and Sarawak. This could exacerbate the current flood situation, increasing the risk of further inundation and landslides. Authorities are on high alert and closely monitoring developments to implement necessary early action measures.

countries.name: Guinea-Bissau

name: GNB: Fire - 2025-01 - Cacheu/Gabu Fires
summary:
Between 19 to 23 January, two major fires hit the villages or Gabu and Djofunco in Guinea-Bissau.
On 19 January 2025, a short circuit triggered a fire in Gabú Central Market, a key economic center in Gabú region, eastern Guinea-Bissau. The blaze destroyed 11 warehouses and damaged 29 cabinets, including 8 that were completely burned. The disaster directly affected 90 traders and 585 dependents, while more than 3,500 people who rely on the market’s services are now facing economic challenges. The market’s loss has further destabilized a region already struggling with limited livelihood options. On 23 January, another fire swept through Djofunco Village in Cacheu Region, destroying 31 homes (12 completely and 19 partially). The fire directly impacted 224 people and indirectly aected the entire village of 800. Families lost homes, food supplies, and farming tools, increasing their economic vulnerability and worsening food insecurity. The village’s remote location and difficult terrain make delivering humanitarian aid even more challenging.

Efforts by affected community to contain the situation went went futile. County Special Programs Team, Kenya Red Cross Response Team, KWS, Police and Community members responded and unsuccessfully established fire breaks. The situation is being worsened by the current dry conditions and strong winds experience in Northern Kenya. The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained.

 As of 1323 Hrs on Thursday 23rd January 2025, the situation was still active and approximately 7 kms to human settlements in Bassa, Matarba, Badana, Biliki and Sericho Locations in Isiolo. According to County Commissioner, Isiolo, at least 190 000 acreages of grazing land had been impacted. Attempts to contain the fire by a multi-agency team consisting of National Disaster Operation Centre, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Wildlife Service, Local Adminstration and Community members are underway amidst mobilisation of specialized equipment at national level to support in the containment.

countries.name: Ghana
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: GHA: Epidemic - 01-2025 - Cholera Outbreak
summary:
In October 2024, the Ghana Health Service has announced a cholera outbreak affecting five regions in the country, notably: Greater Accra,
Central, Western, Eastern and Asanti. As part of the interventions strategies to reverse the spread of the disease, Ghana Health Service in
collaboration with UNICEF and partners in November 2024 introduced cholera vaccine- Oral cholera vaccine (OCV). The vaccine was rolled
out in 3 subdistricts of the Central region, which is the epicenter of the epidemic, and 662,906 out of 792,482 eligible population were
successfully vaccinated. Phase 2 subnational OCV campaign successfully completed in 18 subdistricts within 4 hotspot districts of Western
Region (Sekondi-Takoradi, Ea Kwesimintsim, Shama and Ahanta West) between 15 to 18 December 2024. A total of 596,205 persons
(92.9% of target population) were vaccinated. That said, the unvaccinated gap continues to pose a threat to since the vaccinate region is
still reporting pocket of cases, and other aected regions as well. The Ghana RC has been quite active during the initial phases and needs
more resources to continue playing its auxiliary role to the government in this response.

On December 19, 2024, the outbreak had claimed 27 lives and spread across 36 districts in the Greater Accra, Central, Western, and
Eastern regions, with a total of 3,292 reported cases. While the number of cases in the Western Region is declining mainly due to
the vaccination campaign, there is an increase in geographical spread and a rise in cases in the other regions. Between 24 and 31
December 2024, 29 new cases and 1 new death were recorded, with a cumulative number of 4,850 suspected cases from the begining of
the epidemic and 1 new affected district. These gures indicate that the epidemic continues to spread and there is a need to continue the
initial eorts to ensure an ecient response.

countries.name: Colombia
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: COL: Population Movement - 01-2025 - Effects of the Armed Conflict in Catatumbo
summary:
Since last Thursday, January 15, 2025, the security situation has worsened in Catatumbo, municipality of Tibú Norte de Santander, due to clashes between the ELN and FARC dissidents, a situation that has generated an exodus of around 11 thousand people. with a balance of 80 people dead by violent death and 20 injured, as a result of these clashes, directly affecting the urban capitals of Cúcuta, Ocaña and Tibú, cities of Norte de Santander, and some have even crossed the jungle border into Venezuela. Among the deceased, there are seven peace signatories according to the Ombudsman's Office, reporting in turn confinements in several municipalities.
Many people, including peace signatories, social leaders and their families, and even children, face a special risk of being held or killed. He also reported that hundreds of families are now moving to other municipalities and that in some communities in the region food shortages are beginning to be reported.
Catatumbo is a region with economic complexities, where various armed groups dispute territorial control of crops and corridors for the trafficking of illicit substances.
The FARC signed a peace treaty with the Colombian government in 2016, but different dissident groups have maintained their armed struggle against other guerrillas, including the ELN, and state forces in several regions of the country. The situation in El Catatumbo, a region bordering Venezuela, has had a long history associated with the actions of the armed groups that have been present in the territory.
The situation has worsened particularly since last Wednesday, January 15, when funeral worker Miguel Ángel López was murdered along with his wife and young son on the road between Tibú and Cúcuta, near the border with Venezuela.

summary:
Context and current situation

Following the DRC situation, new arrivals fled to Uganda and neighboring countries. In Uganda, receiving points such as Nyakabande in Kisoro, Matanda in Kanungu, Bubukwanga in Bundibudgyo continued to experience spillover of new arrivals increasing exponentially to over 200% compared to 2024 population movement trends. The interagency report indicate variation in situations in transit centers and further highlights an expected increase of the influx due to a deteriorating situation in Goma and Itumi.

Kisoro. – Nyakabande transit center

In Kisoro, 2,501 (1,199 male and 1,302 female) individuals of 1,340 households of new arrivals were received from 27 February-5 March 2025 compared to 1,866 (968 HH) received in the previous week. This shows an increase of about 25% of the new arrivals this week compared to the previous week. This brings to cumulative figures of 11,481 individuals of 6,175 Households received and registered through level one at the transit centre since January 2025. The total estimated population at the transit centre as of 5 March 2025 was 4,220 individuals of 2,121 HH. Other POCs, upon verification, are transferred to allocated settlements.

Kanungu-  Matanda transit center

In Matanda TC, 642 (344 Male and 298 female) individuals of 374 households of new arrivals were received from 27 February-5 March 2025 compared to 701 (393 HH) received in the previous week. This shows a decrease of about 18% of the new arrivals this week. This brings to cumulative figures of 6,365 individuals of 3,833 Households received and registered through level one at the transit centre since 1 January 2025. The total estimated population at Matanda transit centre as of 26 February 2025 was 2,875 individuals of 1,329 HH. Other POCs, upon verification, are transferred to allocated settlements.

Bundibugyo – Bubukwanga, Kanara and Ntoroko

The total Population at the transit center by 6th March 2025 was at 158HH of 347(179F /51.6%, 168M/48.4%) individuals.  Of the 347, 51.6% (i.e. 179) are Children and 24.5% (85)are male adults  (i.e. 23.9%, 83) are women adults. 

The 24 individuals received by end of 6th March 2025 were walk-ins who reported to have accessed the country through   Mpondwe(10), Bunagana(8), Haibale(5), Kyanika(1) following the seisure of Goma and town by M23. The total Population at the transit center by COB 10th March was at 167HH of 371(190F /51.2%, 181M/48.2%) individuals.  Of the 371, 51.7% (i.e. 192) are Children and 24.3% (.90)are male adults  (23.9%.89) are women adults.

Kikube - Kyangwali

The OPM and UNHCR through the interagency coordination meeting indicated that there was an overwhelming number of new arrivals entering through the boarder entries of Bugoma,Nsonga and Buhuka, statitsics by the time of the meeting were 873 individuals of 391HHs excluding the majority who are recyclers,average 200 individuals per day. 

Despite the collection points getting overwhelmed, the reception center at Kagoma in Kyangwali is equally stressed with numbers of new arrivals. It has been predicted that the trends are likely to increase day by day.

Situation in the receiving settlements

Currently, the OPM and UNHCR gazzeted three settlements to receive new arrivals from the DRC. These include, Nakivale, Kyangwali and Rwamwanja. Apparently, Nakivale that is receiving from Matanada and Nyakabande has been indicated to be full and the UNHCR have already proposed to re-open Oruchinga through formalized schedule has not been communicated yet. In Kyangwali and Nakivale, the OPM is still filling the vacant spaces that are also deemed to be getting filled up.

Humanitarian Impact

Due to daily influx of POCs through transit centers, there is limited access to food, shelter, protection of refugees, education, healthcare, and other essential services.  A number of humanitarian organizations have already either closed or have “Skelton“ presence in all locations i.e. In Kisoro – Nyakabande, Matanda and Bubukwanga including settlements of Nakivale, Kyangwali and Rwamwanja.

countries.name: United States
dtype.name: Fire
name: USA: Fire - 01-2025 - California Fires
summary:
The Palisades Fire ignited on Tuesday, January 7, morning in Pacific Palisades, a neighborhood east of Malibu, as a brush fire. By Sunday night, the blaze had expanded to over 23,713 acres, according to the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire). It was 14% contained, and Cal Fire reported that the fire likely damaged or destroyed 5,316 structures, including hundreds of homes. At least 24 people were killed, including some who perished trying to protect their homes from the flames.

A Los Angeles County fire official indicated that a significant number of injuries were linked to two fires, while a city official in Los Angeles described Tuesday night as “one of the most devastating and terrifying” experiences she had witnessed in her part of the city. The Eaton Fire broke out Tuesday night near a canyon in the vast national forest lands north of downtown Los Angeles. By Monday, it had grown to 14,117 acres and was 33% contained, with Cal Fire estimating that over 7,800 structures were likely damaged or destroyed.

The Hurst Fire began Tuesday night in Sylmar, a suburban neighborhood north of San Fernando, as a brush fire. By Saturday night, it had spread to 799 acres and was 95% contained, with Cal Fire reporting that two structures were likely damaged or destroyed.

While firefighters were combating the largest fires, additional blazes broke out on Wednesday and Friday in the Los Angeles area. Crews successfully halted their spread and contained the fires. As of Sunday evening, the Lidia, Archer, Woodley, Sunset, and Kenneth fires were all 100% contained and no longer active, according to Cal Fire. Together, these fires scorched 1,539 acres.

Homes, infrastructure, and essential services were severely affected by the direct earth quake effect and lava flowing out of the erupted volcano that are covering large living areas, agricultural and grazing land of the Agro-pastoral communities in the affected areas.

Seismic activity continues in the Afar and Oromia regions, with 18 earthquakes (magnitudes 4.3 to 5.2) recorded in the past week, linked to the Fentale volcanic complex. The Government of Ethiopia is evacuating over 60,000 people from high-risk areas to safer locations. These evacuations are occurring in areas affected by ongoing tremors, hilly regions experiencing rockfalls, near sites emitting ash since 2 January, and around a major dam. Some residents, especially pastoralists, are hesitant to leave due to concerns about livestock and property (OCHA 17/01/2025).

summary:
Since January 2025, a total of 446,474 Afghan nationals have returned from Iran through the border crossings of Islam Qala and Malik, driven primarily by Iranian deportation policies and escalating conflict clashes in Iran. This surge in returnees includes many families, particularly women and children, who face harsh conditions upon arrival, such as lack of food, shelter, and medical care. On average, approximately 1,350 families, or around 9,450 individuals, are returning each day, highlighting the urgent need for humanitarian assistance and support to facilitate their reintegration into Afghan society.

 Iran’s tightened regulations on residency and essential services for Afghans and the deteriorating security situation in Iran due to the conflict between Israel and Iran have prompted a huge surge in returns. These developments have spurred a second significant wave of cross-border movement, further straining Afghanistan’s already fragile infrastructure.

Le département du Nord-Ouest d’Haïti a été frappé par des pluies diluviennes qui ont provoqué de sévères inondations à Port-de-Paix, Saint Louis du Nord et Anse-à-Foleur, Bassin-Bleu, Chansolme, Jean-Rabel dans la nuit du 22 au 23 décembre 2024. Selon la Direction départementale de la Direction de la protection civile (DDPC-NO), une direction centrale du ministère de l'Intérieur et des collectivités territoriales (MICT), s'occupant essentiellement de gestion des risques et des désastres (GRD) sur tout le territoire haïtien, les crues de la rivière de Port-de-Paix, la principale ville du département, et le débordement des canaux ont submergé tous les quartiers du centre-ville. Un bilan partiel de la DDPC-NO fait état d’une dizaine de personnes décédées dont une femme enceinte à la suite d’un glissement de terrain, de 3000 personnes déplacées et de 1000 se trouvant des abris provisoires. Par ailleurs, l’on dénombre à date plusieurs centaines de maisons détruites ou fortement endommagées, ainsi que de milliers de maison inondées. L’agriculture et l’élevage ont été également fortement touchés. Les routes restent inaccessibles à cause des inondations et des ponts endommagés. Les pluies incessantes font craindre une aggravation de la situation.

countries.name: Vanuatu
dtype.name: Earthquake
name: Vanuatu Earthquake (December 2024)
summary:
A magnitude 7.3 earthquake hit near Port Vila, Vanuatu, on December 17, 2024, at around 12:47 PM local time. The epicenter was approximately 30 kilometers west of Port Vila at a depth of 57 kilometers. Initial reports suggest at least six unconfirmed fatalities and major communication disruptions, which delayed contact with the National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) and government officials until around 6:30 PM local time. Starlink was eventually activated to restore communication with the NDMO.

Communication, electricity, and water outages have significantly impacted the affected areas following the earthquake. Rapid initial response efforts are underway, with communities urgently requesting shelter for evacuees now staying on football fields without protection. Local authorities have emphasized the need for supplies such as drinking water, tarpaulins, medicine, and shelter materials and tools. Internet services remain down in the affected regions, with Starlink being relied upon for communication as telecom providers Vodafone and Digicel work to assess damages and restore their networks. Reports have confirmed six deaths due to a landslide and two people rescued from a collapsed building, while the search for additional missing individuals is ongoing.

Key highlights:
•    Magnitude 7.3 earthquake near Port Vila, Vanuatu.
•    Occurred on December 17, 2024, at 12:47 PM local time.
•    Epicentre 30 km west of Port Vila at a depth of 57 km.
•    At least 6 unconfirmed deaths.
•    Communication, electricity, and water outages reported.
•    Rapid initial response underway.
•    Evacuees are sheltering on football fields without proper protection.
•    Supplies Needed are Drinking water, Tarpaulins, Medicine, Shelter materials and tools.
•    Internet services still down; Star link activated to support communication.
•    Vodafone and Digicel assessing damages to restore networks.
•    6 deaths confirmed from a landslide.
•    2 rescued from a collapsed building.
•    Search ongoing for additional missing individuals.
•    VRCS Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) activated on 17 December 2024.
•    VRCS Staff on standby for response.
•    10 volunteers deployed to Vila Central Hospital Medical Store.
•    Shelter Officer on route around the island for observation and assessment.

The Government of Vanuatu is leading the humanitarian response and all national clusters are actively coordinating and meeting regularly with all the partners. The Cluster system in Vanuatu is a stand-by committee that is also active during preparedness & response. Clusters are led by the relevant Line Ministry or National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) and co-led by agencies. After a disaster, and upon activation of the State of Emergency, the overall coordination of the response lies with the NDMO & the NDC.

VRCS, with the support of IFRC, Core-leads the Shelter Cluster in Vanuatu, supports the NDMO as lead agency, for this response, as well as it does during preparedness. VRCS operation includes all relevant sectors such as Shelter, WASH, Health, Logistics, Gender and Protection, Displacement and Communication and CVA.

The VRCS staff and volunteers working within each cluster are in continuous liaison and communication with their respective National Cluster groups to ensure information sharing and continuous updates. VRCS Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) was activated on 17 December 2024. 10 volunteers deployed to Vila Central Hospital Medical Store. Shelter Officer en route around the island for observation and assessment.

countries.name: Mozambique
