name: BDI: 2024 Floods Simplified Early Action Protocol
summary:
Due to its quasi-tropical climate, Burundi is at enormous risk of flooding all year round, but flooding is particularly concentrated during the two rainy seasons (September to November and February to June). It should be noted that an increase in the risk of extreme rainfall caused by climate change could change this picture and cause the risk of flooding to be considered widespread. It could also have a greater impact if they affect communities with little experience of this kind of disaster. 

Riverine and urban flooding, the most common type of flooding in Burundi, is characterized by the overflowing of riverbeds due to heavy (and sometimes long-lasting) rainfall in the various catchment areas. This type of flooding affects the communities that live or carry out their economic and subsistence activities on the banks of these rivers. These floods cause enormous human and material damage. In particular, the Burundi Red Cross has listed the primary impacts as deaths and injuries, the destruction of private and public infrastructures, and the overflowing of latrines. Agricultural and forage fields are often flooded, resulting in crop and livestock losses, and households are often displaced in the short and medium (and sometimes long) term. Secondary impacts cascade down, the most important of which are food insecurity, the outbreak of water-borne diseases, and a host of socio-economic and psychosocial impacts.

These situations impose a clear need for assistance, which can be summed up mainly in the following actions, by the various agencies and organizations (including the Burundi RC (CRB)) involved in disaster management. National and provincial platforms play an important role in coordinating emergency response.

At the same time, the Kushiara was flowing 39cm over the danger level at Amolshid point in Zakiganj upazila, and 85cm at Fenchuganj upazila point. The Sari-Gowain in Sylhet was flowing 7cm above the danger level at Sarighat in Jaintapur upazila and 30cm at Gowainghat upazila.

According to the BWDB, in the last 24 hours (18.06.2024) till this morning, 333mm rainfall was recorded in Lalakhal of Sylhet, 327mm in Jaflong, 191mm in Kanaighat, 191mm in Zakiganj, 100mm in Sylhet city, 159mm in Laurer Garh in Sunamganj, and 95mm in Sunamganj city and Chhatak upazila. Besides, 398mm rainfall was recorded in Cherrapunji in Meghalaya, 121mm in Dhubri, and 114mm in Goalpara in Assam of India. Most of the roads in Companiganj, Gowainghat, and Kanaighat of Sylhet, and in Chhatak, Dowarabazar, Biswambharpur, and Sadar upazilas of Sunamganj have gone under water, disrupting communications.

According to the Sylhet district administration, 864 villages are flooded, and around 371,000 people are marooned. Around 4,000 people moved to shelter centres opened by the administration. Considering the situation, the administration has banned travel to all tourist spots, including Bichnakandi, Sadapathar, Jaflong, and Ratargul.

Sylhet Deputy Commissioner Sheikh Russell Hasan said, "Companiganj, Gowainghat, and Kanaighat upazilas of Sylhet are badly hit by flood. Initiatives have been taken to distribute rice and cooked food as relief to the affected areas through the local administration."In the upazilas, many villages have been cut off due to breakdown of road communication, many farmlands have gone underwater damaging large number of crops, and fish have escaped overflowing ponds.

summary:
In Côte d'Ivoire, for the past ten years, the period from May to July, which corresponds to the great rainy season, has been a time of heavy torrential rains causing flooding. The year 2024 was no exception. Indeed, from June 13 to 14, 2024, the District of Abidjan and its suburbs, specifically the communes of Abobo, Yopougon, Cocody, Attécoubé, Adjamé, Port-Bouët, Anyama, Bingerville and Bonoua, were hit by heavy torrential rains. Nearly 500 mm of rain fell during these two days while the SODEXAM (airport, aeronautics and meteorological operating and development company) forecast 800 mm of rain for the months of May to July. In two days, 62.5% of the rainfall forecast for the period from May to July 2024 has fallen, causing a dramatic situation in the Ivorian economic capital and its suburbs. These heavy rains have left behind a heavy human and material toll.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Other
name: ARG: Others - 06-2024 - Economic Crisis
summary:
Argentina is facing one of its most complex economic crises in recent years, generating in a large part of the population situations such as the increase in people in situations of poverty and destitution, limitations in access to health and food services, fall and precariousness of formal and informal sources of work, and difficulties in sustaining livelihoods. among other aspects. As of March 2024, it is estimated that more than 57% of the country is under poverty rates (More than 27 million people), 7 out of 10 children are reached by these indices experiencing significant shortages. According to the UCA, 90.7 children and adolescents from 0 to 17 years of age are below the poverty line and 35.6 in indigence. 

After the 2023 presidential elections, in December a politically opposition government took office and whose party had never acceded to the Executive Branch of the country.

In this context, one of the first measures taken by the current National Government has been the declaration of a public emergency in economic, financial, fiscal, administrative, pension, tariff, health and social matters, through a Decree of Necessity and Urgency (DNU No. 70/2023), in force until December 31, 2025. This document characterizes the current context of the country as "... a situation of unprecedented gravity, generating deep imbalances, which have a negative impact on the entire population, especially in the social and economic spheres". Although its application is immediate until it is repealed by the legislative branch, its treatment has revealed a political polarization that keeps its approval pending in the National Congress. Likewise, since April 2024, a bill called Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines ("Bases Law") has been under discussion, which, among other aspects, would modify the declaration of emergency to four in: administrative, economic, financial and energy matters for a period of one (1) year. On June 13, 2024, the Chamber of Deputies approved the Law in general, and in particular the Declaration of Economic Emergency, which must now be submitted to the Senate for consideration, a situation that will occur in the coming days.

These first measures triggered a series of popular reactions (central and territorial) expressed in mobilizations and protests, in some cases with political-party (opposition), sectoral, union (including to date 2 National General Strikes) and Social Organizations.

name: BIH: Flood - 06-2024 - Storm and Flood
summary:
A recent powerful storm has caused serios demages in the northern part of Bosnia and Herzegovina - municipality of Srbac, located in the Republic of Srpska. The storm has affected more than 100 households, with over 15 residential buildings suffering devastation of the roof. Inside these homes, many rooms have been severely affected by the storm's force.

The local elementary school faced a dire situation as the storm tore off its roof, leading to the urgent evacuation of the students. The floodwaters breached over 70 residential properties, causing extensive damage, while in 20 homes, the flood wave has decimated almost everything essential for the residents' daily activities. The agricultural sector also took a hit, with 7 chicken farms and 3 pig farms sustaining damage. The crops in the area have been severely impacted as well. The disruption in communication further exacerbates the challenges faced by the community.

The local branch of the Red Cross has focus it's activities on assesment of the needs of the affected population, ensuring that all actions in providing humanitarian resposne is in line with the real needs of the endangered. In response to the significant damages and the hardships endured by the local population, the municipality of Srbac has declared a state of natural disaster.

name: LBR: Flood - 06-2024 - Monrovia Floods
summary: Torrential rainfall in Monrovia and its environs has caused flash, coastal and river basin flooding affecting over 35 communities in the last 72 hours. According to a joint assessment conducted by the NDMA local community structures and the Liberian Red Cross Community-Based Action Teams (CBATs) during the last five days in Monrovia and adjacent communities, about 35 communities have reported experiencing flooding over the last 72 hours. Data reported say that about 22,060 persons are caught up in the floods leading to temporary displacement, loss of valuable household items, and huge exposure to risks of disease outbreaks, loss of habitat (sheltering opportunities), livelihoods mechanisms, and water source pollution. About 60% of the affected people are women, children, and other vulnerable groups of people including physically challenged, single mothers, among others seeking shelter with neighbors and relatives in adjacent unflooded communities.

countries.name: Uganda
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: UGA: Population Movement - 06-2024 - SUdanese Refugee Inlfux in Uganda
summary:
The deteriorating security situation in Sudan resulting from the ongoing civil war between the two rival factions of the military government of Sudan, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) is anticipated to push more Sudanese refugees into Uganda. 

The GOvernment of Uganda opened up Kirayndono refugee settlement loctd in Mid-Western region of Uganda to be the resettlement site to the newly arriving refugees and asylum seeker from Sudan.

According to Office of the Prime Minister (OPM) and the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) field offices in Kiryandongo where the new arrivals are being resettled, the number of new arrivals per day is 200 asylum seekers who come on their own, in addition to another 160 individuals who are oficially relocated during a weekly convoy from the South Sudan border of Nimule through Nyumanzi reception centre in Adjumani district. This weekly bus covoy is however being hampered by the current closure of Karuma bridge that is currently under repair and thus    

By end of May 2024, UNHCR refugee respoonse dashboard data shows a total of 106,996 individuals (23,116 households) composed of both the old and new caseloads so far resettled in Kiryandongo refugee settlement, out of whom 8,600 individuals are new arrivals from the recently escalated Sudanase conflict; while other 300 indivuduals who just arrived from Sudan are currently being processed at the reception centre. The number of new arrivals is expected to peak to around 61,824 individuals at any point in the year.

Morover, the capacity of Uganda's operation to provide dignified reception to the refugees without any additional, extraordinary support is already exceeded as the situation is being excercebated by the drastic decline in funding for the refugee response. 

the Uganda Red Cross Society condited a needs assessment in kiryandongo refugee settlement between 10th and 17th june 2024 ad established critical humanitarian gaps in provision of safe water and sanitation coverage especially affected the new arrivals from Sudan. other key needs are in the areas of protection with increasing number of individuals and families seeking training serivces that until recently closed out from this settlement due to funding gaps. There is also major gap accomodation space at the reception centre, as well as no support towards provision of shleters to Person of Special Needs (PSNs) who are unabale to cotruct won houses and latrines. Key institutions including the reception cenre, schools and health facilities too are faced with inadequate toilet facilities, intermitten water supply and challenge of solid waste management. The health care services in Kiryandongo refugee settlement are overwhelmed due to this increasing population pressure; whereby drug stock-outs, limited number if health care workforce, and limited diagnostic capacities is barring the refugees and asylum seekers from accessing proper medical care.

It is feared that the current congestion, poor housing, inadequate WASH infrastructure and the minimal health conditions might lead to major outbreak of communicable diseases, including cholera, typhoid and measles and others. Furthermore, the current overstretched reception capacity including screening, registration and allocation of plots s already resulting in overstays at the reception center that poses increased protection risks. Moreoiver, the inadequate shelter infrastructures for those resettled in the plots of land will expose new arrivals, particulalrly PSNs to adverse weather conditions for the duration of stay that increass their risks to respiratory tract infections and malaria infestations.  

Besides, many of the refugees and asylum seekers might move out to urban centres to seek better living conditions  thus posing risks of family seperations and related protection risks. 

To help mobilse resources to address these gaps, the OPM and UNHCR drafted a Continecy Plan targeting Sudanese refugee influx in Uganda in March 2024 but the response to this appeal is quite slow that leaves many partners very limited response capacities.

countries.name: Nepal
dtype.name: Flood
name: Nepal: Floods EAP, 2024
summary:
Flood is the most severe of the hazards observed in Nepal in terms of physical and socioeconomic losses and destruction. Koshi, Karnali, and Narayani are the major river systems in Nepal, and floods from these large perennial river systems generally impact several districts in the Southern Terai plains. Moreover, rivers such as West Rapti, and Babai Rivers, which originate in the Mahabharat range, do more damage in the Terai floodplains because they frequently generate flash floods during the monsoon. Moreover, the Terai's vulnerable topography, combined with its dependency on agriculture, exacerbates the severity of flood hazards compared to other regions.
 
In 2017, the prolonged rainfall across Nepal from 11-14 August 2017 brought flooding across 31 districts of Nepal. The southern Terai region was particularly affected with an estimated 450,000 people affected by flooding, 43 people were killed. According to the Government of Nepal, National Planning Commission Post Disaster Need Assessment Report (PDNA) 2017, it has been estimated that 41,626 houses were destroyed, and 150,510 houses were damaged by the flooding. Over 126,282 ha of paddy were damaged during the flooding, with higher-value crops such as vegetables and aquaculture also suffering significantly. Moreover, the flooding affected over 812,000 poultry, 9,400 cattle, and 74,000 sheds.
 
The targeted flood-prone areas are the Terai districts along the flood plains of Karnali, Babai and West Rapti rivers, namely Banke, Bardiya and Kailali. frequently affected due to flooding in the monsoon period. People living along these rivers especially low-lying areas, informal settlements, fragile houses, and those who have lowincome status and a number of dependent family members to care for, are highly vulnerable to flooding. 
 
NRCS has undertaken extensive household data collection along the flood plains of Karnali, Babai & West Rapti River basins 2021-2022. The analysis shows that 33,794 families are living in Tikapur Municipality, Janaki Rural Municipality, Geruwa Rural Municipality, Rajapur Municipality and Madhuwan Municipality along the Karnali river. Likewise, 25,247 families are living in Barbardiya Municipality, Thakurbaba Municipality, Madhuwan Municipality and Gulariya Municipality along the Babai River. And 21032 families are living in Rapti Sonari Rural Municipality, Duduwa Rural municipality, and Narinapur Rural Municipality along the West Rapti.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.society_name: The South African Red Cross Society
dtype.name: Flood
name: ZAF: Flood - 06-2024 - Floods in Eastern Cape - Nelson Mandela Bay, Buffalo City and Sara Baartman
summary:
Parts of the Eastern Cape especially Nelson Mandela and Buffalo City Metros experiences heavy rains accompanied by strong winds early hours of the 2nd of June 2024 which resulted in severe flooding in most parts. Over the weekend, the South African Weather Service issued a yellow level 6 warning with predictions of strong winds, snowfalls and flooding in parts of the Western Cape, KwaZulu Natal, Northern Cape and the Eastern Cape.  In addition, dam walls were compromised and canals were unable to deal with heavy rainfall which resulted in water flooding into homes and businesses. So far more than 6000 people have been affected including 2500 people have been displaced and 7 people have lost their lives to the floods and a number still reported missing. https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/condolences-eastern-cape-flood-victims-0 The heavy rains resulted in flash floods especially in the 2 Metros (Nelson Mandela Bay and Buffalo City) wreaking havoc in affected areas. https://www/heraldlive.co.za/news/2024-06-03-heavy-rains-wreak-havoc-in-nelson-mandela-bay  About 70 people have been rescued in 55 operations since Sunday, according to the National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI). People have been evacuated to town halls and schools, however, some families are refusing to relocate because they are concerned over their belongings. https://mg.co.za/news/2024-06-03-six-people-dead-and-hundreds-evacuated-in-eastern-cape-floods/

 

In the Sarah Baartman District Municipalities the areas that are adversely affected by the floods include Kouga area – Sea Vista, Oyster Bay, Jeffreys Bay, Thornhill and in Ndlambe area – New Rest Infomral Settlement was also affected. The Nelson Mandela Metro is the most severe hit area with Kariega in Ward 51 and 48 suffering the worst damage.  Damage to infrastructure included damages to roads, sewer systems, buildings and houses including the Traffic Department and the fire station. School has been disrupted, there are water interruptions and there are electricity interruptions with households not having these two basic services since Sunday. The dam wall near Lapland or Tyriville is currently being assessed as there are fears it will collapse causing further flooding in areas. Bridges have collapsed along the Rocklands Road as well as Matanzima road in Kwanobuhle. It must be noted that many people who have lost their homes and belongings are not at community halls but are residing with family members in Kariega. The areas affected include Kuyga, Kwadwesi, Qunu, Langa and Greenfirelds, Kariega Central and Kamesh, Missionvale, Gerald Smith, De Mist, Doctor Brawn, Eric Dodd. Missionvale, Walmer, Witteklip, Daleview, Kwanoxolo, Vastrap, Jachtvlakte, Rocklands, Zwelidinga, Rosedale, GMV, Riemvasmaak, Kleinskool, Joe Slovo, Lapland and Tyriville.

 

In addition, Buffalo City Metro has been adversely affected leaving 2200 people displaced with the following areas affected, Duncan Village, Amalinda, Gompo, Mdantsane, Stoney Drift, Kelly Road, Vincent Park, Pfefferville. Damages are also reported in Ngqushwa, Great Kei LM and Amahlati. It is worth noting that figures would possibly rise as assessments are ongoing and more information continues to be received.

countries.name: Botswana
dtype.name: Drought
name: BWA: 2024 Drought
summary:
The country has experienced dry spells and rainfall deficits in recent years, leading the government to declare a drought emergency in
July 2023. This marks the third consecutive year of severe drought, affecting arable agricultural land in a context where 70% of the rural population depends on agriculture for their livelihoods, primarily through rain-fed farming. Since then, 163,000 people are affected by drought. The SADC Synthesis Report on The State of Food and Nutrition Security and Vulnerability in Southern Africa indicated that 37,000 individuals in Botswana are experiencing food insecurity in 2024.
The El Niño conditions in Southern Africa have further exacerbated the already critical drought situation. According to the Southern Africa Seasonal Monitor report, Botswana is currently experiencing El Niño conditions, leading to severe rain deficits and challenging harvest conditions across most of the region, with dry spells expected to persist. The government of Botswana expressed concerns about imminent food and livestock feed shortages due to unfavorable weather conditions impacting crop production.

On May 24, 2024, the Rural Development Secretariat under the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development issued a report urging support due to the devastating impact of drought on food security, nutrition, water and food production. The report highlighted a significant decline in crop yields, with a drop from 206,572 tons harvested in 2021/22 to 125,184 tons in 2022/23. Cereal production in 2022/23 reached only 67,530 tons, which is equivalent to just 23% of the national requirement. The 2022/23 cropping season experienced low and highly erratic rainfall, along with extended dry periods, severely impacting food and agricultural production, disrupting urban water supplies, and damaging the rural economy and socio-cultural structures.

countries.name: Cameroon
dtype.name: Fire
name: RMC: Fire - 05-2024 - fire camps IDP's MORA
summary:
On April 26, 2024, following a fire of accidental origin, 03 camps for internally displaced persons set up in the locality of Doulo, district of Mora, were totally destroyed. These are the Talla Moalloum, Goumouldi and Karassi-Limani camps. With the help of the dry season, and the shelters being built of temporary materials, the fire quickly spread beyond the area occupied by these communities, thus nearly 4 hectares were burned.

These affected IDPs are of Kanouri, Shoa and Mandara ethnic affiliation. They are believed to have moved as a result of the internal border conflict in the Far North Region, and have been living in Doulo for more than a decade.

The assessment report of the Departmental Committee of Mayo Sava, which went down to the field as soon as the fire was reported, mentions several material damages, including the loss of livestock; food;   motorcycles and bicycles; cash and essential household items.  

 According to the same report, these communities are currently living in the open without assistance. The affected population is made up of a fairly large number of people with special needs.

  • 64 lactating women
  • 85 pregnant women
  • 50 seniors  
  • 08 people living with a disability
  • 40 orphaned children
  • This situation remains worrying because, if left unchecked, it could lead to other factors that endanger the lives of these people. From the first information received, the police of Mora raided the scene in order to make observations. Members of the Communal Risk Preparedness Committee (CCPR) of the Municipality of Mora went to the scene of the disaster to assess the situation.
  • The displaced communities in Doulo are asking to migrate to another site, already known to the Chief of Doulo and the Mayor of Mora. The reasons given are the ban on IDPs building with sustainable materials on the current site, and the insecurity linked to the incursions of armed people at any time.

countries.name: Armenia
dtype.name: Flood
name: ARM: Flood - 05-2024 - Armenia: Lori's Flash Floods
summary:
On May 26, the Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that as a result of the overflow of Debed River emergency situation was created in Northern parts of Armenia, namely in Lori and Tavush regions. As reported, as result of the flood, a 31 km section of the M6 highway between Vanadzor and Alaverdi was flooded, with a portion approximately 50 meters in length collapsing (the highway connects Armenia to Georgia). The flash flooding also forced authorities to close Armenia’s main border crossing with Georgia and suspend rail service between the two countries.

The Ministry reported that bridges over the Debed River have been destroyed and several settlements were cut off. Many residential houses were flooded prompting the evacuation of hundreds of residents from their homes. Lori town of Alaverdi and nearby communities were hit hardest. The Armenian government set up a task force to cope with the natural disaster led by the Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure Gnel Sanosyan. AM PM Nikol Pashinian visited the flooded areas in the afternoon to inspect rescue efforts and damage caused to them.

name: GEO: Flood - 05-2024 - Heavy Rains and Floods in Georgia
summary:
Mtsketa-Mtianeti

On May 26, severe weather caused widespread devastation floods across several regions in Georgia. Huge amount of rainfall during short time, led to significant problems throughout the Mtskheta-Mtianeti region. The devastating floods severely impacted the Tserovani settlement where IDPs are living, the administrative units of Tianeti and Dusheti municipalities, and various villages within the Mtskheta municipality. The flooding caused extensive damage in the villages of Tskhvarichamia, Lisi, Dzegvi, Nichbisi, Zalisi, Tserovani, and the Navdaraantkari administrative units. After several days of heavy rains, residential houses and internal district roads were flooded, bridges and power lines were damaged, and farm plots and agricultural fields were completely destroyed. The electricity supply was cut off to several villages, exacerbating the difficulties faced by the residents.

In Tianeti, the continuous rainfall created severe issues in the administrative units of Artni, Akhalsofeli, Jeboti, Tianeti township, Sion township, Ghulelebi, Nakalakari, and Simoniantkhevi. The road infrastructure and electric transmission lines were significantly damaged, leaving about 100 families cut off from the outside world. Up to 50 families saw their homes and agricultural plots flooded. The population is unable to leave their homes to buy necessary supplies and they are not being provided with drinking water. The villages of Sakhevi, Chiaura, parts of Chabano, and the "building district" in Nakalakari are isolated, compounding the residents distress.

Kvemo Kartli

The Kvemo Kartli region experienced severe flooding on May 26 due to the overflow of the Algeti River, affecting Sadakhlo, Algeti, Kirachmuganlo, Lezhbadini, the town of Marneuli, and an IDP settlement. The flood impacted local citizens, including ethnic minorities and internally displaced persons. The central market area of Marneuli was also damaged. Flood waters destroyed bridges and affected 400 families. Several families needed helicopter evacuations to ensure their safety.

name: Papua New Guinea Landslide 2024
summary:
A landslide occurred on Friday 24th May 2024 at 03:00 a.m. in Yambali village, Maip Mulitaka LLG of Lagaip-Porgera District, Enga Province, Papua New Guinea. Preliminary reports from the provincial government’s office and IOM suggested a number of deaths but confirmed data has not yet been released. Further numbers of casualties and other details are yet to be verified. Estimation of a minimum 7,849 population have been affected by this disaster.

The landslide has blocked off the main highway that also leads to one of the mine site (Porgera Mine). This will also affect communities on the other side as there is no other load to access for food and other supplies for affected people. This is one of the largest devasting disaster, that nearly wiped out a whole village. Enga province is also known for continuous tribal fighting and thus making the area a high security risk.

The landslide had occurred in the early hours of morning leading to blocking of main highway road resulted in the whole village has been inaccessible. There is much needed support to be provided to this affected population including clean and safe water as their water sources are already contaminated. Potential high figure of children becoming orphaned by either losing a parent or both parents are expected. They are still in a traumatized state where psychosocial support is needed. The affected population have lost their livelihood and means of survival, as their food gardens and other means of livelihood are destroyed. So, there is need to provide significant humanitarian support.

Due to extent of the damage and lack of official information in relation to total population in the affected area, there is still no further confirmation on the total number of deaths, as data and information are still being collated. Enga Provincial Administration office has been working closely with the Disaster Management Team (DMT) secretariat and other humanitarian partners who are present on the ground providing essential needed items, such as food and water.

summary: According to forecasts from local, regional, and international forecasters as well as global forecast models, the well-marked low-pressure area over west central & adjoining south Bay of Bengal is very likely to continue to move northeastwards and concentrate into a Depression (D) over central parts of Bay of Bengal by 06:00 am BST of 24th May 2024. Thereafter, it is very likely to continue to move northeastwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm (CS) over east central Bay of Bengal by 06:00 am BST of 25th May. The outer layer of the Cyclonic Storm (CS) may start landfall from the morning of 26th May with a wind speed ranging 75-85 kmph. The landfall point is varying from Odisha (India) to Bangladesh coasts. Global deterministic forecast models are in good agreement that this CS/D will continue to strengthen in the Bay of Bengal due to favorable environment condition for cyclogenesis. According to IMD GFS forecast model, there is a probability that it would reach near Bangladesh and adjoining west Bengal coasts of India by 6:00pm BST of 26th May as a Severe Cyclonic Storm with a wind speed around 100 kmph.

countries.name: Namibia
dtype.name: Drought
name: Namibia -  Drought
summary:
The erratic and limited rainfall distribution patterns experienced since the start of the agricultural season (November 2022) has resulted in abnormal dry conditions affecting most parts part of the country and resulted in both poor crop performance and reduced rangeland conditions. Additionally, poor rainfall over the north western and southern parts of the country during the 2022/2023 agricultural season has negatively impacted pasture biomass conditions, particularly in the crop growing regions where crops failed to mature and rather withered before reaching maturity, resulting in lowered cereal production expectations. Some households in Ohangwena, Oshana and Omusati regions experienced flash floods during the ploughing season   which resulted in the affected households not being able to cultivate their crop fields.

 

With little rainfall received this year and flash floods experienced in Ohangwena, Oshana and Omusati, all crop growing regions (Omusati, Oshana, Ohangwena, Oshikoto, Kavango East, Kavango West and Zambezi) experienced poor harvest. Trend findings from the Crop Prospects, Food Security and Drought Situation Report (July 2023) by Ministry of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform (MAWLR) shows that Namibia’s Total Cereal Production for 2022/23 was 153 000 MT compared to 168 200 MT harvested in 2021/22 season, of which 81% of the total production was 

from the commercial sector and only 19% produced from the crop production regions, which is 9% lower than the 2021/22 harvest.

Furthermore, the Crop Prospects, Food Security and Drought Situation Report (2023) indicated a significant deterioration of the food security situation as a result of highly unfavorable agricultural production conditions during 2022/2023 cropping season. Ever since, majority of crop farmers have experienced crop failure, which has consequently severely impeded the ability to replenish their food reserves. A considerable number of households in the key communal crop producing regions have reported a depletion of their harvests from the previous season, and currently rely mainly on the market and drought relief food for sustenance. This left most households in a precarious state of food insecurity.

 

The MAWLR Crop Prospects, Food Security and Drought Situation Report (2023), indicate that grazing condition was generally poor in most regions with //Kharas, Hardap, Otjozondjupa, Oshikoto, Oshana, Omusati, Ohangwena, Kavango West experiencing very poor grazing conditions (fig 2). The condition in Kunene region ranges from fair to poor while that in Omaheke, Zambezi & Kavango East regions ranging from poor to fair grazing conditions. Erongo and Khomas regions have fair grazing conditions. The livestock body condition were reported to be generally poor in most parts of the country except for Zambezi, Kavango East, Kavango West regions ranging from good to fair. (MAWLR, 2023).

 

According to the Livelihood Vulnerability Assessment and Analysis (VAA 2023/24) results, a total number of 579,000 people in Namibia equivalent to 22% of the total population were projected to face high levels of acute food insecurity during the period of July – September 2023 and required urgent action to reduce food gaps and protect livelihoods. The report further projected that a total of 695,000 people equivalent to 26% of the total population are subjected to experience high levels of acute food insecurity between October 2023 and March 2024. The most affected regions being Kavango West, Kavango East, Omaheke, Ohangwena, //Kharas, Zambezi, Otjozondjupa, Khomas, Oshana, Omusati, Oshikoto and Kunene regions.  The recent IPC update projected that between July to September 2024, the entire country is expected to be in phase 3 with a total of 1 434 790 people equivalent to 362 663 in need of humanitarian assistance (Fig 3)

countries.name: Belize

summary: The initial situation overview right now is approximately 200 families, totaling around 800 persons were impacted by these fires spread across 19 communities and 600 acres in the Toledo district. The Mountain Pine Ridge reserve is facing severe forest fires that are currently affecting the District of Toledo and the air quality of the Cayo District. The forest fires have been raging in the mountain Pine Ridge area for about three weeks. The local government has mobilized volunteers and defense forces to assist. The Belize Red Cross was asked by NEMO to assist in distributing cooked lunches for the community volunteers and the Belize Defence Force who are assisting with the Fire. Crops such as corn, avocado, coca, pasture forests, tach, and water sources were destroyed with long term devastating effects. Multiple agencies are coming together to provide meals and other relief items. Focus is trying to contain fires and being supportive to the families affected.

summary:

At the time of writing, more than 978 people were evacuated to temporary shelters in at least 8 departments in the provinces of Corrientes and Entre Ríos, while many others had to self-evacuate to the homes of relatives and relatives. For the next 3 days, river levels in some areas of the country are expected to continue to rise, which is why the SN has activated all its response teams.

dtype.name: Other
name: GRD: Other - 05-2024 - Water Shortage
summary:
For the past few months there was a decline in rainfall which ultimately led to a significant shortage in water mainly in the Southern and Eastern parts of the island. As such, NAWASA (National Water & Sewerage Authority) was utilising its back up storage being water from the Grand Etang Lake to supply one of the major dams in Annadale and also implementing valve regulation schedules. These measures, while important, are also creating a challenge for some persons who sometimes will have no water for more than 3 days.
 
However, the National Emergency Advisory Council (NEAC) was advised last Friday that NAWASA reached its capacity in pumping from the Grand Etang Lake and so their back up supply is no more. Dams are drying up, there is little or no rainfall and NAWASA has exhausted their capacities. The water trucks that are being utilised to transport water to different communities and businesses are now being rationed. Community members are crying out for lack of water, the prison, schools, private businesses etc. are also facing the same challenges.
 
As of 12AM on Sunday May 12th, 2024 strict water restrictions were implemented with the hope that persons will comply and conserve. However, there is a potential WASH crisis at hand  if we do not get a significant amount of rainfall soon and the Meteorological Office that may not be within the next week or two. A task force was established with the main objective to establish communication procedures, a prioritization list (persons in most need)and procedures for a state of emergency if it gets to this point.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.society_name: The South African Red Cross Society
dtype.name: Civil Unrest
name: ZAF: 05-2024 Election preparedness
summary:
The South African National Government announced that the 7th National General Election will take place on the 29 May 2024. These elections are anticipated to be the most fiercely contested since the establishment of democracy in 1994. The Voter registration was closed on 23 February 2024 followed by roll objections on the 4 March 2024 and candidate nominations were adjusted then submitted by political parties and independent candidates on 08 March 2024. Voting stations were announced on 12 April 2024 leading to special voting on 27-28 May 2024.

The 2024 general elections in South Africa are set against a backdrop of significant socio-political tension, with heightened risks of electoral violence that could impact lives, livelihoods, well-being, and infrastructure across various regions.

1) High-risk areas such as Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal (KZN), the Eastern Cape, and parts of the Western Cape are particularly vulnerable. Gauteng, with its dense urban centres like Johannesburg and Pretoria with a history of fatal political clashes, are of special concern.

2) Medium-risk provinces such as Limpopo, Mpumalanga, and North West have experienced sporadic disturbances, which, while generally less severe, still require vigilant monitoring.

Conversely, the Free State and Northern Cape are considered low-risk areas due to their historically peaceful elections.

The electoral landscape is informed by historical data which shows that while the 1994 and 2004 elections were largely peaceful, the 2021 local government elections identified 300 hotspots of potential violence, underscoring the ongoing challenges.

The direct impacts of electoral unrest are most acutely felt by vulnerable groups including the elderly, children, people with disabilities, internally displaced persons (IDPs), refugees, and residents of informal settlements. These groups are at a heightened risk of suffering due to their socio-economic conditions, reliance on community and government support, and proximity to politically sensitive areas. Historical precedents indicate that election periods marred by social unrest and violence have not only led to loss of life and injuries but also caused significant disruptions to economic activities and access to essential services, thereby exacerbating the vulnerabilities of already marginalized groups.

name: URY: Flood - 05-2024 - Floods
summary:
The adverse weather events that have been recorded in different parts of the country (very strong storms and heavy rainfall) caused the overflow of several watercourses that in turn determined the displacement of hundreds of people.

The Uruguayan Institute of Meteorology (Inumet) issued a warning to the population informing that from the late hours of Sunday, May 5 to Wednesday, May 8, a deterioration of the weather conditions was expected "with strong and very strong storms accompanied by punctually copious rainfall."
 
Since then and according to forecasts, very strong storms and copious rainfall have been recorded in different parts of the territory and Inumet has been issuing successive yellow and orange level warnings. In addition, the agency updated the forecast of accumulated rainfall and it is expected that in total, throughout the adverse weather event, the accumulated rainfall will be between 150 – 250 mm.

So far, 10 departments have registered displaced persons: Artigas, Cerro Largo, Durazno, Paysandú, Río Negro, Rocha, Salto, Soriano, Tacuarembó and Treinta y Tres.

At the national level, 2,184 people remain displaced from their homes, 534 as evacuees and 1,650 as self-evacuees

The Coordinator of the Departmental Emergency Coordination Center (CECOED) of Artigas reported that the Uruguay River in that department continued to rise and is located at 7.03 m, more than 50 cm above the safety level that is defined at 6.5 m.

The number of displaced people there remains at 25: 13 evacuees and 12 self-evacuees, all of them from the city of Bella Unión.

The water level in Laguna Merín is stable at 4.75 m, when the safety level is set at 6 m. The behavior of the Yaguarón River is also monitored.

In Durazno, the Yí River continues to rise and stands at 8.64 when the safety level is set at 8.20. 

The Cecoed of Paysandú reported that the Uruguay River increased 20 cm compared to yesterday's measurement and is located at 7.15 m, 15 cm above the safety level determined at 7 m.

In Salto, the Uruguay River has already exceeded the safety level of 12.20 m and the current level is 12.65 m. 

In Treinta y Tres , the number of displaced people increased to 1,130: 280 evacuated and 850 self-evacuated. According to the latest measurements, the Olimar River, after reaching the peak of 9.60 m, began to descend and is located at 9.20 m, more than two meters above the safety level established at 7 m.

In that department, the flooding of the Cebollatí and Olimar rivers caused the closure of routes 91 and 17, which in turn determined that the town of La Charqueda is temporarily isolated. Personnel from the fire detachment in coordination with the Prefecture remain in the area, in order to facilitate transportation in case of an emergency.

countries.name: Africa Region
dtype.name: Food Insecurity
name: SOUTHERN AFRICA  DROUGHT
summary:
Since November 2023, the El Niño weather phenomenon has brought high temperatures and below-average rainfall to southern Africa, with significant negative impacts on agriculture, leading to water scarcity, food shortages, and disease outbreaks. The drought began in Botswana in October 2023 and has gradually intensified and spread to Angola, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Namibia, affecting most of southern Africa today. In the last month and a half, the governments of Zambia, Malawi, and Zimbabwe have declared states of emergency. With the resources available, Red Cross National Societies in Southern Africa have provided what support they can to some of the most affected communities in the region. However, more support is urgently needed to provide immediate relief and avert an even worse situation in the near future.

February was the driest month since 1981 for most of Zimbabwe, Zambia, and parts of Botswana and Angola. Forecasts indicate dry conditions and below-normal rainfall for much of southern Africa until at least June 2024. The forecasts suggest little chance of recovery for the remainder of the growing season, posing a significant threat to food security in the region. The prolonged dry spell comes at a critical time when crops most need water to grow and produce grain. Maize production in particular has been severely affected, with poor to failing conditions reported in many parts of Southern Africa. Food prices are rising, with the highest food inflation rates in the region at 84 per cent in Zimbabwe, 42 per cent in Malawi and 25 per cent in Angola in March 2024. With many farmers in the region either in or nearing harvest time, the true impact of this failed season has yet to be felt. This crisis is expected to intensify the already dire food insecurity situation, with food shortages leading to malnutrition and related diseases, putting a heavy strain on limited health services, preventing school attendance, and exacerbating people's general economic hardship. The cholera outbreak in Zimbabwe and Zambia in early 2024 was linked to floods, followed by water shortages, exacerbated by limited access to water and sanitation.

summary:
The Ministry of Health published this Tuesday, April 30, in the Diario Centro América, agreement 152-2024 declaring a national health emergency throughout the territory of the Republic due to the dengue epidemic.

Also in a statement, he stressed that it is essential to protect the health of the population in the face of this epidemic. Dengue is transmitted by the Aedes aegypti mosquito, which affects all age and sex groups.

Accordingly, all centralized and decentralized, autonomous, semi-autonomous, municipal, private, non-governmental and community organizations and public agencies and institutions, whose competence or purpose is the administration of health actions, must coordinate with the Ministry of Health the planning and development of actions to promote, prevent and manage the dengue crisis.

The actions are aimed at mitigating damage and controlling environmental risk factors, and it is essential that joint and coordinated work help to counteract the disease and, above all, ensure the well-being of Guatemalan families.

summary:
In recent days, Rio Grande do Sul has suffered heavy rainfall. The rainfall recorded is equivalent to three times the average for this time of year, according to the National Institute of Meteorology (Inmet). The forecast is that the situation will continue until Saturday (4) with accumulations that could reach up to 400 millimeters, which would be added to the more than 300 millimeters of rain recorded in the last 4 days. In total, 154 of the 496 municipalities of RS have registered some type of problem, affecting 71,300 people.

The main regions affected by the floods are the Metropolitan, Central, Vale do Rio Pardo, Vale do Taquari and Serra Gaúcha. On Wednesday afternoon (1), the National Geological Survey issued a bulletin indicating a significant rise in the water level in the Taquari River basin by the end of the day. According to the report, in Muçum, the river could reach a level of 30 meters and 27 centimeters, with a flood level of 18 meters. In Estrela and Lajeado, the expected level is 30 meters and 95 centimeters, but there is already flooding at 19 meters.

On Thursday morning (02/05), 30 sections of the federal highway were completely blocked due to the disruption caused by the rain. Another section is partially blocked. On state highways, there are 91 points with total blockades. Another 23 sections have traffic partially restricted.

Civil Protection says 60 people are missing and 36 injured. The Civil Defense estimates that there are about 14,800 homeless people, 4,645 in shelters and 10,242 displaced. In total, 154 of the 496 municipalities in RS registered some type of problem, affecting 71,300 people. The death toll has risen to 32, and Civil Defense recorded 29 deaths as of Thursday (2). The other three deaths were confirmed by city councils, the Fire Department, the Military Police and local organizations.

name: LSO: 04-2024 Drought
summary:
According to the weather update for quarter 1 of 2024 issued by the Lesotho Meteorological Services, the persistent heatwaves and exceptionally high temperatures experienced between January and March 2024 have led to widespread dryness of crops across most fields. The continuous crop failures over the past seasons is exacerbated. The past two quarters have seen the same crop failure leading automatically to the high food prices. There are 41% of rural families spending more than half of their income on food while most of the families leave with low income. In two consecutive agricultural seasons (2021/2022 and 2022/2023), Lesotho experienced harsh climatic induced shocks such as hailstorms, pests and heavy rainfall/waterlogging in most parts of the country. On the other hand, the heavy rainfalls in late December 2023 and early 2024 led to waterlogged fields which resulted in crop failure. The inflation resulting from this crop failures or production failures have a direct incidence to the families already struggling with low income and other factors that make them more vulnerable to food insecurity.

Approximately, 325,000 individuals are experiencing the effects of the ongoing food insecurity based on IPC analysis, stemming from the enduring drought that has gripped the nation for years and increased the food insecurity situation. This figure represents approximately 22% of the population. Eight districts on the ten in Lesotho are under Integrated Food Security Phase Classification 3 (IPC 3), signifying a crisis state. Berea, Maseru, Mafeteng, Mohale’s Hoek, Quthing, Thaba Tseka, and Leribe areas. In these districts, access to adequate food and nutrition is severely compromised, necessitating urgent intervention and support measures to alleviate the hardship faced by affected communities.

It is against this background that Lesotho Red Cross request to launch a response intervention to mitigate the drought effects witnessed for the past season with an incidence on food insecurity for around 325,000 people that will certainly not be able to cope with the inflation in an already difficult context. Since OND, Government called for actions. The announcement of the production results and price increase brought Government to renew their call for assistance during the recent emergency coordination meeting.

summary:
At the 23 April , it has been reported by the Obock branch of the Red Crescent, the boat was on its journey from Yemen to the Djiboutian coast. The tragic incident occurred in Godoria, approximately 30 kilometers away from the main town of Obock, resulting in the loss of 21 lives, among them 4 women and 1 child. 32 individuals managed to survive, while over twenty others still missing on the 77 on board.

countries.name: Mauritania
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: MRT: Population displacement - 04-2024 - Mauritania: Population movement in the Hodh El Chargui region in 2024
summary:
The humanitarian crisis that has affected Mali since 2012 has generated massive displacement of populations, both inside and outside the country, with significant repercussions on neighbouring countries, including Mauritania, Burkina Faso and Niger. Since 2012, tens of thousands of Malians have fled to Mauritania for safety due to instability and violence in their country.

The increase in insecurity in Mali in 2024 has caused a massive influx of refugees in the wilaya of Hodh El Chargui, and mainly in the departments of Bassiknou and Adel Bagrou. This new round of violence has exacerbated the situation and led to massive displacement of new arrivals, particularly to the Mali-Mauritania borders.

These new IDPs, made up of Mauritanian returnees and Malian refugees, continue to cross unofficial borders in several locations on Mauritanian territory.

These influxes of displaced people from various regions of Mali have added to the populations of this region already facing major challenges, these new arrivals are not settling in the Mbera camp but in the different localities of Hodh Chargui.

According to reports from UN partners presented on 16 April 2024, 112,827 people have been registered, including 102,353 in Mbéra camp and 10,447 outside the camp. The new arrivals number 92,100 individuals, of whom 82,262 are out of camp and 9,838 in Mbéra camp are awaiting registration.



Most of the sites where IDPs are settling in Hodh El Chargui are in remote areas. 70% of displaced populations without adequate shelter have settled in empty spaces; Socio-health infrastructure is non-existent, leading to open defecation and exposing them to the risk of disease. Many water sources are already inadequate and are not safe to drink. The majority of displaced people outside the camp face food insecurity. More than 50% of the displaced are pastoralists and most have moved with their livestock, which has increased much more pressure on natural resources, especially water and pastures.

At the Mbera camp, needs are almost covered or are being addressed by UN partners and international organizations. However, much remains to be done to care for displaced persons outside the camp.

In this volatile context, it should be noted that official border crossings have been closed since April 17, 2024. Indeed, this situation is likely to worsen with the deterioration of relations between Mauritania and Mali. The most recent border incident recorded between the two countries dates back to just after the Eid al-Fitr holiday when Malian forces and the Wagner Group reportedly entered the Mauritanian village of Med Allah, resulting in civilian injuries and controversial arrests.

countries.name: Nigeria
dtype.name: Chemical Emergency
name: NGA: Chemical Emergency - 04-2024 - Heavy Metal Poisoning
summary:
Heavy metals including cadmium, chromium, lead, and mercury are emitted mainly into the air as a result of various industrial activities including mining especially where regulation is poor. This also contributes to the deposition and build-up in soils. Heavy metals can also contaminate water sources and get into plants if they persist in the soil. Exposure to heavy metals either through the air (dust), soil, plants or water are associated with kidney, brain, liver, and bone damage including cancers of the body depending on the type of heavy metals. Persons most at risk or vulnerable include pregnant women (the unborn babies), infants and children, illegal / artisanal miners, industrial workers etc. Some of the effects of heavy metals are immediate while many will take a long time to manifest.

18 April 2024 | Abuja- NCDC Convenes an Emergency Meeting with Sokoto and Zamfara States to Address Unknown Illness

The Director General (DG) of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Dr Jide Idris, hosted an emergency meeting with two Honourable Commissioners for Health from Sokoto and Kaduna States on April 16, 2024 at NCDC’s Headquarters Abuja and also spoke on telephone with Zamfara’s State Commissioner for Health to unravel the cause as well as contain and mitigate the impact of the ongoing incidents of unknown origin in both Sokoto and Zamfara States. The Honourable Commissioners (Hajiya Asabe Balarabe, Dr. Aisha Anka and Hajiya Umma Ahmed) discussed the current situation, provided updates on response efforts, and agreed with the DG of NCDC on further measures to contain and mitigate the impact of the illness suspected to be heavy metal poisoning possibly linked to mining activities.

As at the 18th of April 2024, a total of 196 suspected cases of the unknown illness with seven (7) deaths have been reported across Isa, Sabon Birni, and Ilella Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Sokoto State. Results of the analyses on the various samples sent to the different sister laboratories including NIPRID, NAFDAC and NIMR are being awaited.

Following reports of similar cases in Zamfara State, another National Rapid Response Team (NRRT) will be deployed this week to assess the situation and provide support to the state.

name: YEM: Flood - 04-2024 - Yemen Floods
summary:
Heavy rains and storms have caused widespread flooding across several governorates in Yemen. Initial assessments indicate significant

damage to infrastructure, displacement of families, and livestock losses. Humanitarian organizations are mobilizing to respond to urgent needs,

but access remains a challenge.

The affected areas are Hadramaut, Al-Jawf, Sana'a (including the capital city), Abyan, Al-Dhalea, Shabwa, and Taiz governorates, which have

reported damage to homes, tents, and infrastructure.

The affected population is about  3,755 households (HHs), including both resident communities and Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs).

Verification is ongoing, with the number expected to rise.

The affected governorates experienced damage to their roads, water sources, electricity networks, drainage systems, and agricultural land.

The number of livestock casualties includes 87 sheep.

 Damaged roads are hindering access to some affected areas, hampering full damage and needs assessments.

 Continued heavy rain raises concerns about further flooding in the same or additional governorates.

There are needs in tents, non-food items, food, clean drinking water, and hygiene kits are the most critical needs.

Urgent Needs

  • Continued field assessments to fully understand the scale of the disaster.
  • Immediate provision of shelter, non-food items, food, water, and hygiene kits for affected families.
  • Repair or reconstruction of damaged infrastructure, prioritizing access roads and water sources.
  • Support for displaced families, including temporary housing and livelihood assistance.

summary:
La montée des eaux du lac Tanganyika, ont provoqué les inondations dans deux provinces de la RDC savoir  la province de Tanganyika et le Sud-Kivu.

Dans la province du Sud-Kivu c’est l’augmentation et l’accru des rivières Mulongwe, Kalimabenge, Kamvimvira et Kabimba du groupement incorporé de Kalungwe, dans l’aire de santé de KABIMBA qui détruit les maisons et les champs environnant la mairie et met à mal la vie de les paisibles citoyens riverains dans la ville d’Uvira. Actuellement les 9 quartiers à savoir : Kavimvira, Kasenga,  Kakombe,   Rombe,  Kimanga,  Nyamianda,  Kilibula,   Kalundu  et Kabimba sont tous fortement touchés par cette monté et le débordement des eaux des rivières ci-haut citées.

Cette monté des eaux, les débordements des rivières ont provoqués plusieurs conséquences en destruction de plusieurs maisons et plusieurs champs sur les environs de Nyangara et Kabimba, ainsi plusieurs personnes sont touchées par cette catastrophe et sont hébergées certains dans des Familles d’accueils, d’autres ont rejoints les autres dans les sites des sinistrés, d’autres sont dans les maisons inachevées et d’autres résistent encore dans leurs maisons inondées à travers la ville d’Uvira et le groupement à Kalungwe.

La situation est aussi déplorable pour la province de Tanganyika ou la montée des eaux du lac ne fais que s’accentuer dans les territoires Moba, Kabalo, Kongolo, Manono et la ville de Kalemie ou même les fosses, les  latrines sont inondées et vidées, les matières fécales se déversent dans les lacs ou les habitants s’approvisionnent en eau. Avec un risque plus élevé de la contamination des maladies d’origine hydrique.

countries.name: Afghanistan
dtype.name: Flood
name: Afghanistan Flash Floods – April 2024
summary:
Afghanistan has been experiencing persistent rainfall on the heels of an uncharacteristically dry and late winter, resulting in floods across 20 provinces: Badghis, Balkh, Daikundi, Farah, Ghor, Helmand, Herat, Kabul, Kandahar, Kapisa, Khost, Kunar, Logar, Laghman, Nangarhar, Nuristan, Parwan, Panjshir, Samangan, and Urozgan. Intense rainfall activity commenced during the week of April 16th culminating on 18th and was potentially associated with the event which impacted neighboring Pakistan, India and as far as Dubai in the United Arab Emirates, which experienced its heaviest rainfall since records began. The heavy rains resulted in another deleterious blow to the agricultural sector, with losses to over 5,428 livestock and over 84,069 acres of land. Further, the heavy rains which resulted in significant flooding is blamed for the loss of 41 lives, 84 injuries, and upwards of 8,273 houses being partially or completely damaged. Assessments continue to determine the full impact of the severe weather event with more rain in the forecast over the coming days.

The rains coincide with a weakening El Nino which is characterized by less precipitation and droughts – an experience which is not in the distant past for Afghanistan. In addition to the injuries and casualties reported, there were also damage and destruction to critical civilian infrastructure such as roads, bridges and culverts causing disruption to transportation networks.

It is anticipated that there will be a great need for urgent humanitarian assistance as the coping capacities of households are already stretched, as they face a compounding reality at a time when their recovery from previous events have been disrupted. The greatest needs will be in the areas of Shelter, Cash, food, Wash assistance and other non-food items (NFIs). With more rains in the forecast, additional flooding in low-lying and flood prone areas remain an existential threat. Additionally, urban flooding is also possible as natural waterways are blocked, and there are inadequate and limited drains. Sites downstream from large reservoirs or rivers are also particularly prone to flash flooding after relatively short periods of intense rainfall.

summary:
From April 10th to April 15th, the National Weather Forecasting Center in Islamabad predicts a series of weather events in various regions of Pakistan. This includes rain, wind, and thunderstorms with intermittent breaks. On April 10th, a westerly wave is expected to enter the upper regions, followed by another potent wave on April 12th affecting most areas until April 15th.

In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, regions such as Chitral, Dir, Swat, Abbottabad, Mansehra, and others will experience these weather conditions during this period, with occasional breaks. Similar conditions are anticipated in Waziristan, Kohat, Peshawar, and surrounding areas from April 12th onwards.

Gilgit-Baltistan and Kashmir should prepare for rain, wind, and thunderstorms (with snowfall in high mountains) from April 10th to April 15th, with breaks in between. Punjab, including Islamabad/Rawalpindi, Murree, and other areas, will also experience these conditions, particularly from April 12th onwards, with isolated windstorms and hailstorms expected from April 13th to April 15th.

Numerous casualties were reported due to severe weather conditions across three provinces, marking a grim situation in the affected areas:

Continuous heavy rainfall coupled with thunderstorms resulted in an additional 12 fatalities on Sunday, bringing the total death toll to at least 39 individuals across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Balochistan over recent days.

In Balochistan, Makran and surrounding areas witnessed ongoing rainfall, contributing to the province's death toll reaching 10 after two more casualties were reported from Kech district due to a lightning strike and a roof collapse incident on Sunday. Coastal towns like Pasni, Kech, and Panjgur districts, as well as Gwadar, faced substantial damages to infrastructure and transportation networks, causing restricted access from Quetta and other districts.

Power supply disruptions were severe, with uprooted electric pylons in Pasni and Panjgur leading to prolonged outages in Quetta and nearby regions. Gas supply issues and low pressure were also noted in various parts of the provincial capital and other cities.

Normal life and traffic were significantly impacted across approximately 25 districts of Balochistan, with incessant rains causing extensive damage to houses and roads, particularly in Pasni and Kech district where mud houses collapsed and link roads were washed away.

The Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) reported five injuries from lightning strikes and assured the provision of medical care to the injured while planning financial assistance for the families of the deceased.

In Punjab, the death toll from lightning strikes rose to 21, with additional casualties reported from various districts, including Muzaffargarh, Rahim Yar Khan, and Bahawalpur.

Karachi also faced rain-related incidents, including traffic accidents resulting in six deaths, alongside concerns over lightning strikes and power outages. Chief Meteorologist Sardar Sarfaraz highlighted the increased risk of tornadoes and lightning due to a combination of sea breeze and cold winds.

Despite the weather system losing intensity, light rains were anticipated early on Monday, with Surjani Town recording the highest rainfall of 29 millimeters, followed by other areas like Nazimabad, Gulshan-i-Hadeed, and Keamari receiving significant amounts of rainfall.

name: KAZ: Flood - 03-2024 - Floods in several regions
summary:
As a result of increasing temperatures and heavy rainfall, several regions of the Republic of Kazakhstan have been affected by heavy flooding. Local authorities have declared a state of emergency in ten regions of the country. Water levels are expected to rise in further seven regions due to precipitation and as the increasing temperature is melting the snow.

According to the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation, flooding has already reached its peak in Akmola, Aktobe, and Karaganda regions, while, in the East-Kazakhstan region, the peak is anticipated in a week. A second wave of floods is further anticipated in the West-Kazakhstan region.

Disburse of water at the Iriklinsky hydroelectric power station in the Russian Federation is still high; the water is expected to reach the border of Kazakhstan in an estimated 15 - 20 days, threatening the settlements in West-Kazakhstan and Atyrau regions. In Kostanai region, the average filling of two main reservoirs is 96 per cent, with water levels growing. The two main reservoirs of North-Kazakhstan region are filled up to 100 per cent and 180 per cent, with an overflow at a record level of 415 cm, putting three districts at risk of flooding in the region.

According to weather forecasts, temperatures will continue to rise in the near future, further melting snow at a high pace and filling reservoirs to their limits. At the time of this IFRC Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) application, the area of snow cover in Kazakhstan is 15 per cent, with an approximate 40 per cent in the northern, eastern, and central regions of the country.

countries.name: Madagascar
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: MDG: Cyclone - 2024-03-27 - TC Gamane
summary:
On March 27, 2024, Tropical Cyclone Gamane made landfall in Madagascar early in the morning, with an average wind speed estimated at 150 km/h with gusts up to 210 km/h. The cyclone hit the commune of Ampisikinana in the Vohémar district of the Sava Region.
The cyclone's path brought severe weather to three regions in Northern Madagascar: Sava, Diana, and Analanjirofo. Since landfall, these regions, particularly Sava, Analanjirofo, and parts of the Diana region, have experienced heavy rainfall, leading to flooding in towns and villages. In the Analanjirofo region, all the fokontany in the Commune Urbaine (CU) of Sambava, as well as the Communes Rurales (CR) of Ambinanitelo and Andranofotsy in the Maroantsetra district, are flooded. Reports from branches, authorities, and partners indicate ongoing flooding aecting parts of the Sava Region, including the towns of Antalaha, Sambava, and Vohemar. A provisional assessment by the National Disaster Risk Management Oce on March 28 shows that three people are missing, 36,934 are affected, and 19,192 are displaced.
Red heavy rainfall warnings were issued for the Diana, Sava, Ambatosoa, and Analanjirofo regions, as well as the Toamasina and Vohibinany districts in the Atsinanana Region. Green heavy rainfall warnings were issued for the Analalava, Antsohihy, Bealanana,
Mandritsara, Befandriana Nord, Antanambao Manampotsy, Marolambo, Mahanoro, and Stone districts in the Alaotra-Mangoro Region.
Red strong wind and heavy swell warnings were also in place for much of Madagascar's eastern, northeastern, and southern coastlines.

countries.name: Liberia

name: LBR: Other - 03-2024 - River Cess Gold Mine Mud Collapse
summary:
On Monday, March 26, at about 11:20 pm, a mining pit collapsed and killed 13 illicit miners, and unidentified numbers are still missing. The incident occurred in a community called Cheoh Town, some 21 kilometers away from Cestos City, the Capital city of River Cess County in south/central Liberia. The miners had gone there at night to conduct mining activities deep into the pit when the loose dirt collapsed, closing the way out of the hole. According to information from the County, this mining site had been closed by the government for some years, but illicit miners still go there at night in search of underground minerals, especially gold. 

After the situation occurred, some friends of the miners and community members carried out a search and rescue effort by digging off the top dirt to enter the pit to rescue some of their colleagues. Still, unfortunately, they retrieved only 13 dead bodies from the pit and three survivors. One of the survivors is currently undergoing treatment at JFK Hospital in Monrovia, and the other two who have broken legs are receiving traditional treatment in River Cess.

Meanwhile, the locals retired the search effort due to the lack of earth-moving equipment to more profound into the ground to dig out the remaining bodies and rescue anybody who was still alive.  On the other hand, The families/relatives of the 13 dead bodies have taken custody of their bodies for burial.

countries.name: Uruguay

name: URY: Flood - 03-2024 - Floods
summary:
Throughout the day of the 20th, much of the territory was under Orange and Yellow Weather Alert. At 6:30 p.m., it was decided to raise it to Red Weather Alert given the expected severity of the meteorological phenomena, and in coordination with the National Water Directorate (DINAGUA) and the National Emergency System (Sinae) due to the potential impacts that these phenomena could have.

The storms of March 21 caused flooding, tree falls, road closures, displacement of people with evacuees and self-evacuees.

As reported by UTE, 87% of interrupted services were restored. In fact, of the 116,000 customers initially affected, 15,000 customers still need to be restored.

The National Emergency System announced in the latest survey that the number of displaced people is 4,112, 803 evacuated people and 3,309 self-evacuated.  Of these, 699 correspond to the department of Canelones, 40 to Cerro Largo, 450 to Colonia, 118 to Durazno, 1,415 to Florida, 12 to Rivera, 1,322 to San José and 56 to Tacuarembó.

The flooding situation in Uruguay has generated a series of challenges in terms of mobility and access to different areas of the country due to the cut routes. Heavy rains and overflowing rivers and streams have caused several roads to be affected, making it difficult for vehicles to move and transport people and goods.

In several regions, authorities have had to take urgent action to close stretches of roads that have been left underwater, especially in areas near rivers that have experienced significant flooding. This has created inconveniences for local residents, as well as for travelers and carriers who rely on these roads to move around the country.

The cut routes have generated diversions and delays in travel, affecting the logistics of various economic and social activities as well as humanitarian aid. In addition, damage to road infrastructure, such as landslides and sinkholes, has been reported in some areas, making it even more difficult to rehabilitate affected roads.

The relevant authorities, together with emergency and road maintenance agencies, are working hard to assess the situation of the routes, make urgent repairs and restore access safely. However, the process may take time due to the extent of flood damage and adverse weather conditions that persist in the region.

In this context, the importance of keeping the population informed about road conditions and available detours is highlighted, as well as taking extra precautions when driving in flood-affected areas to ensure the safety of all road users.

Heavy rains and flooding of rivers in several regions of Uruguay have kept critical areas on high hydrological alert. In particular, attention has been focused on the basins that flow into the Río de la Plata, as well as on the basin of the Santa Lucía and San José rivers.

In these areas, the warning has remained at very high levels due to the transit of the flood wave of the Santa Lucia River, which has generated concern about possible flooding and road closures. Authorities have been closely monitoring the situation in the rivers that flow into the Uruguay River, specifically in the departments of Paysandú, Salto and Artigas, where an orange alert has been decreed.

This orange alert is due to the fact that the rivers and streams in these areas have experienced a significant increase in their levels, which increases the risk of flooding and damage to nearby towns. In particular, attention has been paid to the Yí River and the Cuareim River, where levels are expected to continue to rise, with a high probability of reaching the warning level.

Although the probability of damage to homes has been assessed to be moderate in Durazno and low in Artigas at this time, conditions are constantly being reviewed due to the changing nature of river flooding and persistent rainfall in the region. Authorities have been working on preventive and response measures to mitigate potential impacts on the population and infrastructure of these vulnerable areas.

Faced with this situation, an unprecedented number of evacuees have been attended, covered and contained, mainly in the cities of Florida and in the town of 25 de Agosto. The Departmental Emergency Committee, made up of various government actors and the Department's active forces, has assessed the seriousness of the situation and has suggested the declaration of a "Departmental Emergency". By virtue of the provisions of the Constitution of the Republic and the corresponding laws, the Mayor of Florida has decided to declare a situation of departmental emergency. This measure implies the continuity of immediate and necessary emergency measures to deal with the emergency, as well as the maintenance of the Departmental Emergency Committee in permanent session until the situation generated ceases. The communication and dissemination of this declaration will be carried out through the Communications Unit, with the aim of informing the population and coordinating the necessary actions to address this unprecedented climate crisis.

Hydrological Warning by Hydrographic Regions

countries.name: Iraq
dtype.name: Pluvial/Flash Flood
name: IRQ: Pluvial/Flash Flood - 03-2024 - Flooding and Floods
summary: On the afternoon of 19th March 2024, heavy rain began to fall across all provinces of Iraq in varying amounts. Some provinces were affected by the rain, leading to floods, such as Erbil where 86 families, equivalent to 516 individuals, were affected by floods in areas like Terawa, Badawa, Koyistan, and Dara Tow. Dohuk was affected due to its proximity to neighbouring Turkey, facing floods, torrents, and escalating damages resulting in human and material losses. 160 houses were damaged, 50 cars were destroyed, 3 people died, and 11 others were injured. A total of 627 people were evacuated and accommodated in mosques, schools, and some in hotels. The affected areas in most parts of Dohuk province included Baroshki, Nazarki, Atiti, Naoura, Mahalla Sheli, Hay Al-Jazma, Hay Al-Shurta, Al-Ulya, Kizabra, and Mahalla Kuli. The floods and torrents also caused damage to pavements and roads. As for the provinces of Diyala and Maysan due to their proximity to neighbouring Iran, they also witnessed floods in addition to the rain, resulting in minor material losses due to the flow of floods on the outskirts of Diyala province (areas of Baldrouz, Al-Muqdadiyah) where only two families, equivalent to 12 individuals, were affected. In Maysan, the torrents continued to flow on the outskirts of the province in rural areas, and today on 20th March 2024, the weather is clear. However, weather forecasts predict a resumption of rain, leading to additional floods tomorrow, Thursday, 21st March 2024, in the Kurdistan region.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Flood
name: ARG: Flood - 03-2024 - Floods La Plata
summary:
During the afternoon of Tuesday, March 19, the National Meteorological Service (SMN) issued different levels of meteorological alert followed by "short-term warnings" due to the probability of the occurrence of severe storms with intense rains, gusts and hail for various localities in the Province of Buenos Aires. among them the city of La Plata. As a result of this, and due to the impact that began to be recorded in the center of the Province, the Argentine Red Cross issued the "red alert level" for its territorial network with a focus on the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires (AMBA).

After 6:45 p.m., intense rainfall began to be recorded in La Plata that caused flooding of streets for short periods of time, a situation that quickly normalized until 7:45 p.m. where more than 100 millimeters of water fell in less than 2 hours caused severe flooding that resulted in effects on the main streets of the city both in the city and in the city. downtown area as well as peripheral neighborhoods, mainly in the northern part of the city. These floods generated the entry of water into homes, the power cut in 60% of the town, stranded cars and in many cases floating on public roads, and forced dozens of families to self-evacuate and evacuate during the first hours of the phenomenon.

After 2 a.m., the situation began to normalize, resulting in more than 90 families evacuated in formal temporary accommodation (enabled by the Municipality of La Plata) and informal accommodation (opened by neighbors and civil society organizations), in addition to a hundred families who self-evacuated, while hundreds of neighbors, Despite the influx of water into their homes, they chose to stay in their homes for fear of theft or for fear of losing their property.

Around 5 a.m., new rainfall – minor – was recorded over the city, preventing in some cases the normal runoff of water that remained on the streets.

The above motivated the Argentine Red Cross to declare its level of "Category 1 Emergency" according to the institution's National Response Plan, mobilizing in addition to the entire response structure of the La Plata Branch, various resources in the region, in support of the most exposed communities and local and regional authorities that were working in the field. the area.

Although the most complex situation is currently registered in La Plata, the numbers of the first evaluations emerge from the entire area affected by the hydrometeorological event, which includes the entire metropolitan area and center of the Province.

summary: An earthquake of 4.0 magnitude shook Rasuwa district of Nepal at 9:45 AM local time. According to Mr. Babulal Tamange, President, Nepal Red Cross Society, Rasuwa District Chapter till now there is no any information about the loss and damanges noted due to the earthquake.

countries.name: Nepal

summary:

The local government has made annoucement that the affected families will be provided with NPR. 50,000.00 support to recostruct the damaged houses.

Accroding to President of Nepal Red Red Cross Society, Bhojpur District Chapter has mobilized its human resources to support the affected families with Non-food releif item.

countries.name: Argentina
