summary:
After the heavy and continuous rains in the city of Gualeguay, from Thursday, March 14 until yesterday, March 18, at 11:00 a.m. 514 mm of water accumulated in lower areas of the city. countries.name: Mozambique

summary:
Tropical Storm Filipo is expected to make landfall by early morning 12 March, between Govuro and Vilankulos (Sofala & Inhambane Provinces). The forcasted trajectory of TS Filipo is expected to go down Inhanbane, through Gaza, and out through Maputo province on March 13th. TS Filipo may bring windspeeds of 85Km/h up to a max of 120km/h in some locations. 

The main concern with TS Filipo is the potential flooding across most of the central/southern country due to increased rainfall. It is expected that there will be destriction of crops, flooding of roads & collapse of bridges, flooding of low-laying areas, and flooding of areas near rivers. 

Areas of concern:
Inhambane: Govuro, Vilankulo, Massinga, Inhassoro, Mabote,Panda, Homoine, Morrumbene, Inhambane city and Maxixe
Sofala: Machanga, Chibabava and Buzi
Gaza: Massingir, Chokwe, Chongoene, Bilene, Limpopo, Mandlakazi, Chicualacuala, Mapai,Mabalane, Chigubo, Chibuto, Guija and Cidade de Xai-Xai
Maputo: Flood prone area along Incomati, Umbeluzi and Maputo basins

Overall, up to 12.7 Million people (worst case scenario) could be affected indirectly by flooding. Specifically in Sofala only, government forecasts 136,583 people will be affected overall, with the most affected in southern districts (16,846 people). Government has not yet released potential impacts for other provinces.

countries.name: Cameroon

name: RMC: Other - 03-2024 - High Winds Yaoundé
summary:
On the night of March 08, 2024, heavy rain accompanied by strong winds fell in the city of Yaoundé, Mfoundi Department . Several districts of the department  are concerned, the most affected of which are the districts of Yaoundé 3 and Yaoundé 6.

As a result of this heavy rain, several houses were destroyed as well as household equipment and furniture.  The force of the storm led to the destruction of electrical installations, which plunged the affected areas into darkness. 

According to the information gathered, several neighbourhoods have been affected, including NGOA-EKELLE (University Residential Area);  EFOULAN; MVOGT BETSI; MELEN;OBILI and ETOUG EBE. 

Faced with this situation, the Departmental Committee of MFOUNDI conducted on March 9, an assessment of the situation in the most affected neighborhoods of OBILI, more precisely in front of the Presidential Guard (MELEN BLOCK 8), and ETOUG EBE behind the high school. The provisional toll is: 05 injured, including a pregnant woman;  01 deceased;  several houses partially destroyed due to torn roofs and cracked walls;school infrastructure partially destroyed;  damaged home  equipment; destroyed school supplies; official documents (birth certificates, National Identity Cards, diplomas, etc.) destroyed;  Damaged electronic devices (computers)  

Some residents are trying to redo temporary roofs to shelter from the next rains.

During this assessment visit, about a hundred affected families were visited and several material damages, cases of injury and one death were reported. It should be noted that these neighbourhoods have experienced an explosion in population since the crisis-related population movements in the North-West and South-West regions. These neighborhoods are home to thousands of internally displaced persons (IDPs). Displaced populations live in precarious conditions and are mostly unemployed.The situation in which they find themselves after this rain only exacerbates their already worrying situation, these populations need urgent assistance. 

The rainy season is at the beginning of its season and these populations remain exposed to flooding just as much as the entire city of Yaoundé.

countries.name: Nigeria
dtype.name: Other
name: NGA: Other - 03-2024 - HERDERS ATTACKS
summary:
In the early hours of yesterday evening, unexpected herder attacks led to an alarming loss of lives and injuries. More than 40 innocent people lost their lives while many others suffered severe physical injuries. The scene was chaotic and heart-wrenching, with locals scrambling for their lives and safety.

The hostile activities didn't stop at mere bloodshed; they escalated further into extensive displacement. Families were forced out from their homes with immediate effect due to fear and unpredictability sparked by these violent occurrences. Infrastructure was damaged as well, contributing further to the bleak scenario unfolding here.

At present, local law enforcement agencies are on high alert to prevent any further violence or destruction of property. They're also laboring relentlessly to apprehend the culprits behind this horrific act while lending as much assistance as possible to those affected.

It is crucial that we pool our resources together during such challenging times to provide relief measures for the victims who have been displaced from their homes amidst this turmoil. Your support will be invaluable in delivering immediate aid regarding food, clothing, shelter and medical supplies.

countries.name: Nigeria

summary:
According to the Information received for the Divisional secretary of Ukum division crisis broke out after kidnap, murder of deadly militia leader by rival gang in the Ukum LGA of Benue State

According to report, over 45 persons including a family of seven feared death following the invasion of Gbagir community in the Ukum LGA by suspected Fulani militia men who according to report are been supported by another Tiv arm gang in the Ukum LGA. The report review that this was a fight to oust another Tiv militia gang in the area.

It was gather that most of the dead were members of the rival militia gangs while about 12 innocent farmers were caught in the cross fire which also left over 30 persons injured and many others are declared missing.

According to information, the bloody fight started on Tuesday morning after a Tiv militia leader in the Ukum LGA kidnapped another Fulani militia leader and his family members from the neighboring Chinkai community in the Wukari LGA of Taraba State. Though after a ransom of about N5million was given the gang leaders stills his hostages. And accordingly the killing of the hostage sparked outrage among his gang members in the Taraba State.

According to information, the combined forces of Fulani and Tiv militia gangs started moving into the bushes of Gbagir in their hundreds from Sunday to sack the gang that killed Alhaji Gana the Fulani militia leader from Taraba State. And on Tuesday morning the bloody fight ensued. And from the information gathered over 45 persons who were mainly bandits have been killed and though over 12 farmers were caught in the cross fire and over 30 persons were injured and others are reported missing, and another information has it that the two gangs are evacuating some of their dead members.

Information also review that caught in the cross fire is a family of seven in Tse Adzandeh Mbasaa, Mbajiga, Ityuluv, Torov council ward of Ukum LGA. It was gathered that the Governor of Benue State have alerted the military for swift action.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Flood
name: ARG: Flood - 03-2024 - Flash Floods - Currents
summary:
During the early hours of today, the City of Corrientes, Capital of the Province of Corrientes (Argentina), recorded approximately 200 millimeters of water in less than 5 hours as a result of strong storms, causing sudden floods, being one of the worst in the history of the City. 

Due to this situation, even the first response agencies were affected, a situation that delayed evacuation and rescue tasks, with the neighbors themselves supporting each other during the first hours of the event. At the time of filing this report, rains continue to be recorded in the city, although in many neighborhoods it began to drain quickly, resulting in extensive structural damage and damage to basic goods. 

Most of the basic services are interrupted (Communication, Electricity, Water); It is estimated that the restoration in some areas may begin soon, while in others it will take a few days. 

The Governor of the Province declared an emergency, and the crisis committee was formed, which maintains contact with the Red Cross.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Flood
name: ARG: Flood - 03-2024 - Inundaciones en Corrientes
summary:
Durante la madrugada del 3 de marzo se registraron precipitaciones intensas de más de 200 mm en 4 horas sobre la Capital de la Provincia de Corrientes y alrededores, siendo ésta la inundación más grande de la historia de la Ciudad. Se estimó que más de 400.000 personas fueron afectadas, de las cuales al menos 17.000 lo fueron de manera directa. Las principales afectaciones se vincularon al ingreso de agua en las viviendas y cortes en el suministro eléctrico. El Gobierno de la Provincia de Corrientes declaró el estado de Emergencia y se encontraba trabajando para asistir a las personas afectadas. Según estimaciones de la Defensa Civil Provincial, se reportaron 996 personas evacuadas ubicadas en los centros establecidos en los Barrios Laguna Seca, Mil Viviendas, Ciudades Correntinas, Anahí, San Ignacio y San Jorge. A las 17 hs se reportó la recuperación de los servicios básicos en el 60% de la ciudad, pero continuaba el trabajo con aproximadamente 3.000 operarios en las zonas más bajas, donde el agua se había acumulado. Los asentamientos más afectados fueron los barrios La Olla, Ongay, Santa Teresita y Ponce.

Si bien el agua ya se escurrió en gran parte de la ciudad, en las zonas más bajas el drama continúa y se estima que muchas familias tardarán cerca de una semana en volver a sus casas, en algunos sectores se empezó a restablecer el servicio energético de la capital provincial.

Actualmente el Municipio se encuentra limpiando y profundizado el canal de descarga de la Olla lo mismo que en el barrio Molina Punta, al mismo tiempo el ministerio de Obras y Servicios Públicos, a través de operarios y equipos de Vialidad Urbana, en colaboración con el municipio capitalino, se encuentra limpiando cunetas de descarga  en el sector del asentamiento del Pirayui, obras que aseguran también un adecuado escurrimiento en el barrio de las 550 viviendas.

En el momento de este informe, aproximadamente 700 familias se encuentran alojadas en Centros de Evacuación, aguardando a que el nivel del agua que penetró en sus hogares disminuya para poder ingresar y recuperar lo que haya quedado tras las intensas lluvias.

countries.name: Algeria

summary:
On Thursday, the 29th of February 2024, significant flooding incidents occurred in two regions in the Wilaya of Jijel, exacerbating the already challenging situation caused by the recent heavy rainfall.

In the first region, AADL residencies, a total of 110 houses were affected. Families residing in these houses were forced to evacuate due to damages incurred, which rendered furniture, electronics, and household appliances unusable and ruined

Simultaneously, in the region of Al Ansar Daira, seven families were compelled to evacuate their homes and seek temporary shelter with relatives due to the flooding.

The added the number of families affected and evacuated reached a total of two hundred families.

countries.name: Bolivia
dtype.name: Flood
name: BOL: Flood - 02-2024 - Flood emergency - Bolivia 2024
summary:
On February 24, the Acre River overflowed in the department of Pando (border with Brazil). According to information from the Risk Management Unit (UGR) of the Municipality of Cobija (border with Brazil), so far a total of 15 sectors of the municipality have been flooded between rural and urban areas and a total of 3,604 families affected (approximately 18,020 people).

As a result of the events recorded since February 28, the municipality of Cobija has declared a Municipal Disaster to continue relief actions for the population. Currently, the activation of 8 shelters is registered at the municipal level with a total of 856 people. Likewise, the municipal authority has reported the closure of the bridge that connects the department of Pando with the city of Assis in Brazil due to the risk of rising river levels.

The emergency in the municipality of Cobija is added to a series of emergencies due to rains reported during the last week by the Vice Ministry of Civil Defense, according to estimates from the National Society based on the different information reported by municipal and departmental governments so far more than 28 thousand people would be affected by the rainy season since last week, likewise, the National Service of Hydrometeorology and Hydrology (SENHAMI) has declared a red hydrological alert in the departments of Pando and La Paz and an orange alert in the Departments of Beni, Santa Cruz, Cochabamba and Oruro based on rainfall forecasts for the next 7 days.

In addition to the declaration of emergency in the municipality of Cobija, emergency declarations have been registered in 4 municipalities of the department of Santa Cruz, 2 municipalities of La Paz, 2 municipalities of Oruro and 1 municipality of the department of Cochabamba, highlighting in particular the events registered below:

Santa Cruz: As a result of the flooding of the Pirai River on February 19, a total of 61 families in the municipalities of El Torno, Lagunillas, Quirusilla and Kereimba in high-risk areas have had to evacuate their homes due to the risk of the river overflowing. Likewise, the communities of the municipalities of Moro Moro, Samaipata, El Puente, Vallegrande, Pucará and Postrervalle are on alert on orange alert due to the continuity of the rains.

In Oruro, the overflow of the Paria River floods more than 20 urbanizations in the northern zone of where it caused damage to the homes of 800 families and 100 victims, which has caused their evacuation and referral to shelters.

In La Paz, the overflow of the river due to the intense rains caused the collapse of a platform in Lipari, municipality of Mecapaca (which is under a municipal disaster declaration), and the fall of a public lighting pole, the neighbors ended up incommunicado and without electricity. The population of Umamanta - Lipari has not yet found a solution to the lack of communication due to the collapse of the only road that connected them with the southern area of La Paz. Seven houses are at risk of landslides. Likewise, in the city of El Alto, the Negro River overflowed in District 9, flooding several homes and crops. The community of Pomamaya declared a state of emergency, they say that 50% of the families in the place are affected, they also lost livestock, barley and potato crops. They ask to build gabions in the river.

In Bolivia, floods can generate a series of negative impacts. Among them are the loss of human lives, damage to homes, infrastructure and crops, interruption of basic services such as drinking water and electricity, displacement of people, water contamination and spread of waterborne diseases, among others. Currently in the country, the hydrological forecasting unit of SENAMHI (National Meteorology and Hydrology Service) has issued a Red Alert as the floods of the Acre, La Paz and Ir Pavi rivers have reached critical heights in the country. The National Society continues to monitor the situation to contribute to the response to humanitarian needs in the different municipalities in emergency.

countries.name: Pakistan

summary:
As per the Meteorological Department's predictions, specific regions, notably Gwadar, have encountered exacerbated conditions due to intense rainfall, leading to floods and subsequent disturbances. On February 27th, 2024, torrential rains triggered flooding in Gwadar, submerging several areas including Gwadar city and Sarabandan. The Commissioner of Makran verified that Gwadar witnessed prolonged heavy rainfall spanning nine hours, resulting in the collapse of structures and inundation of settlements around Jinnah Avenue.

The Meteorological Department reports that rainfall has been registered across various districts of Balochistan, with Gwadar recording the highest accumulation at 58 millimeters. Additionally, locations such as Quetta, Dalbandin, Khuzdar, and Turbat also witnessed varying degrees of precipitation.

The department anticipates ongoing rainfall starting from February 29th, 2024, bringing significant downpours to different parts of the province until March 2nd. The following matrix provides details concerning the incurred losses.

Potential Consequences:
• Inclement weather like rainstorms and snowfall may lead to road closures and landslides.

Heavy snowfall, rainfall and low temperatures has affected most of Afghanistan resulting in casualties and widespread disruption to services, blocked roads and significant loss of livestock of livestock between February 26 - March 1. The provinces most affected are: Badghis, Badakhshan, Faryab, Jawzjan, Kandahar, Helmand and Sari Pul.

countries.name: Nigeria
dtype.name: Other
name: NGA: Other - 02-2024 - HERDERS ATTACKED IN THE UKUM LGA OF BENUE STATE
summary:
It is with a heavy heart that I write to inform you about the unfortunate event that has recently taken place in our homeland, specifically, in the Ukum Local Government Area (LGA) of Benue State

There was a sudden and brutal attack by herders which resulted in many casualties. The reports we have received so far are quite distressing - over 30 people have been reportedly killed and more than 10 others seriously injured

The aftermath of these attacks has led to an unprecedented displacement crisis as well, forcing over 40,000 residents from their homes. This situation is truly heartbreaking and requires urgent attention from all quarters. It's imperative for the authorities to step up security measures in vulnerable areas while also providing necessary aid to those displaced.

At present, we are trying to gather as much help as we can. Efforts are being made by local authorities and organizations alike to provide immediate assistance and relief measures for those affected by this tragedy, but there is so much more that needs to be done.

As always, thank you for your time and interest in hearing about what's happening here. We greatly appreciate any help you may be able to provide and look forward to hearing from you soon.

Note: We are still monitoring the situation and detail of the report which shall include the number of displaced persons and the locations were they are currently been camp or staying will be share to you in due course.

countries.name: Mozambique
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: MOZ: Population Movement - 02-2024 - IDPs in Nampula - Cabo Delgado conflict
summary:
Between 19-21 February, attacks in Chuire District led to a large outflow of people into neighboring Erati District, Nampula Province. Due to violence, humanitarian aid implementors in Cabo Delgado areas have had to pause aid delivery in the province. Efforts to reach IDPs in Nampula province are ongoing. Number of IDPs going to Nampula province is increasing rapidly due to the current violence and lack of food, schooling, and health care facilities in Cabo Delgado.Number of IDPs arriving in Erati increased exponentially on the 21st and 22nd of February. 

As of February 23rd, INGD estimates that 33,218 people / 5,976 families (4,100 men, 6,898 women, 11,096 boys, 8,989 girls including 249 pregnant women, 60 Persons with Disabilities, and 419 elderly) arrived in Erati district in Nampula province after fleeing Chiure district, Cabo Delgado due to fear of attacks. 

A joint government-cluster assessment team, including LNGOS, were in Erati on 24 and 25 February. The assessment was conducted using methodologies such as FGD with men and women in two sites: Macucha (transit site where IDPs are hosted at school) and Muanona (registration centre at school), key informant interview with IDP and government key informants, observations. Final report being compiled. Preliminary assessments indicate the need of shelter, water and basic sanitation and supplies such as hygiene kits, mosquito nets, and other basic household supplies. District authorities have requested immediate assistance from humanitarian organizations.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: BFA: Outbreak - 02-2024 - Measles BF2024
summary: Measles outbreaks have been recurrent in Burkina Faso over the past three years. From week 46 of the year 2023 to week 7 of the year 2024, Burkina Faso reported 2089 suspected cases of measles, resulting in seven (7) deaths. In the first seven weeks of 2024, all health facilities recorded 1714 suspected cases of measles. These cases were mainly reported by the Centre, Centre-Nord, Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun and Hauts-Bassins regions. The health districts of Boulmiougou, Bogodogo, Ouahigouya, Tougouri, Boromo and Solenzo are experiencing active measles outbreaks. A new measles outbreak has been declared in the Orodara health district in the Hauts-Bassins region (3 cases at H6 _2024 and 18 cases at S7_2024). The new districts at risk of epidemic in week 7 of 2024 are Houndé, Sapouy Fada, Kaya, Dori. The median age of confirmed cases is 2 years with the minimum age of 1 month and the maximum age of 50 years. Men accounted for 51.38% of confirmed measles cases. The overall trend is upward in all regions of the country. This led the health authorities to formulate a request for support to the CRBF on February 22, 2024.

countries.name: Cameroon

name: CMR: Population displacement - 02-2024 - Movement of Chadian populations in Logone Birni
summary:
On February 21, 2024 at around 3 p.m., four traditional chiefs from the village of GAMAL (Chadian locality) took refuge in the locality of GALA in Cameroon followed by their community. This sudden displacement is said to have started from land disputes with an army general. The populations feeling insecure have moved to Cameroon in the locality of Gala (a neighboring village located on the other side of the Logone River), in the Logone Birni District. To date, there are 225 families with nearly 700 people with special needs (pregnant and breastfeeding women, the elderly, orphaned children, the injured, the disabled).

 These families live in huts, sheds built with makeshift materials, defecating in the open. Settled on the banks of the river, these communities use the water of the river as it is for all use and consumption, which exposes them to the high risk  of waterborne diseases, including cholera.  These communities need urgent assistance.

countries.name: Comoros
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: COM: 2024 Cholera Outbreak
summary:
Following confirmed tests, the Comoros Ministry of Health declared a cholera epidemic on Friday, February 2, 2024, at 8 p.m. local time. A Cholera Treatment Center (CTC) has been activated in Samba to treat cholera cases (hospital on the outskirts of Moroni). This has been confirmed by the Dar Es Alam Laboratory and reaffirmed by the Comoros Ministry of Health. The spread of cholera is progressing steadily. The first locally transmitted cases appeared on Monday, February 5, 2024. As of February 11, a total of 33 cases were confirmed (13 being treated in the CTC, and 2 deaths registered from Grande Comores).

The Comoros Red Crescent is playing a central role in this epidemic. It is recognized as the entity with the most experience and is therefore very much in demand/expected to take part in many activities. The authorities have requested support from the Comoros Red Crescent for various activities:

● Disinfection of homes of patients and contacts.

● Raising public awareness.

● Training health staff.

● Supporting the management and cleaning of cholera treatment centres (CTCs).

● Cholera burials.

countries.name: Malaysia
dtype.name: Heat Wave
name: MYS: Heat Wave - 02-2024 - MYS: Heat Wave 2024 # 1
summary:
Nine areas in the peninsula and one in Sabah recorded alert-level hot weather as of 6 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).

In a statement posted on its Facebook page, MetMalaysia said the nine areas in the peninsula are Langkawi Island, Kota Setar, Yan, Pendang, Pokok Sena, Sik, Baling in Kedah; Seberang Perai Utara in Penang and Kuala Kangsar, Perak, while the area affected in Sabah is Beaufort.

The alert level refers to a daily maximum temperature of 35° to 37°Celsius for at least three consecutive days.

MetMalaysia had previously issued a statement, saying that the country was currently experiencing the final phase of the northeast monsoon, which is expected to last until the end of March.

The department said during the phase, cloud formation and rainfall distribution were generally lower in most places, especially in the northern areas of the peninsula, including Perak, as well as in Pahang and Kelantan.

The absence of rain for a long period could lead to hotter and drier weather than usual, it added.

Hot weather during this period is a recurring phenomenon that occurs annually from February to May. During this period, the daily maximum temperature may surpass 35°Celsius in the early afternoon.

Distressing news to share regarding an unfortunate incident that recently occurred in the Apa LGA.  A group of herders launched a devastating attack on the Imana-Ikobi community and the Adijah Ugbokpo  within the Apa LGA of Benue State. it is reported that many people have lost their lives during the attacked on the 14th February, 2024 with numerous others suffering from injuries of varying severity. According to report the attackers opened fire on the residents and killed unspecified number of persons, and the most of the residents have fled to other nearby communities for safety.

Many families are mourning while others are desperately hoping their loved ones will recover swiftly from their injuries. According to information from the Red Cross Division in the Apa LGA, Suepected Herders invaded and attacked Adijah-Ugbokpo in the Apa LGA along the Oweto-otukpo road about 3:pm. the attackers opened fire on the residenets and killed unspecified numger of persons, the communities have be dispalced into other villages seeking for safety.

name: NGA: Population Movement - 02-2024 - MOVEMENT DISPLACEMENT FOR FEAR OF ATTACKS BY HERDERS
summary:
There's an alarming situation developing in the Gwer LGA and Kwande LGA, Benue State. It's come to my knowledge that there has been a mass displacement movement among the community members due to fear of impending attacks by local herders.
 
According to report from the divisional secretary of the Nigerian Red Cross Benue State Branch has it that over a week now the community members have be moving out of their community for fear of attack from the Fulani Herders whose number is increasing daily in the community. According to information some of the displaced persons are  moving to  LGA Headquarters for safety.
 
The tension escalated rapidly over the last few days, creating a sense of insecurity within the community circle. The residents are now leaving their homes and seeking refuge elsewhere for their safety, leading to a sudden exodus that is disturbing as well as heart-wrenching.
 
It seems that despite attempts from local authorities at maintaining peace, they have not succeeded in reassuring the inhabitants about their security concerns which is causing them to flee.
 
This crisis calls for immediate attention and action on our part. We need assistance from all possible quarters – government bodies, non-profit organizations and even individuals who can provide either financial help or physical resources such as food, clothing or shelter for these displaced people.
 
Would appreciate any guidance or support you could render in this hour of need – every bit counts! Also please share this information with others who might be able to help anyway.

countries.name: Cameroon
dtype.name: Fire
name: RMC: Fire - 02-2024 - KOLOFATA fire
summary:
On the morning of Thursday, February 08, 2024, the internally displaced persons of the IDP camps of Manawatchi, Ndaba, Bamé-mélleri, Kidjimatari and Kordo, installed in the city center of Kolofata on the outskirts of Mayo, were surprised by a fire. Of accidental origin according to the testimonies received, the fire spread at an exponential speed, setting fire to several households in the above-mentioned IDP camps, and whose structures are essentially made of local and temporary materials (millet stalks, tree branches, etc.). The fire lasted about 2 hours before being brought under control by the population.

The Kolofata District Committee, supported by the Departmental Committee, immediately went to the field to provide support (evacuation of the victims; participation in the control of the fire) to the population and conducted a rapid assessment which  reported the destruction of material property (houses, sleeping equipment; kitchen utensils, clothes, food reserves), small financial savings were completely destroyed, serious injuries (1 56-year-old woman) and loss of life (7- and 9-year-old children). A total of 189 households, i.e. approximately 1323 people directly affected. This evaluation involved 6 volunteers.

As soon as the situation was triggered, the Sub-Prefect of the District of Kolofata and his staff, as well as all the traditional authorities, went to the field to take stock of the situation. Other humanitarian actors have remained absent in the area since the call was issued following the kidnapping of Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) personnel.

     Dueto the insecurity in the area; The victims remained at the scene. Community solidarity under the leadership of religious and traditional authorities (Lawanes and Blamas) was set up and the victims were able to receive a few makeshift mats, tarpaulins and used loincloths. 

         The Cameroon Red Cross, through the local branch, continues to provide psychological support to the community and to monitor the evolution of the situation.

countries.name: Georgia
dtype.name: Storm Surge
name: GEO: Storm Surge - 02-2024 - Avalanche, Landslides, Floods in Western Georgia
summary:
As for the Rapid Assessment information, on February 6-7, 2024, Georgia was struck by a series of catastrophic natural disasters, significantly impacting several municipalities. In the regions of Khulo and Keda, heavy snowfall triggered avalanches and landslides, resulting in tragic fatalities and extensive property damage. Particularly poignant was the incident in Zemo Tkhilvana village, where an avalanche buried a house, claiming the life of a 63-year-old woman, and landslides causing widespread destruction in the surrounding areas. Concurrently, the mountainous region of Svaneti, including the Mele village, was severely affected by heavy snowfall and avalanches, leading to infrastructure collapse, blocked roads, and prolonged power outages. In the Lentekhi area, a house was completely destroyed by fire, exacerbated by the inaccessibility for emergency services due to the blocked roads. The Adjara region faced a landslide in the Keda-Tsaniaris area, tragically resulting in the death of a policeman, with the landslide's devastation extending to 10 neighbouring communities, severing crucial connections and isolating villages. This was further complicated by catastrophic floods in Shuakhevi-Kokotauri, leaving Buturauli village in ruins. Similarly, in Samegrelo, 340 families were affected by floods and strong winds that damaged houses and infrastructure, with particular mention of Anaklia, where 16 families suffered extensive flooding and property loss. In Martvili, strong winds caused significant structural damage. The village of Khidikuri in the Shida Kartli region's Khashuri Municipality witnessed overwhelming floods from the Tiliana river, leading to submerged electric substations and extensive damage to residential areas and agricultural fields. Imereti region, specifically the village of Nergeeti in Baghdati, suffered a landslide late at night, causing loss of life and large-scale destruction, burying four houses and leaving several people, including a family of four, missing. This series of disasters across Georgia created a complex emergency scenario, with varying degrees of destruction and humanitarian needs in each affected region.

The affected municipalities by regions:

1. Adjara - Keda, Khulo, Shuakhevi

2. Svaneti - Mele, Lentekhi

3. Samegrelo - Martvili, Tsalenjikha, Anaklia, Chkhorotksu

countries.name: Trinidad and Tobago
countries.society_name: The Trinidad and Tobago Red Cross Society
dtype.name: Other
name: TTO: Other - 02-2024 - Tobago Oil Spill Incident - Canoe Bay Industrial Estate
summary:
On Wednesday 7th February 2024, at 7am reports were recieved by the Tobago Emergency Management Agency (TEMA) of the appareance of an oil-like substance washing onshore at Canoe Bay which is a remote part of the Tobago Shoreline just off the Cove Eco-Industrial Estate. That day officials of the Tobago House of Assembly (THA) and TEMA hosted a media conference indicating that an unidentified vessel had overturned about 200 meters from the costline and was eminating and oil-like substance which began to wash ashore. The THA mobilized assets and divers from its Maritime Services Unit to 1. Identify the vessel and 2. Determine if any souls were on board, the results were inconclusive as divers could not get a good view in the murky waters. However a diver was able to make out the marking "Gulfstream" on the vessel however they were not able to find the IMO vessel identifier therefore to today the vessel is still unidentified. There were no evidence that persons were onboard the vessel. In the past few days coastal clean up has been ongoing. The THA Chief Secretary and TEMA have been calling the incident a Tier 2 diaster where all national resources would be needed. Today there were reports that international assistance may be needed to help contain the situation, which would automatically make the incident an official disaster at level 3. In past major oil spill situation international assistance was needed so this is not new to have international technical assistance mobilized to support. 

A GIS representation of the affected area was done by TEMA and can be accessed here: https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=791943569640726&set=pcb.791943722974044 As the area of the overtunred vessel is solely industrial the only impact is to the environment there is not community near by. The area where the oil is coming onshore is not a tourist site not a fishing port. There may be long term damage to the coral reef at Canoe Bay which may have knock on effects with fishing areas in the vicinity. Assessments for this has not been started.

countries.name: Kenya

countries.name: Democratic Republic of Congo
countries.society_name: Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: DRC : Population Movement - 2024
summary:
Since the beginning of 2024, an intensification of the conflict between the armed forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and their allies against M23 rebel group has had devastating effects on civilians in several towns within North Kivu. Notably, the towns of Mweso, Bambo, Katsiru, Sake, and Goma have been severely impacted. The M23 armed groups have blocked the two main roads leading into Goma, a major city in the region with a population of approximately two million people. As a result, Goma is now isolated from the surrounding farms that supply it with essential resources for now several days.

The ongoing fighting has forced the displacement of around 135,000 people to Goma and an additional 100,000 people into South Kivu (specifically Minova). These displaced individuals face immense challenges, including limited access to basic necessities. The conflict situation is severely restricting humanitarian access to hundreds

of thousands of people in need. The sites designated for internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Goma are overloaded and unable to accommodate new arrivals. International humanitarian organizations operating in the region are facing operational challenges. Some of these organizations are reducing their capacity by evacuating and relocating personnel based in Goma. While most analysts consider a full takeover of Goma by M23 to be unlikely, such an event would have catastrophic humanitarian consequences not only within eastern DRC but also in neighboring countries.

countries.name: Colombia
dtype.name: Drought
name: COL: Droughts - 02-2024
summary: On 27 January 2024, by Decree No. 037, the Government of Colombia declared a National Disaster Situation for a period of 12 months, due to the impact of the "El Niño" phenomenon, which is a climate variability phenomenon that occurs every two to seven years due to the warming of the Pacific Ocean (1). This comes after the Institute of Hydrology, Meteorology, and Environmental Studies (IDEAM, by its initials in Spanish) officially declared the presence of the "El Niño" phenomenon in Colombia on 3 November 2023 (2). The National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD, by its initials in Spanish), through Circular 065 of 18 December 2023, sent to the territories and other members of the National Disaster Risk Management System the guidelines for the preparation and readiness for the events under the influence of the "El Niño" phenomenon 2023-2024, where it is indicated that excess and deficit of precipitation may occur depending on the territory, generating water shortages for aqueducts, mass movements, water shortages for crops, floods, water shortages for animals, gales, forest fires, torrential floods, frosts, river erosion, among others. In recent months, the "El Niño" phenomenon has had evident effects throughout the national territory. During December 2023, precipitation was below normal with a complete absence of rainfall in a large part of the Caribbean region and some areas of the Andean region. Likewise, an average temperature increase of more than 2°C was recorded in departments of the Andean, Caribbean, Pacific, and Orinoco natural regions, including Cesar, Cordoba, Antioquia, Santander, Norte de Santander, Tolima, Huila, Nariño and Casanare. For example, on 23 January 2024, the municipality of Jerusalem (Cundinamarca) reported a record temperature of 40.4 Celsius. Regarding the evolution of the "El Niño" phenomenon in the country, during January 2024, the country was under the influence of strong category events, including rainfall deficits of up to 70%. Due to the scarcity of precipitation and the increase in the average temperature, forest fires have caused 586 municipalities in 28 departments to be on red alert as of 23 January 2024.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.society_name: Red Cross Society of Bosnia and Herzegovina
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: BIH: Epidemic - 01-2024 - Measles Outbreak
summary:
The outbreak of measles in Bosnia and Herzegovina began at the beginning of 2024. According to official data from the Institute of Public Health of the Federation of BiH, in the last three months, from January to March 2024, a total of 1,329 cases of measles have been reported, with the highest number in the Sarajevo Canton (875 cases) and the Tuzla Canton (396 cases).

Initially, in January and February 2024 the highest number of cases was recorded in Bijeljina, Banja Luka, and the Tuzla Canton, specifically in the cities of Tuzla and Živinice. Subsequently, the number increased in the Sarajevo Canton, especially in the mid March where it is still on the rise. Measles cases have also been reported in the Brčko District of BiH. In addition to measles, cases of pertussis (whooping cough) and varicella (chickenpox) are also being recorded. Due to the increased number of cases, a measles epidemic was declared in Bijeljina in February 2024, followed by one in Banja Luka. According to official data from the Institute of Public Health of Republika Srpska, as of March 22, 2024, there have been 30 cases of measles and 125 cases of pertussis reported. The highest number of pertussis cases was recorded in Banja Luka, totaling 105. In the Brčko District of BiH, 28 cases of measles have been reported. According to official data, the vaccination rate is only 52%. Comparing monthly data, a significant increase can be observed from 76 cases in January 2024 to 289 cases in February and 906 cases in March 2024. Due to the deteriorating epidemiological situation in the Tuzla Canton, the Ministry of Health of the Tuzla Canton, upon the proposal of the Institute of Public Health of the Tuzla Canton, issued an order declaring a measles epidemic in the Tuzla Canton on February 23, 2024. In addition to measles, 69 cases of pertussis were recorded in the Tuzla Canton from January to March 2024. By the end of the first week of April, a total of 1,007 cases of measles had been reported in the Sarajevo Canton, mainly among children aged 1 to 4 years (42.4%), followed by the age group of 5 to 9 years (29%) and the age group of 10 to 14 years (11%). There were also 65 cases of measles reported among individuals aged 30 to 65 years. Due to the increased number of reported cases, a measles epidemic was declared in the Sarajevo Canton on February 10, 2024. In addition to the measles outbreak, the Sarajevo Canton has also been burdened with a higher number of pertussis cases. The Ministry of Health of the Sarajevo Canton declared an epidemic of pertussis, also known as whooping cough, on March 12 for the territory of the canton. A total of 112 cases of pertussis were recorded in the Sarajevo Canton from January to March 2024. Cases of pertussis were also reported in the Zenica-Doboj Canton, specifically 88 cases from January to March 2024. Hospital visits are prohibited due to this situation. Additional complications due to chickenpox: During the period from January to March 2024, a higher number of chickenpox cases were recorded, totaling close to 1,500 cases, with the highest numbers in the Sarajevo Canton (357), the Tuzla Canton (308), the Una-Sana Canton (296), and Herzegovina (260). These data represent the situation for January and February 2024. Vaccination coverage rate According to health authorities, less than 60% of the population is vaccinated against measles and rubella. In 2022, Bosnia and Herzegovina achieved a vaccination rate of 60% with two doses of the measles vaccine, which is significantly below the prescribed level of the World Health Organization. Due to the infodemic, an increasing number of young parents are deciding not to vaccinate their children out of fear of worsening their children's health conditions, autism, and the like. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, public trust in vaccines is decreasing, which is one of the reasons for the low vaccination rates and general acceptance of all vaccines. There is a need for considerable efforts to be made to promote and preserve health, emphasize the importance of immunization, and prevent diseases. Measures to mitigate the risk and contain the spread of the disease During the epidemic, measures provided for by laws on the protection of the population from infectious diseases will be implemented. These measures include education on the prevention of infectious diseases, early detection of sources of infection and transmission routes, reporting and isolation of the sick, hospitalization and treatment, as well as enhanced immunization of children, where the Red Cross in Bosnia and Herzegovina plays a significant role.

countries.name: Comoros
dtype.name: Civil Unrest
name: COM: 01-2024 Post-Election Civil Unrest
summary: After the elections organized on 14th January 2024 in the Union of Comoros, the provisional results of the elections for the President of the Union of the Comoros and the 3 Governors were announced at 7 p.m. on Tuesday 16th January 2024. The outgoing President and his 3 Governors of the 3 islands won the elections from the first round with a percentage of more than 50% for the Governors and 62,97% for the President, but there was only 16.30% turnout, according to the official figures announced by the Electoral Commission (Céni). This victory should enable him the President to run for a third consecutive term and remain in power until 2029. The opposition, which is calling for the election to be annulled, has denounced gross fraud" and "ballot box stuffing, calling the population to protest. Due to that situation, the population began demonstrating, blocking the roads with stones and burning the vehicles and some administrative buildings. The national police and army reacted by spreading the population, using tear gas. On Wednesday 17 January, around 30 people were admitted to El-Maarouf national hospital. Road blockages and clashes between the population and the police/army continued on Thursday 18 January, affecting more injured people who have been assisted by Comoros Red Crescent volunteers. Some of them have been transferred to the hospitals. Most businesses kept their curtains down, schools and markets stayed closed, internet was cut and has been very unstable since then. Buildings were vandalized and set on fire, a rice warehouse was looted, and roads blocked by piles of stones and sticks. A night-time curfew has been in place since Wednesday until an unspecified date. A number of arrests have been made, but no figures have been released. However, there have been protests every day. On 24 January, the supreme court announced of final results of the election confirming the re-election of the previous president and 3 governors. A 5-day curfew has been put in place in the country and a big number of army is deployed in many areas to control and ensure security as more demonstrations are expected to happen since the opposition is contesting the results and all their appeals have been rejected.

countries.name: Australia
dtype.name: Flood
name: AUS: Flood - 01-2024 - QLD Severe Weather Jan-Feb 2024
summary:
Tropical Cyclone Kirrily formed on Thursday 25 January 2024 and made landfall as a category 3 cyclone overnight and quickly weakened to a tropical low.

The resulting Tropical Low has produced HEAVY to INTENSE RAINFALL and DAMAGING WINDS to parts of the northern interior and western Queensland. As at 0600 hours 28 January, Ex-Tropical Cyclone Kirrily will remain over inland Queensland in coming days, bringing the risk of significant and widespread rain and flooding to areas of the northern interior, central and western Queensland. 

The low is likely to remain slow moving during the week with potential to move north towards the Gulf of Carpentaria, northwest over the NT or even towards the east coast of north Queensland. At this stage the likelihood of it redeveloping into a tropical cyclone is very low.  

 

On 25 January a cyclone shelter and a place of refuge were opened in Townsville in preparation for TC Kirrily making landfall. In total, nineteen (19) people presented to the Heatley cyclone shelter and 9 people presented at the Townsville refuge in the shelter. 

Whilst Kirrily did not bring the anticipated destruction, the impacts are still being felt by thousands of homes. As at 0600 28 January 23,000 homes remain without power, with Townsville City Council encouraging residents to continue conserving water as the city’s water infrastructure is impacted due to power outage. Townsville City Council have noted health concerns among vulnerable residents due to loss of power and are prioritising access to generators. National Broadband Network and voice data services remain impacted with over 8800 services being affected. On ground rapid impact assessments continue.  

 

As at 27 January, 783 damage assessments have been completed with 35 properties identified as having sustained minor to moderate damage. A number of roads also continue to remain closed due to flash flooding, road damage and debris. Across the state, 16,000 tonnes of incoming freight (including 11,000 tonnes of mining materials) is being blocked. Many communities along the Gulf of Carpentaria remain isolated due to road closures, including Burketown, Doomadgee Normanton, and Gregory.

 

Joint Commonwealth-state Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements (DRFA) have been activated to fund counter disaster operations for Burdekin and Hinchinbrook Shire Councils, Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council and Townsville City Council. The Queensland Government has announced disaster support for communities affected by Tropical Cyclone Kirrily.

Personal hardship financial assistance is now available to residents in Burdekin Shire and Townsville City Local Government Areas. This includes Emergency Hardship, Essential Services Hardship Assistance, Essential Services Safety and Reconnection and Housing assistance is available for residents affected by this event.

As at 29 January six (6) Recovery Hubs will be operating across the Townsville and Burdekin Local Governments areas.

countries.name: Mongolia
dtype.name: Chemical Emergency
name: MNG: Chemical Emergency - 01-2024 - Gas explosion in Urban area
summary:
At 1:25 AM on January 24, 2024, a gas truck exploded on Dunjingarav Street, 26th Khoroo, Bayanzurkh District, Ulaanbaatar City, Mongolia, due to a slippery road condition. The incident impacted a 30-40 meter area, specifically affecting the 207th Apartment, housing 63 households (200 people). Regrettably, three firefighters lost their lives, and 15 individuals, including three children, were hospitalized. Additionally, 61 people, including 17 children and three infants, were evacuated to the hotel and 136th Elementary School in Bayanzurkh District. The remaining 135 displaced people are staying at relatives and friends. 

As of 8 AM, local authorities have successfully contacted 196 families, while 1 family remains unreachable. The National Police Office has temporarily closed main roads within 200-500 meters around the affected area for an indefinite period to ensure public safety.

countries.name: Brazil
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: BRA: Epidemic - 01-2024 - Dengue epidemic, - Arbovirus
summary:
In the first week of April, Brazil surpassed the mark of 3 million dengue cases in 2024. This figure is the highest ever recorded in the entire historical series of the disease in the country, which dates back to the 2000s. At least 13 states and more than 230 municipalities have declared a state of health emergency. 

We understand that there are many factors that have led to this moment: increase in temperatures and rainfall due to climatic phenomena, inadequate basic sanitation, insufficient number of health workers, low effectiveness of government actions to control Aedes aegypti, discontinuity of actions throughout the year, difficulty for the population to eliminate domestic breeding sites,  mosquito resistance to insecticides and the existence of four serotypes circulating at the same time in the country, which favors reinfections.

The Ministry of Health announced on March 18 that it had set aside R$1.5 billion to help states and municipalities in dengue emergencies and has also taken a series of actions to support the response across the country.

Brazil's southern, southeastern and central-western states have the highest concentration of cases and population, which translates into high numbers. We also identified the situation of communities with greater vulnerabilities (less sanitation and education) as a factor in the increase in cases.

The Unified Health System (SUS) is overloaded and has had to expand its structure for care, diagnosis and control of the mosquito.

summary:
On the night of January 23, 2023, at 00:09, a strong earthquake with a magnitude of 8 occurred. The epicenter of the earthquake was located on the border between Kyrgyzstan and China, near the Kyzylsu-Kyrgyz Autonomous Region.

In the Jeti-Oguz district of the Issyk-Kul region, the earthquake was felt with an intensity of 7 points. In the cities of Karakol and Kaji-Sai, its strength reached 4.5 points, in Naryn - 4 points, and in the Kyrgyzstan, Bishkek, - 3 points.

According to initial data from the Ministry of Emergency Situations of the Kyrgyz Republic, there were no casualties or significant damages as a result of the earthquake.

countries.name: Marshall Islands
dtype.name: Storm Surge
name: Marshall Islands: Storm Surge - 2024
summary:
Powerful waves, driven by offshore storm surges, struck several areas in the Marshall Islands on Saturday, January 20. Local media reports indicate that the waves caused flooding, impacting two airports at Ailinglaplap Atoll. The airports remain closed due to rocks, coral, and debris, with repairs expected to take weeks. Additionally, the Army base experienced substantial damage from the massive waves. 

As per a brief update from the IFRC delegate deployed to the Sub Office in the North Pacific, this event originated from a powerful winter storm system in the far northern Pacific. The strong winds generated a large swell that reached Roi Namur Islet in the northern part of Kwajalein Atoll, affecting the US Military base.

This weather-driven wave and inundation event, distinct from a tsunami, resulted from a significant wind-generated swell breaking on the Roi-Namur shores. Reports suggest inundation in other locations, including Arno Atoll and the runway in Ailinglapalap of Marshall Islands.

Limited and delayed ground reports hint at potential impacts on other islands and atolls. Coastal evacuations occurred in Kosrae of Federated States of Micronesia(FSM), with islands across the FSM experiencing inundation.

NOAA staff indicate the possibility of more extensive damage than the December 2008 flood event in the RMI, comparable to the December 2021 King Tide inundation event across the FSM.

summary: 42 migrants, of which 32 Egyptians and 10 Bangladeshis were detected in the early morning, Saturday 01/20/2023, close to Kali Limenes bay, southerly Crete. A cargo ship noticed a distress signal from the boat in which they were traveling. The cargo ship in collaboration with the local civil protection team,  transported them to the bay of Kali Limenes, from where the Coast Guard began an operation to transport them first to a shelter and after to Heraklion in order to temporarily accommodate them. Among the migrants, who are all men, there are also 4 minors.

summary:
Basados en el reporte del Servicio Meteorológico de Chile, desde el martes 30 de enero al sábado 4 de febrero se presenta una alerta por calor extremo. La alerta vigente de Meteorología considera a las siguientes zonas:

 

Región de Coquimbo en la cordillera costa, precordillera y valles precordilleranos con hasta 36°C.

Región de Valparaíso en el litoral, cordillera costa, precordillera y valles precordilleranos con hasta 39°C.

Región Metropolitana en la cordillera costa, valle y precordillera con hasta 38°C.

Región de O’Higgins en el litoral, cordillera costa, valle y precordillera con hasta 37°C.

Región del Maule en el litoral, cordillera costa, valle y precordillera con hasta 38°C.

Región del Ñuble en la cordillera costa, valle y precordillera con hasta 37°C.

 

Durante la semana se presentaron distintos focos de incendios forestales pero actualmente los que presentan mayor intensidad y de características extremas son los incendios que comenzaron el 31 de enero en la comuna La Estrella, Región de O’Higgins el cual sigue activo con más de 2.500 hectáreas. Además, en la Región de Valparaíso durante el 2 de febrero se iniciaron distintos focos de incendio en las comunas de Villa Alemana, Quilpué y Viña del Mar, los cuales han destruido viviendas e infraestructura crítica como antenas de comunicaciones, cortes de carreteras, entre otros. En la Región del Maule se presentan focos activos, los con mayor intensidad son los que se encuentran las comunas de Pencahue y Curepto con cerca de 1.000 hectáreas quemadas.

 

Al día Sábado 03 de febrero, 17:30 hrs, se declaran 45.812 hectáreas afectadas por Incendios Forestales, siendo la región de Valparaíso la más compleja debido a la gran cantidad de zonas urbanas expuestas, en total esta región tiene 12.939 hectáreas afectadas.

Crops expecially maize, legumes, grounds nuts, millet, soghum and others are withering due to insufficient moisture content. Water points are drying up making it difficult for people to access safe and clean water dor domestic consumption. Pasture is drying up making is difficult for livestock. Price for food items and other basic commodities has continued to rise due to high demand as most community members have to depend on the markets. 

The most affected directly are small scale farmers who depend on rainfed cropping, livestock keepers and all community members who depend on natural water bodies and shallow wells for water. 

The situation has come at the time when the government shared the Intergated Food Insecurity Phase Classification (IPC) report indicating that in the period October 2023 and March 2024 an average of 2.04 million people are facing food insecurity.

dtype.name: Epidemic
name: NGA: Epidemic - 01-2024 - Lassa Fever Emergency
summary:
Lassa Fever is an epidemic-prone disease for immediate Integrated Disease notification but case fatality rates range from 3% to 42% (and over the last two years has remained
between 20% and 25%). Historically, outbreaks occur during the dry season (November to April);
however, in recent years, cases have also occurred during the rainy season.

Lassa Fever (LF) remains a health burden and endemic in Nigeria, and the toll in case fatality remains unabated over several decades. The disease results in 500,000 cases annually and approximately 5000 deaths in endemic West Africa. Although the overall case fatality rate is 1% mortality can be as high as 15–20% in hospitalized LF patients and up to 50% during outbreaks

In 80% of human cases, the disease is asymptomatic, but in the remaining 20% a complicated course leading to death may result in nonspecific symptoms indistinguishable from other Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers (VHFs) such as Ebola and Marburg. Typically, human infection results from contact with secretions and excretions of infected rats and other infected persons through respiratory or gastrointestinal tracts. Inhalation of aerosolized infective viral LASV particles is the most significant means of exposure.
 The current situation is exacerbated by stigma and discrimination against infected individuals which poses significant barriers, negatively affecting access to care and treatment. These can substantially increase the suffering of infected individuals and can be strong disincentives for individuals in seeking prompt medical care

countries.name: Bangladesh

name: Bangladesh: Cyclone EAP 2024
summary:
The IFRC Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) has approved a total of CHF 499,987 for the implementation of the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS) cyclone EAP. The approved amount consists of an allocation of CHF 185,858 for readiness, CHF 112,958 for prepositioning and CHF 201,172 allocated to implement early actions once the defined triggers are met.

Allocations are made from the Anticipatory Pillar of the DREF, under the DREF appeal code MDR00001. Unearmarked contributions to the DREF are encouraged to guarantee enough funding is available for the Early Action Protocols being developed.

Bangladesh, owing to its geographical location, is highly exposed to natural hazards especially country’s southern part suffers from cyclones. Having two cyclone seasons in a year, cyclones have a major impact on the population of Bangladesh affecting millions of people in Bangladesh. As one of the major hazards in Bangladesh, cyclones cause loss of life and livelihoods in the 19 districts of the coastal area with 35 million people. Out of the 19 coastal districts (government classified), this EAP covers a total of 14 coastal districts considering the past impact and lesson learnt. The population is vulnerable to cyclones associated with tidal surge particularly in the pre-monsoon months of April-May and post-monsoon months of October-November.

This Early Action Protocol (EAP) has been developed and will be implemented by the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS) with support from IFRC, PNs, Cyclone Preparedness Programme (CPP), and the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD). The EAP of BDRCS is a tool to guide timely and effective implementation of early actions when certain weather or climate forecast shows a high likelihood of impacting people. If the event materializes and there are no preparedness actions in place, there is a high potential of humanitarian crisis. These crises could be avoided or minimized by the joint and timely action of the government, communities at risk, stakeholders, and the host national society. After each activation or at the end of the lifespan of the EAP, i.e., 5 years, (in case of no activation during the lifespan of the EAP), the EAP gets revised to incorporate the learnings and make it compatible with the changing scenario. After activating cyclone EAP in Bangladesh during Cyclone Amphan, BDRCS revised this cyclone EAP with the technical support of IFRC, German Red Cross and Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre (RCCC). In this revision of 2024, the budget has been increased to around 500,000 CHF from 350,000 CHF. The geographical coverage of this EAP is the 14 most vulnerable cyclone prone districts of Bangladesh and is expected to be implemented in the most probable impacted districts on the basis of Impact based Forecast (IbF) analysis.

On the evening of January 16th, a significant explosion occurred at Deji Oyelese Close in Old Bodija, Ibadan, resulting in widespread impact on the surrounding area. The explosion has left a trail of devastation, affecting more than 80 houses in the vicinity. The current context is one of emergency response and recovery efforts as authorities and rescue teams mobilize to address the aftermath.

The blast has taken a toll on the local population, with 77 individuals reported as injured at the time of initial reporting. These casualties have been promptly transferred to health facilities for medical attention. The severity of injuries varies, and the full extent of the impact on the affected individuals is yet to be assessed.

The affected population is experiencing a range of challenges, including physical injuries, trauma, and potential displacement due to damage to their homes. The explosion has not only caused immediate harm but may also have long-term implications for the well-being and livelihoods of those residing in the affected area.

Emergency services are actively engaged in managing the situation, providing medical assistance, and ensuring the safety of the affected population.

Shearline

On January 16, 2024, the PRC started monitoring the flooding caused by the Shear Line. Shear Line affected the eastern section of Mindanao which brought scattered light to heavy rain showers and thunderstorms which resulted in flooding and landslide incidents in some areas in Region XI and CARAGA.

 

On January 17, 2024, the effect of Shearline has weakened. However, it continues to bring scattered rain showers and thunderstorms over Northern Mindanao, CARAGA, and Davao Region in the next 24 hours.

 

On 20 January 2024, the effect of Shear Line has weakened and was no longer directly affecting the country.

 

Trough of Low-Pressure Area

On 28 January 2024, the Northeast Monsoon and the Trough of the Low-Pressure Area affected Mindanao. The Trough of the Low-Pressure Area continued to bring light to heavy rains in Mindanao until 02 February 2024. This resulted in flooding, landslide, and other incidents in some areas in Mindanao.

 

Easterlies affecting the eastern section of the country.

 

As on January 31, 2024, Davao Oriental and Agusan del Sur are under a state of calamity. In addition, Davao del Norte on February 1, 2024.

 

In terms of essential lifelines, the communication signal is weak at Brgy. Cabawan, Agusan del Sur (as of January 30), while there is a power interruption in Mati City, Davao Oriental (as of January 31).

 

The local government announced suspensions of classes and work. All public and private schools in Sultan Kudarat, Davao del Norte, Davao City and Davao Oriental Agusan Del Norte. While Davao City the government employees ordered to work-from-home.

 

According to reports, the state of the dams and rivers in Davao de Oro, Lower Ulip, and Hijo River is critical level.

countries.name: Afghanistan
dtype.name: Earthquake
name: AFG: Badakhshan Earthquake -2024
summary:
On 11.1.2024, a powerful earthquake measuring 6.4 on the Richter scale struck northeastern Afghanistan at 13:50 PM, affecting the provinces of Badakhshan and causing tremors in neighboring Pakistan. This report highlights the actions taken by the (IFRC) and the Afghanistan Red Crescent Society (ARCS) Branch Disaster Response Teams (BDRT) during the initial assessment phase.

The earthquake's epicenter was located in Jurm district in the province of Badakhshan, situated in the mountainous Hindu Kush region. The seismic event caused significant shaking, impacting buildings in Kabul, the capital city of Afghanistan, as well as Islamabad in Pakistan. Fortunately, no casualties have been reported thus far.

IFRC and ARCS Response:

In response to the earthquake, ARCS swiftly mobilized their BDRT teams to the affected areas supported by IFRC team members whom were already in the province distributing relief aid as part of the winterization assistance to the affected communities from the previous floods. The BDRT members and volunteers from ARCS are currently in the epicenter areas conducting the initial assessment. The primary objective of this assessment is to gather essential information about the impact of the earthquake, identify immediate needs, and develop an appropriate response plan.

 

1. Actions Taken:

The IFRC and ARCS BDRT teams have undertaken the following actions during the initial assessment:

1. Activation of the Emergency operations center at Kabul level to ensure monitoring of the situation and ensuring coordinated approach with the movement partners as well as local authorities.

2.Rapid Deployment: BDRT staff and volunteers were promptly deployed to the affected areas, ensuring a rapid response to the emergency. This should allow timely

  collection  of critical information and needs assessment.

2. Needs Assessment:

IFRC and ARCS teams are currently interacting with the affected communities to ascertain their immediate needs. This includes assessing the situation and identifying requirements for emergency shelter, food, clean water, medical assistance, and other necessary relief items if needed. The assessment aims to ensure that the response efforts and plans align with the specific needs of the affected population.

3. Coordination with Local Authorities:

The ARCS are closely collaborating with local authorities, including government agencies, to ensure a coordinated assessment. This approach should ensure consistency of  of information, resources, and efficient delivery of assistance to the affected communities. Working together with local authorities enhances the effectiveness of the response effort.

 

 We will continue to update this report, based on the updated information from the field.

summary:
On January 10, 2024, the Ministry of Health, Wellness, and the Environment issued a press release providing updates on communicable diseases. The mentioned illnesses encompass COVID-19, Dengue Fever, Influenza (specifically Influenza A-HN1, commonly referred to as Swine Flu), and Leptospirosis. Notably, there were 32 confirmed cases of Influenza A-H1N1 between December 25, 2023, and January 6, 2024. In 2023, 243 cases of COVID-19 were reported, with only 2 cases documented in 2024. Dengue Fever had 17 confirmed cases, while Leptospirosis had 20 cases in 2023.

In a subsequent press release on January 16, 2024, the Ministry of Health announced an initiative to monitor leprosy cases in neighboring islands and enhance surveillance within St. Vincent and the Grenadines (SVG). Notably, SVG has not reported any leprosy cases in the past four years.

Recognizing the potential health emergency, the SVG Red Cross has initiated discussions with the Ministry of Health to assess potential areas requiring assistance. To address the situation comprehensively, a Surveillance meeting involving the Ministry of Health, Public Health Office, Epidemiologists, and other medical professionals is scheduled for the upcoming week. Following this meeting, the SVG Red Cross plans to collaborate with the Ministry of Health to determine specific areas and capacities where support can be effectively provided.

countries.name: Kenya
