name: KEN: Population Movement - 01-2024 - Baringo Insecurity
summary:
Baringo County borders Turkana and Samburu Counties to the North, Laikipia to the East, Nakuru and Kericho to the South, Uasin Gishu to the South West, Elgeyo Marakwet and West Pokot to the West. It is administratively divided into seven sub-counties namely: Baringo Central, Baringo North, Baringo South, Mogotio, Koibatek, Tiaty East, and Tiaty West. Baringo North Sub County is among the affected areas by insecurity in Baringo. Administratively, it is divided into four wards: Bartabwa, Saimo Soi, Kabartonjo, and Kabarnet.

Most of the livelihood zones are at a normal stage though worsening especially in some parts of Barweza, Saimo Soi. This has escalated the resource-based conflicts among neighboring communities due to competition over lean resources. From December 2023 to date, there has been unrest and tension in areas of Saimo Soi and Bartabwa wards following rampant banditry attacks, leading to loss of lives.

Since January 2024, a total of 2,781 households have been displaced, 33 fatalities reported and 26 others injured. A total of 37 learning institutions have been closed which include; 2 Secondary schools, 17 primary schools, and 18 ECD centers.

countries.name: Ecuador
dtype.name: Other
name: ECU: Other - 01-2024 - Crisis Seguridad Interna
summary:
El 7 de enero de 2024, donde las Fuerzas Armadas y la Policía Nacional llevaron a cabo un operativo en la cárcel regional de Guayaquil para trasladar a José Adolfo Macías Villamar, conocido como “Fito”, a una cárcel de máxima seguridad (La Roca). Sin embargo, se confirmó que Macías no se encontraba en las instalaciones de la cárcel regional. Como resultado, el presidente de la República convocó a una reunión urgente del Consejo de Seguridad Pública y del Estado (COSEPE) en la ciudad de Guayaquil, para determinar las acciones coordinadas a ejecutarse por el estado y combatir la grave situación de conmoción interna que atraviesa el país en materia de seguridad pública.

Debido a esta acción la mañana y tarde del 8 de enero, se registraron varios motines en los centros
penitenciarios de Guayas, Cotopaxi, Loja, Napo, El Oro, Chimborazo, Tungurahua y Pichincha, además de manera oficial por parte del Servicio Nacional de Atención Integral a Personas Adultas Privadas de la Libertad (SNAI) se tuvo conocimiento que existe personal del servicio penitenciario retenido. En horas de la tarde el Presidente de la República Daniel Noboa expidió el Decreto Ejecutivo de Estado Excepción a nivel nacional Nro. 1101, por grave conmoción interna por 60 días en todo el territorio nacional

La noche del 8 y la madrugada del martes 9 de enero del 2024, se registraron varios atentados en diferentes provincias del Ecuador. A continuación, se detallan los hechos:


➢ Pichincha: En Quito, se reportó la explosión de un coche bomba en el sector de Chillogallo y la detonación de artefactos explosivos en un puente peatonal en el sector de las Orquídeas. Además, un policía fue secuestrado en el UPC ubicado en la parroquia de Calderón. Luego de los hechos violentos ocurridos en la capital, el alcalde del Municipio de Quito Pavel Muñoz emitió un comunicado solicitando al Gobierno ecuatoriano que militarice las instalaciones estratégicas de la ciudad para garantizar su funcionamiento y seguridad de los ciudadanos.
➢ Esmeraldas: Se reportó un atentado al cuartel de la policía del cantón Esmeraldas y dos vehículos fueron incinerados.
➢ Azuay: En Cuenca, se registró un ataque a un camión militar y cinco explosiones de bombas panfletarias en diferentes puntos de la ciudad.
➢ El Oro: En los cantones de Santa Rosa y El Guabo, cuatro vehículos fueron incinerados. Además, dos policías fueron secuestrados en Machala.
➢ Chimborazo: En la Riobamba, se produjo la explosión de un coche bomba en la Plaza Dávalos, así mismo se dio a conocer por parte de las autoridades locales la fuga de 32 PPL entre ellos Fabricio Colón Pico acusado de planificar un atentado contra de la Fiscal de la Nación Diana Salazar
➢ Loja: en la ciudad de Loja se reportó la incineración de cinco vehículos. 
➢ Guayas. en la parroquia Tengel se reportó un artefacto explosivo que causó daños en el UPC del sector.
➢ Los Ríos: Tres servidores públicos de la Policía de Quevedo y Mocache fueron secuestrados sin conocer hasta el momento su ubicación. 

El Ministerio de Educación en base a los Decretos Ejecutivos 110 y 1113se dispone el cambio a la modalidad no presencial en todo el Sistema Educativo Nacional. Esto implica instituciones educativas fiscales, fiscomisionales, municipales y particulares hasta el viernes 12 de enero de 2024. 


El Ministerio de Salud mediante Memorando oficial, suspendió en el Primer Nivel de Atención, las atenciones extramurales y los servicios de consulta externa, se mantienen los servicios de emergencia en centros de salud tipo C y segundo nivel de atención.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.society_name: The South African Red Cross Society
dtype.name: Storm Surge
name: ZAF: 01-2024 Storm Surge
summary:
In South Africa, natural disasters such as floods, severe storms have led to significant social and economic losses, which is anticipated to exacerbate as consequence of climate change. On the 7th of January 2024 to date, storm surge which resulted in flooding affected KwaZulu Natal and Free State province. Overall, 1,226 households(6,418 people) were affected.

In the KwaZulu-Natal province approximately 814 households (4,297 people) were affected as per the preliminary report from the Government. According to the reports by Government, 41 fatalities(including 21 from Ladysmith) have been confirmed, and 4 people still missing in KwaZulu Natal province. The heavy storms have affected different districts in KwaZulu Natal, especially uThukela (Ladysmith), uMzinyathi, Amajuba district Municipality where fatalities were reported due to drowning, same displaced and other people still reported missing.

On the other hand, the Free State province has encountered unprecedented and remarkable levels of precipitation, accompanied by severe thunderstorms and destructive winds, resulting in extensive damage to households in formal and informal settlements within the Mangaung, Lejweleputswa, Thabo Mofutsanyane, Fezile-Dabi, and Xhariep district, farmers within have lost crop damages within the Mangaung Metro Municipality and the Thabo Mofutsanyane area since the 7th and 8th of January 2024 and adverse weather conditions continue exposing vulnerabilities a storm surge accompanied with flooding occurred in Ficksburg and Jaggersfontein and affected almost 412 households (2,121 people). Currently displaced people are accommodated by friends, relatives and neighbors.

countries.name: Tanzania, United Republic of
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: TZA: Epidemic - 01-2024 - TANZANIA CHOLERA OUTBREAK
summary:
Since September 5th, 2023, a cholera outbreak has been reported in 13 regions of Mara, Arusha, Kilimanjaro, Kigoma, Kagera, Singida, Simiyu, Shinyanga, Tabora, Ruvuma, Dodoma, Mwanza, and Geita in Tanzania Mainland, with cumulatively 1,521 cases and 34 deaths (CFR of 2.3%) reported. Out of 13 regions, a Cholera outbreak was declared over in 5 regions (Mara, Kigoma, Arusha, Kilimanjaro, and Dodoma). Cases in Mwanza, Shinyanga, Simiyu and Kagera regions have continued to increase to date, making these regions the most affected at present. The trend of this disease shows that there is a risk of the disease spreading further, if necessary, measures are not put in place. With the ongoing El nino a long rains period expected to start in March through May 2024, there is a probability that these cases will rise, and more regions will be affected. 

Tanzania has never experienced an almost countrywide spread of cholera infections in the last 4 decades. At most, it has only been witnessed and quickly contained in up to two regions concurrently per year. With the present El Nino rains in all 31 administrative regions of Tanzania, the existing wastewater drainage systems have been overwhelmed and many have collapsed completely, particularly those of Mwanza, Shinyanga and Kagera. The regions also happen to be the most densely populated in the country; Mwanza has the highest number of squatter-settlements with unplanned hillside infrastructure and unplanned fish markets. Shinyanga is a mining region with widespread open defecation practices in the popular weekly community food markets. The scale of this year’s heavy rainfall, the resultant overflow of latrine facilities and poor hygiene practices in the affected communities have made this epidemic spread much faster than the country’s coping mechanism could contain it.

countries.name: Uganda
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: UGA: Epidemic - 01-2024 - Measles Outbreak
summary:
Uganda has registered measles outbreaks in eight districts/cities across the country since January 2024. The Ministry of Health conducted a rapid measles risk assessment which revealed that an estimated 41 districts are at high risk of measles, an additional 73 districts are considered at moderate risk of measles and other vaccine preventable diseases. This is a threat to the current progress Uganda has made to stop measles in the country.
Data from all the measles outbreaks investigated indicates that the outbreaks are due to pockets of unimmunized or under immunized children, which is made further made worse by porous borders, free population movements and sub optimal active surveillance in some regions.

countries.name: Japan
dtype.name: Earthquake
name: JPN: Noto Peninsula Earthquake 01-2024
summary:
On 1 January 2024 at 16:10 (Japan Standard Time), a magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck the Noto Peninsula in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan. As the epicentre was very shallow, large tremors were observed in many places and a tsunami warning was issued. As a result of the quake, power and water supplies were cut, communications were disrupted and hundreds of houses were reported to have collapsed.

The Japanese Red Cross Society began its response immediately after the disaster and its branches in the affected areas are working with Red Cross hospitals and Red Cross Blood Centres to assess the extent of the damage. Cross-organisational coordination, medical response and the distribution of relief goods are underway.

countries.name: Nigeria
dtype.name: Food Insecurity
name: NGA: 2024 Severe Acute Malnutrition
summary:
The severe malnutrition crisis in northeast Nigeria has been exacerbated by ongoing conflict, displacement, and limited access to essential
services. Children are particularly vulnerable, facing heightened risks of morbidity and mortality. The healthcare system, already strained
by high demand, is struggling to cope with the escalating needs, highlighting an urgent need for increased support and intervention to
address the malnutrition emergency.


Humanitarian organizations in northeast Nigeria have issued urgent warnings due to a dramatic surge in malnutrition among children in
Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) States. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) which is leading the case management pillar of the Nutrition
cluster in Nigeria, has observed a significant increase in admissions of severely malnourished children with life-threatening complications
across seven northern Nigerian states, including the BAY states, with some areas experiencing admissions double those of 2023.
The BAY states' nutrition sector reported a 63 percent increase in admissions of children with complicated severe acute malnutrition
(SAM) between January and April 2024, compared to the same period in 2023. The worsening nutrition situation has overwhelmed the
healthcare system, with bed occupancy rates reaching 100 percent well before the expected peak of the lean season.
According to the UNOCHA report, In April 2024 alone, MSF admitted 1,250 severely malnourished children with complications to its
inpatient therapeutic feeding centers across the BAY states. This number is double the admissions recorded in April 2023. By the end of
May 2024, MSF's facilities in these states were accommodating 350 patients, far exceeding the 200-bed capacity initially set for the peak of
the lean season, which spans from June to August.


In addition, Nutrition surveillance data from April among displaced populations from remote and hard-to-reach communities in the BAY
states revealed an alarming 18 percent prevalence of SAM and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) among children aged 6-59 months.
The data also indicated a 1.2 percent increase in the overall prevalence of malnutrition and a 0.9 percent increase in SAM cases among
children compared to March 2024. This trend underscores a critical and deteriorating nutrition situation that requires an immediate and
collaborative response.


Since January, humanitarian partners in the BAY states have been providing either food or cash transfers to support displaced people
living in camps or with host communities, as well as vulnerable host populations. With diminishing resources, partners have reached over
1.1 million vulnerable people with food assistance out of 4.8 million in need this lean season. Despite the alarming situation, the overall
humanitarian response remains inadequate. Funding for the ongoing humanitarian response in the BAY states remains a major
challenge. As of 12 June, the 2024 Humanitarian Response Plan, which needs $926.5 million, is only 20.5 percent funded. The nutrition
sector has reported that the ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) and ready-to-use supplementary food (RUSF) pipelines may break in
July due to an increase in acute malnutrition admissions during the first quarter of 2024.


Furthermore, the outbreaks of AWD and measles in the BAY states have exacerbated the malnutrition crisis, leading to higher rates of SAM, increased morbidity, and mortality, decreased nutrient absorption, exacerbated nutritional deficiencies, and a strained healthcare
system. Children who were already moderately malnourished are quickly deteriorating to severe malnutrition due to the additional
health burdens, leading to a significant rise in the number of children suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM). Lack of access to
healthcare services, especially in hard-to-reach communities has led to complications such as severe dehydration and contributed to
poor management and control of AWD outbreaks, allowing the disease to spread more rapidly within communities.

To mitigate these effects, integrated health and nutrition interventions are essential, including disease prevention, nutritional support,
and strengthening of healthcare systems. The NRCS, through its grassroots presence of community-based skilled volunteer structures,
seeks to complement the efforts of the Government to strengthen Health and Nutrition Services through Community-Based Surveillance
(CBS), Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF), Protection, Gender, and Inclusion
(PGI) and WASH in Adamawa, Yobe and Borno States.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.society_name: Red Cross Society of Bosnia and Herzegovina
dtype.name: Earthquake
name: BIH: Earthquake - 12-2023 - Earthquake - December 2023
summary:
On December 30, 2023, at 9:43 PM, an earthquake with a magnitude of 4.8 on the Richter scale struck Bosnia and Herzegovina. The location of the epicenter was near Zenica, and significant tremors were felt in the broader region of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The earthquake caused significant damage to at least 14 residential buildings in the Zenica area. Four (4) people were injured, and two of them were hospitalized. The earthquake also caused damage to the road infrastructure, leading to a traffic accident in which one person was injured. Alongside the damages to residential buildings, the earthquake significantly affected other properties of the affected households. Media outlets have reported significant concerns among the population in the affected area, including statements that some residents whose properties were damaged or are close to the epicenter are afraid to return home, fearing further tremors.

Although the earthquake caused the most damage in the Zenica area, tremors were evidenced throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina, including Travnik, Sarajevo, and Banja Luka.

countries.name: Greece
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: GRC: Population Movement - 12-2023 - Rethymno, Dec 2023
summary:
29 people (2 of them minors) were located Saturday morning 30/12/2023, in Agia Galini of Rethymno by the Hellenic Authorities.

They started their journey in a boat,  from a beach near the "Kambut" region of Libya. After being rounded up, were safely transported to the port of Agia Galini and from there in a temporary accommodation facility of the Municipality of Rethymno and eventually in Pireus, Attica.

countries.name: Democratic Republic of Congo
countries.society_name: Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
dtype.name: Flood
name: COD: 01-2024 Floods
summary:
The Democratic Republic of Congo is currently experiencing its worst Congo River flooding in 60 years, following weeks of heavy rainfall. As of December 29, 2023, the Government of the Republic of Congo already issued an alert for the level of the Congo River with a flood of 5.94m. As of January 10, the river level was still above the overflow threshold, 6.20 meters above sea level, close to the 1961 record of 6.26 meters. This statement by the Reuters agency Ferry Mowa (hydrology specialist of the DRC Waterways Authority), maintains the level of emergency in several provinces already severely affected by violent floods for several weeks with about 300 deaths in the two Congos. Following the deadly toll and the impact of the floods presented on January 5, the Minister of Social Affairs, Humanitarian Actions and National Solidarity of the DRC launched an appeal for solidarity and emergency relief addressed to the authorities of the Central Government and to the entire national and international community in order to allow the deployment of substantial aid and teams on the ground.

According to the monitoring of the Régie des voies fluviales, the most affected provinces are: Tshopo, Mongala, Equateur, North Ubangi and South Ubangi, Kwilu, Mai-Ndombe, Kongo-Central, Lomami, Kasai, Kasai-Central, South Kivu, Haut Uele, Kinshasa and Tshuapa.

These floods observed across the Republic have affected 304,521 households, In addition, more than 43,750 houses have collapsed, 1325 schools destroyed, 269 health centers affected, 41 public markets affected and 85 agricultural service roads devastated

countries.name: Burundi
dtype.name: Pluvial/Flash Flood
name: BDI: Pluvial/Flash Flood - 12-2023 - Burundi-Pluvial/Floods
summary:
On the night of 26th to 27th of December 2023, heavy rain occurred in Bujumbura town and caused floods in some quarters of Ntahangwa, Muha Communes of Bujumbura.

Burundi Red Cross conducted a joint needs assessment with the local administrative authority and data are shown in that report keys findings.

countries.name: Indonesia
dtype.name: Volcanic Eruption

summary:

c.       Communal facilities

countries.name: Congo
dtype.name: Flood
name: COG: Flood - 12-2023 - FLOOD IN CONGO BRAZZAVILLE
summary:
The Republic of Congo has been facing exceptionally severe rainfall over almost all of the national territory for several weeks. According to experts, this precipitation is twice as much as the usual average. This situation is at the root of the floods in the country, which already has 320,891 people directly affected by the floods, subject to displacement and severe losses as a result of this disaster.

 

The most affected departments are mainly Likouala, Sangha, Cuvette, Plateaux, Niari, Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire (large torrential rains), with 361 villages and 36 neighborhoods submerged due to the exceptional flooding of the Congo River and its tributaries. The impact of the rains to date on the population already far exceeds the number of affected populations over the period of OND during the floods in 2021 (164,679 personnes_Evaluation with the Government) and 2022 (222,000 people).

Floods caused 17 deaths in the departments of the Likouala, Plateaux, Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire.

6 people are missing in the departments of Likouala and Cuvette. In total, more than 2,292 hectares of land are flooded.

countries.name: Australia
dtype.name: Flood
name: AUS: Flood - 12-2023 - South East Queensland
summary:
Southeast Queensland has been severely impacted by two thunderstorms  – one on Christmas Day and one on New Years Day. The most affected Local Government areas are Gold Coast, Logan, and Scenic Rim. 6,000 homes are still without power after the Christmas Day storm. The Bureau of Meteorology issued an urgent warning for dangerous and life-threatening flash flooding on New Years Day. Isolated rainfall totals in some areas for the 24 hour period exceeded 300mm. The storm is expected to continue into Tuesday 02/01. 

 Sadly, there have been seven deaths in the region related to the Christmas Day storms. 

Two Evacuation Centres were stood up on New Years Day on the Gold Coast and some scheduled recovery activities related to the Christmas Day storms were postponed due to the storm.

countries.name: Nigeria
dtype.name: Civil Unrest
name: NGA: Civil Unrest - 12-2023 - Gunmen Attack
summary:
On the night of Saturday, 23rd December 2023, a series of violent coordinated attacks by suspected gunmen erupted in Lisha community, extending to neighboring communities such as Kwahasnat, KambarIpelli, Mutfyan, among others. The incident unfolded at approximately 22:45 hours, leading to a devastating impact on the affected areas.

Preliminary reports by volunteers of the Nigerian Red Cross Society after an on-the-spot assessment indicate that not fewer than 213 individuals lost their lives as a result of the attacks. The casualties are spread across multiple communities affected by the violence.

Approximately 100 individuals sustained severe injuries and have been evacuated to medical facilities for urgent treatment. The injured have been transported to Jos University Teaching Hospital (JUTH) and Bokkos Medical Center to receive medical attention. The assessment also showed that around 200 individuals with minor injuries were treated and subsequently discharged after receiving medical care.

Immediate response efforts focused on the evacuation and treatment of the injured. Security forces and emergency response teams are currently on-site to stabilize the situation, provide necessary security, and offer support to the affected communities. The government of Plateau State has also appealed for coordination efforts to ensure the effective delivery of aid, medical assistance, and logistical support to those impacted by the incident.

As of the latest reports, the situation remains volatile and fluid, with ongoing efforts to stabilize the affected areas. Security forces and emergency response teams are actively engaged in restoring order, providing security, and supporting affected communities. This attack has left more than 11,000 people already displaced, and not fewer than 221 houses burned, with properties worth millions of Naira destroyed.

While the casualty figures continue to rise, the coordinated attacks on 23 villages in Bokkos and Barkin Ladi local government areas of Plateau State have created immediate humanitarian needs such as medical supplies, food, and shelter to support the affected communities.

The affected population is grappling with profound psychological trauma due to the loss of loved ones, witnessing violence, and the overall disruption of their community and daily lives. Also, the displaced individuals and those directly affected by the violence are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance, including shelter, food, and medical care. The disrupted infrastructure and security situation pose significant challenges to the effective delivery of aid.

countries.name: Czech Republic
dtype.name: Other
name: CZE: Other - 12-2023 - Mass Shooting
summary:
Incident Overview:
On the afternoon of December 21, 2023, an active shooter incident occurred at the Faculty of Philosophy building of Charles University in the center of Prague. The armed assailant entered the building and opened fire. A total of 14 individuals were fatally wounded, with the assailant being the fifteenth casualty. Additionally, 25 individuals sustained injuries, with ten suffering severe trauma. Among the deceased and injured were foreign nationals. The building was fully operational at the time, with standard academic activities in progress. Police evacuated hundreds of individuals, predominantly students.

Response by the Czech Red Cross:
The local branch of the Czech Red Cross activated its Emergency Plan in response to requests from the Emergency Services System. A team was dispatched to the site with the objective of providing support, including thermal comfort, beverages, and food, to both affected individuals and responders. Over the course of 17 hours, assistance was provided to more than 200 individuals on-site.

Simultaneously, the Czech Red Cross was involved in the operation of the official crisis hotline. Basic information about the incident and initial psychological aid were provided through this service. In the first 17 hours of operation, Czech Red Cross interveners handled 120 calls.

countries.name: Togo
dtype.name: Fire
name: TGO: Fire - 12-2023 - icendie of the Agoè Market
summary: The Agoè Assiyéyé market located in the commune of Agoè-Nyivé 1 (Grand Lomé), one of the largest in the Togolese capital Lomé, was hit by a violent fire in the town of Agoè-Nyivé 1 (Grand Lomé). The fire, which broke out around 9:30 p.m., ravaged the entire south side and part of the north side, i.e. 3/4 of the total area, causing significant material damage, thousands of businesses swept away,  just before the end of year celebrations. However, with the reinforcements of the port, the airport, the STSL, PIA, ANASAP, and military engineers, as well as the mobilization of the public security services and the local population, this fire was brought under control at around 3 a.m. The local committees of the Togolese Red Cross with the National Agency for Civil Protection are currently evaluating the best way to support the victims affected by this disaster.

countries.name: Mauritius
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: MUS: Epidemic - 12-2023 - Dengue Outbreak
summary: Mauritius is facing an alarming dengue outbreak. The situation is particularly concerning in Port-Louis and its surrounding areas due to favourable climate conditions for mosquito breeding. Since the end of last year few cases of dengue (imported cases) has been registered in the lower Plaine Wilhems district. Unfortunately, with the heavy rainfall episodes of December 2023 and of January 2024 resulted in water accumulation thereby increasing mosquito density and rapidly several cases were registered in the region of Port-Louis and its vicinity, in the northern regions, in district of Plaine Wilhems, and even in Rodrigues. As of 16 February, the cumulative cases since December last year have reached 1,456 including 865 active cases and 2 deaths.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
dtype.name: Pluvial/Flash Flood
name: SUN: Pluvial Flood - 12-2023 - Vaguada Effects in Dominican Republic
summary:
By virtue of the above, due to the humidity conditions in the soil, due to the rains of the last (2) days and the provisions of article 2, chapter 1, of Law 147-02, on Risk Management, this Emergency Operations Center (COE), modifies the ALERT Levels for possible river floods,  streams and ravines, as well as flash or urban flooding.

On the Atlantic and Caribbean coasts, operators of fragile, small and medium-sized vessels, as well as first responders, must strictly follow the restriction contained in today's marine report from the National Meteorological Office.

SAN CRISTOBAL:

The Civil Defense reports that due to the flooding of the Haina River, which is above Puente el Baden Km 40, the communities of La Cuchilla, Medina and La Presa of the Villa Altagracia Municipality are partially cut off. In addition, responding to a call from the National Emergency Response System 9.1.1, due to urban flooding on 8th Street, two people were displaced from their home, to the Manuel Montero Valgas Community Center shelter.

MONTE PLATA:

The Civil Defense reports that due to the flooding of the Ozama River, the communities of Peralvillo and Yamasá are partially cut off from La Cuaba and the community of Los Botados is partially cut off from Santo Domingo due to the flooding of the La Leonora River.

countries.name: Trinidad and Tobago
countries.society_name: The Trinidad and Tobago Red Cross Society
dtype.name: Flood
name: TTO: Flood - 12-2023 - Localized flooding and landslide
summary:
During an intense period of adverse weather which included intense heavy rainfall on the eastern coast of Tobago, incidents of one major landslide and street and flash flooding was reported. 

Area: Charlotteville, Tobago (Located on the northeastern side of the island)

Agencies involved and responding: Tobago Emergency Management Agency, Tobago Emergency Operations Centre, Community Emergency Response Team, Division of Infrastructure, Quarries and Urban Development

·        No Adverse Weather Alert from the Trinidad and Tobago Met Service.

·        More than 50 millimeters of rainfall across northeastern coastal Tobago.

·        Main road near Hairpin Bend blocked due to landslide.

·        One unoccupied residence structurally damaged (no one displaced).

·        Residents in Top River facing further impacts of landslides if the rains persisted, but this did not occur.

·        At 4:45, the TEOC had recorded five incidents, including residential and roadway flooding, landslides, blocked roads and fallen utility poles.

·        Distribution of packages with cleaning agents and other essential items was done by TEMA.

·        Clearing of blockages, tree-cutting, preliminary damage assessments started today 20/12/2023.

·        One affected homeowner noted that it was the first disaster of that magnitude that the community had ever experienced.

countries.name: Australia
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: AUS: Cyclone - 12-2023 - Tropical Cyclone Jasper - NT
summary: The NT Emergency Services team have received an Early Watching briefing for Cyclone Jasper. TC Jasper is now tracking across FNQ and is forecasted to enter the Gulf of Carpentaria on Friday 15 December 2023 as a tropical low. It is anticipated that EX TC Jasper will then continue moving across the gulf towards the NT. There is a possibility that it may re-intensify to cyclone strength as it approaches the NT however this is not confirmed. The BOM will continue to track and report on the movements of Ex TC Jasper in the coming days. Depending on the cyclone movement and intensity there might be requirement to establish an evacuation centre or sheltering in Darwin. Ex TC Jasper is slowly tracking across Far North Queensland  and is forecasted to enter the Gulf of Carpentaria by Thursday 20 December 2023. There is a low chance of the system redeveloping into a tropical cyclone when it reacheds the Gulf of Carpentaria and forecast predictions now show the system moving back east and away form the Northern Territory.

countries.name: Guinea
dtype.name: Fire
name: GIN: Fire - 12-2023 - Guinea Kaloum Fire
summary:
In the morning hours of Monday 18 December 2023, a major explosion occurred at Guinea's primary oil terminal situated in the Kaloum administrative district of Conakry, blowing out the windows of several nearby homes and forcing hundreds to flee.  The incident led to a massive fire and the release of dense black smoke, visible from a considerable distance. Swiftly, firefighters arrived at the scene, while several tanker trucks departed from the depot, escorted by soldiers and police for protection. Even after the firefighters successfully brought the fire under control later in the day, a thick column of smoke and some flames remained visible. It is worth noting that Guinea does not produce oil and lacks oil refining capabilities. Instead, it relies on importing refined products, which are primarily stored in the Kaloum terminal and distributed throughout the country via trucks.

The current extent of the damage sustained by the terminal remains uncertain at this moment. However, this unfortunate incident has resulted in the loss of both lives and properties. The initial report on human casualties indicates that there are at least 12 fatalities, 131 individuals injured, and several people still missing. The injured have been promptly evacuated to Donka and Ignace Deen hospitals, while the deceased have been transported to the respective morgues. The current situation does not provide a definite count of the displaced individuals and the overall number of affected people. Nevertheless, the ongoing process of registration and assessment will offer a comprehensive understanding of the extent of the damage and the number of individuals requiring assistance. This information will be provided in SitRep#2, which will be issued subsequent to a scheduled meeting with the Guinea Red Cross on the morning of Tuesday, December 19, 2023.

The government has issued a statement acknowledging that the cause of the fire is currently unknown. They have also announced the initiation of an investigation to determine the origin and any potential causes of the fire. The government expressed deep concern and emphasized the significant impact this incident could have on the population. The Command Post situated at the Ministry of Defense serves as the central hub for the Minister of Security to coordinate the state's response efforts. The Minister has given assurance that the fire is presently being brought under control and extinguished. As the situation is being brought under control, the government has advised citizens to stay at home. Furthermore, the following measures were put into effect on Monday, December 18, 2023...

Ø  Workers in the public and private sectors, except the defense and security forces and the medical profession, are requested to stay at home 

Ø  Public and private schools closed 

Ø  Gas stations closed, except for emergency services.

countries.name: Mozambique
dtype.name: Flood
name: Mozambique: Floods EAP
summary:
The IFRC Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) has approved a total of CHF 549,929 for the implementation of the Mozambique Red Cross Flood EAP. The approved amount consists of an allocation of CHF 357,352 for readiness and prepositioning and CHF 192,578 allocated to implement early actions once the defined triggers are met. Allocations are made from the Anticipatory Pillar of the DREF, under the DREF appeal code MDR00001. Unearmarked contributions to the DREF are encouraged to guarantee enough funding is available for the Early Action Protocols being developed. This EAP is focused on floods, which might occur anywhere in Mozambique from October to April (the rainy/cyclone season). The actions proposed will be activated on the basis of hydro-meteorological warnings indicating that the trigger level (water level correspondent to discharge of five-year return period at the river basin reference station) will be reached within 72 hours (3 days), which is the lead time within which the CVM can act in advance before a flood event reaches the districts and communities potentially at risk. All actions included in the EAP are based on this preparation time window.

The hydro-meteorological forecast will be provided by the National Institute of Meteorology (INAM), the National Directorate of Water Resources Management (DNGRH) and by REPRESA project through GloFAS, with whom the FbF team has developed longstanding collaboration at the technical level, focusing on the provision of data, as well as providing forecasts in a timely manner. This EAP seeks to achieve two objectives: first to ensure that the selected early actions are evidencebased and that they are effective in reducing the prioritized humanitarian impact of floods in Mozambique. Actions are proposed on the basis of sound risk information (Chapter 3), and reliable climate information that events of a certain magnitude are linked to high levels of impact. Secondly, the protocol describes how CVM selected and will organize the actions. G

eographical scope - the present EAP covers four Mozambican hydrographic basins: Limpopo, Buzi, Zambezi and Licungo with special focus on the at-risk districts downstream, in total 12: Gaza Province; Chokwe, Guija, Chibuti, Limpopo, Sofala Province; Buzi, Caia, Marromeu. Zambezia Province: Mocuba, Namacurra, Maganja da Costa, Mopeia and Luabo. The target population are those communities living along the flood plains particularly in the provinces of Gaza, Sofala and Zambezia.

countries.name: Argentina
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: ARG: Ciclón - 12-2023 - Vientos huracanados - Tormentas severas
summary:
Luego de que el Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) emitiera diversos avisos a corto plazo (ACP), y alertas meteorológicas, a raíz de un evento hidrometeorológico que trajo asociados vientos superiores a los 140Km/h (Según información del Municipio), y gran cantidad de agua caida, diversas zonas del Municipio de Bahía Blanca se vieron afectadas. Particularmente en el Club Bahiense del Norte los fuertes vientos colapsaron parte de la estructura y producto de este evento puntual perdieron la vida al menos 13 personas, en tanto otras debieron ser derivadas al sistema de salud. Al momento gran parte de la zona no cuenta con suministro electrico producto del evento, y hay significativas fallas en los sistemas de comunicación. 3 centros de evacuados se encuetran habilitados, y existe un COE Municipal. 

Autoridades locales, de la Provincia de Buenos Aires (Incluyendo al Ministro de Seguridad, el Director de Protección Civil, el Director de Emergencias Sanitarias, autoridades de Bomberos, y otros organismos), y de la Nación Argentina (Protección Civil, a cargo del Director de dicha dependencia, y otras autoridades) se encuentra en terreno o movilizandose a la zona, junto con distintos recursos logisticos y humanos, incluyendo a la Armada Argentina

countries.name: Sri Lanka
dtype.name: Flood
name: LKA: Flood - 12-2023 - North East Monsoon
summary: The northeast monsoon weather conditions have caused rainfalls since 17 December 2023 in the north east parts of the island. By 19 December, the precipitation triggered a flood situation in the country, which has affected thousands of lives and livelihoods, as well as caused property damage. According to the situation update by the Disaster Management Centre (DMC) of Sri Lanka confirmed that a total of 10,958 people in 12 districts have been affected due heavy rains and strong winds. Currently, 849 families have been evacuated into 32 welfare centers. Kilinorchchi, Mullaitivu, Mannar, Batticaloa, Trincomalee and Puttlam are the worst affected districts. dtype.name: Cyclone
name: AUS: Cyclone - 12-2023 - Tropical Cyclone Jasper - QLD
summary:
On Wednesday 13 December 2023 Tropical Cyclone Jasper crossed the coast of Queensland north of Port Douglas as a Category 2 cyclone. Communities on Far North Queensland had undergone five days of preparation in the lead up to the cyclone taking protective measures to secure homes and livelihoods as well as protect life. Cyclone shelters and storm tide shelters were established across the communities of Cairns, Port Douglas, Tablelands, Yarrabah, and Cooktown to provide last resort shelter for those at greatest risk.  

 

Emergency Services agencies (Police, Fire & Rescue, Ambulance, SES) pre-positioned additional teams and resources in close proximity to the expected impact zones for rapid deployment once the Cyclone had passed.  

 

Ex TC Jasper is now moving west bringing continued flood risk to the Cairns and Douglas shire region. There are major flood warnings in place for the Daintree and Mossman rivers, with flash flooding occurring overnight in Mossman resulting in the rapid evacuation of up to 50 people. 

 

From14 December 2023 to current time, the Ex TC Jasper low pressure system has caused heavy and widespread rainfall of more than 600mls to fall in Far North Queensland (FNQ). With the rain not predicted to ease until Tuesday 19 December a dangerous and major flood emergency is occurring across large areas of FNQ. Flash flooding has resulted in emergency evacuations being undertaken with people being rescued from rising flood waters by helicopters and boats. Properties and businesses have been inundated and many communities are now isolated by flood water. Cairns airport has closed hampering efforts to move emergency services agencies to and from the affected areas.

Ex-tropical cyclone Jasper is now a tropical low and continues to slowly track west over Cape York towards the Gulf of Carpentaria. At this stage, there is a low chance of the system redeveloping into a tropical cyclone when it reaches the Gulf of Carpentaria later this week. Some forecast predictions see the system moving back east towards East Arnhem land and back across Cape York Peninsula or into the Coral Sea. 

 

As at Monday 18 December 2023, Ex TC Jasper is causing major flooding including flask flooding across Far North Queensland, with many communities isolated, properties and infrastructure damaged, the closure of Cairns Airport and multiple evacuation centres and places of refuge established.

Planned recovery activity has been delayed due to the current dynamic flood emergency.

summary:
Filariasis is caused by a chronic mosquito-borne parasitic infection, which can lead to swelling of the extremities, hydroceles, and testicular masses. The disease is usually caused by Culex pipiens, a type of mosquito found in congested or dirty water.

Maldives was the first in the Region to be certified as having eliminated the disease as a public health problem in 2016. To do so it sustained a mass drug administration campaign that provided at-risk communities several rounds of preventive drugs annually. This occurred alongside mosquito control efforts, as well as a greater emphasis on case identification and treatment. A robust surveillance system, meanwhile, monitored progress and provided authorities the information to better target their interventions.

In December 2023, Filariasis 25 postive cases was identified in Kulhudhuffushi City, northern province of the Maldives during a Health screening event held for Migrant communities during 01-02nd December 2023. During the screening 25 confirmed cases has been identified.  An additional case also has been identified in Greater Male' Area.

In total 607 Screening of Individuals (All Migrant Individuals) has been conducted by Health Authorities. Out of which 594 Screening was focused in Kulhudhuffushi City and 13 Screenings in Greater Male' Area. Additional Screening Activities focused towards Migrant Communities in Greater Male' Area was carried out on 23rd December 2023 jointly with Maldivian RC.  Based on the initial findings, the Government expects a nationwide spread and requirement of immediate interventions.

Ministry of Health and Health Protection Agency are carrying out Screening Tests in Wider Cities across the Maldives with a particular focus on the Migrant Community. The Maldivian RC has been requested to support in prevention and community engagement in particular with vulnerable groups such as Migrant Communities (Reported 120,000 Expatriate Workers living in Maldives with expected 50,000 undocumented Migrants) as well as immediate support in the procurement of screening kits & medication required for infected individuals. 

As part of the Interventions, the Government would like to target interventions in City Level Islands, on-going Construction Sites, Migrant Accommodation Blocks as currently the assumption is the outbreak within the migrant communities. 

The Health Protection currently reports that the source of the disease is from migrant individuals who have travelled to the Maldives from regions where the disease is endemic, namely Bahar,Uttar Pradesh, Gopalganj and Tamil Nadu India as well as Comilla , Bangladesh.

1. MRC Kulhudhuffushi City Office has mobilized volunteers to support vector control initiatives in coordination with Kulhudhuffushi Regional Hospital to identify and eliminate mosquito breeding sites and to administer Bti to the drainages in asphalted roads. Furthermore, MRC will be roll out community engagement initiatives to create awareness on Filariasis in the community. 

2. MRC Male' City Office is supporting the Health Screening Activities organized by Ministry of Health and Health Protection Agency in Greater Male' Area with volunteers mobilized to support with community engagement, communication and translation support during the process. Additional community engagement and community outreach activities will be rolled out subsequently to address misinformation and prevention.

countries.name: Mozambique
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: Mozambique: Cyclone EAP
summary:
The Early Action Protocol (EAP) for Cyclones in Mozambique was created through a collaboration with the German Red Cross (GRC), along with technical input from the National Institute of Disaster Management (INGC), National Meteorological Institute (INAM), and National Directorate of Water Resources Management (DNGRH). This protocol was developed based on extensive research and consultations with stakeholders at the national, provincial, district, and community levels in areas highly susceptible to cyclones. The selection of actions to be taken in the EAP was guided by several criteria, such as whether it aligns with the Disaster Risk Management System in Mozambique, the ability of the Cruz Vermelha de Mozambique (CVM) to execute the action (including the presence of volunteers), and whether the community craftsman and the CLGRC can support the CVM in its implementation. Other factors considered were the action's effectiveness in reducing the impact of the cyclone, the shelf life of NFIs required, and whether it can benefit communities even in the absence of a cyclone.

The EAP will be implemented by CVM in coordination and collaboration with other stakeholders, early actions early warning working group, Disaster Management Authority (INGD) and with technical support from IFRC. The EAP can in principle be used nationwide, however, activation is anticipated to be concentrated in coastal districts in northern and central Mozambique with possibility to activate in 3 districts simultaneously. Taking into consideration the physical context, logistics, and the capacity of the NS, an activation will at a maximum involve three districts and target 2000 households (10000 people).

The EAP focuses on prioritizing the reinforcement of individual houses and primary schools built with local materials. These schools receive students from 1st to 5th grade. Another important objective of the plan is to prevent endemic diseases, especially reducing the incidence of diarrhoea and cholera after storms. These diseases only add to the vulnerability of the communities affected by cyclones.

countries.name: Chile
dtype.name: Heat Wave
name: CHL: Heat Wave - 12-2023 - National Heat Alert
summary:
In response to the commitments made in the Nationally Determined Contribution of the Framework Law on Climate Change No. 21,455 of the Ministry of the Environment to strengthen the capacity to adapt to climate-related risks and the capacity to manage the adverse effects caused by socio-natural disasters in the country,  The National Disaster Prevention and Response Service has prepared and approved an Annex to the National Emergency Plan for the threat of extreme heat, through the intersectoral work of the roundtable by meteorological risk variable.
Based on the above, given the need to activate the Annex of the National Emergency Plan due to the threat of extreme heat, SENAPRED declares a Preventive Early Warning for the entire national territory due to heat, effective from today until March 31, 2024.
The declaration of this alert constitutes a state of reinforcement of vigilance, through the precise and rigorous monitoring of the risk conditions and the respective vulnerabilities associated with the threat, coordinating and activating the National Disaster Prevention and Response System (SENAPRED) in order to act in a timely manner in the event of an emergency.

High temperatures can have multiple impacts in the fields of health, ecosystems, and the economy, among others. A notorious example of impact are forest fires, which involve a loss of vegetation cover (native forests, forest and agricultural plantations, shrubland), destruction of human settlements and air pollution (De la Barrera et. Al, 2018). However, the most direct and important impacts are on people. The main risks caused by extreme heat are dehydration, cramps, sunburn, heat exhaustion and heat stroke, affecting above all the population that is in a situation of greater vulnerability such as the elderly, children, people with chronic diseases, pregnant people, people with disabilities, among others, and also those who regularly carry out outdoor activities in areas of intense solar radiation.
Heat-related illnesses range from mild to life-threatening, and heat exposure exacerbates common health conditions, including heart, respiratory, and kidney disease. It should be noted that the health effects of high temperature do not necessarily involve exposure to direct solar radiation, but are the product of prolonged exposure to temperatures that exceed the physiological response capacity of the affected people.

Table of impacts by sector:

Health: Dehydration, cramps, sunburn, heat exhaustion, heat stroke, which could have lethal consequences. Worsening of health in people with vulnerable conditions such as the presence of chronic diseases and extreme ages.

Urban centres: Heat island effect. Worsening air quality. Mortality. Power outages.

Agriculture: Decreased productivity, impacts on food security, livestock and crops.

Ecological: Drying up aquifers, melting snowpacks, damage to trees and forests. The start and development of forest fires and soil erosion are encouraged.

Fisheries and aquaculture: Promotes the increase in the presence of harmful, toxic and non-toxic microalgae. Stratification of the water column, decrease of dissolved oxygen content in the water column, mass mortality of resources, exclusion of species, closures of areas due to red tide for the extraction of bivalve shellfish, among others.

Water stress: Increased dry conditions accentuating drought and aridity, generating a decrease in plant growth and affecting the body condition of animals, increased evapotranspiration and dehydration, especially in rainfed areas, affecting various productive sectors such as agriculture and energy, among others.

Energy: Decrease in the production of energy resources, increase in cable buckling and conductor expansion, decrease in the transmission capacity of the system, increase in system operating costs, among others.

Most vulnerable population:

High temperature affects all populations, however, some are more exposed or vulnerable to heat due to their physiological or socioeconomic characteristics and are the ones that suffer the greatest consequences. In this sense, two large groups can be considered: those who are more vulnerable due to physiological conditions and those due to exposure conditions. Regarding physiological conditions, they are those groups that have their thermoregulatory capacity still immature or altered by various circumstances. Regarding the conditions of vulnerability associated with exposure, it refers to groups that, due to their work, recreation or sociodemographic activities, may be at greater risk of exposure to extreme temperatures.

Group by physiological conditions in heat:
-Elderly
- Newborns (RNs), boys and girls.
- Pregnant people
- People with chronic diseases and drug dependents
- People with disabilities, dependency and/or reduced mobility
- Alcohol and/or drug users

Group by Exposure Conditions:

- People who work outdoors
- People who play sports
- People living on the streets or in social isolation
- People with socioeconomic vulnerability
- People living in urban areas
- People living in critical and saturated areas

name: CMR: Other - 12-2023 - Risk of diphtheria epidemic Cameroon
summary:
The Minister of Public Health, in a letter dated November 07, 2023, instructed the regional public health delegates to strengthen diphtheria surveillance.  This communication from the Minister of Public Health comes following the notification of a suspected case in Yaoundé, Central Region, by the central hospital.
Diphtheria is a serious, infectious and contagious, sometimes fatal, bacterial infection of the upper airways. Signs and symptoms usually appear 2 to 5 days after exposure and range in severity from mild to severe. It is caused by a bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae that releases a powerful toxin, which can damage the heart, kidneys and nervous system. It is spread through direct contact or through the air, with respiratory droplets emitted when a person coughs or sneezes. The disease can also be spread through contact with contaminated clothing or objects. 

according to the WHO health emergency report of 12 November 2023 on the diphtheria outbreak, several African countries are currently in an epidemic situation, including Guinea, Niger, Mauritania, South Africa and Nigeria. Nigeria has the highest number of cases with 83.0% of all cases and 73.3% of deaths in epidemiological week 45.
According to the Government, Nigeroa has nearly 7,000 confirmed cases with 471 deaths. To consider the geographical position with Cameroon; the risk of importation of the epidemic is very high both in the border regions (South-West, West, North), and in the interior of the country, especially in the large cities (Yaoundé, Douala, Bafoussam).
 The Centre Region has an estimated population of more than 5 million inhabitants, with the city of Yaoundé alone having nearly 3 million inhabitants, according to the National Institute of Statistics (2015). If the outbreak were to be confirmed and spread, approximately 12 million people would be exposed. 
The overcrowded conditions in several parts of the city are a very important factor that would favour a rapid spread of the disease if it were to reach the population.
It should also be noted that the lack of knowledge of the population about this disease may represent a risk.

name: TZA: 2023 Floods and Landslides
summary:
Torrential rains that began in mid-November have been bringing severe flooding to Tanzania causing numerous fatalities and destruction of infrastructure in Dar Es Salaam, Kigoma, Kagera, Geita and Unguja. Overall, initial estimates suggest that over 75,000 people are directly affected and in need of urgent assistance. The Tanzania Meteorological Agency estimates that over 6 million people have suffered some form of impact from the heavy rains and weather models now indicate that the there is more rain due over at least in the next five days. On 3 December alone, torrential rains caused massive landslides near Mount Hanang, Manyara region, in northern Tanzania. The floods swept away houses, roads and bridges, killing at least 68 people and injuring 116. Thousands of families have lost their homes and are sheltering in public buildings and with host families. Thus far homes belonging to at least 1,150 households (5,600 people) have been damaged, with 750 acres of farmland inundated.

The damage and loss of life are expected to increase as the true extent of the disaster is understood and as more areas are accessed by search and rescue teams. Rescue operations are underway with the help of the military as people are feared buried in thick mud, and the extent of mudslides has made retrieval of bodies and delivery of aid very challenging. Road access is limited, thus air transport is being used. Telecommunication has also been disrupted. Livelihoods have been severely affected, as most of the population depends on agriculture and livestock. This heightens the risk of increased food insecurity, in a country that has seen a spike in food insecurity and malnutrition in 2023 (over 60% increase).

Response: Tanzania Red Cross Society (TRCS) has sent disaster teams and 300 volunteers from the Manyara regional branch and surrounding branches to the affected areas to aid in search and rescue and first-aid, supporting those displaced with essential household items, food, water and sanitation. However, stocks are limited and much more support is needed. The Government has requested TRCS to scale up their support, and they are closely coordinating with the Department of Disaster Management within the Office of the Prime Minister.

countries.name: Micronesia, Federated States of
dtype.name: Drought
name: FSM: Drought - 2023-12 - El Nino Watch
summary:
The situation is still evolving with over 95% of the possibility of occurrence of El Niño. This has placed North Pacific on El Niño alert triggering our need for early actions and preparedness for drought. According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), a transition from ENSO-neutral to El Niño has taken place during May-July 2023. According to the International Research Institute (IRI) of Columbia Climate School, as of mid-Aug 2023, the previously moderate El Niño conditions in the central-eastern equatorial Pacific have strengthened further. Key oceanic and atmospheric variables are consistent with the El Niño, though the atmosphere is not yet fully coupled to the warm sea surface temperature anomalies in the central-eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. A CPC El Niño advisory remains in place for August 2023. Almost all of the models in the IRI ENSO prediction plume forecast an El Niño event during boreal autumn continuing into winter and early spring of 2024, while weakening during the end of the forecast and ENSO-neutral become the most likely category (Apr-Jun 2024 with 59% chance)

El Nino is an evolving situation where the ocean temperature is expected to rise. Warmer waters in the Equatorial Pacific Ocean can suppress the formation of clouds and rain. The hot weather in the North Pacific will trigger more evaporation and available water sources will deplete, while demands for water may increase. Many North Pacific Islands are dependent on the rains to meet daily water demands. The increase in heat and decrease in rainfall means the scarcity of water for inhabitants of the islands. Most of the Islands in the North Pacific countries are remote and transportation is very expensive that which may worsen the situation if early readiness actions are not taken place. Recent El Niño events occurred in 2015-16 and 2018-19. The El Nino in 2015-16 was very strong which resulted in the worst drought in the history of the North Pacific affecting Palau, Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), and the Marshall Islands. The El Nino was much weaker in 2018-2019 however most of Micronesia i.e., Yap state, Palau, and Mariana Islands experienced extensive drought in the early months of 2020. In the past El Niño years, FSM suffered from drought conditions during the winter and spring months. Because they are further west, Yap and western Chuuk tend to be affected earlier and more harshly. In an El Niño year, the winds are weaker than normal (or absent). Warm ocean water from Micronesia surges into the central and eastern Pacific Ocean. This leads to a falling sea level and a greater chance of drought in Micronesia.

countries.name: Somalia

name: SOM: Somaliland Dec 2023 Cholera Outbreak
summary:
On 6th December 2023, the first suspected cholera outbreak was reported in Maroodijeh region and then spread to other regions of Somaliland.

Acute watery Diarrhoea (AWD)/cholera is being reported in two regions of Northern Somalia in the Somaliland regions of Awdal and Hargeisa. As of 5th of February the line has reached 474 cases with nine (9) fatalities reported. According to the Ministry of Health and Development submission to the Health and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Clusters, the deaths reflect a Case Fatality Ratio (CFR) of 1.9 percent, which is above the World Health Organization (WHO) emergency threshold of ≥1 percent. In Somaliland, since December 2023, cholera outbreak cases have been on the increase from the regular/weekly MoHD updates investigation of AWDs in the period 6th Dec 23 to 18th Jan 2024. The MOHD reported 14 cases of testing using RDT and Culture. Out of these tests, 4 cases of tested became AWD/Cholera positive using RDT, where 3 of them were confirmed by culture. This indicates a case positivity rate of 29% by RDT and 21% by Culture. Additionally, it was reported that one of the fatalities from Hargeisa district particularly in October village died on transit (pre-hospital).

The current cholera outbreak is attributed to limited access to safe water, proper sanitation, primary health care services and lowered immunity among children experiencing high levels of acute malnutrition that lowers their immunity to cholera infections. Cholera is an acute intestinal infection that spreads through food and water contaminated with bacteria, often from faeces. While the triggers for outbreaks-like poverty and conflict-are enduring, extreme climate events like floods and droughts reduce access to clean water and create an ideal environment for cholera to thrive. While safe water and proper sanitation can prevent AWD/ cholera, 28% (Source) of Somali families are estimated to lack a functional sanitation facility while 34 percent practice open defecation and 80% lack a handwashing facility.

The Somalia Red Crescent Society Hargeisa Coordination office is working closely with the Ministry of Health and other organizations  responding to the cholera outbreak to ensure that their response is in line with the national response plan. The National Society is also using its network of community volunteers who will receive some training and help to respond to the outbreak.

 
The Ministry of Human and Development has since gone ahead and announced on 4th February 2024(Annexed letter) the outbreak
officially after the confirmation of the test results.

name: AGO: 11-2023 Floods
summary:
Five days of cumulative heavy rains were witness in Angola, resulting in significant floods on 30th November. According to the Angolan Civil Protection and Fire service (SPCB), preliminary data estimates 30 deaths, 5,292 affected households (26,460 people), and farmlands belonging to 10,895 households have been inundated with water. In total, 15 of the 18 Provinces are affected, with the most critical being Luanda, Huambo, Bie, Malanje and Cuanza Norte. The Government continues with Assessments at country level.

The number of victims and damages continues to rise due to the amount of rainfall that has been recorded, causing rivers to overflow, and flooding neighbouring communities in the main city of Luanda, the capital. The populations living in the urban areas have lost their houses, basic sanitation is depleted. There is growing concern in the heath sector due to scarcity of drinking water, contamination of water sources and the long-term stagnation of mixed water obstructed drainage routes can lead to the increase of water-borne diseases such as diarrhoea, cholera and the proliferation of malaria and dengue, diseases that are considered endemic in Angola.

name: CPV: Earthquake - 11-2023 - Seismic Event in Brava
summary:
The island of Brava has about 5,500 inhabitants and is located 120 kilometers west of the capital, Praia, on the island of Santiago.

"Given the situation, the INMG maintains the island's state of alert at level 3, due to the occurrence of frequent earthquakes" which are a sign that "the amount of magma accumulated at the base of the island has increased".

In technical terms, the institute refers to a "harmonic tremor" that occurred early Sunday morning, i.e. a type of "continuous" tremor characterized by "multiple frequencies", produced by the "flow of volcanic gases" in the subsurface.

Seismic tremors are part of the island's history, which has already recorded spikes in activity at the beginning of the year, in May and a fortnight ago, with an earthquake measuring 4.8 on the Richter scale that caused minor damage and cracks in some homes and other structures.

countries.name: Ethiopia
dtype.name: Flood
name: ETH: 2023 Floods
summary:
The months of October to December (OND) constitute an important rainfall season contributing to 20-70 per cent of the annual total rainfall, particularly in the equatorial parts of the Greater Horn of Africa (GHA). Accordingly, there is an exceptionally high forecast probability (>80 per cent) of experiencing wetter than normal rainfall conditions in southern Ethiopia. Elevated rainfall during OND 2023 and favoured by forecasts is already contributing to flooding in areas prone to floods. 
El Niño conditions started between July and August 2023, with the realization of forecasts of wetter than usual rainfall conditions and flood incidences in various parts of Ethiopia in the OND 2023 - January 2024 period.

Floods since rains started in October, have affected at least 763,100 people across several regions and 33 lives lost (in Somali Region alone) and immense damage brought to health, transportation, school infrastructure and livelihoods. The impact of flooding due to seasonal deyr rains  (October to December) in the Somali Region continues to grow as reported by Regional Disaster Risk Management Bureau (DRMB) a total of 33 woredas/districts and 156 sites in nine (9) zones, namely Afder, Daawa, Doolo, Erer, Jarar, Korahe, Liban, Nogob and Shabelle, have been affected by flash and river floods (Afder, Liban and Shabelle having been the most affected). Over 101,940 households (HHs) or more than 611,640 people have been affected and over 40,000 HHs
(close to 240,000 people) displaced as of 15 November. About 300 children have been separated from both parents and require alternative care option and family tracing. Thirty three (33) human deaths and loss of over 4,806 livestock have also been reported, while several villages remain cut off, and over 16,363 ha of cropland and 191 irrigation facilities are reportedly damaged. Most public facilities, in thousands, including schools, health clinics/posts, community centres, water intakes/wells and others, have been damaged or destroyed by the flood in the most affected areas. In Dolo Ado, for example some 5,332 students across six schools are out of school due to damage from floods or are being used as shelters for the displaced community.

name: SUR: Other - 11-2023 - Collapsed mine (goldmine)
summary:
A gold well collapsed in the Matawai area in Suriname today. A number of illegal gold diggers were buried under the rubble. The tragic event took place near Kleine Saramacca, at the illegal mine shaft Camp 21 Pasi and has just been confirmed by President Mr.  Santokhi during the General Political Reflections in the National Assembly. The Surinamese police, the army and the National Coordination Center for Disaster Management are on their way to the area in Brokopondo. The Vice President Mr. Ronnie Brunswijk was flown to the area to take stock.

In the Matawai area in Suriname, where illegal gold seekers were buried on Monday afternoon after a gold pit collapsed, 14 bodies have been recovered at the time of writing. It is expected that there are more victims.

The incident occurred on Monday around 3.30 pm in an area where a gold vein had previously been discovered and large groups had moved there. An excavator was carrying out work at that location when something went wrong.

The Surinamese government launched a major operation and put together a technical team consisting of the Ministers of Natural Resources (NH), Defense, Justice and Police, Regional Development and Sport (ROS) and Finance and Planning.

A team from this cluster is now in the area and is engaged in rescue work, information, recovery and transport of the bodies of the victims and forensic investigation.

There will also be an investigation team led by the Attorney General to thoroughly investigate this incident. Furthermore, options will be examined to request assistance from abroad, if necessary.

The area where the incident took place has been turbulent for some time. Gold company ZIJIN had already requested security measures and the army and police had already destroyed camps set up by illegal gold miners and ordered people to leave the place.

dtype.name: Food Insecurity
name: SWZ: 2023 Eswatini Drought
summary:
The persistent drought is further exacerbating the country’s existing challenges of food insecurity and ability to attain development goals. Consequences of severe, recent droughts for the country have resulted in 25% of the population is vulnerable and acknowledged as food and water insecure, with many households still reliant on welfare and social safety nets. The regions with the highest prevalence of food insecurity are Lubombo and Shiswelweni, the areas most affected by the drought.

The Integrated- Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report published in 2023, indicates that approximately 238,500 people (20%) of the population were estimated to be facing acute food insecurity and requiring urgent humanitarian assistance with Crisis food insecurity which is Phase 3 (crises) of the IPC) in June to September 2023. From October 2023 to March 2024, it is projected that approximately 268,000 people will be classified in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis), and nearly 15,000 will be in IPC Phase 4 (Emergency). The IPC report further indicates that Dry Middleveld (DMV) and the Lowveld Cattle and Maize (LCM) have the highest proportion of the population (30%) classified in IPC Phase 3 indicative of high food insecurity levels in the zones for the current period (Oct 2023-March 2024). During the projected period, these zones will see an increase of 5% of their population in IPC Phase 3 or above and have the highest number of people in IPC Phase 3 or above for both periods of the analysis. Additionally, the Lubombo Plateau will also see 10% of its population falling to worse phases increasing the population in IPC Phase 3 or above to 35% (16,000 from 11,000).  

The Government of Eswatini through the National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) requested the Eswatini humanitarian actors and the Eswatini National Food Security Consortium partners in September 2023 for intervention as currently the Government does not have sufficient funds to respond to the humanitarian/food insecurity needs. There has been no response to the food-insecure communities from June to date (except as planned by RC for October - Jan 2024).

The Red Cross is in parts of Lubombo and Shiselweni regions (the total number of people targeted by the Red Cross interventions is 30,380 people). The total number of estimated food insecure in the Lubombo and Shiselweni regions is 126,074 persons (44,5% of total food insecure), where RC covers only 24% leaving a gap of 76% presently. Food insecurity in the country is likely to worsen with the forecasted El ‘Nino (January- March period).

countries.name: Mongolia

name: MNG: Mongolia Cold Wave (Dzud) response-2024
summary:
This Autumn, snow fell in early November, and as of November 10, more than 57 percent of the country has been covered by snow, in comparison with the previous year (snow cover was 11 percent of the country by November 8, 2022) it is 5 times more this year. 

As of November 27, snow thickness is 50cm in the West, and 20-40cm in the Central part of the country including Tuv, Dornogovi, Dornod, Khentii, Uvs, Zavkhan, and Khovd provinces. In a normal summer year, when the average thickness of snow covering the dominant pasture reaches 12-15 cm in the steppe region, 8-10cm in the mountainous region, and 5-6cm in the Gobi region, it is challenging for animals to feed.

Dzud risk map was produced by NAMEM on November 10, more than 50 percent of the country is at high risk (9 percent at highest, 45 percent at high risk), 40 percent is at moderate, while only 10 percent is at low dzud risk. 

Dzud risk is high in Gobi and Western regions due to drought low precipitation in summer and high frequency of snowstorms across the country. However, Eastern and Central parts of the country experienced a good summer, the risk was significantly increased due to heavy snowfall and snowstorms in early November, causing a hard winter and spring for herder communities. The current winter situation is increasing vulnerability due to the fact that weak livestock, heavy snow-covered pastures, compacted snow surface, extreme coldness, low preparation of hay and fodder, and lack of cash for herders while there is limited market to sell livestock in the high-risk dzud areas.

As of November 30, the second Dzud risk map has been shared by NAMEM. According to the updated Dzud risk map, high-risk areas have been increased to 70% (26% is at high highest risk, 43% is at high risk), 26% is at moderate, and only 5% is at low risk of Dzud. Most parts of Uvs (west), Sukhbaatar (east), and Dornogovi (south) provinces, and some parts of Bayan-Ulgii, Khovd, Zavkhan, Govi-Altai (west), Arkhangai (central), Umnugobi (south), Dornod (east) provinces are at highest risk of Dzud. 

NAMEM has issued early warnings on heavy snow and dust storms that are taking place for this week in the western, central, and southern regions of the country, and the wind speed was expected to reach 18-24m/sec as of December 1. It is anticipated that the snowstorms may worsen the current winter conditions.

Over in Selangor, four districts – Gombak, Hulu Selangor, Hulu Langat, and Sepang – were affected by floods. summary:
A dramatic surge in the number of people returning to Afghanistan from Pakistan since Pakistan’s announcement that all undocumented Afghans must vacate the country by 1 November or risk deportation. The daily number of arrivals, which now ranges between 9,000 and 10,000 individuals, marks a stark contrast to the previous average of approximately 300 individuals a day before the announcement on 15 September 2023. As many as 1.7 million people could be affected. 

The conditions in which they arrive in Afghanistan are dire, with many having endured arduous journeys spanning several days, exposed to the elements, and often forced to part with their possessions in exchange for transportation. 

Many of the humanitarian teams stationed in the areas where people are returning from Pakistan have reported chaotic and desperate scenes among those who have returned. 

Over 29 million Afghans inside the country are currently in need of humanitarian assistance according to UN estimates, with 17.2 million people, 40 percent of the population, struggling to meet their basic food needs. IFRC has wider Humanitarian Crises Operation across 34 provinces of the country. As of 5 November, the Emergency Appeal is 36.5 percent funded.  

The crossing points are Torkham in Nangarhar and Spin Boldak in Kandahar reception, and it will be a prospect that provinces are listed below as cross points which means that some returnees will cross the border from this point as well. countries.name: Kenya

name: KEN: 2023 Floods
summary:
Kenya has been experiencing enhanced rains since September, with alarming levels of rainfall as a result of El Nino conditions and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) which are currently present in Pacic Ocean and Indian Ocean respectively. The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) indicate the rains are expected to peak in November but may continue into January 2024. From beginning of November, the first regions to experience significant and widespread floods were the Northeastern, Eastern followed by the Coastal. The riverine and flash floods have so far caused more damage and displacement. As the floods materialized, KRCS started their response actions immediately. But other regions are now also reporting flood events.

KRCS carried out an aerial survey on 7 Nov and confirmed that several areas remained inaccessible due to the floods and damaged roads, particularly in Mandera County. The extent of floods spread to 37 counties with most affected areas being the Northeastern of the country. While the impact of the rains has been building since early October, signicant impact to which the KRCS mobilized a national response started from 3 Nov with heavy rains, flash floods, and increasing river levels that have caused fatalities, displacement of thousands of people, damage of infrastructure, loss of livestock and property, and restricted access to roads in various regions of the country. The rains have washed away homes and rendered roads impassable leaving thousands homeless. The loss of lives, extensive damage to property, and disruptions in infrastructure underscore the urgency of the situation.

Areas of particular concern include Mandera, Garissa, Wajir, and Tana River, in northern Kenya, where communities have long displayed resilience in the face of water scarcity and hunger during droughts.

Impact as at 6 December:

37 counties are affected by floods.

130,198 households affected of which 59,002 households are displaced.

It's reported that there are 143 fatalities, 240 people injured and 38 are missing.

Livestock, agriculture, infrastructure: 17,287 livestock deaths, 18,394 acres of farmland destroyed. WASH and road infrastructure have also been damaged or destroyed in some affected areas. Local health facilities, schools and other public places have been submerged in water in some of the affected counties.
