summary:
Tana River basin constitutes one of the main river basins in Kenya. Over lower Tana basin, floods have previously been experienced, adversely affecting the communities resulting in humanitarian crises in the years 2013, 2015, 2018 and 2020 according to the Kenya Flood EAP. For this reason, the Kenya flood EAP covers this and two other basins (Nzoia and Athi). On July 4, 2023, the World Meteorological Organization declared onset of El Nino. The phenomenon is known to enhance seasonal rainfall over Kenya and most parts of the world. In August 2023, the Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) issued the October to December seasonal forecast for Kenya that emphasized on above average seasonal rainfall expected, driven by El Nino coupled with a positive Indian Ocean Dipole. The rainfall season began peaking in the last week of October. Since the onset of the season in October, the season is exhibiting rainfall that lately, has abruptly been filling up the river channels. Throughout this period, KRCS has been monitoring the risk of flooding. On 02 November, a flood wave was observed over Garissa Bridge— the first gauging station over lower Tana. The water level at this point reached 4 meters, a level that has been earmarked as alarming, for which the discharge overtops the riverbanks leading to flooding further downstream. The level is red-marked by the Water Resources Authority in Kenya to serve a flood alarm over the river basin.

A flood wave observed at Garissa Bridge takes about 48 hours to reach the next station (Hola) in the downstream. By November 4th, water levels at Garissa had surpassed 5 meter mark— bordering the highest mark of the river gauge while the levels at Hola have reached alarm level. Additionally, rainfall forecast for the current week1 indicates Kenyan central highlands are expected to continue receiving heavy rainfall. The flood wave is expected to begin overtopping riverbanks along the lower Tana as heavy rains continue to be experienced over central highlands and other Tana basin source regions. At this time, streamflow forecast at Garissa Bridge from GLoFAS model remain low, under the 1-in-2 year flood. While the GLoFAS forecast is the trigger as per the Kenya flood EAP, caution is taken not to ignore the observed imminent flood at this time. But we choose to proceed with activation of the flood Early Actions despite GLoFAS’s miss of this flood wave. We recognize analysis of the GLoFAS skill over Tana basin was relatively low with about double False Alarm Ratio (at 0.5) compared to performance of the model in other basins. The low forecast skill in GLoFAS is likely related to lack of assimilation of observed data.

2 conditions for activating the flood EAP have been met:

a) A threshold for extreme flood has been met at Garissa Bridge and Hola giving creating anticipation of floods in the next few days

b) Short range forecast indicates that heavy rainfall is expected to continue accumulating over the source region of River Tana.

Wind speed reached 16-22 m/s causing a strong snowstorm that lasted about 5-15 hours. Early warnings were issued 2nd of November by NEMA.  Due to the hazardous snow storm, 37 out of 46 people who went missing while driving or herding have been rescued, 42 vehicles and 113 individuals have been evacuated to a safe place by the NEMA search and rescue team in 10 locations of 8 provinces including Khovd, Uvs, Zavkhan, Arkhangai, Tuv, Uvurkhangai, Selenge, and Dornod provinces. 8 casualties including 1 child have been reported in Tuv and Uvurkhangai provinces. According to NAMEM, another snowstorm is expected to occur between the 6 and 7th of this month in the West, North, and Central part of the country and the second early warning have been issued by NEMA on the 6th.

According to NAMEM, the third early warning of snow-storm issued on November 16th, and a heavy snowstorm occurred on November 21st night in Bulgan, Selenge, Tuv, Uvurkhangai, Dundgovi, Umnugovi, Khentii, Dornod, Sukhbaatar, and Dornogov provinces. The road access has been closed from Khentii provincial to Berkh village, and the road access from Baruun-Urt soum in Sukhbaatar provinces on November 22 for 13 hours, due to the snowstorm. A total of 333 people who went missing were rescued by the NEMA search and rescue team in 27 soums of Sukhbaatar, Dornod, Khentii, and Dornogovi provinces, and one casualty has been reported in Dorgovi province while herding. 

On November 27, another snow-storm occurred in some parts of Zavkhan, Khuvsgul, Arkhangai, and Uvurkhangai provinces, and 6 out of 40 vehicles stuck in the snow were rescued by the NEMA search and rescue team in Zavkhan province. The relevant government agencies are taking immediate action to clean the road for safeties is ongoing.  

Next snowstorms are expected to occur in the East, West, and Northern parts of the country between November 28-30, and air temperature is expected to reach (-24C) - (-30C) Celsius. 

NAMEM has issued early warnings on heavy snow and dust storms that are taking place for this week in western, central, and southern parts of the country, and were expected to reach 18-24m/sec as of December 1.  

As of December 4, a strong wind has started from 3 AM in Khovd, Uvs, Zavkhan, Bayan-Ulgii, Govi-Altai (west), and Khuvsgul (north)  provinces speeding up to 10-38m/sec. Due to the storm, a total of 1672 people are out of power at 3 locations in Khovd province, and the entire region of Govi-Altai provinces (population 58,735, source: National Statistics Office, 2022). Local authorities are taking immediate action to restore power is ongoing. After the local action, the same night, 12 out of 18 soums' power has been restored and 6 soums are having power outages where approximately 14,894 people live. Road access from and to Zavkhan (west) province has been closed due to the storms and it is not possible to take any action from the government during the storms. An emergency working group led by NEMA is monitoring the situation and preparing to take action. 

It is forecasted that the next snowstorms will occur between December 6-9 in western, eastern, northern, and central parts of the country reaching the speed of 14-20m/sec. The early warnings have been issued by NAMEM, NEMA, and the MRCS in the target regions through social media and mass messaging.

name: CAF: High Winds CAR 2023
summary:
Between 31 October and 1 November 2023, torrential rains accompanied by violent winds occurred in twelve neighbourhoods, including: Borno, Amameu, Yadouma, Yafara, Boy-gbaya, Moussa-Gbadou 1, 2 and 3 in the town of Bria, capital of the Haute Kotto Prefecture, causing damage to property and injuries to people.

Impact of torrential rains/strong winds

726 households (6,006 people) affected: 1480 men, 1,502 women and 3,024 children.

7 people were injured, including 1 by lightning.

406 houses partially destroyed.

300 houses completely destroyed.

26 family latrines damaged.

12 community wells damaged.

Almost all affected households live with host families and in schools.

The town of Bria is already hosting more than 500 Sudanese refugees who have not yet been relocated to the site designated by the government in agreement with the UNHCR. The intensive exploitation of mining sites for several decades exposed the area to intense deforestation and therefore subject to the effects of climate change marked by the occurrence of violent winds.

The local branch of the Central African Red Cross mobilized and deployed 20 rescue volunteers who assessed the situation, counted households, evacuated the injured to the Bria hospital and relocated the victims to shelters, with the support of local authorities.

The atmosphere will be cool at night and early morning. These conditions are due to the influence of Tropical Depression 19-E.

Immediately after the first tremor NRCS, EOC has contacted Dhading and Chitwan District Chapters and inquire about the possible impact of the tremor. According to respective President of the chatpters, there were no infromation about the any type of causalities reported yet in both the districts. However, EOC is in continuous in-touch with other adjoing districts also to get reports of any possible impacts of the earthquake.

countries.name: Yemen
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: YEM: Cyclone - 2023-10 - - Cyclone Tej-Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm (Yemen)
summary:
Tropical cyclone TEJ made landfall over the southern coast of Al Mahrah Governorate on the night of 23 October and continued to move northwestward. On 24 October at 0.00 UTC, its centre was located about 20 km south of Al Ghaidah (Yemen) and 240 km west-southwest of Salalah (Oman).According to the media, some houses have been severely impacted, as well as roads and crops in Al-Mahra Governorate. In addition, interruptions of the communications and electricity networks have been reported.The authorities of Al-Mahra Governorate asked the citizens living in the affected areas to go to nearby shelters.TEJ is forecast to move further north-westward weakening and dissipating on 25 October. For the next 24 hours, more heavy rainfall is forecast over the Al-Mahra, Hadramout and Shabwa Governorates of Yemen and over the Dhofar governorate in Oman.( ECHO Daily Flash of 24 October 2023)

Large areas of Al Mahrah experienced heavy rain, flooding, and strong winds as a result of the cyclone since Monday morning.

A Yemeni family, consisting of 7 individuals, died in Al-Mahra Governorate after the collapse of their house in the Huswain District due to torrential floods resulting from the tropical condition Tej.

The cyclone also partially damaged many other homes and swept away large agricultural areas across Al Mahrah. Hundreds of families have fled to schools and shelters.There are now more 53 accomedation centers distributed over Al Ghaydah Al Masilah , SayhutHat and Shahan which are buildings and offices and Schools, Learning centers.

The number of affected HHs and individuals is 1711 HHs and 11977 individuals at Al Ghaydah Al Masilah Sayhut , Hat , Hsahan Districts.

A total of 400 shelters have been completely demolished, while 1311 have been partially destroyed.

The displacement of many families from the Al-Abri area, as well as Muhafeef and the neighborhood of Kalshat in Al-Ghaydah district, to hotels inside Al-Ghaydah district

Due to the strength of the winds, several residential water tanks flew into the air, along with some road regulations, many trees, and portions of older homes falling to the ground.

Needs:

Water points, latrines, and water tanks are urgently needed, as are NFIs, as well as food for the 1711 HHs. Cash assistance as well as psychological support are also needed.

The Yemeni Meteorological Center said that the tropical situation will continue during the upcoming hours with heavy rain across Al Mahrah and other eastern provinces, calling on local residents to take caution.

In Socotra , Heavy rains in the Socotra archipelago caused the displacement of dozens of families from the 14th of October neighborhood near the coast of Hadibo. Families affected by the floods were transferred to schools, and the rain and winds caused the closure of some roads as a result of the torrential rains washing away the dust, and a number of Farms were exposed to drift, and dozens of livestock died.  Earlier on On Sunday, there is one case of infection of a child after the door of their house fell on him in the district of Qalansiya and his condition is stable.  Rain, wind and high waves caused two fishing vessels to sink in the port of Hulaf, and there were no human casualties. The toll of damage so far is 314 houses completely damaged, 227 partially damaged , and two ferries / fishing boats were damaged, and two others drowned due to the cyclone.

In Hadramout , High waves and sea frenzy on the coasts of Corniche Mukalla and the branch will warn residents in Low-lying areas of the coast will be evacuated. An ambulance moves from the branch to the city of Mukalla to prepare and station to face any emergency matters. Yemen faces dire humanitarian conditions due to over nine years of war. Natural disasters exacerbate the suffering of millions in the country.

countries.name: Antigua and Barbuda
dtype.name: Other
name: ATG: Other - 2023-10 - Tropical Storm Tammy
summary:
The Antigua and Barbuda Meteorological Services issued a Tropical Cyclone Alert on October 18, 2023, raising concerns about a possible weather disturbance, also known as AL94, which is moving closer to the Northeast Caribbean.

The system has sustained winds less than 30 mph. The system is not yet a tropical cyclone but has an 80% chance of becoming one.

The projected forecast path, AL94, could be near the region by late Friday or early Saturday, potentially as a tropical storm.

The National Office of Disaster Services issued a press release to urge residents to activate their hurricane plans and take all the necessary action required to prepare for the pending weather.

The Antigua and Barbuda Red Cross Secretariat has briefed their staff and volunteer teams to prepare for possible deployment and activation of the EOC.

countries.name: Antigua and Barbuda
dtype.name: Other
name: ATG: Other - 2023-10 - Tropical Storm Tammy
summary:
A Tropical Storm Watch was issued for Antigua and Barbuda at 5 a.m. Thursday morning. Tammy was located about 467 miles southeast of Antigua with winds of 60 mph, moving west-northwest at 15 mph. There is now a 77% chance of storm winds for Barbuda and 64% of the same for Antigua. Further, there is a 12% chance of hurricane winds for Barbuda and a 1% chance for Antigua. A TS watch remains in effect for both islands; however, we are considering a TS warning and a H watch later today. Storm conditions are most likely to start Friday evening and could last for up to 10 hours. In the worst-case scenario, there could be hurricane winds for a couple hours.

On October 19, 2023, the government of Antigua issued a tropical storm warning and a hurricane watch for Antigua and Barbuda.

According to Tammy's current forecast track, Antigua and Barbuda are expected to face the brunt of its impact. Storm-force winds and gusts of hurricane strength, in addition to up to 8 inches of rain, are forecast.

The National Society continued its preparatory actions,

The President of the Antigua and Barbuda Red Cross Society, Dr. Jose Humphreys, has officially activated the NS's Emergency Operations Center. A number of volunteers will be equipped and dispatched to the various centers across the country while reporting and receiving support from the EOC Team at the National Society's headquarters on Old Parham Road. The EOC team is supported by the Antigua and Barbuda Fire Brigade and will closely monitor the storm in real time and offer ongoing support as the need arises. The ABRCS will continue to collaborate with the National Office of Disaster Services and other lead agencies to ensure minimal impact and post-disaster recovery.

All ABRCS Disaster Response personnel are fully equipped with medical and general disaster response equipment and trained in emergency medical and disaster response. The President of ABRCS is reminding all residents to take the necessary preparatory steps to mitigate risks and protect life and property.

countries.name: Djibouti
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: DJI: Epidemic - 2023-10 - acute diarrhea
summary:
The town of Obock and its outlying areas are experiencing an unprecedented surge in migrants, who are piling up by the thousands.  The strong presence and, above all, the considerable increase in the number of migrants in Obock is due to the closure of the borders by the Yemenis on the other side of the Red Sea.
As a result, the interior of Obock's districts, the beaches and especially the Fanteherou area, a popular district which is the last and main gathering place for migrants before crossing to Yemen, remain flooded with them. 
All the watering places are overflowing. These migrants share the same environmental space as the host population. As a result, the first cases of acute diarrhoea appeared among the migrant population in the Fanteherou district. 
Initially, at wednesday 18th October 9 cases were detected among the migrant population, but in the same afternoon this number rose to 18. The next day was counted  33 case were recorded and one dead person. 
The local health authorities declared an epidemic of acute diarrhoea in the town of Obock on the morning of Wednesday October 18, and a care and treatment center has been set up in the main courtyard of the Obock medical-hospital center to receive patients suffering from the epidemic.
So far 33 cases have been recorded, all from the migrant population. The host population is unaffected, but the situation is likely to worsen with the onset of the cool season if measures are not taken.

summary:
According to NSW Rural Fire service reports a fire began in Moparrabah, about 30 kilometres west of Kempsey, on the afternoon of Monday 16 October 2023 and has since burnt through more than 10,000 hectares.

Throughout the day more than 1,000 firefighters were active across the state with three fires reaching emergency level. As of 17 October, 70 fires are burning around the state with 30 yet to be contained.

The NSW Rural Fire Service said properties have been lost, but it was not clear how many or if that included any homes.

Two evacuation centres opened at Kempsey (Newcastle Region) and Kyogle (Northern Rivers Region). An evacuation centre set up at the Kempsey Showground West Kempsey with some residents and domestic animals staying on site.

Sadly a man died after the bushfire impacted his property 30km west of Kempsey.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.society_name: The South African Red Cross Society
dtype.name: Flood
name: ZAF:2023-10 Floods in Western Cape
summary:
Severe weather between Sept. 23-26 resulted in flooding, loss of life and displacement of residents, severe damage on private and public infrastructure, road closures, and power outages across Western Cape province. The severe weather and flooding have affected at large group of people in the and around the city, including eight fatalities due to electrocution by illegal electricity connections. Damage assessments are ongoing, but initial reports indicate more than 1,500 structures impacted by flooding. The Kuils River overflowed, flooding Mfuleni Township and forcing around 2,710 families to evacuate. Reports also indicate evacuations in Faure and Sandvlei. Over 16,000 people have been reported to be affected by the floods.

This is whilst 7,100 informal structures were adversely affected. According to News 24, it reported 11 fatalities in the affected areas. Furthermore, there are reports of nearly 250 schools which are affected by the disaster.

The Bot River overflowed in the town of Botrivier, flooding large parts of the N2 Highway and cutting off road access.

Flooding also resulted in closures across other highways, including parts of the N1, R60, and R62. More than 100,000 people in Western Cape Province were without power at the height of the storm. Authorities have not restored power to most people, and around 15,000 remain without electricity as of Sept. 27.

Authorities in Cape Town issued a major incident declaration due to the flooding. Flooding and associated disruptions are still ongoing across Western Cape Province.

summary:
The recent flooding triggered by heavy monsoon rains in Myanmar’s southern areas. That has displaced more than 3,400 families and disrupted traffic on the rail lines that connect the country’s biggest cities.

4.     It seems that the impact of floods is likely to rise.

countries.name: Malaysia
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: Malaysia - Dengue 2023
summary: Uncertain weather conditions are among the contributing factors to the increase in dengue fever cases in Kelantan. State Health Department (JKNK) director Datuk Dr. Zaini Hussin said this was due to the hot weather and heavy rain that occurred recently, which provided favorable conditions for the breeding of Aedes mosquitoes. Dengue fever is still endemic in Kelantan with cases reported throughout the year and until September with a cumulative total of more than 1,500 cases. For Tumpat district, 220 cases have been reported up to September 30 this year compared with only 38 cases recorded in the same period last year, which is an increase of 479 percent. meanwhile, in Perak, the cumulative number of dengue fever cases increased to 2,762 cases from January to September this year, compared to 851 cases in the same period last year. State Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs, and National Integration Committee chairman A. Sivanesan said this was an increase of 1,911 cases or 224.6 percent. He said one death was recorded in Kuala Kangsar during this period while there were no fatalities during the same period last year. “A total of 75 dengue fever cases were recorded in the 39th epidemiological week (ME) this year compared to only 24 cases last year. Among the areas with the most number of dengue fever cases recorded are Kampung Tersusun Batu 5 in the Kinta district with 23 cases while Block A (Zone 1) of the Royal Malaysian Navy Base in Manjung district had 10 cases.

countries.name: Somalia
dtype.name: Flood
name: SOM:2023 Floods
summary:
In July, ICPAC issued the seasonal forecast alerting on the El Nino phenomenon that will be coupled with the effect of Indian ocean. The effect of El Nino as per the past is usually higher in Eastern and Southern countries. In the East, the most impacted following the forecast include Somalia with onset to materialize during the Deyr season and with a peak to impact from September 24 to October 24. Refer to figure 3 of ICPAC report generated by utilizing daily rainfall forecasts derived from three Global Climate Models (namely ECMWF, Mateo-France, and ECCC-Canada) from the C3S Climate Data Store, incorporating a collective of 112 ensemble members).

According to ICPAC, DEYR 2023 climate outlook and its implication on livelihoods and programming over Somalia issued on 05 September 2023 mentioned that the “Deyr Short Rains’’ season would have an exceptionally high likelihood (from 55% to 85 %) of 10 consecutive rainy days. Rainy days are expected with higher likelihood of cumulative amounts exceeding 150 mm. El Nino, as per historical analysis will enhance the predictions. The past 4 incidence of El Nino have been during the same onset period for East Africa. The highest impact was constantly between September to December, with a decline in January. Analysis includes 1997, 2009 and 2006 and 2016 with extreme disaster events. El Nino probability of occurrence analyzed in July showed a 90% probability to materialize.

According to images broadcast by national channels, a group of Guatemalans protesting in the Plaza de la Constitución was repressed by agents later that infiltrators with their faces covered and sticks caused the riots.
After the disturbances that occurred in the Plaza de la Constitución, the National Civil Police reports the apprehension of Gilberth "N" of 18 years, Diego "N" of 26 years and Juan "N" of 21 years, after having caught them carrying metal pipes, throwing stones, disturbing public order.

The Minister of the Interior, David Napoleón Barrientos, confirms that a group of infiltrators identified themselves within the demonstration in the Plaza de la Constitution.
Alleged protesters break glass in a municipal exhibition hall in the Central Plaza. Riot police arrive at the place and a cistern to push people back.
A few minutes later, the President of the Republic, on national television, condemns the road blockades and says that there is an arrest warrant against leaders who have Organized the general strike. The organizers have been identified even there are foreigners," says the President. Calls on President-elect Bernardo Arévalo, meet to continue the transition with the mediation of the OAS.

countries.name: Cameroon
dtype.name: Landslide
name: WRC: Landslide - 2023-10 - Landslide MBANKOLO-YAOUNDE
summary:
in the

evening of October 08, 2023 at around 6 p.m. following a very heavy and long rain of more than 2 hours of the time, landslides occurred in the Mankolo district lieut called "Febe village". at the site of the disaster there was a large ravine that shelters one of the sources of the Mfoundi River, and that rainwater over time has eroded. More than forty years ago, an artificial lake was built on this site, and several populations have settled there because of the beauty of the place,  which has become almost a tourist site. Due to the relief of the site, which is very steep, the riverine populations had built a retaining wall on the slope of the lake, leaving a very small runoff passage for the water.

After this very heavy rain, the waters of the lake could not find a way through and broke the protective wall, grazing all the houses in the path. All these houses were buried in the mudslide.

To date, the damage is incalculable as many people remain unaccounted for and excavations continue. According to the figures made public at the moment, 28 deceased people have been found, many people remain missing, more than twenty houses have been  devastated by the violent and sudden mudslide. 

Evaluations are underway and the figures may evolve according to the progress of the excavations and researches.

countries.name: Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, MENA Region, Syrian Arab Republic
countries.society_name: Egyptian Red Crescent Society, Jordan National Red Crescent Society, Lebanese Red Cross, IFRC MENA, Syrian Arab Red Crescent
dtype.name: Complex Emergency
name: Middle East Crisis | MENA
summary:
Since 7 October 2023, hostilities have significantly escalated across the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, leading to a severe humanitarian crisis in the occupied Palestinian territories (oPt). The situation continues to deteriorate rapidly, with increasing casualties, damaged infrastructure, restricted access, and mass internal displacement.

As of 15 September 2024, more than 41,252 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza [OCHA]. Over 1.9 million people in Gaza are estimated to be internally displaced [OCHA]. The Gaza Strip has been under an electricity blackout since 11 October 2023, and a severe fuel shortage has led to the closure of most hospitals, particularly in the north. This has increased the pressure on remaining medical facilities and resulted in a rise in medical evacuations to neighboring countries.

Food and water supplies in Gaza are critically low, with only a fraction of the needed aid arriving through the borders. Humanitarian access remains highly restricted, with significant challenges including fuel shortages, communication shutdowns, and stringent restrictions. Safe passage for humanitarian aid remains key to deliver life-saving supplies. [OCHA]

In the West Bank, as of 10 September 2024, at least 705 Palestinians have been killed and over 5,700 injured since 7 October 2023 [OCHA]. The region has seen a significant increase in violence: between 7 October 2023 and 12 August 2024, OCHA recorded around 1,250 attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinians, leading to fatalities, injuries, and property damage. 

The humanitarian situation is further compounded by movement restrictions. This has disrupted access to essential services, including healthcare, which has faced over 500 attacks since October 2023. Displacement is also a major issue with 88 thousands IDPs according to UN reports.

Meanwhile, increased conflicts along the southern borders of Lebanon in recent months, with a spike in September 2024, have led to a sharp increase in internal displacement, with different reports indicating the number of IDPs as anywhere between 200,000 upwards to the hundreds of thousands. As of 27 September 2024, at least 1640 civilians have been killed, and 8408 injured. [MoPH]. Lebanon is experiencing a multi-layered crisis, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict. The country is dealing with a protracted political, financial, and socio-economic crisis, which has severely impacted the availability and affordability of basic services such as healthcare, education, and clean water.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) and its National Societies have been providing critical assistance, including medical care, food, water, and shelter. Despite these efforts, the scale of the crisis requires more resources and support to meet the growing needs.

countries.name: Afghanistan

summary:
Multiple earthquakes struck western Afghanistan on Saturday between 11am-12 local time, with the first and largest at a magnitude of 6.3, according to U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). Some humanitarian impacted is expected. NS collecting information, according to initial unverified information from ARCS there are five deaths and 30 injuries around Zinda Jan.

 The earthquake’s epicentre was in Zinda Jan, 40 km northwest of Herat.  As of now, no official reports of casualties. However, some structural damages to houses and buildings have been observed in certain areas

In Herat City, hundreds of people left their homes and workplaces, and headed to the streets.

According to preliminary information from ARCS, there are five deaths and 100 injuries around Zinda Jan, but this is yet to be verified with the authorities. ARCS has activated their emergency operations centre to monitor and closely coordinate the response . IFRC is coordinating with PNS in the country as well as with ANDMA , the national disaster management agency. 

According to initial findings of the assessment the authorities, 2,445 people died, with a further 9,240 people injured. Partners and local authorities anticipate the number of casualties to increase as search and rescue efforts continue amid reports that some people may be trapped under collapsed buildings.

countries.name: Israel
dtype.name: Complex Emergency
name: Israel - Complex Emergency
summary:
In the early morning of 7 October 2023, armed groups launched a multi-front (land, air, and sea) operation against Israel. The assault combined gunmen crossing into several Israeli towns targeting various Israeli military installations and nearby settlements with a heavy barrage of rockets fired from Gaza. Rockets have been fired from Gaza towards Israeli villages and cities surrounding and up to 170 km from the border, including the major cities of Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, and Beer-Sheba. On 13 October a rocket was fired to the Galilee (North of Israel). Ongoing rocket launches and fighting has taken place since the armed hostilities began. 

The deadliest attack in Israel in decades, (source Israeli Defense Forces – IDF spokesperson) more than 1,300 Israeli and foreign nationals, including women, children, and the elderly, were killed in Israel by members of the armed groups, including 3 Magen David Adom in Israel (MDA) members . According to the Ministry of Health, at least 3,391 people have been injured.

During the attacks on Israeli communities and military bases, dozens of Israeli captives - including numerous women, children and elderly - are believed to have been taken into Gaza (as of 13 October, as per IDF spokesperson, 97 persons are confirmed to be abducted) .

There are also several security incidents registered in the Northern border of Israel (with Lebanon and Syria). There have been reported attacks against military bases and attempts to cross the border by arms barriers, mortar shelling and drone attacks.

The Israeli Defense Forces have closed roads near Gaza, as well as the Allenby/King Hussein bridge. Restrictions are in place in many other areas within rocket reach. A "state of emergency" in Israel and a "state of war" have officially been declared by the Israeli government, with limitations on public gatherings in all the territory up to 80 km from Gaza, and no schools open until 14 October.

The communities around Gaza have been evacuated and the inhabitants of Shderot (the largest town in the area, have been offered the opportunity to evacuate). Some communities in the north (very close to the border) have been evacuated as well. Bed-driven patients in the affected communities have been evacuated. Hospitals in the north and the south of Israel have been transferred to facilities in the center to free bad capacity. Contingency plans in all the hospitals have been activated and wards moved to underground sheltered facilities.

name: PSE: Complex Emergency - 10-2023 - OpT Conflict Escalation#313 up to 24/2/2024
summary:
In the wake of the Israeli aggression on the Gaza Strip starting October 2023, and the escalation of attacks in the West Bank, the Palestine Red Crescent Society has increased its preparedness to address the humanitarian, relief, and medical needs of those affected by the Israeli attacks in the occupied Palestinian territory. 

North Gaza and Gaza Governorate:
• Gaza Branch and its Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Center: The facilities of the Gaza branch were entirely damaged by the intense bombardment in the Tal al-Hawa region of Gaza City. Consequently, PRCS ceased its service provision as of 14/11/2023, compelling the medical and administrative staff to evacuate the area.
• PRCS Al-Quds Hospital: Suffered substantial damage from the Israeli shelling surrounding it and the direct strikes on various parts of facilities and sections. Following a siege lasting over 14 days, operations were halted, leading to the displacement of its staff, patients, and approximately 14,000 persons southward on 14/11/2023. To date, the hospital remains non-operational. It had attended to (1,169) injuries from October 2023 until 11/11/2023.
• North Gaza Branch and its EMS Center: Endured significant destruction due to relentless bombing by Israeli forces, rendering the provision of EMS services unfeasible. The emergency response teams were thus relocated to a “safer” location in the center of Jabalia refugee camp, away from the intense bombings. An UNRWA clinic was adapted as a temporary base for providing EMS services in the North Gaza governorate.
PRCS Branch and EMS Center: EMS and relief staff are operational 24/7 to respond to the humanitarian needs of both residents and displaced individuals within the governorate. The branch's facility in Deir al-Balah currently accommodates approximately 300 displaced people from the North Gaza region.
PRCS Branch and its Service Centers: Since the onset of January, the headquarters and various PRCS service centers in Khan Younis have been subject to repeated attacks by the Israeli occupation forces. These attacks have led to casualties among the displaced seeking a safe refuge at the facility, with the numbers exceeding 7,000individuals. Not only has the facility sustained significant damages due to the bombings, but also the Israeli occupation forces have enforced a stringent blockade around the premises, severely restricting the movement of PRCS staff and hindering their capacity to execute their humanitarian mandate within the governorate. The continuous and direct attacks necessitated the evacuation of displaced individuals through a humanitarian corridor. This was devised to safeguard their lives, particularly after the tragic loss of (27) individuals during the siege due to Israeli targeting. Faced with logistical challenges in transporting the deceased civilian martyrs, the staff were forced to bury them within the grounds of Al-Amal Hospital.
• Al-Amal Hospital: it has repeatedly been the target of military attacks by the Israeli occupation forces, leading to significant damage to different sections and floors and threatening the life of the PRCS staff and patients. summary:
A magnitude of 5.3 earthquake hit western Nepal on Monday, 3 October 2022, at 14.40 PM local time. Strong aftershock with 6.3 Richter scale occurred immediately after main shock at 15:06 PM and second after shock of 5.1 Richter scale recorded. The epicenter of the quake was located in Bajhang district. Tremors were felt in neighboring districts (Doti, Achham, Bajura, Dadeldhura, Baitadi and Darchula) as well as Kathmandu, Nepal and also in New Delhi, India. Initially, it was reported that earthquake has impacted houses, schools and public building. In the earthquake affected districts people are staying in open spaces, neighbor houses and the nearest schools that are located in the safe place.

According to situation report published by Provincial Emergency Operation Centre (PEOC) of Sudur-Paschim Province, moderate impact has been reported in seven districts. Data received from districts are as follows:

Doti district: The impact of earthquake is nominal in the district. As per the PEOC situation report, there is no any human casualty however, 1 house is partially damaged and 8 school buildings are damaged.

Achham district: The earthquake has damaged 12 house fully, 2 houses are partially, 15 people are displaced and 5 people are injured.

Bajura district: As per the IRA report received from district, 199 houses are fully damaged, 548 houses are partially damaged and 2 people are injured in this district.

Bajhang district: As per the IRA report received from district, 91 houses are fully damaged, 318 houses are partially damaged, 20 people are injured and 1 woman is missing due to landslide triggered by the earthquake. One section of main highway (Jaya Prithvi highway) is blocked due to landslide the district is isolated from road transportation service.

Dadeldhura district: 4 houses are partially damaged and there is no any further impact so far.

Baitadi district: 2 houses are fully damaged, 3 houses are partially damaged and 2 people are injured in this district.

Darchula district: 1 house is partially damaged and the impact of earthquake is comparatively less in this district.

Nepal Red Cross Society is working in the affected districts to distribute the tarpaulins, collecting detail information. Further details about the activities are described below.

name: PAK: Population Movement - 2023-10 - Pakistan Issues Ultimatum to Afghan Refugees: Leave or Face Deportation
summary:
Pakistan's Interior Minister, Sarfraz Bugti, has announced a stringent crackdown targeting "undocumented immigrants," including Afghan nationals, in Pakistan. Over recent years, a significant number of Afghans, fleeing the threat of persecution following the Taliban's takeover of Afghanistan in August 2021, sought refuge in Pakistan. Unfortunately, they have encountered many challenges, such as arbitrary detentions, arrests, and the constant specter of deportation. The extensive registration process has left the majority without Proof of Registration (PoR) or Afghan Citizen Card (ACC) credentials, which are vital for maintaining legal status as Afghan refugees in Pakistan. Many initially entered Pakistan with regular visas, which have since lapsed.

 

The UNHCR has issued a non-return advisory for Afghans residing outside their homeland following the Taliban's ascent to power. As per UNHCR data, there are over 3.7 million Afghans in Pakistan, who left Afghanistan due to both economic hardships and political instability. Regrettably, only 1.4 million of them possess formal registration.

 

"Afghans in Pakistan are fleeing persecution by the Taliban, leading them to live in highly precarious circumstances. They are forced to navigate complex procedures for refugee registration in Pakistan or endure protracted waits for potential relocation to other countries. Forcing their return to Afghanistan could place them in severe jeopardy."

"Afghans in Pakistan are in desperate need of increased support. The obstacles and delays they encounter in the process of registering as refugees or pursuing relocation to third countries have left them in legal limbo, rendering them even more susceptible to harassment and social stigma."

Current Updates:

Numerous organizations are actively formulating their official positions on this issue, with the intention of sharing them with the public in due course.

We have engaged with various stakeholders to evaluate the patterns of repatriation along the borders. Although there has been movement observed, it remains uncertain whether these movements are in response to the current circumstances or for other reasons.

Housing societies in Islamabad have issued notices to property owners who have rented their premises to Afghan migrants. The notices request the evacuation of Afghan nationals from these properties. It is emphasized that any discovery of illegal immigrants during the evacuation will result in legal action against the property owner. (Translation of the attached notice)

Interim Foreign Minister Jalil Abbas Jilani defended the order for all illegal immigrants, including 1.73 million Afghans, to depart, asserting that no other country permits illegal immigration, and this decision aligns with international norms.

Media reports have brought attention to the apprehension of illegal immigrants in Islamabad and Quetta.

Additionally, media reports have indicated that a delegation established by the Islamic Emirate to oversee the return of refugees from Pakistan has announced plans to establish a new refugee camp in the Lalapor district of Nangarhar.

We are available and ready to provide any necessary assistance.

summary:
The Air Pollution Index (API) readings in 15 locations across the country continue to be unhealthy as of 8 a.m. today. A check on the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website shows that Cheras has the highest reading of 164, followed closely by Nilai at 163. Cheras reached a reading of 160 as early as 1 a.m., and the maximum reading of 165 was recorded at 7 a.m. today. Nilai, on the contrary, has recorded a reading of 163 since 6 a.m. Other areas in the unhealthy category are Petaling Jaya, Shah Alam, and Seremban, all at 158, Putrajaya and Banting (157), and Port Dickson (156). They are followed by Batu Muda (154), Klang, Johan Setia, and Bukit Rambai (153), Alor Gajah (136), Taiping (129), and Tangkak (107).

 

APIMS measures the API readings between 0 and 50 as good, 51 and 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy and any readings of 300 and above are declared as hazardous. Malaysia is suffering from the haze due to the re-emergence of transboundary haze pollution from Indonesia. Department of Environment director-general Wan Abdul Latiff Wan Jaffar in a statement on Friday, attributed the latest smog to hundreds of forest fires in Indonesia. He added the fires were worsening air pollution on the country's west coast and in Sarawak on the Malaysian part of Borneo Island. "Overall air quality in the country shows deterioration. Forest fires that occur in the southern part of Sumatra and the central and southern parts of Kalimantan (Borneo), Indonesia have caused a haze to cross borders," he said. He also said satellite imagery showed 52 forest fire "hotspots" in Sumatra and 264 in Borneo, according to a report from the Singapore-based Asean Specialized Meteorological Centre (ASMC), which tracks haze affecting Southeast Asia.

summary:
With the intensification of the southwest monsoon, Sri Lanka has experienced heavy rainfall in Western, Sabaragamuwa, provinces and in Galle and Matara districts, which are the most affected areas. Indeed, the heavy rains, high winds, and floods due to the water levels of the Nilwala Gin Kalu and athtnagalu oya Rivers have risen to alarming levels. In the Matara and Gampaha districts, according to the Disaster Management Center (DMC), most damages were reported. total of thirty-two Divisional Secretary divisions are severely affected. As a result of the continued heavy rains and strong winds (over 70 km/h) houses have been damaged and trees have fallen, blocking the main access to several districts. In addition, due to the severity of the situation, agricultural lands and standing crops have been damaged in low-lying areas of the districts of Galle and Matara caused by flooding, while houses, common buildings, and markets are inundated. Due to the increase in the water level of the main rivers, the small and medium-scale bridges, and culverts have gone under the water, cutting off access roads at several places where people were stranded or forced to wait until the water receded. The DMC also reported that many schools have been flooded due to the heavy rainfall in those areas since 19th September and that students have lost their school materials/stationery during the flooding that affected their houses. Schools in several educational zones in the Matara district schools were temporarily closed on the 9th and 10th of October due to unfavorable weather conditions. The Department of Irrigation has extended a flood warning message issued for the Gin River Basin and Nilwala River. Accordingly, a significant level of flooding was experienced in the low-lying areas of the Matara Gamapaha and Galle due to major rivers more than 50,000 thousand persons were affected As of 07th October 2023, the DMC situational report indicated that 13,000families have been affected by the floods.

The flood has disrupted access to health services, essential medicines, and food supply chains, leading to a reliance on dry rations and sanitary items. Basic needs like drinking water, electricity, and gas are in short supply in most areas. more than 10,000 wells are contaminated and lack of access to safe drinking water due to continuous rain and flooding. This is a serious issue that can have significant health implications for affected communities.

Moreover, people are experiencing a lack of access to essential goods and services due to transportation deficiencies. It is crucial to underscore that these multifaceted challenges are not limited to specific geographic areas but affect both rural and urban communities. 

Dengue cases have been on the rise since the beginning of monsoon rains. Indeed, the cases reported are higher than those recorded in the corresponding period of the last two years. A higher number of cases are recorded in the Western and southern provinces, especially in Colombo, Gampaha, Kalutara, Galle, and Matara districts. The National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU) reported nearly 2,000 cases of the dengue virus.

countries.name: Armenia
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: Armenia - Population Movement
summary:
The Republic of Armenia (RA) has experienced an influx of 101,848 individuals since 24 September 2023, due to the escalation of hostilities in the region, which began on September 19. On 2 October, the Government of Armenia (GoA) officially requested international assistance after activating the Union Civil Protection Mechanism (UCPM) on September 29. Out of 97,840 registered (some arriving person have not registered yet), 52% are female, 48% male, 18% over 60, 31% under 18, and 16% have disabilities, as well as 230 are pregnant women among the arrivals. This situation is further exacerbated by the presence of 20,000 people who were displaced during the 2020 and 2022 conflict, still requiring support, placing a significant socio-economic burden on the RA. The recent displacement accounts for 3% of Armenia's total population, posing integration and employment challenges in an already economically strained environment with 26.5% of its overall population living below the poverty line, and an unemployment rate constituting 13%.

The humanitarian consequences of the escalation of hostilities require a comprehensive and sustained response. Governmental entities, non-governmental organizations, and volunteers are working collaboratively to address the pressing needs of the affected population. Recognizing the humanitarian needs, the Government of Armenia (GoA) has been mobilizing national governmental resources, as well as regional and local authorities. The GoA has invited relevant national and international organizations to support the coordination framework. Several inter-agency working groups (e.g., protection, health, CVA, food security) have been established, and are proactively attended by Movement partners.

A vast majority of the people arriving hold Armenian passports/IDs, with authorities stating that access to health and social services is thereby ensured. However, there are concerns that despite the access to essential service in principle, practical access may still be a challenge with regard to service capacities. In addition, many face issues with documentation, leading to the government offering temporary identification assistance.

According to the triangulation of primary data collection efforts and rapid needs assessments carried out by multiple actors, the immediate primary needs of those who left for Armenia include the provision of food, essential household items, psychosocial support, first aid and medical referrals, running helplines, and Restoring Family Links (RFL) services. Maintaining safe shelter is also a clear priority, with arriving people currently being hosted in temporary collective centers, hotels, boarding institutions, and with friends, relatives, and other types of host families. Notably, 48,649 individuals are accommodated in various shelters and settlements currently, while a minimum of 22,650 registered families will require rental support in the following 6 months. The types of accommodation range from private housing, living with host families, in hotels and pensions, to staying in collective centers (such as adapted former educational institutions and sports halls).

The Government of Armenia (GoA) sought the Armenian Red Cross Society’s (ARCS) assistance in registering persons at reception points established in Goris, Kornizor and Vayk, who arrived in the country. The ARCS has therefore played a prominent role from the onset of the immediate response, so far deploying 1,500 dedicated staff and volunteers, for the response operation. Alongside registration, ARCS distributed food and essential household items at reception points in Southern Armenia, with an additional focus on delivering psychological first aid (PFA). At present, with no further relevant influx since the first week of October, ARCS response focusses on the distribution of food and essential household items, as well as mental health and psychological support (MHPSS) assistance, across the country. A needs assessment surveying 5,962 individuals (representing 40,887 members of their households) who reached out to ARCS for assistance, was conducted, revealing pressing requirements in several key areas: There is a significant need for safe shelter and accommodation for those arriving in Armenia, as well as support for host communities. Additionally, immediate needs such as food and essential household items require to be addressed. The expected long-term duration of displacement respectively permanent stay in Armenia, necessitates a focus on transitioning to livelihood assistance and socio-economic integration at early stage. The preference among those affected leans towards cash and voucher assistance (CVA). Furthermore, there is a growing demand for MHPSS, with psychological support ranking as a top priority. Given that 31% of the arrivals are children, addressing their educational needs is a key priority.

The Volcanological Observatory of the Southern Andes (OVDAS) of the National Geology and Mining Service (SERNAGEOMIN), through its Special Report of Volcanic Activity (REAV) issued during this day, indicates that the technical alert level is modified from Yellow to Orange, which includes significant variations in the development of the volcanic process derived from the analysis of the indicators of The monitoring parameters, hence a probable eruption, could develop over a period of days or weeks.

With respect to the last REAV, it is reported that since Saturday, September 23, there has been a gradual increase in energy and occurrence in tremor-type signals (associated with movements). of fluids) reaching the maximum signal at a value of 64.7 cm2 of reduced displacement (DR), with an associated acoustic signal of 21.8 Pascals (Pa) and values of high thermal anomalies, with its maximum value of 107 MW. In turn, RSAM values have reached maximum values of 5.82 um/s, values considered high for this volcano. Additionally, Strombolian explosions have been observed that generate emissions of ballistic pyroclastic material in the area proximal to the crater and dispersion of fine material, incandescence and detection of thermal anomalies.

The above suggests that the volcanic system has evolved towards a phase of greater instability, therefore, SERNAGEOMIN raises its technical alert from Yellow to Orange and modifies the zone of potential affectationVolcanic hazards within a radius of 8 kilometers measured from the center of the active crater.

According to the technical background provided by SERNAGEOMIN and SENAPRED, THE REGIONAL PRESIDENTIAL DELEGATIONS OF LA ARAUCANÍA AND LOS RÍOS MANAGE THE MODIFICATION OF THE PERIMETER SECURITY.

In consideration of this technical background provided by SERNAGEOMIN, SENAPRED updates the current Yellow Alert for the communes of Villarrica, Pucón and Curarrehue in the Region of La Araucanía and commune of Panguipulli in the Region of Los Ríos, due to activity of the Villarrica volcano, which remains in force since November 8, 2022.

With the update of the Yellow Alert, the necessary resources will be kept staggered to intervene according to the evolution of the event, in order to prevent the It grows in extent and severity, minimizing the negative effects on people, their goods and the environment.

For its part, SERNAGEOMIN continues with the permanent surveillance of the volcanic complex and the Regional Directorates of SENAPRED La Araucanía and Los Ríos, will maintain the coordination with the members of the National System for Disaster Prevention and Response (SINAPRED), to timely alert and provide an adequate response to possible emergency situations.

These measures imply the reinforcement of the technical monitoring of the behavior of the Villarrica volcano, the application of the Emergency Community Plans in the phases corresponding to the enlistment and provision of resources of the National System for Disaster Prevention and Response (SINAPRED), to prevent and / or control possible situations derived from this natural phenomenon.

To the Municipalities, CONAF, SENAPRED Regional, Carabineros, Chilean Army, Firefighters, Health Service, Roads, General Director of Water, all Regional Ministerial Secretariats, SERNATUR and other public and private entities will act in coordination and adopt preparedness, support and response measures to possible variations in the alert situation, informing the Regional Level of the decisions and the development of the actions taken in effect. Likewise, the National Forestry Corporation (CONAF) will inform the Villarrica National Park of this alert and courses of action for the knowledge of its officials and visitors.

The Municipalities and Regional Directorates of SENAPRED will maintain the cadastre of the areas surrounding the volcano, with an estimate of the population and productive sector that could be be affected by a possible increase in volcanic activity, in order to establish the necessary courses of action for adequate care of the vulnerable population.

SERNAGEOMIN, the National Early Warning Center, together with the Regional Directorates of SENAPRED La Araucanía and Los Ríos, maintain constant monitoring of this situation.

SERNAGEOMIN declares orange technical alert for Villarrica volcano

  • For its part, SENAPRED indicated that technical monitoring of the behavior of the volcano will be reinforced, maintaining the yellow alert for the communes of Villarrica, Pucón, Curarrehue and Panguipulli.

name: LBY: إعصار - 2023-09 -Libya, Storm Daniel
summary:
DISASTER OVERVIEW

On September 10, 2023, northeastern Libya was struck by Storm Daniel, a severe weather system bringing winds of 70 to 80 km/h and an unprecedented rainfall of up to 240 mm. Derna, a coastal city, bore the brunt of this storm, experiencing significant damage to its dams. The resultant floodwaters, rising up to three meters, engulfed entire neighborhoods, sweeping them into the sea. The storm impacted major urban areas such as Benghazi, Tobruk, Toukra, Talmeitha, Almarj, Taknes, Al Owailia, Bayada, Albayda, Shahhat, and Sousa.

As reported by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) by October 31, the storm resulted in 4,352 fatalities and over 8,000 individuals unaccounted for. Additionally, it led to the displacement of more than 43,400 people, with 7,000 families left without shelter. The storm intensified the already difficult situation in eastern Libya, a region hosting 46,000 displaced persons and numerous migrants prior to the event.

The storm caused extensive damage to communication and electricity infrastructure, as evidenced by videos shared on social media and by the Libyan Red Crescent Society (LRCs). These videos depicted scenes of submerged vehicles, collapsed structures, and powerful floodwaters raging through city streets.

In response, the Libyan Government in the East declared an emergency and urged medical personnel and assistants to head to Derna. The Libyan parliament sought assistance from the international community and all humanitarian actors within the nation.

Tropical Storm Daniel further complicated the existing situation in Libya, a country that has been managing complex population movements, including over 706,000 migrants, refugees, and internally displaced people since the 2011 crisis. The country's health system, already under strain from a decade of conflict, faced additional pressures. Low vaccination rates increase susceptibility to preventable diseases, and the global price surges due to the Ukraine crisis have severely affected Libya's food security. Dependent on wheat and grain imports, particularly from Russia and Ukraine, the nation confronts escalating food costs, compelling many to reduce daily food intake.

As internally displaced persons gradually return to their homes, they encounter challenges like damaged housing and limited access to essential services. There has also been a notable rise in forced expulsions of migrants, triggering significant human rights concerns.

Furthermore, the risk of gender-based violence remains high for women and girls in Libya, aggravated by factors such as fear, social stigma, discrimination, and limited access to services, especially in remote areas. Despite reduced large-scale hostilities, the threat posed by explosive remnants of war, including landmines and improvised explosive devices (IEDs), persists, emphasizing the need for ongoing risk identification and mitigation efforts.

Shelter and Housing:

    Long-term support for permanent housing solutions.

  • Immediate healthcare interventions are needed due to a high incidence of diseases like diarrhea.
  • Water and sanitation issues necessitate access to clean water and sanitation facilities.
  • Mental health support and counseling for those traumatized by the hurricane.
  • Restoring and strengthening healthcare referral systems, with a focus on emergency care, chronic disease treatment, and reproductive health services.

Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH):

  • Need to distribute safe water to remote areas and subsidize water costs.
  • Rehabilitate wastewater drainage and improve WASH facilities.

Protection of Vulnerable Groups:

  • Addressing needs of unaccompanied and separated children who face risks of exploitation and abuse.
  • Focused support for migrant women, IDPs, lone women, widows, and female heads of households, including protection from gender-based violence and health challenges.

dtype.name: Earthquake
name: Morocco - Earthquake-2023-09
summary:
Please click here to view all IFRC interviews about the Moroccan earthquake.

 

Overview 

An earthquake with a 6.8 magnitude shook Morocco on 8 September 2023, at 11 p.m. local time. According to the US Geological Survey (USGS), the quake originated at a depth of18.5km below the surface. Its epicentre was identified in the High Atlas Mountains, located 71km south-west of the city of Marrakesh, a major economic center.

The earthquake was felt as far away as Portugal and Algeria, according to the Portuguese Institute for Sea and Atmosphere and Algeria’s Civil Defence agency. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) reported that a magnitude-4.9 aftershock hit 19 minutes later. The earthquake's aftershocks instilled fear among the survivors, forcing many to sleep in the streets. According to Reuters, the continued risk of landslides and the large distances involved complicated the rescue and relief efforts.The remote villages nestled in the High Atlas Mountains, right at the earthquake's epicentre, suffered substantial losses. Due to the blocked roads and the challenging terrain, emergency services faced difficulties in reaching the wounded.

Remote villages high in the Atlas Mountains, near the earthquake's epicenter, suffered substantial damage. The Moroccan search and rescue teams, with the support of teams from Spain, Britain, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates stepped up a massive effort to bring relief to devastated mountain villages. This earthquake was the deadliest in Morocco since 2004. According to the national authorities, 2,946 people died while the amount of injured reached 5,674. It is estimated that 59,674 houses were destroyed or damaged. According to the ministry, 1,404 of the injured were in critical condition.

 

Geographic priorities are hard to reach areas in:

Haouz Province

Taroudant Province

Marrakech-Safi Region

Chichaoua Province

 

Sectoral Needs:

Food Security and Livelihoods: 3.5 months post-earthquake, the market supply has returned to normal, but elevated prices persist due to the country's inflation, mirroring global economic trends. While some camp sites continue to receive food assistance from various organizations and the Government, those residing in remote mountain areas confront food shortages. On one hand, the initial wave of  solidarity  has dwindled, and on the other, families lack the means to purchase essential supplies. In these remote regions, families heavily rely on remittances sent by individuals (men) who had migrated to urban areas for employment. The earthquake prompted their return, jeopardizing their jobs, and they are hesitant to go back to the cities until their families are relocated to more secure shelters or their homes are rebuilt. They're going to stay until the breaking point, they said in Ighermane-Chichaoua Province.

Agricultural activities have resumed but farmers unusual weather patterns, such as delayed rains with no precipitation in mid-December (compared to the usual mid-November onset), this will disrupt the farming cycle. Compounding this issue is the inability to replace deceased animals due to challenges in providing adequate shelter, limited space near tent sites, and insufficient fodder.

 

At present, priority for families is to stockpile food as the winter peak approaches (January/February). Access becomes challenging  with roads rendered impassable due to snow and ice. As a result, securing sufficient provisions before winter sets in is crucial for their sustenance and survival.

 

Health: Post-earthquake health care has improved, with emergency treatments provided for various ailments and PTSD. Al-Haouz's remote areas report multiple health concerns, while Marrakech's hospital system faces high demand. Health care workers struggle emotionally, and there's a significant need for logistical and psychological support. Data on affected populations remains inconsistent.

 

Protection: The earthquake in Morocco disrupted communal living spaces, especially in Al Haouz, posing risks to privacy, especially for women, girls and children. Over 530 schools were damaged, placing approximately 100,000 children at elevated protection risk. While temporary tent classrooms provide a short-term solution, halted education exposes children to potential exploitation. Vulnerable groups, including children, women, the elderly, and marginalized individuals, face intensified vulnerabilities and require specialized protection, support, and safety measures. Efforts are being made by Moroccan associations to mitigate risks, especially for women and children.

 

Shelter/NFIs: The earthquake severely impacted Al Haouz, Taroudant, Marrakech-Safi, and Chichaoua, with clay-constructed villages like Douar El Darb and Tizi Natast facing massive displacements. Traditional mud houses suffered the most, rendering many homeless, adding to a total of 59k houses damaged and 19k destroyed. Mountainous areas, particularly in Tinmel and Ouarzazate, urgently require tents, blankets, and warm clothing, underscoring the need for timely and equitable aid distribution.

 

WASH: Following the earthquake, most mountains areas within the districts of El Houz, Chichaoua and Taroudant faced significant water disruptions, waternetwork and watertanks being broken by falling rocks. During first weeks, irrigation canals were used to provide low quality drinking water. Open air defacation  was the solution used for sanitation. Three month after the earthquale, simple sanitation facilities were created by the community and brought by several organization includint Morocco Red Crescent, IFRC and other members of the RCRC movement. Demand for quality and quantity improveent of clear water, sanitation facilities and hygiene promotion is still high in most of the areas, particularly the most remoted valleys.

A devastating landslide and flooding have struck the Guria and Adjara regions in Georgia's western part. According to the Georgian Internal Affairs Ministry's report on Friday, three individuals, including two minors, are currently missing in the aftermath of this disaster.

 

The Public Safety Command Centre has received over 100 notifications from the affected zone. The landslide has resulted in the flooding of residential houses, uprooted trees, and extensive damage to critical infrastructure. Additionally, heavy rainfall and subsequent landslides have cut off several villages in the Guria region, exacerbating the crisis.

 

Search and rescue operations are underway. The Ministry of Internal Affaris reported the discovery of the body of one minor during rescue operations in the village of Jumati. The search for the remaining two missing individuals is ongoing.

 

This natural disaster has caused significant damage to the region's infrastructure, including houses, bridges, and roads connecting villages. Various departments of the Ministry of Interior are actively present on the ground, with mobilized equipment and an active response mode.

 

The Ministry of Internal Affaris urgently advises residents in the affected area not to relocate and to strictly adhere to the instructions provided by its representatives on-site.

 

According to Aleksandre Sarishvili, the mayor of Lanchkhuti, landslides have impacted several villages in the Chochkhati community, resulting in the destruction of at least 10 houses.

 

The Emergency Management Service (112) of Guria and Adjara regions has received more than 100 reports, indicating the widespread impact and urgent need for assistance.

countries.name: Costa Rica

name: CRI: Dengue outbreak
summary:
La cuarta semana de agosto reportó 8261 nuevos casos de dengue, lo que significa un aumento de casi el doble de los enfermos que se reportaron en la misma fecha del 2022.

El Ministerio de Salud emitió, este miércoles, una nueva alerta sanitaria debido al aumento de casos de dengue que ha registrado el país en las últimas semanas.

Según datos de la institución la semana epidemiológica 34 que abarcó del 20 al 26 de agosto reportó 8.261 nuevos casos de la enfermedad, lo que significa un aumento de casi el doble de los enfermos que se reportaron por dengue en las mismas fechas del 2022, pues se pasó de 4780 el año pasado a 8261 este año (un 42% más).

Los cantones con mayor número de casos son Sarapiquí (con 964 casos), Siquirres (con 732 casos), Pococí (con 682 casos), Puntarenas (con 625 casos), Talamanca (con 566 casos) y Limón (con 556 casos).

Sin embargo y según Salud "en el resto de los cantones del país también se reportan casos por lo que es importante que la población no baje la guardia".

Según indicó la ministra de la cartera, Mary Munive Angermüller:

 

Toda la ayuda por parte de la población es de gran importancia para poder disminuir la cantidad de casos, el trabajo en conjunto entre nosotros desde el Ministerio y la comunidad es primordial para que juntos combatamos esta enfermedad. Necesitamos que usted, que está en su casa, elimine todos los criaderos y enseñe a sus niños para que crezcan con esta cultura y así disminuyamos los casos".

Tras la declaración sanitaria Salud reforzará las campañas de fumigación y de recolección de llantas, así como las alianzas con distintas instituciones y empresas para intervenir zonas prioritarias.

Asimismo semanas atrás se lanzó la campaña “Basta de aplausos” con el objetivo de llegar a la población por medio de mensajes sobre la eliminación de criaderos para combatir las enfermedades vectoriales.

El ministerio agregó que:

A la población en general se le insta a revisar periódicamente sus casas, patios y comunidades para eliminar potenciales criaderos del mosquito transmisor del dengue, así como estar pendientes de las comunicaciones de este ministerio con las recomendaciones".

summary: On today, September 1, 2023, coastal floods and erosion swept through the Kru Town beach fishing community of Robersport City (capital of Grand Cape Mount County) in Western Liberia bordering Sierra Leone. The community of Kru Town has suffered sporadic incidents of erosion and flooding over the years. 1,955 persons are affected so far with 520 displaced in public buildings. The Liberian Red Cross has been coordinating with the National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) on the response in the last 24 hours. The NS has deployed a surge support team from its HQ in Monrovia to the affected area to provide support to the volunteers and staff who are already conducting rapid assessments. NS is mobilizing local supplies from its warehouses to provide an initial response while engaging partners' support. The NDMA will support the response with coordination. Women and children are the most affected as photos show them displaced and sleeping in open buildings with no proper safety measures in place.

summary:
Heavy rainfall that occurred in Tajikistan on August 27-28, 2023, caused widespread flooding, mudflows, landslides, and rockfalls.

The affected areas include Dushanbe, Vahdat, and Hisor cities, and Rudaki, Varzob, Devashtich, Rasht, Sangvor, and Tojikobod districts.

As of August 30, 20 casualties have been reported, and the death toll is expected to rise as mud cleaning and debris removal operations continue.

The disaster has also damaged or destroyed homes, roads, bridges, schools, agricultural land, livestock, and other infrastructure.

The State Emergency Situations Commission (ESC) has been set up and is working to assess the full extent of the damage.

According to the preliminary assessment of the ESC as of 30 August, the disaster caused damage to 1,021 residential and auxiliary buildings and household/kitchen plots.

Local emergency services, supported by the local population, are engaged in response operations, including mud cleaning and debris removal.

countries.name: United States

name: USA: Fire - 2023-08 - Hawaii Wildfires
summary:
Since the fires began, the American Red Cross and county government have provided more than 5,300 overnight shelter stays in 16 emergency shelters on Maui and Oahu. The Red Cross is working with the Hawaiian Emergency Management Agency (HIEMA) to move displaced residents to hotels rather than congregate shelters. This temporary solution will help residents feel more comfortable as more permanent plans are developed. Many people continue to search for missing loved ones while also facing the loss of their homes and all of their belongings. Early reports indicate the climate-driven fires destroyed as many as 2,200 structures, most of which were homes.

 

More than 300 trained Red Cross disaster workers from Maui, other Hawaiian Islands and all corners of the country are working 24/7 with partners to get help to people as quickly as possible. With the help of partners, Red Cross has provided more than 32,600 meals and snacks to people in need. Emergency shelters are serving as multi-purpose service centers where people can access hot meals, relief supplies, health, mental health and spiritual care services, support with finding loved ones and casework assistance.

 

Approximately 6,000 local residents have begun their Red Cross volunteer training since the fires began. Preliminary damage assessment process is days ahead of our normal timeline, a result of our partnership with Microsoft's AI for Good Research Lab that is using sophisticated AI models and satellite imagery to analyze the extent of the damage. Damage assessment information is vital as it’s used to make operational decisions such as where to focus our services. It’s also the first step in validating addresses for residents that may qualify for Red Cross financial assistance.

name: ETH:Drought(EAP)
summary:
Recurring droughts and floods have the most severe impact on Ethiopia’s population and the country has a long history of recurring droughts, which have increased in magnitude, frequency, and impact since the 1970s. The pastoral and agro-pastoral communities in drought prone areas, increasing aridity and recurring drought conditions present the most significant climate hazard. Ethiopia is highly vulnerable to climate shocks and is one of the most drought-prone countries in the world. The severe drought that began in late 2020 has continued into 2023 with the passing of five poor to failed rainy seasons. Under the 2023 Humanitarian Requirement Document (HRD),13 million people require humanitarian response in drought affected areas.

The following areas were identified as drought prone and where timely early actions could make a difference in mitigating the negative impacts, includes Belg receiving (East and West Harerge), Northern pastorals (Afar Zone 1 and Zone 3, Norther Shewa, North and south Wollo, South Gonder, and Southern Tigray region) and Southern pastoral livelihood zones (seven zones in Somali (Afder, Dhawa, Dollo, Fafan,, korah, liben and Shebelle zones), Borena and Guji, Erer, and East Bale zones) are identified as high risk areas.

name: PAK: Flood - 2023-08 - Monsoon Rains in Pakistan
summary:
During this monsoon season, numerous regions have been impacted by a combination of floods, landslides, and substantial rainfall.

On Saturday, the Sutlej River reached "exceptionally high levels" at the Ganda Singh Wala Barrage, evacuating hundreds of families from 72 villages in Kasur and Chunian. Tragically, during this flood event in Kasur, three individuals lost their lives while attempting to seek higher ground. 

The Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) has issued a report indicating severe flooding in the Sutlej River. The outcome hinges on the water flow at Harike Headworks and Ferozepur Headworks. Currently, the water level at the Ganda Singh Wala Barrage has risen to 23 feet, with a flow rate of 269,000 cusecs. In Sulemanki, there is a moderate level of flooding with a flow rate of 83,072 cusecs. There is a looming threat of extremely high-level flooding at Head Sulemanki in the next 24 hours.

At Head Islam, the water flow has surged to 30,142 cusecs. The potential for extreme flooding at Head Islam is anticipated to commence on August 22. However, the water flow in Sindh, Jhelum, Chenab, and Ravi rivers remains normal.

The administrative authorities of the districts adjacent to the Sutlej River were put on high alert and measures had been implemented to restrict the movement of people in areas near Sutlej. Relevant deputy commissioners have been directed to reinforce the dykes along the Sutlej River.

Additionally, in a distinct incident, more than 100 buffaloes owned by a farmer in Usmanwala village, close to Ganda Singh, were carried away by the floodwaters while they were being relocated. Numerous individuals and animals found themselves trapped in the floodwaters because, despite early warnings of severe flooding during the past week, the authorities did not manage to evacuate them from their homes.

countries.name: Niger
dtype.name: Flood
name: NER: Imminent floods 2023
summary:
Niger is currently in the midst of the rainy season, with the heaviest rainfall expected in late August or early September. The Ministry of Humanitarian Action has predicted that around 300,000 people will be affected by flooding this year between July and September. Based on historical data from the Ministry of Humanitarian Action (flooding in 2020, 2021, and 2022), an average of 250,000 people are affected by the impacts of floods each year in the high-risk flood-prone regions. This year, based on seasonal forecasts (a mapping of risk-prone regions has been conducted, identifying regions such as Maradi, Zinder, Dosso, and Tahoua with low risk), it is projected that the floods for this year will have a greater impact than in previous years. It is therefore anticipated that the number of victims could exceed 300,000 people, given the vulnerability of the populations to the predicted amount of rainfall in these areas this year. Examining historical data, it is anticipated that people will suffer damage to homes and property, as well as losses in agricultural fields. In June, the FAO emphasized that the increased risk of flooding in the coming months could worsen, which is an already alarming food security situation.

Floods that damage crops and cause harvest losses, along with the destruction of property and loss of livestock in exposed areas, are identified risks that could contribute to an increase in food insecurity among affected the populations. In 2022, approximately 100,000 hectares of crops were destroyed, leading to the loss of livelihoods for around 256,000 people. As Niger is in the midst of the rainy season, the early consequences of the rains are already visible. Above-average rainfall has been recorded since May 2023. According to the results of field assessments by OCHA, heavy rains have displaced over 85,000 people in Zinder and affected over 80,000 people in Maradi. According to the Minister of Humanitarian Action, 146 people were affected by floods in the Dosso region in July. Through other programs, the Red Cross of Niger has sought to assist these affected individuals. However, it should be noted that the impacts on these families remain relatively limited. With the peak of the rainy season being three weeks away, there is still time to trigger and implement activities in the coming seven days. Given the forecasts outlined by meteorological institutions, the contamination of water points is a concern, which could facilitate the emergence and spread of waterborne epidemics and other diseases (cholera, acute diarrhea, malaria, etc.). These risks are even higher for the most marginalized and vulnerable groups such as women, disabled individuals, displaced persons, and children.
