name: ESP: Fire - 2023-08 - Incendio Forestal Arafo Candelaria
summary:
El fuego, que sigue sin control, afecta ya a 8.400 hectáreas y ocupa un perímetro de 70 kilómetros. La orografía y la existencia de combustible seco por las altas temperaturas de los últimos días complicaron las tareas de extinción desde el primer momento. El incendio se ha propagado por los términos municipales de 11 de los 31 municipios de la isla (Arafo, Candelaria, El Rosario, La Orotava, Santa Úrsula, La Victoria, El Sauzal, La Matanza, Güímar, Tacoronte y Los Realejos). La zona más afectada hasta el sábado era el monte de La Esperanza, cerca del núcleo de población de El Rosario, y el parque natural de La Corona Forestal, en el noreste de la isla. El pronóstico de la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) para este sábado era de calor y calima en las islas Canarias, con temperaturas que podrían llegar hasta los 34 grados. El viento cambiante podría complicar las labores de extinción. La proximidad de las llamas ha obligado a la evacuación de 12.279 personas.

The fire, which remains uncontrolled, already affects 8,400 hectares and occupies a perimeter of 70 kilometers. The orography and the existence of dry fuel due to the high temperatures of the last days complicated the extinguishing tasks from the first moment. The fire has spread through the municipalities of 11 of the 31 municipalities of the island (Arafo, Candelaria, El Rosario, La Orotava, Santa Úrsula, La Victoria, El Sauzal, La Matanza, Güímar, Tacoronte and Los Realejos). The most affected area until Saturday was the mountain of La Esperanza, near the town of El Rosario, and the natural park of La Corona Forestal, in the northeast of the island. The forecast of the State Meteorological Agency (Aemet) for this Saturday was for heat and haze in the Canary Islands, with temperatures that could reach up to 34 degrees. The changing wind could complicate the extinguishing work. The proximity of the flames has forced the evacuation of 12,279 people.

summary: Typhoon Khanun originated in the east of the Philippines on 28 July, and moved toward the Korean Peninsula, making its closest approach to Okinawa, Japan on 2 August. It is expected to be the fisrt typhoon ever to cross the Korean Peninsula, and according to the Korea Meteorological Administration, the entire country is expected to experience heavy rainfall of up to 600mm and strong winds of up to 40m/sec between 9 and 11 of August. There is no loss of life but 7,606 households(10,373 people) are temporarily evacuated from 11 cities and provinces.

countries.name: Mongolia

name: MNG: Epidemic - 2023-08 - Bubonic plague
summary: On August 8, 2023, today, one case of bubonic plague was reported in Ulaanbaatar. The patient was isolated in the National Center for Zoonotic Dissease (NCZD) and treatment was started. Responding measures are being organized by Zoonotic Disease Response Unit in Khentii province where the case is expected to be originated from. Five first contacts have been isolated and preventive treatment has been started. The Rapid Response Team of NCZD is working at the scene

countries.name: United States
dtype.name: Fire
name: USA: Fire - 2023-08 - Hawaii Wildfires
summary: In early August 2023, a series of wildfires broke out in the U.S. state of Hawaii, predominantly on the island of Maui. They have been recorded as the the deadliest U.S. wildfires in recent history and have damaged or destroyed more than 2,200 structures in the historic town of Lahaina. Most of these were homes, and now thousands of residents are displaced. More than 220 trained American Red Cross disaster workers from Maui, other Hawaiian islands, and all corners of the country are helping now with more on their way. Disaster workers are also virtually helping people affected by the fires. When the fires began, the Red Cross responded immediately, opening shelters for those affected by this climate-driven crisis. The Red Cross keeps disaster supplies pre-positioned on the islands, which allowed volunteers on Maui to offer immediate help to evacuees. Today our teams are working alongside partners to provide people with a safe place to stay, food to eat and emotional support during this challenging time. In partnership with the county government, trained Red Cross disaster workers are supporting emergency shelters on the islands of Maui and Oahu. The shelter on Oahu is helping Maui residents and tourists that fled in search of safety from the fires. Since the fires began, the Red Cross and partners have provided more than 3,300 overnight shelter stays. First responders are still conducting search and rescue efforts, and officials report communities will not reopen until these efforts are completed. Some power has been restored, but more than 5,000 customers remain without electricity. Communications are difficult with most cell service down, and critical infrastructure has been destroyed. Officials indicate it could be weeks before these systems are restored.

countries.name: Mongolia
dtype.name: Flood
name: MNG: Flood - 2023-08 - Mongolia floods
summary: Heavy rainfall occurred on August 5 between 19:30 - 20:30 across central area of Mongolia including Ulaanbaatar city. Flash floods were triggered due to rainfall in 2 locations of Ulaanbaatar. Flooding caused 4 (2 adults, 2 children) casualties. Currently, confirmed damage data states 18 households had their gers completely destroyed, 246 households' gers, houses, fences, 105 vehicles were severely damaged. Due to increased risk of electricity failure, 6926 households were cut off from electricity on August 5 and 178 households are currently under power outage on the reporting date. As of August 7, 59 (49 adults and 10 children) people are at temporary shelter.

countries.name: Norway
dtype.name: Flood
name: NOR: Flood - 2023-08 - Extreme weather, flooding and land slides in Southern Norway
summary: The rainstorm "Hans" passed Northern Europe this week, and hit parts of Southern Norway with heavy rainshowers up to 120 mm per day, startin on the evening of Monday the 7th of August. Raining continued through the night and through the following two days, showering large areas with the same amount in 24 hours, that is a normal amount in the month of August alltogether. Many municipalities were severely affected, leading to flooding, land and mud slides, and disruption of critical infrastructure in large parts of inland Southern Norway. All main roads from Oslo going North and Northwest were closed due to slides and flooding, as well as rail connections and smaller roads, isolating towns and villages. Several days after the rains subsiding, the large amounts of water is still affecting huge areas, now mainly with flooding, as the risk of land slides is now more moderate. The situation has been, and still is, serious, leading to large evacuations of several thousand people, as well as destroyed infrastructure, reduced accessibility to critical services for the population. There is still a risk to life and health, and this will carry on for the next few days as the flooding continues in to early next week.

countries.name: Bangladesh
dtype.name: Flood
name: BGD: Flood - 2023-08 - Flash Flood and Landslide' in Chattogram Region
summary:
Heavy rain triggered flash flood in the hilly district of Bandarban on 6 August 2023 afternoon as the Matamuhuri river flowed up to 13.79 meters which was 199 cm above its danger mark at Lama sub-district. on 7 August 2023 the water level of river Sangu rose to 17.63 meters which is 283 cm above the danger mark according to Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) of the Government of Bangladesh (GoB).

 

The FFWC in its daily bulletin issued on 7 August 2023 morning indicated that there is a chance of heavy to very heavy rainfall in the South-eastern hill basin & adjacent upstream parts of Bangladesh in next 24-48 hours. For this reason, all the major rivers (Muhuri, Feni, Halda, Karnafuli, Sangu, Matamuhuri) in the South-eastern region of the country may rise. In the next 24 hours, the rivers (Muhuri, Sangu & Matamuhuri) in the Chattogram, Feni, Bandarban & Cox`s Bazar districts may flow above their respective danger levels deteriorating the flood situation in the low-lying areas. According to the bulletin, Bandarban’s Lama recorded 227 mm of rainfall in the preceding 24 hours, which is the highest amount recorded in the current year. The hill basin also drains water from upstream areas in neighbouring India and Myanmar, where India’s Mizoram recorded 71 percent excess rainfall and Tripura 35 percent in the 24 hours until 8:00 am on 6 August 2023.

 

Chattogram has experienced 322 mm of precipitation in the past 24 hours, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD). BMD also issued a severe to extremely severe rainfall warning for six districts, including the capital Dhaka. It also issued a landslide alert for the Chattogram division because of potential heavy rain.

Residents of vulnerable areas in all the upazilas in Bandarban are advised to seek shelter through miking by the local administration as heavy rains are likely to cause further landslides. The fire service is carrying out drives in various areas with the assistance of the local administration. In fear of loss of life, families who live near the riverbank and foothills have been shifted to shelter centre facilities. Meanwhile 193 temporary shelters have been opened and 43 medical teams are ready to deal with the situation. The local administration has allocated 20 tons of rice and cash support for the flash flood victims.

 

According to the BMD, Cox's Bazar is expected to receive rainfall > 345 mm over the next five days, which could potentially trigger landslides in high-risk areas. Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (RIMES) has also forecasted medium to heavy rainfall for this week in Cox’s Bazar. Based on the 5-day rainfall forecast by RIMES suggests that most of the sub-districts of Cox’s Bazar may experience more volume of accumulated precipitation amounting to 88mm-106mmrain during 7– 8 August which may slightly improve from 9 August 2023. The areas which are highly susceptible to landslide are Cox’s Bazar municipality, part of Hnila (Nayapara RegisteredCamp and adjacent areas) and Baharchhara unions of Teknaf sub-district, Marine drive/Jaliapalong adjacent areas, Balukhali areas of Ukhiya sub-district and part of Khuniapalong of Ramu sub-district. Besides, few camps are also given with landslide alert which are camp 4, 8W, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 20-Ext and 21.

countries.name: Guinea
dtype.name: Flood
name: GIN: Flood - 2023-08 - Coyah Floods
summary:
August has recorded significant heavy rains across Guinea, affecting several prefectures of the country. In the morning hours of August 6, 2023, heavy rain in the prefecture of Coyah and its surroundings overflowed the Sarinka River, resulting in flooding in the Urban and Rural Communities of Maneah and Kouriah, affecting nine localities: Fily, Tougandé,  Batouyah, and Sambaya in the urban communities; Tanènè and Tanènè2 in the Rural Commune of Kouria, and Boguitagui, Bangouyah, and Kouria center in the Rural Commune of Kouria, destroying several homes and washing away properties of affected families. During evacuation and rescue, some women, children, and the elderly were identified to be ill that require urgent medical support, while others were trapped in their houses, and some sitting on the roof of their houses requesting rescue. Flooding has also been reported in other locations due to continuous downpours of rains. Faced with this situation, an emergency team was deployed comprising the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, the Director General of ANGUCH, the Regional Director of Civil Protection, the Red Cross and the Environment as well as medical teams and gendarmerie and police units.

The initial assessments provided by the Guinea Red Cross indicate floods reportedly killed three people, leaving 933 more injured. In this locality of Coyah with 281,757 inhabitants and 40,251 households, a total of 3,448 families amounting to 24135 people have been reported to be displaced. This same rainfall caused a landslide in the urban community of Kindia causing the fall of a tree from the top of a valley on a dwelling house leaving people injured. The technical services of the National Agency for Emergency Management and Humanitarian Disasters, the Guinea Red Cross, and the environment continue to assess the damage on the ground.

The coping capacities of affected households have already been stretched considering the floods have washed away all household items including reserved food, added to the economic crisis that has been impacting the country. While the situation remained fluid, the additional impact of flooding implies that vulnerabilities continue to increase as the capacity to cope decreases.

The Guinea Meteorological Department is forecasting more heavy rain for several prefectures that might result in floods, especially in flood-prone communities, and areas close to rivers where overflow is likely. The incessant flooding in these locations, coupled with the fact that affected people are currently without support calls for urgent efforts to address immediate humanitarian needs. The mayor, who is the political head of the Coyah prefecture has called for immediate support from humanitarian organizations and well-wishers.

countries.name: Ghana
dtype.name: Flood
name: GHA: 2023 Imminent floods
summary:
According to the Ghana Met (GMet) Agency forecast June to September 2023 issued on 5th May 2023, incidence of above normal rainfall are forecasted in the peak of rainy season (end August to early September) in Upper east region while the overall Northern part of the country ranking from normal to above normal is also likely to face mainly flash floods and revering floods incidence exacerbated by the annual opening of Bagre dam in Burkina Faso once it reach the 235m during the same period.

The National Disaster Management Organization (NADMO) and the Meteorological Agency have issued a warming of increased rainfall and flooding and advised people who live in high risk flooding areas to move to higher grounds. It is forecasted that more regions in the northern part will experience flooding as a result of above normal rainfall. The historical impact analysis has shown that, over the past years, the floods impacted around 70,000 people (source: CIMA, UNIDSR, 2018, Ghana Disaster Risk Profile)

Ghana is affected by:
- Flash floods worst in urban areas due to urbanization challenges
- Revering flooding mainly linked to the important river systems length crossing from Others countries, especially Burkina Faso and going through all the North regions up to the South of Ghana. The most overflowing rivers are the White and black Volta and its tributaries like Oti River, which flows into Lake Volta from the northeast.

The connection of this river system with Burkina Faso is worsening the overall flooding situation in Ghana since the annual spilling of water from Bagre Dam in Burkina Faso make an overflowing of all the river system in Ghana, impacting first the Northern regions and areas around the rivers, beaches and dams in Northern region, Upper East, Savannah, Northeast, and Upper West. Bagre Dam is open annually when it reach 255 M which is the maximum level.

GRCS historical data analysis shows that authorities usually alert the NADMO (National Disaster Management Organization) in Ghana in charge of disseminating the information. In the past, Hydroelectric Production Department of SONABEL of Burkina Faso, open the Bagre Dam on 1st September 2022 when it reach 235M. In 2018 it was in 31 August. In general, over the years, the opening of Dam happen from 30 August to 3rd September. Others dam spilling can also be recorded but Bagre is the recurrent one.

countries.name: Nepal
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: NPL: Epidemic - 2023-08 - Dengue Prevention and Response
summary:
In Nepal, dengue is a rapidly emerging disease. Endemic across most provinces, dengue incidence has increased in recent years largely due to expansion of the vector Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, as well as the movement of people and the introduction of imported cases. All 4 dengue serotypes exist in Nepal, with DENV-1 and 2 historically contributing the highest burden (EDCD, 2019). The first case of dengue in Nepal was reported in 2004. Since then, dengue cases have been gradually reported in Nepal, with an outbreak in the year 2019 (n=17,992) reported from 68 districts and in 2022 (n=54,784) from all 77 districts. According to EDCD of MoHP, among the total of 54,000 cases, majority of dengue cases (n=28109) including 38 deaths happened between January to September 2022 coinciding with the peak rainy season in the country. This is indicative of exponential surge in dengue cases during July/ September considering the overall weather conditions and monsoon season which provides hibernating infected mosquitoes with an optimal environment for breeding. Until epidemiological week 29 (first week of August 2023, EWARS report, EDCD), 7,253 dengue cases has already been diagnosed which is highly alarming as this is the very first time that dengue has occurred in the consecutive year in contrary to the usual cyclical pattern of dengue incidence in Nepal. In addition, dengue incidence started even during winter season and is in increasing trend. According to a mathematical modelling projection conducted by WHO (2022), the projection shows that cases have already exceeded the alert threshold since beginning of 2023 when compared to the reported dengue cases in EWARS, indicating Dengue outbreak in Nepal. Since dengue is relatively new for Nepal, there is low level of knowledge and awareness among people. Even the priority for dengue prevention was less priority in the country until last year, Nepal government has been sincerely trying to address the emerging trend of dengue through joint planning and implementation from this year. Therefore, Nepal government, municipal authority to the national level, have requested NRCS for better coordination and collaboration in dengue prevention and response to the current outbreak. 
Furthermore, Dengue has disparate effect on different population strata. While pregnant and lactating women, children and elderly population are vulnerable to dengue, young adult population working outside (with low socio-economic status) have higher exposure risk to dengue infected vectors. The number of hospitalized cases has increased exponentially overwhelming the health facilities in Sunsari district. The current daily average cases shows that similar situation might be experienced in the affected districts in coming weeks or months. 
Likewise, the supply of blood (Platelets-rich Plasma-PRPs) will be the challenge to meet the demand. Because of all these factors the severity and mortality cases will be increased in the country. In addition, the urban design of major cities in Nepal lacks in infrastructural public health aspects along with challenging waste management system and poor sanitation facilities which provides vectors with optimal environment for breeding. People residing in slums, densely populated urban cities with poor sanitation facilities are at greater risk of being affected.

countries.name: Liberia
dtype.name: Flood
name: LBR: Flood - 2023-08 - Liberia Floods
summary: Two weeks of sporadic rainfall in Montserrado County (especially Monrovia) and Grand Cape Mount County respectively has led to flooding affecting 1,556 and displacing about 119 persons in Monrovia and adjacent communities in Grand Cape Mount County in the western part of the country at the border with Sierra Leone. Monrovia and its adjacent communities have a record of flooding in recent years. In the last 4 years, over 40,000 persons have been affected by flooding in most slum communities according to the National Disaster Management Agency. Since the last week of July, over 1,000 households have been affected by flood especially living in wetlands, swamps, and low flood plains in the slums of Monrovia and Robertsports (Capital of Grand Cape Mount County). Families are displaced in public and private facilities such as schools, health centers, churches, and mosques. In some instances in Monrovia, families are restrcited to leave their homes by high level rise of flood waters; they remain in their houses and are assisted with food and water by canoes reaching them by neighbors. Community roads and bridges are washed away preventing community people to have access to basic services. The poor conditions of community public utility facilities such as roads, bridges, etc also contribute to the risk and vulnerability of the affected population.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
dtype.name: Other
name: ZWE: Election Preparedness
summary:
In line with the Zimbabwe Constitution, the country holds national harmonized elections every five years, also called general elections. Hence, the next elections will be held on the 23rd of August 2023 and will include the Presidential, Parliamentary and Local council elections. Following the constitution, If there is no outright winner in the presidential contest (winning with more than 50% votes), a run-off will is held six weeks later (october). Dubbed as “dry run” to this year’s contested election, the by-election tension, voting process and the extreme political polarization in the country may lead to situations of violence during the election period. Already, politically linked violent events have been reported successively since 2022. The most significant recent examples include some skirmishes reported in recent weeks which led malicious damage to property, livelihoods and infrastructure reported in Nyatsime, Chitungwiza on the outskirts of Harare.

Hence, multiple elements are indicating a possibility of violence in the impending 2023 elections.

This analysis highlighted by several analysis from experts, media National and international is premised on the following indicators:

a. The historical trend in Zimbabwe depicts an upsurge of violence around elections time. Inter and intra-political party skirmishes at recent political meetings and the 22 March 2022 By-election. In March 2022, the country held by-elections to fill vacant parliamentary and council seats. The run-up to these by-elections witnessed violence incidences and, in some cases, Red Cross volunteers assisted the victims.

b. There are verbal attacks and counter attacks in the media between the political parties with increased political activism in the country leading to a tense political environment.

c. Lack of political tolerance in some areas which has previously experienced disputed election results which in turn ignited violence.

d. Inadequate reconciliation efforts post 2008 violence and the deaths and injuries in the post 2018 election period which predisposes people towards a tendency of violence as revenge.

e. Possibility of an increase in migration towards the elections as people return to vote.

f. Emerging pressure groups which are not directly affiliated to political parties wield potential influence in political agitation.

g. Proliferation of social media (Facebook, Twitter & WhatsApp) as political mobilization tools may result in mass agitation and protests.

h. The economic challenges and hardships have heightened tension which may cause political agitation and sporadic incidences of public disobedience (riots and protests).

countries.name: Azerbaijan
dtype.name: Flood
name: AZE: Flood - 2023-08 - Flooding in Barda
summary:
On August 02, 2023, as a result of the collapse of a part of the “Upper Karabakh” water channel of the Barda region of Azerbaijan, the village of Garagoyunlu of this region was flooded. The cause of the catastrophe was the rise of the water level in the canal as a result of heavy rain a few days ago.

The basements of about 65 houses and the houses of 30 houses were flooded. A large number of chickens, freshly harvested crops and melon plants were significantly damaged. As a result of the severe consequences of the flood, it became much more difficult for villagers to enter their homes or yards.

countries.name: Kyrgyzstan
dtype.name: Flood
name: KGZ: Flood - 2023-08 - Mudflows Kyrgyzstan Issyk-Kul province
summary:
According to the Ministry of Emergency Situations dated August 2, 2023,  about 18:30, short-term heavy rains in Ken-Suu and Uzun-Sai villages of the Tyup district, Issyk-Kul province caused mudflows that flooded houses, agriculture fields, roads and bridges. According to preliminary collected information from Ken-Suu, residents of the affected villages faced the following consequences:
 
- 31 households in Ken-Suu village were affected,
- 6  houses with flooded basements,
- 1 house destroyed walls
- 3 barns with destroyed walls.
- 24.5 hectares of arable land were flooded, out of which:
Wheat: 4.5 hectares
Barley: 16.5 hectares
Potatoes: 1.5 hectares
Clover: 2 hectares
 
In Baizak village:
- 12 houses were damaged by mudflows
- 2 of them with flooded basements.
 
In Balbay village
- houses were damaged by mudflows
 
On August 3, 2023, the Ministry of Emergency Situations allocated the following equipment to respond to the consequences of the mudflows:
2 bulldozers
2 sewage collectors
2 loaders
1 grader
6 excavators
5 motor pumps
1 fire engine

Additionally, 72 rescuers from the Ministry of Emergency Situations, 40 people from the local community, and 5 RCSK volunteers arrived at the disaster area.
 
The Issyk-Kul regional branch of RCSK allocated 50,000 KGS from the emergency fund to cover fuel for response activities.
 
Also, according to preliminary information, on August 7, 2023, around 17:00 hours, mudflows occurred in the villages of Taldy-Suu, Korumdu, and the Karkyr community in the Tup district of the Issyk-Kul province due to heavy rains. MoES staff had conducted household survey and gathered data as follows:
 
- 28 houses including its basements, internal roads are flooded in In Taldy-Suu village.
- 40 houses including its basements, some houses itself and internal roads are flooded in Korumdu.
- 24 houses including its basements were flooded in Koochu village.

145 Households affected in total. State of Emergency was declared on 3rd August in Issyk-Kul province

Mudflows flooded agricultural fields in rural areas. After detailed assessment, specialists from the District Department of Agrarian Development will provide additional information on affected area indicating types of crops.

The MoES mobnilized 41 rescuers, 1excavator, 1 loader and 1 cargo dump truck, local authorities provided 1 grader, 3 excavators, 1 tractor.

In all affected villages people face difficulties with hygiene conditions and in some even with drinking water.

RCSK staff is on the spot of disaster and in close contact with affected communities and state structures. Due to big scale of disaster and limited resources the RCSK team is discussing possibility of allocating DREF funds.

countries.name: Viet Nam
dtype.name: Flood
name: VNM: Flood - 2023-08 - VNM: Flood - 2023-08 - flash flood and landslide
summary:
Heavy rains have caused local floods on small rivers and streams, flash floods, and landslides in many localities in the Northern mountainous region, causing damages to people, houses, production, infrastructure, especially in the provinces of Lai Chau, Yen Bai, Son La, and Lao Cai, Lai Chau, Dak Lak, Dak Nong, Gia Lai since 2 August 2023. 

 

Since August 4, the region has recorded downpours with rainfalls of 100 - 200mm, even nearly 400mm in some areas, causing flooding on small rivers and springs, flash floods, and landslides in some localities and also resulting in human and property losses, especially in Lai Chau, Yen Bai, and Son La provinces. The National Centre for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting has predicted that downpours will continue in this region from now through August 8, with rainfalls of 50-120mm, even over 180mm, which will continue posing very high risks of floods, flash floods, and landslides.

From 5 August 5 to 18:00 on 6 August, downpours and floods caused 10 casualties in northern mountainous and midland localities, including seven in Lai Chau, two in Yen Bai and one in Son La, along with heavy property losses, reported the Standing Office of the National Steering Committee.

 

According to a report from the National Commanding Committee for Natural Disaster Prevention and Control (NDPC) of Lai Chau Province, floods have caused 4 deaths and 3 injuries in Ta Mung commune, Khoen On commune, Than Uyen district, affecting 75 houses, of which 39 are in Nam Nhun district, 25 are in Than Uyen district, 10 are in Phong Tho district, the rest are in Sin Ho district. Over 3ha of rice and tea has been eroded and completely buried.

 

Floods have caused subsidence and landslides of many roads in the province with a volume of about 23,000 cubic meters of soil and rock. About 14 km of affected roads include: landslides, road talus, longitudinal trenches and some broken sections causing traffic jams on National Highway 4H at Km 272+200, Km 272+922, Km15+ 420, Km293+930, Km270+300, Km196+090. Flood also caused landslides and damaged 4 irrigation works in Than Uyen district.

A dam containing 1.2 million cubic meters of water, a volume equivalent to 480 Olympic-size swimming pools, in Dak Nong Province has showed signs of cracks following days of heavy rain. Dak Nong province has declared an emergency on natural disasters to handle situations. According to the Provincial People's Committee (PPC), from the end of 6 – 7 August, the area experienced prolonged heavy rains, the total rainfall at Dak Ha station was nearly 400 mm.

 

By 7 August, the cracks on the foot of the dam spanned around 500 m and were around 150 m deep, and showed no signs of abating. On the right side of the dam, around 10 ha of crops are sinking. An estimated 1 million cubic meters of soil has risk of landslides. The dam itself also has large cracks spanning 10-20 cm. The Dak N’Ting reservoir project cost around VND137 billion ($5.78 million), was built to irrigate around 700 ha of crops in Quang Son Commune. To ensure safety, authorities have blocked entrances into the dam area and evacuated 34 families with around 100 people.

At around 8:30 a.m on 8 August, the stream of blackish water coming from a reservoir that contains waste from the extraction of copper from ores rushed towards Ta Phoi Commune, Lao Cai province. The wastewater inundated houses and the commune's People’s Committee office. A local said the stream came quickly and without warning, so they could only escape with their lives, not having enough time to take their belongings.

 The Lao Cai People’s Committee said long-lasting rains have contributed to the breakage, and the exact amount of damage incurred is being evaluated. Lao Cai has been seeing rains over the past week, with the highest amount of rainfall seen on Monday night at 80 mm, according to the National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting. Heavy rains have triggered erosion at over 140 locations in Lao Cai, damaging more than 30 houses and flooding more than 110 others. Over 340 ha of crops and around 2 ha of aquaculture have also been damaged.

countries.name: Indonesia
dtype.name: Drought
name: IDN: Drought - 2023-08 - Drought due to El Nino and IOD Phenomena
summary:
Situation Update

In March 2023, the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) issued advice that the intensifying El Niño phenomenon and positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) may cause a drought during the dry season in Indonesia. As explained by Head of the BMKG in her statement to the press, El Niño and the Indian Ocean Dipole, both of which are cause by temperature changes in the Pacific and Indian oceans respectively, are anticipated to occur simultaneously during this year's dry season.

The concurrence of both phenomena in the latter part of 2023 is likely to exacerbate impacts of El Niño, leading to decreased rainfall in some areas of Indonesia throughout the dry season. A number of regions are predicted to experience rain intensity at below normal levels, or drier than usual conditions. 

BMKG has provided historical data from a similar situation in 2019, when El Niño coincided with IOD, and El Niño in Indonesia reached “Moderate” status, triggering more than 4000 hotspots. This saw significant impacts to communities, including forest fires in a number of provinces in Indonesia, leading to a loss in productivity of around 5.2 billion USD according to World Bank data.

According to BMKG, climate phenomena recorded in Pacific Ocean waters in May and June of 2023 could lead to El Niño in June, which could cause the region to feel warmer. Anomalies in Pacific Ocean temperatures have been growing, with the index reaching 0.8, concerningly close to the threshold of 1, at which point the El Niño status goes from “Weak” to “Moderate”. Currently, Trends show a consistent increase and there is an 80% chance that the El Niño status will escalate.

The figures below, issued by BMKG, illustrate monthly rainfall forecast from June to November 2023. The forecasts indicate a high probability that several Indonesian provinces will see rainfall intensity of around 0-20mm below normal during August and September 2023. BMKG has circulated an early warning of potential drought causing water scarcity, particularly in Java and Bali, and the southern part of Sumatra. 

The BMKG website (CEWS | Climate Early Warning System (bmkg.go.id)), as at the first ten-day reporting period for August 2023, identifies a Red (Alert) status for the following districts/cities:

1. Bali: Karangasem

2. Central Java: Boyolali, Karanganyar, Klaten, Semarang, Sragen, Sukoharjo

3. East Java: Bangkalan, Banyuwangi, Bojonegoro, Bondowoso, Jombang, Kediri, Kota Pasuruan, Kota Surabaya, Madiun, Mojokerto, Nganjuk, Kabupaten Pasuruan, Probolinggo, Sidoarjo, Situbondo

4. East Nusa Tenggara: Bima, Lombok Tengah, Lombok Timur, Manggarai Timur, Rote Ndao, Sumba Tengah, Sumba Timur

While the number of areas classified as “Red” remains unchanged from the third 10-day period of July, there is significant increase to the number of areas classified as “Orange” (Standby), from 23 to 42 areas, an increase of almost 100%. Meanwhile, the total number of areas with “Yellow” (Caution) status has risen from 11 to 89, indicating a spike of over 800% for areas showing signs of initial stages of drought. 

Based on information collected from the media and PMI Situation Reports, water scarcity has been broadly reported. In some areas, the government at Province/District/City level have declared “initial emergency (siaga darurat)” status, which is akin to an activation for early action relating to potential impacts of decreased rainfall. Affected provinces include East Nusa Tenggara, East Java, West Java, and South Kalimantan.

In other areas, including Mojokerto, Lumajang, Jember, and Pasuruan, local governments have declared ‘emergency’ status.

These status declarations, to some extent, corroborate BMKG’s warnings and forecasts. 

Government Response:

Early warning information has been circulated by the Indonesian Government to all sectoral ministries, ensuring preparedness for the potential impacts of drought. Preparation measures include ensuring sufficient food stocks and urging governments at sub-national level to maintain vigilance in readiness for potential impact of El Niño.

RCRC response

In a number of areas, PMI has been providing support to those impacted by the drought, including water distribution for daily consumption and conducting awareness raising activities. 

As auxiliary to the Government, PMI has been providing support to those impacted by the drought, including water distribution for daily consumption and conducting awareness raising activities. Currently, there are PMI team from across four Provinces namely Banten, West Java, Central Java and West Kalimantan provinces who are already on the field providing support to the affected community. In total of 56 personnel mobilized to operate 49 unit of water trucks on daily basis. As per this report circulated, PMI managed to distribute 965,000 liter of water across the four provinces.

PMI NHq has developed a national operational plan to respond to the impact of El Niño, including drought. The following plan has been established by PMI NHq in readiness:

- Mobilizing water trucks from the regional warehouses, prioritizing provinces which are located in red zones

- Providing clean water through water trucking

- Implement drought awareness raising and preparedness session to the communities at risk

countries.name: Sudan
dtype.name: Flood
name: SDN: Flood - 2023-08 - Sudan Flash Floods
summary: On the first week of August 2023, a flash flood hits the city of Al-Jabalain in White Nile State - Al-Jabalain locality, as a result of heavy rains downpours for hours in the eastern highlands of the town. A massive water run down the southern and western parts of the city it swept away and destroyed everything in its path so that the residents of these areas found themselves within the moments homeless. Many houses have been destroyed as well families lost their properties in ten areas. Total HHs affected 632 (416 HH totally damaged and 216 HH partially damaged). In Northern State 6,670 families were affected by flash floods, 1,580 houses were totally affected, 5,090 houses were partially affected and 2,250 latrines were destroyed by flash floods.

countries.name: Liberia
dtype.name: Flood
name: LBR: September 2023 Floods
summary:
From 1st to 4th September, Liberia has experienced excessive heavy rainfall in several cities with highest flooding reported in North-Eastern counties of Liberia: Grand Cape Mount, Bong and Montserrado. Areas especially affected are Kru Town; Gbarnga City and Monrovia coastal and urban side as well as the surrounding areas. In total, around 15,200 people are reported to be affected by both urban and coastal floods which swept away infrastructure, fishing settlements, houses, communities' facilities etc. On 4th September, Monrovia and its environs recorded the major impact following the five days cumulative rains from 30 August that affected approximately 12,450 persons (1,778 HHs). The affected are mostly surrounding Moronvia or bordering Sierra Leone and the river crossing the North Est of the country.

The Liberia Meteorological Department has predicted continuous rains in September and October 2023 across all counties in the country. Obviously, with continuous heavy rainfall, it could trigger additional flooding in low-lying communities near rivers and streams. Urban flooding is also possible in areas with poor drainage systems. Sites downstream from large rivers are also vulnerable to flash flooding after relatively short periods of intense rainfall. These rains can cause further damage to infrastructure, road closures, and contamination.

countries.name: Mauritania
dtype.name: Flood
name: MRT: Flood - 2023-07 - Flood in Boghé
summary:
Monday, 31/07/2023, the Moughataa of Bogué under the wilaya of Baraka in southern Mauritania, located 320 km from the capital, experienced torrential rains exceeding the barrier by 150 mm in some areas, causing flooding in several districts of the city, causing the death of a child in the village of Hamdoullah in the commune of Dar El Avia.

 

On this occasion, the government instructed the National Office of Sanitation ONAS to quickly move its machines to the city of Bogue to contribute to the water pumping operation.  

The National Sanitation Office has mobilized 7 large pumping stations, in addition to 6 km of transport pipes, and a number of reservoirs in order to evacuate water from the city.

On Tuesday of 01/08/2023, the Minister of Water and Sanitation went to the city of Bogué to learn about the situation and the work of the teams.

Since the early hours of the floods, the CRM through its disaster management center has regularly monitored the evolution of the situation with the support of the local committee of Boghé.

countries.name: Mauritania
dtype.name: Flood
name: MRT: Flood - 2023-07 - Boghé Flood 2023
summary:
On the night of Sunday to Monday, July 31, 2023, torrential rains that lasted several consecutive hours, exceeding the 150 mm barrier in some areas, fell on the department of Boghé under the wilaya of Brakna in southern Mauritania, causing loss of life in the village of Hamdallah in the municipality of Dar El Avia and extensive damage to infrastructure, homes and livelihoods. The collapse of the houses caused the displacement of several dozen families.

Affected families who lost their shelters took refuge in schools. The schools transformed into reception sites are Emirates School and School 08 and several homeless families have been accommodated by parents and neighbours who have not been affected by the floods.

In general, the floods have stapled the living conditions of the populations, and have accentuated the vulnerabilities of affected households. The weak local capacity to respond to these floods pushes actors to ask for external support. The affected populations are supported by people of good will, nationals of the department of Boghé and elected officials of the city who raised their voices during the parliamentary session at the National Assembly to draw attention to the victims of the floods in Boghé. The flood is due to the surge of rainwater from the upstream slopes (top) of the village Aari Hara, this village is on a small mountain upstream of Boghé. The city of Boghé, the area most affected by flooding, runoff water has ravaged everything in its path, the "Moussafrine" area which includes several neighborhoods and the most populated was invaded by rainwater as well as part of the Nioly district. The Boghé Dow district and neighbouring neighbourhoods, located as an extension of the Manantali electrical installations, are also heavily affected by the floods. The electricity was cut off by the Somelec as a safety measure because the electricity stations that supply the area were completely flooded. On the other hand, in the districts of the Carrefour de Nioly to the bridge and Boghé Escale, the flood did little damage.

With regard to the flood situation in the other communes of the department of Boghé, it should also be noted that the communes of Dar El Avia and Ould Birom have recorded significant material damage, water pollution, destruction of agricultural perimeters and part of the main road (Boghé-Rosso axis). The quality of telephone communication was partially disrupted.

2. Summary

The joint CRM/CRF rapid assessment mission in Boghé assessed flood damage and priority needs. Interviews with local authorities and key informants collected the following data:

o 01 Deaths recorded

o 1200 households affected or 7200 people

o 330 houses totally destroyed

o 250 houses partially damaged

o 527 homeless households

o 1101 displaced persons

o 02 reception sites occupied

o 26 families accommodated in the sites

o 1200 households lost utensils and work materials (Agricultural tools and others)

o 42 Water points destroyed

o 567 families have difficulty accessing drinking water

o 530 Collapsed latrines

o 22 cases of water-related diseases and poor hygiene reported

o 1200 households lost their food stock

o 12 hectares of submerged crops

o 1294 Livestock taken away (small remunerants)

o 573 households in need of food assistance

o 343 households lost their work equipment

countries.name: Guatemala

summary:
Los departamentos de Izabal, Huehuetenango, Suchitepéques y Guatemala registran los primeros daños por las lluvias del paso de una Onda del Este. Se estima que las lluvias continúen 2 días y provocarán más datos en las comunidades más vulnerables. 

Entre las principales afectaciones se encuentran colapsos de vías, viviendas inundadas, deslizamientos y caídas de árboles y rótulos.

countries.name: Lebanon
dtype.name: Civil Unrest
name: LBN: Civil Unrest - 2023-07 - Ain Al Helwe Clashes
summary:
Deadly clashes between rival groups in South Lebanon, Saida’s Ain al-Hilweh Palestinian refugee camp have been ongoing since Saturday 29th  July 2023, killing more than 14 individuals and injuring more than 60 as more than half of the camps residents fled their homes, security sources inside the camp stated. 

Among the injured was a Lebanese Army soldier who was hurt by shrapnel from a mortar shell that fell on a military barracks, the army announced on Twitter. The soldier’s condition was described as stable.

In-fighting is still at large at the time of writing, with automatic machine guns, Rocket Propelled Grenades, and medium sized artilary being used by the multiple factions. The fighting was started on Saturday after the assasination of a Palestinian Command official.

countries.name: Gabon
dtype.name: Other
name: GAB: 2023 Election preparedness
summary:
The 2023 electoral calendar is as follows:

-11 July: Deadlines for the filing of declarations of candidacy.

-11 August: Start of electoral campaigns for the presidential election.

-16 August: Start of electoral campaigns for the legislative election coupled with departmental and council elections.

-25 August: End of the electoral campaign period. -

26 August: General elections.

The most likely period of impact is upon publication of results.

 

Although apparently stable, the situation in the country was rocked in recent years by a series of events that are still likely to wreck mayhem. On 7 January 2019, mutineers attempted to overthrow the government following a prolonged absence of the President from the country due to ill health. Since then, the illness and partial incapacity of the Head of State have been seen as a weakness, providing an opportunity to some political opponents to take over power. For the younger generation, this is the reason why they are clamouring for a swing of the pendulum.

Uncertainty about the Head of State's ability to continue in office has led to a power struggle within his own party. In addition, the current term of office is marred by allegations of bad governance and repeated scandals that increasingly make the government unpopular with certain segments of the population, especially the youths. According to Charles M'Ba, an opposition leader, "these seven years of political unrest left their mark, and severely damaged the confidence of the people of Gabon in the State, and in the entire system: its administration, its school and judicial systems, and its police force". Despite attempts at appeasement by the current government, through a dialogue initiated with the bone and sinew of the country in a bid to lead to a peaceful election, some opposition heavyweights remained aloof. Charles M'Ba, a member of the opposition Union nationale (UN) party and former Minister of Finance under Omar Bongo Ondimba, said at the time that he was not very convinced by the rounds of meetings under engineered by the government. “Loving kind words are good, but proof of love is better," he summed up. Listening to your opponents is a good thing. Now, let’s get down to work. Today, the country is at peace, OK, but that doesn't stop me from being worried about the months to come." Source: https://www.lepoint.fr/afrique/gabon-a-quelques-mois-des-elections-un-climat-poli- tique-tendu-03-04-2023-2514692_3826.php du 3 avril 2023. Not very long ago, an opposition coalition strongly denounced the poor organization of the recent revision of the electoral lists and threatened not to recognize the lists that were to be published. Several opposition leaders continue to express their dissatisfaction with the lack of transparency in the electoral process. The political strife between the government and the opposition keeps raging, and this is something that arouses fears of an outbreak of violence during the upcoming elections. These fears are also heightened by the fact that the elections will be threefold (presidential, legislative and local). Therefore, the stakes could be significantly higher, as there could be negative consequences of any protests. Although the harbingers of pre- and/or post-election violence are not yet clearly visible, it is nonetheless worth noting that the pressure increases as the date draws nearer. Political one-upmanship is gaining grounds in public debates and with the economic conditions of the population (high cost of living, water and electricity supply), there is no guarantee that things won't get out of hand.

countries.name: Honduras
dtype.name: Other
name: HND: Others - 2023-07 - Dengue epidemic outbreak
summary:
Due to the increasing number of suspected cases accumulated to date of S.E 28 of 2023. With a total of 8,621 registered cases, this mosquito-borne disease has impacted the population in a worrying way.

Of these cases, dengue is presented as the main arbovirus, representing 99.7% of the accumulated total. Within dengue cases, it has been observed that a significant percentage corresponds to cases with alarm signs and without alarm signs, with a total of 8,545 cases, representing 99% of total dengue cases. In addition, 62 cases of severe dengue have been reported, highlighting the importance of taking urgent measures to prevent a further increase in severe cases.

Although the numbers of chikungunya and Zika are relatively low compared to dengue, with 2 cases (0.2%) and 12 cases (0.3%) respectively, it is crucial not to underestimate the presence of these diseases, as they can also have a significant impact on public health and require appropriate care.

countries.name: Syrian Arab Republic
dtype.name: Fire
name: SYR: Fire - 2023-07 - Syria Wild Fires July 2023
summary:
Multiple Fires have broken out around the coastal and central areas and in Syria. Possible reasons behind these fires differ, including the warm eastern winds that are active during this time of the year in Syria, in addition during the summer there are many dry herbs that burn quickly and the moisture content of the trees is less What is possible during periods of the year, in addition to the high temperature during this period. It is not excluded that there are fires caused by human errors and the intensity of the fires increased from 15 July 2023, which included the  Homs governorate, Hama governorate, and  Lattakia governorate. Most of the fires were in rugged mountainous remote areas. The intensity and size of bushfires in some areas have led to the creation of their own weather systems, generating pyro cumulonimbus clouds, trapping heat, and generating strong wind, in turn sparking further fires. High winds have also helped the bushfires to spread, with some fires jumping over highways and roads. These fires led to material and environmental damage, as a few homes of a number of residents were torched, in addition to burning agricultural crops on which they depend as a main source of livelihood, in addition to burning a large part of the vegetation, forests, and natural reserves.

In addition, there are many warnings by the government, which are as follows:

High levels of fire risk are expected to continue affecting most forest sites in the governorates of Hama and Homs and the eastern parts of the governorates of Lattakia and Tartous during Friday 21 and Saturday 22 July 2023, with the participation of the impact of medium levels on forest sites close to the coastal strip. Normal conditions of heat and dryness continue to support high levels of fire hazard.

So far the directly affected families numbers are limited comparing with previous years, all  the hazards mentioned above are raising the expectations for more fires during the coming days, the indirect effect of this fires will increase our challenges against alleviate the sufferance of the families in the affected areas and protect the remaining resilience in these communities.

countries.name: Algeria
dtype.name: Fire
name: DZA: Fire - 2023-07 - Northeast Wildfires
summary: Wildfires have been rapidly spreading across the northeastern region of Algeria since July 24th causing extensive devastation. The disaster has had a profound impact on 4000 families, with the Algerian Government reporting 34 confirmed deaths. The affected population heavily relies on crops and livestock, both of which have been severely impacted by the wildfires, resulting in further hardships for the communities. Many homes have been reduced to ashes, leaving families displaced and vulnerable. The dire situation has also affected the health of the population, as the flames and smoke have led to thousands of injuries. The magnitude of the disaster requires urgent attention and support to address the immediate needs of those affected. However, the prevailing weather conditions remain a cause for concern. With temperatures exceeding 45 degrees Celsius and wind speeds exceeding 50 km/h on the Tunisian borders, coupled with low humidity, the conditions continue to favor the expansion and intensification of the wildfires.

countries.name: Philippines
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: Super Typhoon Doksuri
summary:
At 10 AM of 21 July 2023, the low pressure area of East of Southeastern Luzon developed into a Tropical Depression locally named “Egay” by the State Weather Bureau.

 

Egay intensified into a Tropical Storm on 22 July 2023 and further intensified into a Sever Tropical Storm on 23 July 2023. On same day, tropical cyclone wind signal was declared in effect. Egay intensifies into a Typhoon at 11 PM of 23 July 2023,  undergoes rapid intensification as it moves over the Philippine Sea, and reached the Super Typhoon Category at 7 AM today, 25 July 2023.

 

The center of the eye of Super Typhoon “Egay” as estimated based on all available data over the coastal waters of Aparri (Fuga Is.), Cagayan (18.7 °N, 121.4 °E ) with a maximum sustained winds of 175 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 240 km/h, and central pressure of 9355 hPa. It is moving west southwestward at 15 km/h.

summary: According to the data released by the Ministry if Interior & Safety of RoK on August 2nd, the heatwave in RoK this summer has resulted 16 deaths from heat-related illnesses in RoK under a prolonged heat wave with temperature above 38 degrees Celsius in some parts of the country. A total of 1,284 people reported suffering heat-related illnesses as of Tuesday August 2nd.  More than 80 participants at the World Scout Jamboree were sent to the hospital after the opening ceremony and more than 1,000 participants are suffering from heat-related illnesses.

countries.name: Cameroon

name: WRC: Flood - 2023-07 - FLOODS FAKO
summary:
Heavy rain accompanied by winds fell continuously in the city of Limbe from 18 to 19 July 2023. These rains caused flooding in several areas of the city of Limbé (including Church Street, and Down Beach) and landslides in Mawoh. Many damages could be observed including destruction of residential houses, destruction of shops; destruction of household property, disappearance, and loss of life.

The ONCC report  indicates that this decade will be marked by heavy rains accompanied by strong winds, thunderstorms, lightning and hail in many localities in the Regions of the Centre, South, East, Littoral, South-West and West, with a risk of recording flood situations in certain agglomerations of the Littoral region (Douala, Nkongsamba) and South-West (Limbe, Tiko).

According to the weather forecast for the decade from 04 to 14 July, the South-West Region will experience a significant increase in precipitation  throughout the rainy season .
it should be remembered that On March 18, 2023, the city of Buea located in the South-West Region of the country, already knew flooding due to runoff from Mount Cameroon.
As the rainy season is only at the beginning of the rainy season, the situation could intensify, endangering people's lives.

During the night of Monday, July

17 and the early morning of Tuesday, July 18, 2023, there have been heavy rains in the eastern part of the department of Cundinamarca; due to this, a torrential avenue was generated in the Naranjal village located in the municipality of Quetame - Cundinamarca, this situation caused 11 deaths, 6 people injured and 35 people evacuated, as well as significant damage to some homes and road infrastructure.

summary: The city of Dolisie, in the Republic of Congo, is in epidemic of cholera, shigellosis and typhoid fever, following the appearance of a disease that already causes 12 deaths, said Monday night the Congolese government, urging departments not yet in epidemic to "put themselves on alert". On July 18, 2023, the government indicates that Dolisie, capital of the Congolese department of Niari, is in epidemic of cholera, shigellosis and typhoid fever, due to the health situation of the city, marked by a disease, with to date 1,365 suspected cases, including 12 deaths, according to a statement from the Ministry of Health. In order to reduce the spread of this epidemic in the departments of Niari and Pointe-Noire, the local Red Cross of Niari actively participates in the various inter-agency coordination meetings and contributes to the active surveillance of cases, contact monitoring and social mobilization and the prevention of hygiene rules. To do this, the local Red Cross deployed 10 teams of 5 Volunteers in the town of Dolisie with 5 supervisors.

countries.name: Nigeria
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: NGA: Epidemic - 2023-07 - Anthrax Outbreak in Nigeria
summary:
The Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (FMARD) has confirmed one case of Anthrax disease in a mixed livestock farm in Niger State. This is the first animal case to be reported in Nigeria since the beginning of the West Africa outbreak in Ghana in June 2023. On 13th July 2023, the sudden deaths of livestock in this farm with eight (8) mortality was reported. In addition, the animals who died were observed to have been bleeding from external orifices without blood clotting. The Nigerian Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has said that anthrax disease may have spread to every part of the country. The NCDC said this hours after the Federal Government through the Ministry of Agriculture confirmed the first case of the disease in Niger state.
The case was in a multi-specie animal farm comprising of cattle, sheep and goats located at Gajiri, in Suleja Local Government Area, Niger State, where some of the animals had symptoms including oozing of blood from their body openings – anus, nose, eyes, and ears.
According to the Spokesperson of FMARD, there were significant movements of animals in the area of the last religious feast. The areas are called down south, and it’s possible that in that region where animals are infected may have made their way into the country. Most especially for animals that were brought in across the borders. So, in this context, there may be other animals with it.
The country’s Ministry of Health also expressed worry that anthrax has spread across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Stating that it is possible that the disease is currently across the country and likely other cases that are yet to be notified.

The signs of anthrax-infected animals include the oozing of blood from their body openings – (anus, nose, eyes, and ears), and high fever; it should be noted that, in many cases, the sign is not visible and leads to sudden death.

Following the report, samples were collected on 14th July 2023 from multiple species in this livestock farm and transported to the National Veterinary Research Institute (NVRI), VOM, Plateau State for testing and the results were positive for anthrax.

Further investigation is also ongoing to trace the source of the infection and to identify the spread to other farms and humans. Though human exposure has been reported, there are no reports so far of human symptoms or mortality. The FMARD and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) are currently working closely with the Niger State Ministries of Health and Agriculture to identify, isolate and follow up all exposed persons.

countries.name: Greece

name: GRC: Fire - 2023-07 - Greece Fires
summary:
The last days many wildfires hitting several areas in Greece, Firefighters are working on 90 fire fronts across the state. According to the infromation it is expected to be the warmest July on record in more than 50 years. Due to high temperatures and the strong winds most of the fires aren't under control. The wilfire in Euboea in the municipality of Karystos, cost the life of two pilots of a Canadair-style water bomber during their effort to put out the fire, and the life of a cattle breeder, also in mountainous Euboea. In the wilfire that broke out in Magnisia, Volos July 26, an eledry woman was found charred inside a mobile home, also a shepherd lost his life during his effort to save his flock. Thousand of hectares, hundred of houses, hotels, cars, factories, businesses and animals were burned. Overall, more than 35.000 thousand residents and tourists were forced to evacuate.

Attica: July 17, a wildfire broke out in east Attica, Kouvaras. The fire very quickly expanded to other nearby areas, Anavyssos, Saronida and Lagonisi. More than 30.000 hectares and several houses were burned. Eight areas were forced to evacuate. Also, due to the large fire, the Police has proceeded to stop the traffic of vehicles in nearby areas.

Rhodes: July 18, a wildfire borke out on the island of Rhodes, south aegean Greece, at Emponas area. Today is the ninth day after the fire started and are three active fronts. Around 260 firefighters, 42 fire trucks, 4 helicopters and 3 planes, hundreds of volunteers, the Greek army and the coast guard battle the blaze burning and support the evacution and other procedures. More assistant was requested. At the moment there are thousands of burned lands, houses, hotels and animals. Twelve areas were evacuated by the sea and by land. In the beggining, there are several shelters to accommodate the fire victims. Fire is not yet under control. At the moment, firefighting forces are focusing on the villages of Vati, Asklipieio and Archangelosthe. The island is in a state of Emergency. 

Eboea: July 23, a wildfires broke out in Eboea, Karystos. The fire started on three different fronts and immediately took on large proportions. At present, the situation in Karystos shows improvement, with firefighters successfully tackling scattered outbreaks. The fire has burned houses, many livestock facilities and animals. Residents and tourists of 6 areas were forced to evacuate. At the area 93 firefighters with 3 groups of pedestrians and 32 vehicles are operating at the scene, while from the air 3 is assistance from helicopters and aircraft as well as earthmoving machines and water carriers of the local municipality. 

Corfu: July 23, a wildfire broke out in northeast Corfu, burning forest and grassland areas with two big fronts which are located in the northeastern part of the island. The first goes from the village of Palia Perithia to Lavki and the second near Imerolia. Around 60 firefighters with 21 water trucks and three groups of firefighters on foot are operating, assisted by two helicopters and two PZL airplanes. Regarding the burned hectares, the estimation is around 20.000. More than 12 settlements were forced evacuation. After three days, seems that the fire is under control. 

Magnisia: July 26, a wilfire broke out in Velestino, Volos, Magnisia. At present, are two active fronts. Six areas were forced evacuation. While in the territory there are electricity issues due to the fire. Strong ground forces and air forces are working to extinguish the fire.

Other: July 17, a wildfire broke out about 30 kilometers northwest of Athens, in Dervenochoria, which by July 21 had burned an area of ​​more than 100,000 hectares and damaged many houses

July 23, a wildfire broke out in Aigio, Peloponnisos. With many scattered outbreaks of fire in an area which is inaccessible and very difficult for the intervention of ground forces. 

July 26, Large fronts broke out Lamia, Central Greece, which areas were being evacuated.

countries.name: Mongolia

summary:
Between July 3-5, rainfall of 28.4 mm have occured in 26 hours in central area of Mongolia including Ulaanbaatar. Prolonged rainfall has increased the water level of rivers by 10-30 cm from average height.  Selbe and Dund rivers run across Ulaanbaatar city and due to rainfall, both rivers are flooding and affecting the apartments nearby. The dam for the Selbe river has collapsed due to the overflooding. As of July 5, 54 apartments, 1 garage of mall, 5 houses, 15 gers, 2 main roads, 2 tunnels are in standing water caused by flood and 397 staff are working at the affected sites by draining the water with suction pumps. National Emergency Management has assisted 526 people including the elderly, disabled people and children who had been isolated by the standing water and flood and 306 vehicles have been moved from the flooded areas. In the flooded apartments, there's an electricity blackout and people are evacuating from their apartments.

Meanwhile in the ger district, there are households who are affected by the flash floods in Bayanzurkh, Chingeltei districts. Main concern is flooded pit latrines which is increasing the risk of contagious and water-borne diseases. The number of affected houses are being verified by the RC branches and will update the report once it's verified. 

The rain is expected to continue until July 10.

name: PAK: Flood - 2023-06 - Monsoon Rain in Pakistan
summary:
According to officials from the National Disaster Management Authority, there have been a total of 76 reported deaths in various rain-related incidents across Pakistan since the onset of the monsoon season on 25th June 2023. Additionally, 133 individuals have sustained injuries in multiple incidents. The majority of the fatalities occurred in Punjab and were primarily caused by electrocution and building collapses.

 In the provincial capital of Punjab, Lahore, there has been an unprecedented amount of rainfall, resulting in roads being transformed into waterways. This severe weather has left approximately 35% of the city without access to electricity and water this week. According to the Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA), the rainfall in Lahore has broken a 30-year record, with twelve out of sixteen monitoring points in the city recording rainfall exceeding 200 millimeters.

 

In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a tragic incident occurred in the Shangla district, where the bodies of eight children were recovered from a landslide on Thursday, as reported by the spokesperson of the emergency service Rescue 1122.

Please refer to the table below, extracted from the NDMA website, for a summary of the total rainfall data.

The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has issued a forecast for the next three days. According to their alert issued on 5th July, there is a prediction of widespread heavy to very heavy rainfall, with extremely heavy falls expected at scattered areas in the upper catchments of Rivers Sutlej, Ravi, Chenab, and partially Jhelum between 8th and 10th July 2023.

 

Additionally, the PMD has warned about the likelihood of severe thunderstorms and heavy rainfall in North and Northeastern Punjab, which may result in urban flooding in municipal areas and landslides in hilly regions.

 In Sindh, including cities like Karachi, Tharparkar, Sukkur, Larkana, Hyderabad, and Shaheed Benazir Abad, the Meteorological Office has forecasted potential thunderstorms and heavy rainfall. Furthermore, there is a possibility of thunderstorms in Northeastern Balochistan.

name: Flood - Monsoon Rains in Pakistan
summary:
The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) predicts more monsoon rains for Punjab and other parts of the country in the coming days. A weather system originating from the Bay of Bengal, along with a westerly trough affecting the upper regions, will persist until July 26th. The advisory warns of rain and thundershowers in various areas, including Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Lahore, Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan, Murree, and Galliyat.

Residents in low-lying areas of twin cities, Peshawar, Gujranwala, and Lahore, should be cautious of possible urban flooding from July 22nd to 26th. Landslide warnings are also in place for vulnerable areas of Murree, Galliyat, Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan, and hilly parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during this period. Tourists visiting these regions are urged to remain vigilant and take necessary precautions.

The PMD's advisory highlights that monsoon currents of good intensity continue to penetrate into Sindh and the eastern parts of the country. As a result, dust-thunderstorm/rain with a few heavy falls are likely in specific districts, with occasional gaps till July 25th.

Areas including Tharparkar, Umerkot, Mirpurkhas, Badin, Thatta, Sujawal, Kambar Shahdadkot, Dadu, Jamshoro, Matiari, Hyderabad, Tando Allahyar, Tando Muhammad Khan, and Sanghar districts, as well as Karachi division, may experience heavy falls leading to waterlogging and localized urban flooding on July 23-24.

The advisory also warns that wind/dust storms may cause damage to loose structures like electric poles, solar panels, and trees. Farmers are advised to plan their activities considering the forecast, and the general public is urged to stay vigilant.

Currently, the majority of Pakistan is experiencing monsoon rains, but in the next 24 hours, there is a chance of thundercloud formation and rainfall across all provinces, including northeastern Punjab, Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Sindh, upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan, and scattered locations in northern, central, and southern Punjab. Coastal areas, including Karachi, may expect continuous rainfall, humid evenings, and occasional light clouds during the evening hours. However, the likelihood of rainfall in the upcoming days is low.

Rainfall is expected in various areas of Punjab, eastern Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan, and Balochistan in Pakistan, particularly in central and northern regions, due to westerly winds coming from the western region.

Over the course of last month, starting from June 25, 2023, at least 133 people, including 55 children and 21 females, have lost their lives in weather-related incidents caused by heavy monsoon rains across Pakistan. During the same period, 215 people were injured. The province of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa witnessed the highest number of fatalities, which were primarily due to electrocution, building collapses, landslides, and drowning. As a result of the heavy rains that began on June 23, the rivers of the province of Neuquén are experiencing historic floods that according to specialists have not been recorded for 10 years. countries.name: Colombia
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: COL: Population Movement - 2023-06 - Risk of Massive Arrival of Migrant Population and Colombian Population from Venezuela ZUELA TO GUAINÍA
summary: Based on the situation that may arise, due to the situation at the Yapacana Mine in Venezuela with influence in the Department of Guainía and in the municipality of Inírida, some gaps and needs that may arise have been evidenced: Health: Given that this is a complex context with working conditions in the mines,  It is presumed that there is a high incidence of tropical, vector-borne and sexually transmitted diseases, among others, in people who potentially arrive in the area. Accommodation: although it is presumed that the people who potentially arrive would seek shelter in homes of their support networks, situations of overcrowding, saturation of the demand for housing/rent, rent overruns, among others, are presumed. Food Security: in the face of a possible restriction of economic resources, food needs are presumed. Profiles such as children, pregnant/lactating women and older adults (relatives of people in the mines who eventually arrive with them) would be especially vulnerable profiles. Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH): conditions in some reception sites (e.g. temporary shelters) are deficient in water and sanitation; In addition, hygiene kits may be required for people arriving. Protection: Due to the dynamics in the places of origin, as well as the profile of the people who would eventually arrive in Colombia, legal guidance, legal assistance and possibly psychosocial support would be required. Livelihoods: the pre-existing economic vulnerability of local communities, as well as the conditions of dependence of the local economy on mining on the other side of the border, lead to a deterioration of the general situation in the municipality, exacerbated by new arrivals of people. On the part of the section, coordination is established with the different authorities in the territory in order to coordinate the necessary actions for a possible response.

summary:
The flood was caused by the overflowing of the artificial lake in the city's park built on 12 hectares, which is more devastating than the previous floods that hit Ganja city in late May 2023.

Most of the houses based in the lower part of the park were damaged. The walls of most houses cracked, basements and backyards flooded with water.

As of June 23, more than 30 houses were damaged due to the flooding. A serious collapse has already been observed in the second concrete dam of the lake and as a result of unstable weather conditions (according to the information received from hydrometeorologists, heavy rains, hailstorms are expected in the next couple of days in the western regions of Azerbaijan, and the river waters in this region is expected to rise), the second dam is expected to collapse, which would dramatically increase the scale of the emergency.

Currently, the rescue teams of the Ganja Regional Center of the Ministry of Emergency Situations are carrying out high priority emergency work to reduce the water level in the lake. They are aiming at draining the water to prevent it from overflowing. Natural draining is not possible for the moment.

summary:
Since 17 June, in the Province of Jujuy, a series of peaceful demonstrations have been taking place led by indigenous communities and trade unions against the constitutional reform in the Province of Jujuy and demanding salary increases and union issues for teachers in the province.

On June 20, the proposed constitutional reform was approved. This led to an increase in tension in the streets with approximately 20 seriously injured. Likewise, movement through the capital city and its outskirts is limited, causing, for example, a cessation in the air activity of the local airport due to the impossibility of access for its employees or limitations in the supply of supplies in hospitals.

The situation in Jujuy involved a mobilization on June 21 in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires from the obelisk to the headquarters of the House of the Province of Jujuy in the downtown area of the city. Various organizations, unions and political spaces have participated in this mobilization, which did not present major inconveniences and took place peacefully.
