name: GEO: Pluvial/Flash Flood - 2023-06 - Flash Floods in Eastern Georgia
summary: In 15th of June, Gurjaani, a municipality in Georgia, experienced a significant disaster resulting from heavy rainfall, flooding, and hailstorms. The disaster impacted various areas within Gurjaani, affecting both urban and rural settlements. As a consequence of the heavy rainfall, the central streets of Gurjaani municipality and surrounding areas were flooded, causing severe difficulties in transportation and mobility. In addition, the sudden mudflows and landslides resulted in the destruction of roads, blockages caused by fallen trees, and damage to vital infrastructure such as bridges and power transmission towers. Gurjaani, Chumlaki, Tchandari, Vejini, Dzirkoki, Kolagi, Bakurtsikhe, Kodalo villages were flooded, and other state infrastructure such as bridges and inland roads, and power transmission towers were damaged. The disaster also had a detrimental impact on the agricultural sector, with flooding damaging agricultural lands and destroying crops. This has significant implications for the livelihoods of the affected population, as agriculture serves as a crucial source of income for many households in Gurjaani. During the Gurjaani disaster, the heavy flooding had a profound impact on the affected households. As families typically stored basic household items and food on the first floor, the floodwaters resulted in significant damage to essential supplies, appliances, furniture, and various household items. This loss added to the already challenging situation faced by the affected population

countries.name: Zimbabwe
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: ZWE:Cholera Outbreak
summary:
The first cholera outbreak of 2023 started on 12 February 2023 in Chegutu town in Mashonaland West Province. As of 20th January 2024, Zimbabwe has recorded 19,477 suspected cholera cases , 71 laboratory confirmed deaths, 350 suspected cholera deaths & 2,252 laboratory confirmed cases. The crude mortality rate remains above 2.2% and raises concerns regarding case management and the quality of care. Due to the high rate of transmission, the disease is now affecting people across multiple geographical areas. To date, suspected and confirmed cases have been reported in 45 out of 62 districts and in all 10 provinces of the country. The outbreak has now spread to more than the 17 traditional cholera hotspot districts, putting at risk over 10 million people, including more than five million children. Transmission routes from Buhera and Mutare have contributed to the spread of the outbreak in urban populations as well as the spike in cases in Harare and Chitungwiza.

 

The capacity of the Ministry of Health and Child Care has been stretched due to the high number of admissions, lack of human resources to manage the caseload, and lack of cholera supplies, including disinfection liquids, to stop the transmission. There is a disrupted community health care system where primary health care - which is responsible for ensuring that community members adhere to water, sanitation, and hygiene practices - is overwhelmed. Active case findings and surveillance have been challenged, compounded by inadequate logistical supplies. There is a need to mobilise and train more volunteers to support task shifting from medical personnel to volunteers, as well as support in increasing the awareness of risks and treatment.

 

In June 2023, the Zimbabwe Red Cross Society (ZRCS) requested CHF 464,595 from the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) Disaster Response Emergency Fund to fight the cholera outbreak, which showed a positive response in the targeted districts. However, the outbreak has spread to new districts, prompting the ZMRC to move the current situation in its scenario planning to a “worst-case scenario”. The launch of this Emergency Appeal for CHF 3 million is to enable the ZRCS to further scale-up their response, with 550,455 people targeted across the most affected and vulnerable districts and their communities.

countries.name: Greece
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: GRC: Population Movement - 2023-06 - Greece - Peloponnese Shipwreck
summary:
Early on Wednesday 14 June a fishing boat capsized in international waters 47 nautical miles southwest of Pylos in southern Greece, in one of the deepest areas in the Mediterranean. The bodies of dozens of individuals have been recovered with hundreds feared missing as reports suggest that 400-750 people were onboard.  104 individuals were rescued -none of whom were wearing a life jacket- however, as the time passes hopes of finding survivors are diminishing. This is the deadliest shipwreck off Greece in several years.

The boat had sailed from the Libyan town of Tobruk, which lies south of the Greek island of Crete, with most on board being young men in their 20s. Coast guard said the boat, which was en route to Italy, was spotted in international waters late on Tuesday 13 June by an aircraft belonging to EU border agency Frontex and two nearby vessels. It said those on board had refused assistance offered by Greek authorities late on Tuesday. A few hours later the boat capsized and sank, triggering a massive search-and-rescue operation mounted by the Hellenic Coast Guard.

Four rescued migrants were rushed to Kalamata hospital in a Super-Puma helicopter while the other rescued individuals were taken to the port of Kalamata, where preparations for their reception have been made with the assistance of the general secretariat of Civil Protection.

The Hellenic Red Cross, with the specialized nursing staff and the volunteers of the Health Sector of the Kalamata Regional Department assisted from the first moment the survivors of the wreck. Volunteer Samaritans-Rescuers of the HRC were also deployed and supported more than 80 migrants (including 20 children), providing first aid and distributing food and basic necessities while offering psychological support to the rescued migrants. The main health problems faced are secondary drowning, shortness of breath, dehydration, asthma attacks, high fever, exhaustion, dysuria, hematuria, and otitis. 

Staff of the Research & Restoring Family Links (RFL) Sector of the HRC arrived today in Kalamata, in order to coordinate from the spot the actions for the search for the missing people and the restoration of the family ties of the survivors, with the support of the ICRC team in Greece. 

The HRC will remain at the scene for as long as necessary.

name: SRB: Flood - 2023-06 - June floods
summary:
For two weeks before the date of the disaster, which occurred on 12-16 June, the Republic of Serbia was affected by heavy rainfall. The affected areas are the city of Belgrade and Kolubarski, Moravicki, Pomoravski, Raski, Zlatiborski, Rasinski, Nisavski, Toplicki, Zlatiborski, Jablanicki district and municipalities in Kosovo and Metohija. 7 municipalities and cities reported from the 4th to 6th of June that were affected by heavy rain that caused flash floods and floods. Heavy rainfalls were in the municipalities and cities of Loznica, Sabac, Babusnica, Aleksinac, Grocka, Aleksandrovac, Kursumlija, Cacak, and Vrnjacka Banja. In these municipalities and cities, it was reported that from 10 to 40 liters per square fell in just 3 hours which lead to floods and flash floods. Local streams and rivers of Dumaca and Dobrava, Mozgovacka River, Rasina, Bresnica, Bukovac, Zutaja, Vrnjacka, Lipovacka, and Rsovacka were spilled. Agriculture fields and roads were flooded, and accumulated water covered several rural roads and bridges.

From the 12th to 16th of June, due to new heavy rainfalls, additional 16 municipalities and cities declared a state of emergency due to flooding and flash floods (Arilje, Trstenik, Kursumlija, Prokuplje, Vučitrn, Varvarin, Novi Pazar, Rekovac, Kruševac, Jagodina, Despotovac, Sokobanja, Cicevac, Svilajnac, Koceljava, Kosjeric). During this period on each day in different parts of the Republic of Serbia, there were heavy rainfalls with intensity from 30 liters to 80 liters per square meter in 12 hours.

countries.name: Djibouti
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: DJI: Cyclone - 2023-06 - High Winds/Rain
summary:
On the evenings of Saturday, June 10 and Sunday, June 12, 2023, 2 localities (Omar Jagaa and Sankal) located respectively in the administrative regions of Arta and Dikhil of the Republic of Djibouti were affected by strong winds accompanied by sporadic showers.  These two affected localities are areas inhabited by particularly vulnerable internally displaced persons.  

This natural event linked to climate change has been described by the local community as unprecedented in its violence and spontaneity. Hence a certain fear that remains perceptible.

The regional branches of the Djibouti Red Crescent Society and local public authorities have undertaken post-disaster  assessment missions to assess the extent of the damage caused by this event.

No loss of human life was reported. Most of the damage is limited to the destruction of habitats, latrines and water storage equipment. Due to their limited financial resources, the settlements are built from makeshift materials. 

In  total, the number of affected households is 128. That is 768 people according to the average household size in Djibouti which is 6 people.

countries.name: Philippines
dtype.name: Volcanic Eruption
name: PHL: Volcanic Eruption - 2023-06 - Mayon Volcano
summary:
Mayon Volcano is placed under Alert Level III, indicating relatively high unrest, that Mayon is exhibiting magmatic eruption of a summit lava dome, with increased chances of lava flows and hazardous PDCs affecting the upper to middle slopes of the volcano and of potential explosive activity within weeks or even days.

 A total of 267 rockfall events and 2 volcanic earthquakes were recorded from 05 to 08 June, compared to 54 rockfall events from 01 to 04 June 2023. These events had durations of one (1) to three (3) minutes and transported lava debris within a kilometer range of the southern upper slopes. The volume of discrete rockfall events increased on 3 June based on the seismic record, signaling an increase in the rate of dome growth. Three (3) pyroclastic density current or PDC events on the Bonga (southeast) and Basud (east) Gullies were observed today at 6:18 AM, 9:53 AM and 11:00 AM. The PDCs lasted four to five minutes based on the seismic record and emplaced within a kilometer of the summit crater. In contrast, SO2 emission remains at baseline or background levels. The overall monitoring parameters indicate that very slow extrusion of shallow degassed magma is ongoing and is incrementally increasing in rate; i.e., effusive magmatic eruption is taking place.

countries.name: Philippines

name: PHL: Volcanic Eruption - 2023-06 - Mayon Volcanic Eruption
summary:
In the past 24-hour period, the Mayon Volcano Network recorded six (6) dome-collapse Pyroclastic Density Currents (PDC) that lasted three (3) to six (6) minutes and one hundred ninety-nine (199) rockfall events based on seismic and visual observations.  The PDC and rockfall events emplaced lava debris on the southern gullies within two kilometers from the summit crater. Thin light brown ash from the rockfalls and continuous moderate degassing from the summit crater produced steam-laden plumes that were bent and drifted to the general south. 
The Albay Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (PDRRMC) on Thursday ordered the evacuation of residents in areas surrounding Mayon Volcano (6 km radius) in order to protect lives and properties due to its increased activity.

countries.name: Sierra Leone
dtype.name: Other
name: SLE: Election preparedness
summary:
General elections are scheduled in Sierra Leone from June to July 2023 following the calendar issued by the Electoral Commission for Sierra Leone (ECSL). This election includes, first, a Presidential election and a Parliamentary process across the country. The Election campaign started in 2022 and was completed in May 2023. There have been indicators that social or civil unrest would likely be experienced during the election period, requiring heightened readiness of the National Society to support potentially affected communities under its mandate.

The coming elections will be held as follows:

• 24th June 2023 Presidential - voting day in the 16 districts of the country.

• 25th to 28th June 2023, Proclamation of the results of the presidential election. This is an estimated date based onhistorical process which usually takes up to 4 days.

• Proclamation of Parliamentary representative following the Proportional representative system established in early 2023. The date for the start and end of this is not specified but all election processes must be completed from June to July. Following the NS contingency planning, a period of two weeks is estimated for planning purposes.

With regards to the upcoming 2023 General Elections period, incidences of inter-communal conflict have so far been observed in many parts of the country. Indeed, these elections will be held against the backdrop of a severe complex economic crisis and periods of civil unrest surrounding governance issues. In the period leading to the election, the country has witnessed civil unrest, economic instability, currency devaluation, and multiple disasters, especially in the country’s capital city, Freetown. The widespread protest of August 2022 was a violent example of turmoil in Freetown and other cities in Sierra Leone. Indeed, thousands of protesters mobilized around the country, blocking roads and main supply routes demonstrating unemployment, economic hardship, and injustices, demanding reductions in fuel prices, economic relief for indebted families, fair prices for agricultural products, employment and labour rights, security, and protection. Over 34 people were injured, 30 deaths (including 3 police officers), and many detained in different parts of the country. These events are analyzed to be the reflection of what could happen during the upcoming general elections. Moreover, some recent analyses report that ahead of the June 24 poll, a rematch of the 2018 vote, identity issues and economic stagnation are also on the ballot. After the change of the Parliamentary voting system in early 2023 from a complete election system to a Proportional representative system. Proportional Representation is a type of electoral system under which subgroups of an electorate are reflected proportionately in the elected body. This could add more expectations from the population on the Presidential elections, given that level of changes in the presidential votes may also lead to parallel changes of the National and local possible representatives across the country. The hope for politico-economical changes is highly expected based on some allegations and past analysis reporting a high corruption level across the country with some economical challenges not resolved.

The period preceding the elections (until late March) has seen episodic protests and reports of intimidation against opposition parties. This and the intimidation actions already reported against the opposition indicate that the relative calm reported in other sources can also deteriorate. Between the most recent event, there has been members of the opposition wounded or shoot and some violence in the past weeks since the campaign. Whilst the priority is to support peacebuilding and prevention of violence efforts, previous outbreaks of violence have demonstrated the importance of planning for potential humanitarian response activities.

countries.name: Pakistan
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: PAK: Cyclone - 2023-06 - Tropical Cyclone (BIPARJOY) Formed over Southeast Arabian Sea
summary:
The Depression over the southeast Arabian Sea has strengthened and is now a Cyclonic Storm named "BIPARJOY." It is currently located at Latitude 12.3°N and Longitude 66.0°E, approximately 1420km south of Karachi. The maximum sustained surface winds around the center of the storm are 60-70 Km/hour, with gusts up to 80 Km/hour. The environmental conditions, including a sea surface temperature of 30-32°C, low vertical wind shear, and upper-level divergence, are favorable for further intensification. The system is expected to become a Severe Cyclonic Storm within the next 24 to 36 hours and continue moving in the north/northwest direction.

The low-pressure area over the Southeast Arabian Sea has developed into a Depression, which is now a strong LPA. It is positioned near Latitude 11.5°N and Longitude 66.0°E, about 1500km south of Karachi. The environmental conditions, including a sea surface temperature of 30-31°C, low vertical wind shear, and upper-level divergence, are conducive for further intensification. The system is likely to progress into a Tropical Storm within the next 18 to 24 hours while moving in the north/northwest direction.

At present, none of the coastal areas in Pakistan are under threat from the cyclonic storm. The Pakistan Meteorological Department's cyclone warning center in Karachi is closely monitoring the system and will provide updates accordingly.

summary:
According to the bulletin of the Pan American Health Organization / World Health Organization (PAHO / WHO) as of July 31 indicates that in the 2023, between EW 1 and EW 28, a total of 127,631 cases of dengue were reported, with a cumulative incidence rate in the subregion of 69.7 cases per 100,000 population. In this year, of the 127,631 cases of dengue reported, 10,861 (8.5%) were laboratory confirmed and 269 (0.21%) were classified as severe dengue, so a request is made to member countries to <span lang="ES">review and adjust their preparedness and response plans to make "mso-ansi-language: ES-CR;" > against outbreaks of dengue and other arboviruses, in order to prevent complications and deaths associated with these diseases.

 The four dengue virus serotypes (DENV1, DENV2, DENV3 and DENV4) are present in the Central American and Mexico subregion. In 2023, until EW 28, the simultaneous circulation of all of them has been detected in Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico; while in Panama, the serotypes DENV1, DENV2 and DENV3 circulate, and in Nicaragua the serotypes DENV1, DENV3 and DENV4 (PAHO/WHO).

In Costa Rica, the presence of the mosquito "Aedes aegypti" is increased during the rainy season, which is influencing the appearance of 15,417 cases of dengue in the last 6 weeks, according to data from the Health Situation Analysis of the Ministry of Health of Costa Rica, 2023.

The SN has been in contact with the Ministry of Health at the Central and Regional levels, who have requested support from the institution to address this issue.

countries.name: Nepal
dtype.name: Other
name: NPL: Other - 2023-06 - Dengue prevention and control
summary: In Nepal, dengue is a rapidly emerging disease. Endemic across most provinces, dengue incidence has increased in recent years largely due to expansion of the vector Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, as well as the movement of people and the introduction of imported cases. All 4 dengue serotypes exist in Nepal, with DENV-1 and 2 historically contributing the highest burden (EDCD, 2019). The first case of dengue in Nepal was reported in 2004. Since then, dengue cases have been gradually reported in Nepal, with an outbreak in the year 2019 (n=17,992) reported from 68 districts and in 2022 (n=54,784) from all 77 districts. According to EDCD of MoHP, among the total of 54,000 cases, majority of dengue cases (n=28109) including 38 deaths happened between January to September 2022 coinciding with the peak rainy season in the country. This is indicative of exponential surge in dengue cases during July/ September considering the overall weather conditions and monsoon season which provides hibernating infected mosquitoes with an optimal environment for breeding. Until epidemiological week 17 (end of April 2023, EWARS report, EDCD), 600 dengue cases has already been diagnosed which is highly alarming as this is the very first time that dengue has occurred in the consecutive year in contrary to the usual cyclical pattern of dengue incidence in Nepal. In addition, dengue incidence started even during winter season and is steadily rising over the weeks. According to a mathematical modelling projection conducted by WHO (2022), the projection shows that cases are already exceeded the alert threshold since beginning of 2023 when compared to the reported dengue cases in EWARS, indicating early signs on outbreak in Nepal. On average, 20-30 cases of dengue have been found each week in different regions of Nepal. Since dengue is relatively new for Nepal, there is low level of knowledge and awareness among people. Even the priority for dengue prevention was less priority in the country until last year, Nepal government has been sincerely trying to address the emerging trend of dengue through joint planning and implementation from this year. Therefore, Nepal government, municipal authority to the national level, have requested NRCS for better coordination and collaboration in dengue prevention initiatives. Ongoing reported cases of COVID-19 and dengue infection has overarching effects on country’s health system with challenges to properly manage the cases. Furthermore, Dengue has disparate effect on different population strata. While pregnant and lactating women, children and elderly population are vulnerable to dengue, young adult population working outside (with low socio-economic status) have higher exposure risk to dengue infected vectors. Hence, the number of hospitalized cases will be increased in coming 3-4 months and hospital facilities will be overwhelmed. Likewise, the supply of blood (Platelets-rich Plasma-PRPs) will be the challenge to meet the demand. Because of all these factors the severity and mortality cases will be increased in the country. In addition, the urban design of major cities in Nepal lacks in infrastructural public health aspects along with challenging waste management system and poor sanitation facilities which provides vectors with optimal environment for breeding. People residing in slums, densely populated urban cities with poor sanitation facilities are at greater risk of being affected. Hence, exponential rise in dengue cases can not only overwhelm health systems but also affect the most vulnerable population with low socio-economic conditions.

countries.name: Kenya
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: KEN: Population Movement - 2023-05 - Population Influx
summary:
Kitale Transit Centre and Kakuma Refugee Camp

According to UNHCR, the number of refugees in Kenya has continually increased over the past years, mainly due to the volatile political and security situations in several neighbouring countries. Recently, over 20,000 new arrivals have been registered with more than 10,000 recorded in the first quarter of 2023. The majority are mainly from South Sudan, with some citing drought, flooding, and food insecurity among their reasons for flight in addition to conflict and insecurity. In Kitale Transit Centre, an estimated 1,700 asylum seekers have been recorded as new arrivals with no refugee status. The centre is only able to hold 200 people resulting in over-stretching of the available planned resources where the asylum seekers are now hosted in Kitale Agriculture Society of Kenya (ASK grounds). As a result, the reception centres in both Kakuma camp and Kalobeyei settlement are holding more than their capacity, leading to congestion and posing serious health risks. There has been a discussion with the authority in Kenya as to whether register or take back those in transit and a decision has not yet been made since 23rd April hence resulting in the over-stretching of humanitarian needs in both Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kalobeyei and Kitale Transit Centre. 

Daadab Refugee Camp

Somalia continues to face the longest and the most severe drought in its recent history, due to the failure of five consecutive rainy seasons, with a sixth failed rainy season predicted. Reduced access to water and the ever-shrinking pasture have affected pastoralist and agrarian communities throughout the region, forcing them to leave their places of origin in search of water, food, pastures, or humanitarian assistance. More than 1.3 million Somalis have been displaced internally due to drought since 2022. According to the UNHCR-led Protection and Return Monitoring Network (PRMN), 234,000 displacements within Somalia were recorded in February 2023. Out of the total displacements during the reporting month, the majority, 62% were attributed to conflict/insecurity, 34% due to the drought, and 4% due to other reasons. The top five humanitarian needs of the displaced families were food (53%), followed by shelter (18%), and livelihood (12%).

Based on the arrival statistics in the first quarter of 2023, over 110,000 new arrivals have been recorded in the Dadaab Refugee camp. The three Dadaab camps do not have adequate space to host newly arrived refugees, forcing many to reside in makeshift shelters along the outskirts of the camps, where clean water and sanitation facilities are either grossly insufficient or non-existent.  Late last year, the Government of Kenya agreed to the reopening of the Ifo 2 site in Dadaab to host the new arrivals which was actioned in March 2023. The Government has also agreed to the proposed remodelling of this site into an integrated settlement similar to Kalobeyei, to provide humanitarian assistance sustainably to both the refugees and host communities.

Effects

There is a need to address the most urgent/lifesaving needs of the most vulnerable arriving population in Dadaab’s newly opened IFO2 camp (4,704 Households) and 10,700 asylum seekers in Kalobeyei Reception Centre for access to basic WASH facilities and adequate nutrition. These interventions will improve the health and well-being of the asylum seekers who have been forced to flee their homes due to conflict and/or drought. 

Needs

In its mandate to protect and provide humanitarian assistance and coordinate other partners, UNHCR continues to support through nutrition and health provision to the asylum seekers. However, given the skyrocketing arrivals in the camp and its localities, both asylum seekers and host communities are experiencing a myriad of needs that ought to be addressed amidst the ongoing crisis: 

  •  ·       Supply of Clean drinking water and extending sanitation and hygiene facilities to the outskirts of the camps.  

    ·       Provision of targeted protection services for the most vulnerable to ensure their needs are met.  

    ·       Malnourished children are being screened and admitted to stabilization centres.  

    ·       Plans are underway to boost assistance by providing additional basic relief items including dignity kits for women and girls. 

    ·       UNHCR is also working to assist host communities surrounding Dadaab by rehabilitating boreholes, providing generators for water pumps, and trucking in water.  

    ·       Together with health partners, setting up additional treatment centres to increase access to health care for new arrivals and to be prepared in the event more cholera cases are reported. 

    ·       More support is needed not only in Kenya but also in Uganda, South Sudan, Somalia and Ethiopia, where millions of people are facing dire humanitarian conditions as the rains continue to fail.

countries.name: United States
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: USA: Cyclone - 2023-05 - Super Typhoon Mawar
summary: More than a week after Typhoon Mawar hit Guam, many residents are still without power and water and it could be weeks before these systems are fully restored on the western Pacific islands. The American Red Cross is helping people with medical or disability needs, as well as emotional and spiritual support during these challenging times. More than 180 trained Red Cross disaster workers from all over the United States are on the islands working closely with officials, partners and community, and humanitarian agencies; distributing relief supplies (clean-up kits, tarps, coolers, flashlights and personal hygiene supplies), supporting feeding efforts in community-run shelters, and assessing residential damage to help and support people affected by this powerful storm. The American Red Cross has served approximately 2,400 households so far and are working with village mayors to begin hosting community distribution sites for impacted residents to find relief supplies, recovery assistance and information. The American Red Cross is also supporting feeding in the community-run shelters and has provided as many as 26,000 meals and snacks since the storm hit the islands. The Red Cross is supporting the military Emergency Family Assistance Center (EFAC) on Andersen Air Force Base and Navy Base Guam where families can receive disaster relief services and information.

countries.name: Central African Republic
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: CAF: Population movement from Sudan
summary: The populations coming from Sudan are currently arriving in Amdafock and are still located in the village, in a temporary site. According to information reported by the Birao RC committee, the number of refugees received as of 6 May is estimated to be 5,000, with approximately 1,000 returnees. These figures were updated on 8 May by OCHA with 9,700 people arriving in Am-Dafock since the beginning of the crisis. At least 10,000 refugees could arrive in CAR in the coming weeks and 15,000 returnees according to UN projections. Am Dafok is a village in the Vakaga prefecture. However, other entry points remain possible based on lessons learned from previous crises in the area. Notably, the border is the state of South Darfur. According to the 2003 census, Am Dafok has a population of about 3,500. Other villages on the border between the two countries are also expected to see an influx of people in the coming days due to the limited capacity of Am Dafok and the projected influx of up to 15,000 people in the coming days. Increased entry in Tchad bordering the North of Birao is also part of the possible parameter in the development of this crisis.

countries.name: Italy
dtype.name: Flood
name: ITA: Flood - 2023-05 - Emilia Romagna Flood
summary:
After an initial warning, the first event occurred at the beginning of the month: harsh meteorological conditions have caused localised floods and land-slides, managed at local and regional level.

A second warning have been issued on May 14th, the national response had been ignited, according to the EWEA protocol in place, but after the 200 mm of rain which had already fallen in the first days of May, an out of scale event had occurred, with about 350 million cubic meters of water falling in the most affected area (800 km2 of territory), 100 municipalities involved, 23 rivers and watercourses flooded, another 13 which saw the alarm level exceeded, thousands of landslides (376 the main ones) between hills and mountains.

The emergency machine was already alerted, and was involved in several fronts; the European Civil Protection intervention system was activated, deploying high capacity pumping modules. The regional civil protection is intervening with 63 construction sites to make the rivers safe (e.g. some rivers, like Idice and Sillaro have changed course). 

15 people died, mainly due to a landslide, and about 23,067 people are sill evacuated. The majority 16,445, in the Ravenna area, then 4,462 in the province of Forlì-Cesena and 2,160 in the Bologna area.

There are 2,694 citizens welcomed in the hotels and in the structures set up by the Municipalities: schools, sports halls and gyms; the others have found alternative accommodations (second homes, friends and relatives). In particular, 2,094 in the Ravenna area, 351 in the Bologna area, 243 in the Forlì-Cesena area and 6 in the Rimini area.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
dtype.name: Epidemic
name: Sri Lanka - Dengue Outbreak & Floods
summary:
Dengue cases are on the rise since the beginning of the year in the country. The cases reported in 2023 are three times higher than those recorded in the corresponding period of the last two years. A higher number of cases are recorded in the Western, Southwestern, and Eastern provinces, especially in Colombo, Gampaha, Kalutara, Batticaloa, Trincomalee, Galle, and Kandy districts. According to the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU), the ongoing inclement weather conditions only further aggravate the breeding of mosquitos. The NDCU further revealed that the Den-3 variant of the Dengue virus spreading among the population in the country creates a high risk of accelerating the process of the virus spread and a total of 34,279 dengue cases have reportedly been recorded across the island as of 18 May 2023, among them over 50% of the cases were reported from the Western Province.

Meanwhile, Colombo District recorded the highest number of dengue cases numbering 7,017, followed by 7,602 from Gampaha and 1,984 from Kalutara. The National Dengue Prevention Unit said 22 Dengue-related fatalities have been reported so far this year with 07 of them being reported from the Western Province. This includes 02 deaths from Colombo, 04 from Gampaha, and one death from Kalutara. Against this backdrop, several dengue prevention programs were carried out in various areas of Colombo today. Meanwhile, it is reported that ‘red notice’ warnings have been issued on 1,308 houses and other properties in Colombo City where the respective premises were maintained in a careless manner allowing the breeding of mosquitoes. The National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU) has reported nearly 4,000 novel cases of the dengue virus within the first two weeks of this month, raising grave concerns about a potential epidemic. Meanwhile, reports have also revealed that, as of now, the highest number of dengue patients are being treated at the Colombo National Hospital, District General Hospital in Negombo, Infectious Disease Hospital (IDH), Colombo South Teaching Hospital (Kalubowila), Trincomalee General Hospital, Lady Ridgeway Hospital and the National Teaching Hospital in Kandy.

Further, the Southwest monsoon activation has also been intensifying rainfall in Sri Lanka since ‘Mocha‘ crossed the country, mostly affecting Galle and Matara districts due to heavy rains, high winds, and flash floods due to the water level of the Nilwala and Gin River’s have risen alarmingly. In the Matara district, according to the Department of Meteorology Centre (DMC), most damages were reported on 16 May, and a total of 8 Divisional Secretary divisions are severely affected.  The Department of Irrigation has extended the flood warning message issued for the Gin River Basin on 16 May 2023. Accordingly, the Irrigation Department warned that there may be a significant level of flooding in the low-lying areas of the Gin River situated in Baddegama, Niyagama, and Nagoda Divisional Secretariat Divisions of Galle district.

The continues heavy rains coupled with high winds over 70 km/hr due to the indirect impact of the cyclonic storm – ‘Mocha‘ have caused damage to the houses, fallen trees, road embankment failures/cutting failures, and blockages of the main access across various districts. Further, due to the severity of the situation, agricultural lands and standing crops were also damaged in low-lying areas due to the flash flooding in both districts while houses and common buildings, and markets are inundated with flash floods and major damages have also been reported.

countries.name: Syrian Arab Republic
dtype.name: Drought
name: SYR: Drought - 2023-05 - Syria Droughts 2023
summary:
After more than ten years of conflict in Syria, access to water has become one of the most prominent humanitarian challenges, which is exacerbated by climate change. According to severity scale updated in June 2023, all of Al-Sweida’s districts are ranked at levels 3 to 5, meaning they are facing a major, severe, or critical problem in water needs. The Al-Sweida governorate faced during this period a sharp decline in the water availability, the causes of which appear to be the intertwining of many factors: Loss of the main source of drinking water since 2012 the increase of the population between 2010 and 2022, increasing the demand on water and pressure on resources, and the decrease in the maintenance and technical level of logistical operating equipment. The level of the surface dams has decreased to a hazardous level and with some close to being completely dry.

 

The main reasons relate to the fact that rainfall has decreased significantly in recent years, additionally climate change has led to a lack of snowfall in large quantities which is the main source of dam water collection. Other reasons involve low electrical voltage because of the huge destruction of the infrastructures related to electrical supplies and lack of fuel and spare parts, which is the main cause of the malfunction of the pumps,
 in addition to the technical and logistical problems of the Water Corporation in Al-Sweida Governorate, which led to a large number of wells being out of service (around 80%). Moreover, Land irrigation, illegal extraction, and vandalism also helped exacerbate the water crisis in the governorate, with no capacity to replace or maintain due to the continue crises and sanctions among other clear effects of the climate changes and global warming. In June of 2023, reports confirmed through official channels that the water crisis in Al-Sweida governorate is severe, and that within two months, water will run out in surface dams. Not solving the problem of pumps in the wells will lead to the exit of more wells from the service, and thus exacerbate the water crisis that leads to a severe humanitarian disaster affecting 650,000 people. This will increase challenges and decrease resilience in these communities.

countries.name: Bangladesh
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: BGD: Cyclone - 2023-05 - Cyclone Mocha
summary:
Cyclone ‘Mocha’ was first noticed as a low-pressure area in the greater North Indian Ocean on 8 May 2023 by the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD), which gradually intensified and transformed into a very severe cyclonic storm. According to Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) it turned into a deep depression and on 11 May 2023 morning intensified into a cyclonic storm “Mocha” (pronunciation: Mokha) over the same area (ref. BMD bulletin number 1).

On 13 May 2023, BMD issued ‘great danger’ signal number 10 (ten) for one of the coastal districts Cox’s Bazar coastal district and their offshore islands and chars (char in Bangladesh refers to island in river, a piece of land surrounded by water). At the same time, BMD issued ‘great danger’ signal number 8 (eight) for Chattogram, Feni, Noakhali, Laksmipur, Chandpur, Barishal, Bhola, Patuakhali, Jhalakati, Pirojpur, Barguna districts and their offshore islands and chars (ref. BMD bulletin number 12).

According to the special weather bulletin number 17 of BMD on 14 May 2023, 2:00 am Bangladesh Standard Time (BST), the very severe cyclonic storm 'Mocha' over the east central Bay of Bengal and adjoining area moved in a North-Northeasterly direction, intensified over the same area and has centred about 490 km South-Southwest of Chattogram port, 410 km of South-west of Cox's Bazar port, 530 km South of Mongla port and 460 km south of Payra port of Bangladesh.

According to the Needs Assessment Working Group (NAWG), following the great danger signal and evacuation order of the Government of Bangladesh (GoB), over 750,000 people were evacuated to safety in Cox’s Bazar and other areas.

The cyclone Mocha made landfall in southeast Bangladesh and north Myanmar coasts around 3:00 pm BST on 14 May 2023 with a maximum sustained wind speed of 190-210 km/h gusting to 220 km/h and affected tens of thousands of families and homes and key facilities have been destroyed, especially in the camps settlement and neighbouring local communities.

During the landfall of cyclone Mocha, a strong surge with 6-7 feet tides across the coastal districts namely Cox’s Bazar, Chattogram, Noakhali, and Feni and with the storm and heavy rain destroyed a huge number of jhupri (shacks; made of jute sticks, tree leaves, jute sacks, etc.) and kutcha (temporary; made of mud brick, bamboo, sun-grass, wood and occasionally corrugated iron sheets as roofs) houses in Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Chattogram, Rangamati districts.

countries.name: Myanmar
dtype.name: Cyclone
name: Myanmar: Cyclone MOCHA 2023
summary:
On 14 May 2023 at 12:30 local time, Cyclone Mocha made landfall in Myanmar as an extremely severe cyclonic storm with winds gusting up to 230-250 km/h. Mocha crossed the interior near Sittwe in Rakhine State, and moved North-Eastwards to Hakha and Paletwa townships in Chin State, with wind speed of approximately 115 km/h.  By morning of 15 May, Mocha reached Sagaing region as a deep land depression with a wind speed 78 km/h.

Mocha caused storm surges in excess of two meters, strong winds and very heavy rainfall with heavy inundation reported in low-lying areas of Rakhine, particularly in and around the state capital Sittwe, and in Chin state, Magway, Ayeyarwaddy and Mandalay regions as well as lower Sagaing region. Houses,  sanitation facilities and public infrastructure were damaged or destroyed by the cyclone, including hospitals, transport infrastructure such as roads and airports, a water dam, and agricultural land and equipment was washed away. Based on available sources, at least 105,000 people were exposed to floods likely to have destructive impact on shelters and livelihoods.

On 15 May, the State Administration Council declared all 17 townships of Rakhine state as disaster affected areas under section 11 of the Natural Disaster Management Law, which recognizes the special role of the Myanmar Red Cross in disaster management.  On 16 May, a similar announcement was made for four townships in Chin State (Tiddim, Matupi, Paletwa and Hakha).

Early, local reports indicate several human casualties and hundreds of people injured, while over 137,000 people were evacuated prior to the landfall, based on Myanmar Red Cross reports from their branches. Monasteries, schools, and religious sites were designated as evacuation centers by local authorities in Rakhine, Chin, Magway and Sagaing. Communication services to Rakhine and main road access to Sittwe were cut and slowly being reestablished as of 16 May and Sittwe Airport remains closed as of 15 May. Efforts to identify impact and needs have started but there are challenges to access the affected areas, especially Northern Rakhine, Magway and Northern Sagaing; the safety and security of first responders will continue to be prioritized.

countries.name: Malaysia
dtype.name: Heat Wave
name: MYS: Heat Wave - 2023-05 - Heat Wave #3
summary:
The Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a level one hot weather status for four areas in the peninsula and one in Sarawak. According to the latest hot weather data uploaded on the department’s Facebook today, the four areas in Peninsula Malaysia involved Baling in Kedah as well as Hulu Perak, Kinta, and Manjung in Perak. Meanwhile, the level one area in Sarawak is Mukah. “No areas in Sabah are at level one,” The alert level is when the maximum daily temperature is between 35 to 37 degrees Celsius for at least three days consecutively.

on April 27 last An 18-month-old girl in Kelantan was reported to have died on Tuesday, believed to be due to heat stroke, the second victim due to the hot weather in the state. According to a Berita Harian report, the child's father, Ahmad Faris Fazli Mohd Nasir said, he took his only child Nur Imani to the Emergency Unit of Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital last Monday after his son vomited. According to him, the autopsy report conducted at the hospital found that the cause of Nur Imani's death was due to heat stroke. Previously on April 25, an 11-year-old boy from Kampung Perupok in Bachok, Kelantan was reported to be the first victim of heat stroke when he reportedly died. The victim, Muhamad Syamil Aqil, is said to have died at 9.27 am while receiving treatment at a clinic.

 

Also on May 5, Utusan Malaysia reported that schools across the country had been told to stop all outdoor activities, including cross-country running, amid the heat wave. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the ministry sent a circular informing all principals and school administrations about this decision.

Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the secretariat of the National Disaster Management Committee has met and carried out coordination efforts with various relevant ministries and departments to help the people cope with this new phenomenon.

 

MRCS NHQ has coordinated with the MRCS of the states involved for the purpose of monitoring the effects of heat waves and identifying the appropriate form and type of response that will be channeled. At the same time, MRCS is arranging coordination with relevant government agencies at the national and state levels for appropriate response purposes.

countries.name: Israel
dtype.name: Complex Emergency
name: ISR: Complex Emergency - 2023-05 - Rocket attack on cities in the south and center of Israel
summary:
Updated: May 13th, 20:00 (IDT)

On May 9th, 2023, in the morning hours, the Israeli authorities declared a state of emergency for the cities and villages 40 km from the Gaza Strip border. For the population in this area, restrictions on gathering, workplaces, and educational activities are in place. Several roads are closed for civilian movement. According to the Ministry of Defense reports, about 12,000 people who live near the border were evacuated to safer areas in Israel with the authorities support.

From May 10th to May 13th, two people were killed, several injured, and damages were caused to buildings, roads, and agricultural facilities in a series of rocket attacks from the Gaza Strip toward cities in the south and center of the country and cities near Jerusalem. Rockets hits were reported in Ashkelon, Sderot, Rechovot, Netivot, and other villages.

In Rechovot, one person died and several were moderately and lightly injured when a rocket hit a building on May 11th. In another rocket attack near Shokeda on May 13th, one person died and another was severely injured.  Several casualties suffer moderate and minor injuries from rockets and shrapnel hits, and when falling on their way to shelters during the attacks.

The state of emergency was extended until Monday (May 15th) at 20:00 (IDT).

In total, according to the Home Front Command (IDF) reports, more than 1,234 rockets were fired in these attacks. During and after the attacks, the population in the areas at higher risk is called to stay in or close to a shelter.

countries.name: Ethiopia
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: ETH: Population movement from Sudan
summary: On April 15, a conflict between the two main factions of the military regime in Sudan, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), broke out in Khartoum, the nation’s capital. Since then, there have been clashes between SAF and RSF in different areas of the country. According to the Sudanese Ministry of Health (MoH) more than 450 deaths and more than 4,000 injuries have been recorded since the conflict started. However, the actual death toll is likely much higher, as current figures include only deaths reported to health facilities and access to many locations within the country is restricted. As of April 27, at least 18 humanitarian aid workers have been killed. Since mid April, the situation in bordering countries, include Ethiopia has severely deteriorated and are expected to get worst in the coming weeks. While other bordering cuntries started receiving population fleeing from Sudan, for the case of Ethiopia, there was no movement of populations until the temporary ceasefire of 24th April. The first case load was received in the border point of Metema where the National Society and ICRC conducted a rapid assessment mission complemented by the UNHCR report of 1st May 2023 reporting more than 8,900 people arrived in Ethiopia and 50,000 projected to arrived. (https://reliefweb.int/map/sudan/sudan-situation-overview-01-may-2023). With a temporary pause in fighting in some areas, both Sudanese and foreign nationals have been trying to flee the country to neighboring countries including Ethiopia. Ethiopia is sharing a 1,600 km border with Sudan with entry points in three regions: Tigray, Amhara and Benishangul-Gumuz. So far the majority of the people crossing into Ethiopia has been entering through Metema border post. According to UNCHR more than 73,000 Ethiopian refugees are living in Sudan, most of them having fled Ethiopia during the 2 year long Tigray conflict. It is anticipated that many of them will return to Ethiopia as the conflict in Sudan is unfolding.

countries.name: Malaysia
dtype.name: Heat Wave
name: MYS: Heat Wave - 2023-05 - Heat Wave
summary:
According to media reports (Utusan Malaysia) the current hot and dry weather has destroyed 7,800 acres of rice planted in Kelantan. The extremely hot weather not only stunted the plants but also affected the water sources. This will cause a loss of income and have an impact on food security in the state.

Local authorities through Kemubu Agricultural Development Authority (Kada) have handed over an additional 16 water pumps with a capacity of three to 20 cubic feet a second, to alleviate the situation. Kada will also supply farmers who are registered with the agency with the diesel fuel needed to run the water pumps.

 

In the meantime, MRCS is monitoring the situation and if the situation worsens MRCS will conduct a rapid assessment to see the appropriate response to help those affected especially in the livelihood sector.

countries.name: Mongolia
dtype.name: Cold Wave
name: MNG: Cold Wave - 2023-05 - Snow and dust storms
summary: Violent storms are sweeping across western Mongolia with heavy precipitation starting from May 5th to current period (May 8, 23). According to Khovd provincial emergency commission, the snow height has reached 80-120 cm in the mountanous areas, at least 40 cm in the steppe areas completely isolating (disabling the all means of transportation) Duut, Munkhkhairkhan , Zereg, Darvi soums. On May 7, a herder household was affected by the storm and 18 staff from local emergency managemnet agency worked for 18 hours to rescue the household members and took them to the hospital. Due to the isolation from the snow, about 350 households can no longer take their herd on pasture and their livestock are being exposed to cold and malnourishment. Eventually, the malnourishment and cold exposure are expected to be become issue for the herders themselves. In the affected population, there are about 72 disabled person, 480 children and 21 pregnant women.

countries.name: Democratic Republic of Congo
countries.society_name: Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

summary:
On the night of May 4 to 5, 2023, a torencial rain fell on the villages of Bushushu and Nyamukubi in the territory of Kalehe in the province of South Kivu. This continued on May 6, 2023 and caused flooding and landslides, causing approximately 400 deaths, several missing people and loss of livelihoods.

The DRC Red Cross, through its South Kivu Branch, has deployed a team on the ground for rapid assessments and to contribute to humanitarian assistance to the affected people.

countries.name: Guatemala
dtype.name: Volcanic Eruption
name: GTM: Volcanic eruption - 2023-05 - Fuego Volcano Eruption
summary:
The volcanic monitoring network of the National Institute of Seismology, Volcanology, Meteorology and Hydrology (INSIVUMEH) records the descent of pyroclastic flows through the Ceniza Canyon. It has weak to moderate characteristics, but is likely to increase, causing ashfall in nearby areas.
These flows are a mixture of gases, ash, and high-temperature rock blocks that descend at high speed down the flanks of the volcano. It is not ruled out that in the following hours more pyroclastic flows of weak, moderate and strong characteristics with greater reach to other directions may be generated.

countries.name: Guatemala
dtype.name: Volcanic Eruption
name: GTM: Volcanic Eruption - 2023-05 - Fuego Volcano Eruption
summary: According to the  SPECIAL VOLCANOLOGICAL BULLETIN BEFGO #023-2023 UPDATE OF THE ERUPTION Guatemala, of May 04, 2023, 12:35 p.m. (Local Time), in the last few hours the eruptive activity continues at a high level, maintaining a column of gases and abundant ash at a height of more than 6000 meters (19,685 feet), which, according to GOES-16 satellite imagery products, continues to move westward and southwest at distances of more than 100 kilometers. The ejection of this eruptive column is accompanied by constant moderate and strong rumblings and shock waves, as well as the descent of moderate and strong pyroclastic flows that travel between 5 and 7 kilometers away along the Ceniza Canyons. Las Lajas, Seca and Santa Teresa. In the last few minutes, the strongest pyroclastic flow has descended in the Ceniza Canyon. These pyroclastic flows continue to cause constant and abundant ashfall in the communities located in the vicinity of the canyons where these flows continue to descend. The dispersion of the eruptive column produces slight ashfalls over several municipalities in the department of Suchitepéquez.

countries.name: Rwanda
dtype.name: Pluvial/Flash Flood
name: RWA: Pluvial/Flash Flood - 2023-05 - Heavy rains causing floods and landslides
summary:
The heavy rains registered within three consecutive days have caused intensive damages in various parts of country, particuolarly the Western province, Northern province and Southern province. The death toll is high, amounting to 130 people people dead; 77 were injured; 5 persons are missing. Overall, 7684 households were evacutated (with over 38,000 people) as a result of total destroyed houses or heavily damaged.

In addition, the people's livelihoods were affected: livestock dead, destroyed crops, food stocks and households were destroyed and merged with mud, the market supply system is particially functionnal due to damaged roads, market places and shops. 

As well, in different parts of the country, public infrastrure were affected: Damaged roads (8 National and 9 districts roads section, 26 bridges); 6 Water Treatment Plants flooded and not functional; 8 health facilities (2 health Posts, 5 health centers and 1 hospital (Shyira) were affected.

People are in heavy distress and required PSS. The burial services have strated as well as the medical care for injured people, while the surch of missing 5 people is ongoing. 

These numbers are likely to increase due to ongoing assessment together with local and security autorities and RRCS volunteers. As well, the meteo forcast predicts more intense rainfalls in coming days.

countries.name: China
dtype.name: Earthquake
name: CHN: Earthquake - 2023-05 - M5.2 Earthquake in Baoshan, Yunnan Province
summary: A 5.2-magnitude earthquake hit the city of Baoshan in Southwest China's Yunnan province at 11:27 pm (Beijing Time) on May 2nd, 2023, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). The epicenter was monitored at 25.35 degrees north latitude and 99.28 degrees east longitude, with a depth of 10 km. A magnitude 3.0 earthquake was registered at 3am on May 3rd, 2023. 3 people are reported to have been mildly injured in the earthquake. 2,805 houses are reported damaged in Longyang District. 37,941 people took emergency evacuation.

countries.name: Israel
dtype.name: Complex Emergency
name: ISR: Complex Emergency - 2023-05 - Rocket attack on cities in the south of Israel
summary:
On May 2nd, 2023, since the morning hours, Israel faced a series of rocket attacks from the Gaza Strip toward cities in the south of the country, resulting in several casualties, damage to buildings and cars, and fires.

In the afternoon hours (IDT) on May 2nd, a rocket attack of 22 launches from Gaza was initiated toward cities in the south of Israel. Four people were injured, several others suffered stress related conditions, and damage was caused to buildings in Sderot and villages.

Later that day, at around 21:30 and during the night, more rockets were fired from the Gaza Strip, resulting in a series of rocket alarms in cities in the south of the country.

In total, according to the Home Front Command (IDF) reports, 104 rockets were fired in this attack. During and after the attacks, the population in the regions at higher risk is called to stay in or close to a shelter.

countries.name: Tanzania, United Republic of

summary: According to the Government of Tanzania, Nachingwea district in Lindi region has recently faced a significant challenge of elephants invansion into farmsland and subsequent distruction of crops. A total of 14 out of 36 wards have been affected, and more than 730 households have been affected as well. This situation has resulted into severe food insecurity and nutrition, posing the threats to the well-being of the local communities. This also exacerbarates the human-elephants conflicts. The government through the District Administrative Secretary of Nachingwea district has requested for the urgent assistance to the affected households for food so as to meet their daily dietary needs.

In the Sverdlovsk, Kurgan and Tyumen regions, as a result of the spread of fire in 25 settlements, more than 6 thousand buildings were damaged, including 802 residential buildings. In order to stabilize the situation, more than 2,000 people and more than 300 units were involved in the localization and extinguishing of natural fires. equipment, including 21 aircraft. The main efforts of the EMERCOM of Russia are focused on the protection of settlements.

According to Russian Red Cross,  in Sverdlovsk region only a total of 659 people, including 148 children, lost their houses.

summary:
Tanzania is currently experiencing one of the worst cholera outbreaks in years. The first case was registered in Ilala district in the Dar es salaam  region on 20 April 2023. The Tanzania Ministry of Health declared the cholera outbreak on 24 April 2023 after the increase and spread of confirmed cases. The cholera outbreak, initially limited to the eastern part of the country, has now spread from Kivule wards to Ilala and Buguruni wards in Dar es salaam region. 
There is also spread to neighboring Zambia, Mozambique, Malawi and Zimbabwe where outbreaks are being declared.

Tanzania Red Cross Society report that there is an urgent need to address the risk factors of the outbreak, such as the provision of safe drinking water, especially in the hotspot areas. Several displaced communities in areas that were affected in 2023 by the Floods Dar es salaam and Mtwara are still living in precarious hygienic conditions due to high rainfall still increasing and raining. The floods and associated malnutrition that has affected vast areas of Tanzania are making the communities, particularly children, more at risk of mortality due to the increased vulnerability caused by their poor nutritional status.

Effected Population are with family and friends. Food supplies are still at a good level

countries.name: Nepal
dtype.name: Heat Wave
name: NPL: Heat Wave - 2023-04 - Heat wave preparedness and response
summary:
If temperature in these areas keep increasing over coming 3-4 days, the health condition of people will be deteriorated in the districts situated in southern belt of Nepal. Heatwave aggravated by forest fire, air pollutions and emergence of different infectious diseases can have disproportionate effects. 


In terms of heatwave, the most commonly children, elderly population, pregnant and lactating mothers, people with disability and daily wage labors/ people with low-income will have direct impact on their health, nutrition and living conditions. The extreme hot weather may have direct affect on health due to high incidence of dengue in approaching monsoon with overarching effects on overall health system. As a result cardiovascular effects to elderly population due to prolonged heatwaves including aggravated effects due to underlying health conditions may occur in these areas. Furthermore, extreme heat can increase the risk for preterm birth, low birth weight, fetal death, and infant mortality alongwith heat related injuries and illness among daily-wage workers due to exposure to prolonged heat.

countries.name: Chad
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: DBT: Displacement from Sudan to Chad
summary:
Following the attack on the villages of Tendulti on the Sudanese side, there was a movement of Sudanese populations on Chadian territory in the villages of Koufroune, Madjiguilta and Dizé Birte. Between 10,000 and 20,000 people have settled along the border, under the trees, including a large number of women and children at risk. The priority needs noted are access to water, shelter, food, health and some non-food items. The food stocks of asylum seekers will run out in 3 to 5 days. A dozen seriously wounded Sudanese army personnel were registered and hospitalized at the hospital in Adre. It was reported that 3 of them died in hospital as a result of their injuries. A few other seriously injured people were evacuated to the provincial hospital of Abeche. Authorities are providing security along the border and have launched an appeal for humanitarian assistance to assist the new arrivals.

The continuation of the conflicts in Sudan could see the displacement crisis observed on the Chad side worsen. The possible lull resulting from the call for a ceasefire in Sudan would be an opportunity for a greater rush of displaced people to the nearest border countries, with Chad being the majority concerned. Based on historical and current data, the trend will most certainly increase in the coming weeks.

On the night 17 and 18 April 2023, the villages around the Kiwira, Mbaka and Lufilyo rivers at  Kyela District, Mbeya Region experienced severe floods as a result of heavy downpour from the ongoing monsoon rains. So far, this flood has affected a total of 3 wards, and 9 villages including; Lupaso, Kilwa, Buluma, Kabanga, Isaka, Ndwanga, Kisyosyo, Ntundumano and Lusungo. Approximately 945 households  and 4725 population have been misplaced after their houses being surrounded by water and 113 houses have been destroyed. addiitonally, number of assets have been destroyed, farms, livestock and infrastructures. More damage is anticipanted as it keeps on raining. This calls for immediate response from the government and the National Society.

The affected three wards host around 6000 households, that approximately 30,000 population. The main economic activity in these wards is agriculture,livestock keeping and Fishing. The cultivated crops are rice, maize, cassava, sweetpotatoes, groundnuts and Cocoa. Most of the agricultural areas washed away by floods. TRCS branch (Mbeya Red Cross regional team) aside of local authorities visited the affected villages on 18th April 2023 and issued initial assessment data to start guiding the first emergency assistance to the affected communities

countries.name: Sudan
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: Sudan Crisis: Population Movement Neighbouring Countries
summary:
The Sudan conflict does not stop at the border. Due to the increase of the significant cross-border population movements out of Sudan as a result of the ongoing conflict and the deepening humanitarian crisis, the IFRC has revised the Emergency Appeal to support the humanitarian response of National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in neighbouring countries — Chad, Egypt, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Central African Republic (CAR) and Libya. Developed in close coordination with Movement partners, this Appeal complements the IFRC Sudan Emergency Appeal and reflects a shared commitment to address urgent humanitarian needs and protection risks affecting displaced populations and host communities across the region.

The conflict in Sudan has generated one of the world’s largest displacement crises, driving 4,400,882 people to flee areas of active fighting in search of safety. Displacement continues both internally and across borders as violence persists, essential services collapse, and humanitarian access remains constrained. Those who flee include Sudanese refugees, returnees and third-country nationals, with a high proportion of women and children, and many older people and persons living with disabilities. The scale and complexity of displacement is compounded by repeated floods, including seasonal hazards and disease outbreaks, which further increase humanitarian needs and reduce coping capacity.

People arriving in neighbouring countries report severe and prolonged hardship during their journeys. Many have been exposed to violence, extortion, while facing dangerous travel conditions and long periods without reliable access to food, clean water, health services, and basic shelter. Psychological distress is widespread due to trauma, family separation and uncertainty, while protection risks, including sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), remain acute and are often heightened during transit and at border entry points.

Upon arrival, refugees and returnees continue to face significant challenges. They frequently with limited resources or documentation, requiring urgent assistance to meet basic needs and access essential services. While host governments and communities have demonstrated solidarity, the size and pace of arrivals are exceeding local capacities, particularly in remote border areas where infrastructure and services are already limited. The pressure on health, water, education, shelter, and livelihoods is increasing, placing additional strain on the most vulnerable host families and raising the risk of social tension. The Sudan conflict is therefore not only a national tragedy but a regional humanitarian emergency that requires sustained international support and protection for displaced populations. The needs remain incredibly high, since people are not only affected by ongoing violence, but also by recurring droughts, floods, and disease outbreaks. Sudanese refugees and host communities are not affected once or twice, but repeatedly hit in every aspect of their lives.

As the crisis continues and humanitarian needs intensify, National Societies are providing critical, trusted, community-based support at points of entry and in areas hosting refugees and returnees. National Societies in Egypt, Chad, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Uganda are planning to scale up the response capacities to support current situation. This Revised Emergency Appeal will strengthen the ability of National Society staff and volunteers to implement their national response plans, maintain safe and accountable operations, and sustain essential humanitarian services for displaced people and the most vulnerable host communities. Through this Appeal, the IFRC will reinforce the collective Federation-Wide response to reduce suffering, protect dignity, and support resilience for people affected by the Sudan crisis across borders.

countries.name: Sudan
dtype.name: Complex Emergency
name: Sudan Crisis - Complex Emergency Sudan
summary:
Sudan was plunged into a dire humanitarian crisis as a result of armed conflict. In the early morning of 15 April 2023, Khartoum woke up to the sound of gunfire and explosions. This was the first time that Sudan’s capital city was at the epicentre of a fierce conflict between two powerful groups, the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The conflict has resulted in one of the biggest displacement crises globally, with more than 6 million people internally displaced by April 2024.

People trapped in conflict areas are running out of survival means and are being forced to take risks to make ends meet. Many families have had to make the hard choice to evacuate children and youth, accompanied by their mothers. In some instances, evacuation buses have been attacked, and there are reports of increased sexual violence against people on the move. The fighting in Khartoum and other parts of the country is taking place in densely populated urban areas and endangering the lives of civilians. Shrapnel and stray bullets are flying around in residential neighbourhoods.

Prices of food, fuel and other basic goods are spiking throughout Sudan with prices of many staples rising significantly. Access to essential services such as healthcare, markets and schools continues to be highly limited nationwide while frequent power outages and communication blackouts are being reported. Given the fragility of ceasefire efforts, this downward trajectory will likely continue, driving need among resident and displaced populations.

 

The IFRC Emergency Appeal aims to support the response of the Sudanese RC, as well as its staff and volunteers, to continue delivering essential humanitarian assistance to the most affected.

countries.name: Kenya
dtype.name: Complex Emergency
name: KEN: Complex Emergency - 2023-04 - Sudan Evacuation Operation in Kenya
summary:
An armed conflict between rival factions of the military government of Sudan began on 15th April 2023. The conflict started when clashes broke out across mostly the West side of Sudan, as well as in the capital city of Khartoum and Darfur Region.

Heavy gunfire and explosions have been witnessed in several parts of Khartoum and Darfur as Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) continue to engage the Rapid Support Forces, a paramilitary group, in what is being described as a ‘power struggle’ over who gets to run the country. Today (Monday, 22nd May 2023) marked the 39th day since the clashes began.

 

The Government of Kenya through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs have been evacuating its nationals, amongst them being students, workers, etc., through Ethiopia and South Sudan.

countries.name: Burundi

summary:
Following heavy rain, the Rusizi River overflowed and caused flooding in 5 hills in the Gatumba Zone. These floods have caused the displacement of 679 households from Kinyinya I, Kinyinya II, Mushasha I and II hills as well as Gaharawe hill. These households have partially or totally destroyed houses.

Currently, these households are in makeshift houses and only 200 have already benefited from family tents and NFI kits from the Burundi Red Cross. The newly displaced are concentrated in the Kinyinya Site2) and others are massed around the Gatumba-Border Road in very unfavourable conditions.

 

It should be noted that the flooding continues to such an extent that there are new households that continue to be affected and consequently increase the number of displaced households.

countries.name: Chile
dtype.name: Population Movement
name: CHL: Population Movement - 2023-04 - Migration Crisis in the Northern Zone of Chile
summary:
For some years now, the city of Iquique has been part of the migratory route of people who travel mainly from Venezuela, crossing countries such as Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia to Chile, who enter Chile through unauthorized crossings on the northern border in the town of Colchane, which is located on the border with Bolivia.

 

As a last contingency, the municipal authorities of Colchane received about 300 migrants who were stranded in the town of Pisiga Carpa in the Chilean commune of Colchane, foreigners of various nationalities were prevented from crossing from Chile to Bolivia due to their situation as irregular migrants.

 

Among the hundreds of stranded migrants are children and older adults who suffered from various ailments due to the altitude (3,700 meters above sea level) and the intense cold of the highlands. Thanks to the efforts of the municipality of Colchane with the provincial delegation, it was possible for them to enter the migrant shelter in the border complex of Chile and Bolivia.

 

Foreigners of various nationalities were prevented from crossing from Chile to Bolivia due to their migrant status. However, due to the negotiations between the municipality and the provincial delegation, it was possible for them to enter the migrant shelter at the Chile-Bolivia Border Complex.

 

The population of Colchane has a transitional system where humanitarian services were previously provided by the various organizations, however, currently, due to administrative and operational situations, it is not fully operational.

 

In the city of Iquique, there is also the "Lobitos" transitory device, which is located at a distance of approximately 15 km from Iquique, therefore, people who arrive at this device have difficulty moving to carry out procedures or errands with the organizations that provide humanitarian assistance in the city.

 

During March, the migratory flow in the city has increased, so sometimes groups of people arrive at the Iquique branch directly requesting the services that were previously provided with the population mobility project, to which they respond with what is available at the moment, for example, water, food or some hygiene items, psychosocial support and FCR.

 

On the other hand, due to the acts of violence that have been seen in recent months in the regions, an emphasis has been placed on inspecting foreigners in an irregular situation and reporting them to the administrative authorities.

 

In the City of Arica, specifically on the Arica-Tacna Border, there are 150 people (during the week of April 20, a population that would be increasing) who cannot enter Peru, settling on the Concordia line and preventing the passage to the Santa Rosa Border Control (Peru) where the documentation process for the exit from Chile and entry into Peru is carried out.
 
These people are mainly Venezuelan and Haitian nationals who arrive in the city by bus or plane, and then travel on foot to the border.
